presses, and `^k` opens the first link, not the PR). No notification row for a failed pipeline:
the feed, the card and the crown carry it. GitLab names no failing job on this road (one more
call per MR). A GitHub Enterprise host is told from a GitLab one only by which CLI's `auth status`
passes. The `m` hint on the ticket page still reads `m merge` with a PR open; the daemon's
sentence answers the press.

**Tests.** `forge_e2e` (a stub `gh` on the daemon's PATH: the PR binds by the ticket's branch,
its red pipeline reaches the snapshot and refuses a `requires_pipeline` column in its words, `m`
says the PR is the merge, the forge's merge reads merged with `main (PR #42)`, DONE's `Arrives
here when: merged` takes the ticket, the merge commit's pipeline reads off check-runs, the feed
says the merge and nothing of the first read); units beside `core::forge` (both JSON shapes, the
fold, the remote parser, the binding rule, the set, the detector on both transcripts, the URL
number, the deployments, the name cap), `daemon::forge` (the delta, the edge, the reflog, the
cadence, the CLI lookup), `cost` (a `pr create` and its result across two passes), `train` (an
open PR, a conflict, a stale verdict), `prefs` (both new keys), the keymap laws, goldens
`settings_behaviour_*`, `settings_appearance_board_60`, `settings_groups_*`, `column_settings_120`,
`ticket_prs_120`, `board_prs_120`. The rig's F1 (`ci/rig/tests.toml`; `forge_pr`, `forge_fail`,
`forge_off` steps put a stub `gh` first on the rig daemon's PATH and write the worker's PR, the
`woke:<cause>` check reads the feed's wakes): on the real Sonnet, 2026-10-13, PASS in 68 s —
the board woke the crown `pipeline`, the crown's `ask_agent` reached the worker, which replied
`noted`. `cargo nextest run --workspace`: 2319 passed.

## On a forge board, ahead counts against the upstream, and a leg keeps the MR that merged it (T-786, 2026-10-15, follow-up to T-779 and T-780)

**Found in forge lab run 3.** D1 (T-17): the `delivered` wake said `ahead api 5` for a branch one
commit ahead of `origin/main`. Since T-779 a forge board's worktree is cut from the upstream when
the local `main` is behind it, but `ahead` and `needs_rebase` were still counted against the local
`main`, which nothing moves on a board whose merges happen on the forge: every PR ticket read
ahead by everything the forge merged since the checkout last moved. A (T-13): !9 from the ticket
branch merged and the leg read `main (MR !9)`; then !11 from `fix/a` merged, `origin/main` moved,
the git road re-judged the leg by patch-id against it, and since `forge::merged_at` asked the
repository's *newest* PR to be merged at the tip, !11 unnamed it and the card said `origin/main`.

**The counts.** `compute_flags` takes `forge` (the `RepoQuery`'s, from `forge.remotes`, parsed on
the worker where the cache has none). Where it is set and the pass's target is the upstream
(which it is only when the upstream holds everything the local base holds) and the two tips
differ, `ahead` and `needs_rebase` come from a second `rev-list --left-right --count
origin/main...branch`, one more fork per binding and only while the local base is behind.
`WtFlags::counted` names that ref, and `base_tip` is then the upstream's tip, so the train's
rebase asks and refusals (keyed on it) re-arm when the forge merges. Ancestry, `merged` and
`merged_in` stay the local base's: the DONE gate, the ff merge and the content verdict are
unchanged. Equal tips, no forge remote, or a local base ahead or diverged keep today's counts.
**The words:** the ticket page says `1 ahead of origin/main` and `origin/main moved`
(`WorktreeItem.counted`, off the wire when empty); the rebase ask and `merge_ticket`'s refusal
name `origin/main` (`RepoFlags::against`). The crown's words keep `ahead api 1`.

**The merge words.** `merged_at` is now the newest merged PR in the repository whose head is the
tip: a commit after the merge still leaves the tip no merged head, and a later PR from another
branch, merged or open, no longer unnames the one that landed the leg. An open one holds the
ticket's merge on its own (`holding`, T-774); `get_ticket`'s PR rows carry the rest.

**Tests.** Unit `a_forge_repository_counts_against_the_upstream_that_moved_ahead` (forge and not,
behind the upstream, equal, diverged) and `a_leg_merged_by_the_forge_keeps_its_words_after_a_later_merge`
(worktree); `the_set_is_newest_first_without_the_abandoned` widened (core forge);
`the_workspace_row_names_the_upstream_it_counts_against` (TUI).
`worktree_e2e::a_forge_boards_worktree_starts_at_the_fetched_upstream` now moves the remote four
merges ahead and commits once on the branch: `ahead` 1, `counted` `origin/main` (5 and empty with
the choice switched off). `cargo nextest run --workspace`: 2419 passed.

## An open MR's head and pipeline are read from the MR itself (T-784, 2026-10-15, follow-up to T-739 and T-780)

**Measured in forge lab run 3, on gitlab.com.** The worker pushed a fix (`ebf3084`) to MR !9's
branch at ~00:32 local; its pipeline passed at 00:34. At 00:37 both `glab mr list --output json`
and the REST list `projects/:id/merge_requests?state=opened` still served `"sha": "dc82695…"` (the
failed commit) and an `updated_at` from before the push: five minutes and counting. The single
read `projects/:id/merge_requests/9` named `ebf3084` and `head_pipeline.status: success`.
**GitLab's MR list lags a push by minutes; its single-MR read does not.** Since T-780 the gate
holds a pipeline whose head is not the leg's tip, so the ticket sat `pipeline not read` for as
long as the list lagged.

**The read.** On the worker, after the list and the binding, an open GitLab MR is read whole
(`glab api projects/<id>/merge_requests/<iid>`, `forge::parse_glab_mr`) when `mr_unsure`: its
list head is not the tip of the ticket's branch in its repository's leg, or no tip judges it (a
repository with no leg, an MR from another branch, as `head_unread` reads them) and the ticket's
reads never held it (`TicketQuery::held`). `Pr::take_read` takes the head, the conflict and the
merge status's review word; the read's `head_pipeline` is the pipeline, its job named by the
same jobs read (`named_job`), and only where it is absent, of another sha, or of a status the
board has no word for is the pipeline read by sha as before. A failed read keeps the list's row,
and the T-780 gate then holds, as it should. An MR the list already has at the tip costs nothing
more. The tips are read on the worker (`branch_tip` in each leg's worktree), not taken from
`wt_repos`: the flags' tip is a slow bucket old at the turn's end that pushed, the window T-780
read fresh for the same reason.

**GitHub, unchanged.** `gh pr list` is GraphQL, and the lab's #3 showed no such lag in run 3,
so no per-PR read was added. If one is ever
seen, the same shape is `gh pr view <n> --json headRefOid,statusCheckRollup,mergeable` under
`mr_unsure`.

**Deploy words in event order.** Lab C2 (#3, GitHub) woke the crown with `deployed to production
#3, deployed to staging #3`; staging had deployed 5 s first. `deployments` returned GitHub's list
order, newest first. It now returns `forge::deploy_order`: by the deployment's time (GitHub's
success status `created_at`, GitLab's `finished_at`, else `updated_at`, else `created_at`) when
every one has a time, else by the order the board's columns ask for them, never by name. An
environment a later pass finds is appended after those already known, which is its time order.

**Tests.** Unit `a_single_mr_read_overrides_the_lists_stale_head` and
`deployments_are_said_in_the_order_they_happened` (core forge),
`an_mr_is_read_whole_only_where_the_list_may_be_stale` (daemon forge).
`forge_e2e::an_open_mrs_head_and_pipeline_are_read_from_the_mr_itself`: !9 binds failed, the
turn commits a fix, the stub's `mr list` keeps the failed head while its `api …/merge_requests/9`
names the fix with a passed head pipeline, and REVIEW's `pipeline passes` arrival takes the
ticket with the list never caught up. With the read switched off the same test times out held.
`cargo nextest run --workspace`: 2414 passed.

## Every open GitLab MR is read by itself, and a forge board's rebase ask names the upstream (T-787, 2026-10-15, follow-up to T-784 and T-779)

**Measured in forge lab run 3, on gitlab.com.** !11 (`fix/a`) merged on GitLab at 00:59:27
local. At 01:00:24 the board still read it `open, pipeline passed`, and REVIEW's `Arrives here
when: pipeline passes` pulled lab ticket T-13 from PROD back to REVIEW; at 01:01:34 the list said
`merged` and the ticket went to PROD again. The list's head was current, so T-784's `mr_unsure`
never asked: **GitLab's list lags a merge's state as it lags a push's head.**

**The read.** Every GitLab MR the list calls open (`opened`, draft) is read by itself on every
pass (`gitlab_mr`), and `Pr::take_read` now takes the read's state, head, conflict, review word
and merge commit (`merge_commit_sha`, else `squash_commit_sha`), and its `updated_at` where it is
the later one. An MR the read finds merged or closed gets no head pipeline: `merged_reads` reads
its merge commit's, as for a merge the list said. The set is re-sorted by `ticket_set` after any
read, so a closed one leaves it and the newest-touched leads. `mr_unsure` and
`TicketQuery::held` are gone; a board has few open MRs, so the price is one call per open MR per
pass. A failed read keeps the list's row, and the T-780 gate holds a stale head as before.

**GitHub, not measured.** The probe (open a PR on the private `forge-lab` repo, push, merge, and
poll the daemon's own `gh pr list --author @me --state all --json …` once a second) was refused by
the session's permission mode at the merge, which needs a person. `gh pr list` is unchanged; the
lab's #3 showed no lag in run 3. If a person's probe sees one, the shape is T-784's note.

**The rebase ask on a forge board.** D1's worker (lab T-17, MR !12) was asked to rebase `onto
main (api)`: on a forge board the local base never moves (T-779), so that base was stale. T-786,
landed first, already names the ref the flags counted against (`RepoFlags::against`,
`origin/main` where the local base is strictly behind it), so this ticket's own ref choice (an
ask-time ancestry check, equal tips included) was dropped at the rebase in favour of T-786's
single source, which the train's base tip is keyed on too. What T-787 adds is the fetch: a rebase
ask whose legs include one counted against the upstream begins `Run git fetch first.` (`Run git
fetch in api first.` on a workspace, the asked legs by `leg_word`; `worktree::fetch_words`). A
board with no forge remote, a local base equal to, ahead of or diverged from its upstream, and the
merged notice read as before.

**Tests.** Unit `a_single_mr_read_overrides_the_lists_stale_state` (core forge: list `opened`,
read `merged` → merged with its merge commit, no longer `holding`), the T-784 unit test now
asserting the read's later time; `a_forge_legs_rebase_ask_begins_with_the_fetch` (daemon
worktree: a local leg's words unchanged, a counted leg's full sentence, a workspace's fetch naming
only the legs onto an upstream).
`forge_e2e::an_open_mrs_state_is_read_from_the_mr_itself`: !11 binds running, the stub's single
read says merged while its list keeps `opened` and the head's pipeline passes; DONE's `merged`
takes the ticket and REVIEW never does. With the single read switched off the same test times out
in REVIEW. No rig test covers the rebase ask: the rig board runs on this repository's refs, whose
`main` is ahead of `origin/main`, so the new words are unreachable there without moving the
author's real refs; a rig of its own repository is what one needs. `ci/rig.py --only F1` passed on
claude 2.1.300 (the forge pass end to end). `cargo nextest run --workspace`: 2416 of 2418, the two
load flakes (`forge_e2e::an_open_pr_holds_done_and_a_ticket_there_reads_unmerged`, a GitHub stub,
and `mod_plugin`, the real `claude`) green alone.

## The pipeline gate judges the branch's tip, and the forge names a merge git found first (T-780, 2026-10-14, follow-up to T-739)

**Found in forge lab run 2.** T-9: MR !5's pipeline had passed; the worker pushed a `FAIL` commit
and its turn ended at ~17:41:07, and the `on_done` move into REVIEW (`requires_pipeline`) was
allowed on the board's last reading, `passed`, which was the commit before the push's. The read
at 17:41:31 showed the new pipeline running, then failed; the fix's push was then held on that
old `failed`, the right outcome for the wrong reason. T-10: both legs read merged by the git
road's patch-id against `origin/main` before the forge's read, so the fold skipped them and the
card said `origin/main` where T-9 had said `main (MR !5)`.

**The gate.** `forge::head_unread(set, branch, tips)`: an open PR from the ticket's branch (or
with no `head_ref`) whose `head_oid` is not that leg's tip now. Its pipeline says nothing of the
branch as it stands, whether the forge has not read the push yet or the commit was never pushed,
and `pipeline_refusal` answers `pipeline not read` before anything else, so `column_gate`,
`agent_allowed_columns` and the held-automove line say it alike. The tip is read fresh
(`worktree::branch_tip`, one `rev-parse` per leg that holds an open PR, writer thread):
`wt_repos`' tip is a slow bucket old at the turn's end that pushed, which is exactly the window
the lab hit. Not judged: a PR from another branch (bound by URL or reflog, whose head need not
be ours), a repository with no leg, an empty head or tip, and merged PRs (their pipeline is the
merge commit's, T-767).

**The arrival.** `Edge::passed` also fires when an open PR's head moved between two reads and
the set reads passed: a push the forge ran and passed between reads is a new commit's pass,
where before it read as passed-to-passed and no edge, which would have left the ticket the gate
just held stuck. `Arrival::PipelinePasses` takes the ticket only when `head_unread` is false.

**The merge words.** `forge_fold_legs` no longer skips a leg git read merged:
`RepoFlags::fold_forge_merge` writes `merged_in = "{base} ({noun} {label})"` and the PR's merge
commit wherever the repository's newest PR is merged at the leg's tip, whichever road read the
merge first, and returns false when the words are already those (every pass folds). A leg
already merged is never a landing here (`was == Some(true)`), so the crown hears nothing twice.

**Tests.** Unit `a_pr_whose_head_is_not_the_tip_is_unread` (core forge), `a_pass_on_a_moved_head_is_an_edge`
(daemon forge), `the_forge_names_a_merge_the_git_road_found_first` (worktree).
`forge_e2e::the_pipeline_gate_judges_the_branchs_tip`: PR #42 passed at the first commit, a
commit in the turn, the turn's end refused `pipeline not read — before REVIEW` and REVIEW off
`get_ticket`'s columns; the stub moves the head, passed, and REVIEW's `pipeline passes` arrival
takes it; then git reads an ff-merge first (the stub listing nothing, since an open PR holds it
unmerged) and the merged PR renames it `main (PR #42)`. `cargo nextest run --workspace`: 2403
passed.

## A forge board's worktree starts at the fetched upstream (T-779, 2026-10-14, follow-up to T-739)

**Found in forge lab run 2.** On a board whose work merges on GitLab nothing moves the
checkout's local `main`: the forge merges and the fetch row moves `origin/main` only (promise 1).
The lab's `api` main sat at its first commit while `origin/main` held run 1's merges; the next
ticket's worktree was cut from that stale `main`, its MR conflicted with `origin/main` from
birth, and the train asked a rebase for a conflict the worker never made.

**The cut point.** `worktree::cut_point(repo, base, local)` is asked by `provision` and by each
leg of `provision_workspace` (in the precheck, which still writes nothing): when the repository's
remote parses as a forge's (`forge::remote_of`, the same reader that fills `forge.remotes`) and
its upstream (`upstream_base`, `origin/main`) strictly descends from the local base, the branch
starts at the upstream's tip; equal, ahead or diverged, and any repository with no forge remote,
keep the local base, so a person's unpushed commits stay theirs. The cut is the leg's `base_oid`
as before, so the diff, "no work yet" (`tip == base_oid`) and teardown's branch delete read the
new branch right. Everything else keeps reading the local base (`ahead`, the train's ff-merge,
the DONE gate): such a branch counts the fetched merges as ahead of local `main`, which on a PR
board the forge, not the local merge, lands. Writes are what provisioning wrote before: one
branch ref and one worktree.

**Doctor.** The `branch` line on such a checkout ends `; local main is N behind origin/main; new
worktrees start from origin/main` (`worktree::cut_words`).

**Tests.** `worktree::tests::a_fresh_branch_starts_at_an_upstream_that_moved_ahead` (equal,
upstream ahead, no forge remote, local ahead, diverged, the doctor words, and `provision` taking
the cut with local `main` unmoved); `worktree_e2e::a_forge_boards_worktree_starts_at_the_fetched_upstream`
(a bare remote moved ahead by a second clone, fetched, the URL then a GitLab one: the ticket's
branch starts at `origin/main`, reads unmerged, and local `main` never moves). `cargo nextest run
--workspace`: 2399 passed.

## An open PR holds DONE, as it holds the train (T-774, 2026-10-14, follow-up to T-739)

**Why.** The forge lab's finding 14 (2026-10-13, scenario B3): ticket A1's MR !1 merged, the
branch read merged and the card went to DONE; the worker then opened MR !2 from `fix/greeting`
on the same ticket. The card read `◯!2 ●!1`, `merge_state` stayed `merged` and DONE kept it
while !2 was in review. The train already read an open PR as unfinished (`pr_open`); the merge
gate did not.

**The decision, and it is provisional.** The author, 2026-10-14: an open PR holds DONE, to be
revisited after dogfooding. An open PR on the ticket, on any repository and any branch
(`PrState::Open | Draft`, `forge::holding`), means its work has not landed:
- `ticket_merged` answers false while one is open, so the DONE gate, the delete gate, the
  archive and `m` read it unmerged; `column_gate` names it first, in `merge_ticket`'s sentence
  plus the column (`MR !2 open — merge it on GitLab before DONE`, `forge::open_refusal`), for
  every mover, a person included, and on a checkout ticket too.
- The card and the page (`WorktreeItem.merged`) read it unmerged where the branch landed, so
  the reclaim and sleep offers hold off; `get_ticket`'s `merge_state` reads `open MR !2` there
  (the four words otherwise); `agent_allowed_columns` drops a `requires_merge` column.
- A gate refuses entry and never evicts: a ticket already in DONE stays, unmerged, and an
  arrival rule moves it as any ticket.
- **Not changed:** `wt_agg.merged` stays the branch's reading, so the train (which holds on
  `pr_open` already) and the crown's wake words (`merge_state merged`, T-757's later-PR wake)
  are as they were. The hold is read at the readers above, not folded into the aggregate.

**Tests.** Unit `an_open_pr_on_a_merged_ticket_holds_the_merge` (core forge: the open MR on
another branch holds with the refusal's words; a draft on another repository holds beside a
merged-at-tip PR; merged, nothing holds). `forge_e2e::an_open_pr_holds_done_and_a_ticket_there_reads_unmerged`:
two tickets ff-merged and one moved to DONE, then PRs on side branches bind by reflog; the one
in DONE stays and reads unmerged with `merge_state` `open PR #2`, a hand move of the other is
refused `PR #3 open — merge it on GitHub before DONE`, and once both merge DONE admits it. With
the gate clause removed the e2e fails at the hand move. Rig F6 (`forge_later_open`, checks
`not_column`/`crown_reply`): on the real Sonnet, 2026-10-14, PASS in 72 s — asked to move the
merged ticket to DONE with PR #43 open, the crown answered `F6 held: PR #43 open — merge it on
GitHub before DONE`. `cargo nextest run --workspace`: 2377 passed.

## A ticket arrives as its least advanced PR (T-768, 2026-10-14, follow-up to T-739)

**Why.** The forge lab's finding 8 (2026-10-13, scenario C1: one ticket, MRs on `api` and `web`).
STAGING took the ticket when web's !1 was merged and on staging while api's !3 was still open,
and PROD when web's !1 reached production while api's !3 waited on `deploy:production`.
`forge::edge` built `deployed` from the union of every merged PR's environments, so one
repository's progress was the ticket's.

**The rule.** An arrival is the ticket's, and the ticket is as far as its least advanced PR:
- `Edge.merged`: every PR of the set merged. Already so (`all_merged`; a closed PR is out of the
  set, `forge::ticket_set`), and what `ticket_merged`'s forge clause asks per leg.
- `Edge.deployed` to E (`forge::arrived_envs`): no PR open, and each repository's newest merged
  PR's merge commit reached E. The newest alone, because it is the one a read asks deployments
  of, and an older merge on that repository is in its history.
- `Edge.passed`: every open PR passed, which T-767's worst-over-open already reads.

**The crown's words stay per PR.** `Edge.reached` keeps each merged PR's newly reached
environments by label, read against that PR's own last read, and `Edge::news` says
`deployed to staging !1` from it: an edge, heard before the ticket arrives. It also names the PR
correctly where the old fallback found the first merged PR with the environment, and it says a
later PR's deployment on a repository an earlier one had already put there.

**Tests.** Unit `a_ticket_arrives_as_its_least_advanced_pr` (web merged and on staging beside
api open: neither merged nor deployed, `deployed to staging !1` heard; both merged, one on
staging: merged, not deployed; both: deployed, `deployed to staging !3` heard; production the
same; an older merged PR on a repository does not hold it back; a pass is every open PR's).
`forge_e2e::a_deployed_arrival_waits_for_every_repositorys_pr`: a folder workspace with `api`
and `web`, a PR in each, REVIEW on `deployed: staging`; the ticket stays put while api's PR is
open and while its merge commit is off staging, and arrives once it is on. It fails on the old
rule.

## A merged PR's pipeline is no pass (T-767, 2026-10-14, follow-up to T-739)

**Why.** The forge lab's worst finding (2026-10-13, scenario C1): a ticket whose two MRs had
merged and deployed sat in PROD, and then api's main pipeline went `waiting` → `passed` as its
manual `deploy:production` finished. `forge::edge` filled `passed` from `pipeline_of`, which reads
the merge commit's pipeline once nothing is open, so REVIEW's `Arrives here when: pipeline passes`
took the edge and pulled the ticket back from PROD; the train then claimed it, and the
`deployed to production` for the other MR never came, since `forge_arrivals` takes the furthest
stage of one pass and that pass held the pass alone.

**The rule.** `Edge.passed` is the worst pipeline over the *open* PRs turning passed: what
`requires_pipeline` waits for. A merged commit's pipeline is the deploy run; it feeds
`Edge.waiting`, `Edge.failed`, `Edge.deployed` and the crown's words for those, never an arrival
on `pipeline passes` and never `pipeline passed` in a crown wake. A follow-up PR that opens green
on a merged set is a pass (the old rule missed it, the set's word having read passed already).
`Edge::news` names the open PRs for it, the merged fallback gone.

**An opening is said once.** `forge::State::held` keeps every PR, by repository and number, a
ticket's reads have held since this start, seeded from `forge.json` on restore; the caller keeps
`Edge.opened` only for an open PR not held before (`State::opens`). A PR a read missed (a
repository that failed on the ticket's first read, a binding that flickered) or a reopened one is
a re-read, not an opening. Memory only: the restored sets are the baseline it needs.

**Finding 10's answer: "Entry needs a passed pipeline" is entry-only.** It refuses a move into
the column while the pipeline has not passed; a pipeline that fails after the ticket entered is
the crown's forge wake (`pipeline failed !1: job`) and never a move out.

**Tests.** Units `a_merged_commits_pipeline_passing_is_no_pass` (running → passed and waiting →
passed on a merged set: no `passed`, the deployment as before; an open PR's pass beside a merged
one, and a follow-up opening green) and `an_opening_is_said_once`; the edge test's merge no
longer reads as a pass. `forge_e2e`: the merge commit's check-runs go from in progress to
success with REVIEW on `pipeline passes`, and the ticket stays in DONE; the crown hears
`pipeline passed #42` for the open PR alone, not when the merge commit's pipeline passes, and
not `pipeline passed #43` beside `merged #43`. Both e2e assertions fail on the old rule.

## An older PR keeps its pipeline and deployments (T-771, 2026-10-14, follow-up to T-739)

**Why.** Forge lab finding 15 (2026-10-13, scenario B3): once !2's merge commit deployed to
staging, !1's row fell from `pipeline passed`, deployed `[staging, production]` to `pipeline
unknown` with nothing deployed. `forge::sample` read the merge commit's pipeline and deployments
for the newest merged PR of each repository alone; the older PR took the list's words (GitLab's
list says no pipeline; GitHub's rollup is the head's, not the merge commit's) and an empty
deployed list, though `State` still held what earlier passes had read of its merge commit.

**The rule: per PR.** `forge::merged_reads` walks every merged PR of a set: what earlier passes
read of its merge commit (`commit_pipelines`, `deployed`, by repository and oid) is its own, a
pipeline is read again until it passes or fails, and deployments until every wanted environment
is in (a deployment is permanent, per PR). `commit_pipelines` now keeps the last read of any
word but `unknown`, so an unanswered call keeps the last reading rather than blanking it, and
`forge.json`'s commits restore the same. No schema bump: an older build restores the settled
words alone, as before.

**The bound.** A settled, covered PR is never read. A merge commit a newer one of the same
repository superseded is read only for `SUPERSEDED_READ_MS` (a day) after its merge, then keeps
what was read: a superseded commit's manual job left waiting, or an environment it will never
reach, costs nothing after that. The newest keeps the old cadence.

**The edge needed nothing of its own.** T-768, which landed first, made `Edge.deployed` the
ticket's arrival off each repository's newest merged PR and `Edge.reached` the crown's words,
per PR against the same PR's last read: an older PR keeping its environments neither hides a
newer one's deployment nor is said again. The card's brief, the page's rows and `^h`'s dialog
already drew each PR's own words, so the TUI is unchanged.

**Tests.** Unit `each_merged_pr_keeps_its_own_pipeline_and_deployments` (the newer PR's reads do
not touch the older one's; a settled, covered PR is not asked; an unanswered call keeps the last
read; a superseded day-old merge is not read; the edge says !2's staging and not !1's again).
`forge_e2e::an_older_pr_keeps_its_pipeline_and_deployments_after_a_newer_one_merges`: #42 merges,
passes and reaches staging, #43 merges and reaches staging, and #42 still reads passed and
deployed. The stub answers check-runs and deployments by sha; the e2e fails on the old code with
#42 at `running`, deployed `[]`.

## Forge words name what they are about (T-772, 2026-10-14, follow-up to T-739)

**Why.** Forge lab findings 13, 18, 19, 20 and 22 (2026-10-13): five words an agent or the crown
read that named the wrong thing or nothing. Words only; no schema bump.

**What changed.**
- `get_ticket` carries `merged_in` (13): the worktree row's word, `main (MR !1)` where the forge
  merged it or the ref a squash was found on, once `merge_state` reads `merged`; each workspace
  repo carries its own. Absent for a plain merge into the checkout's branch, which the row calls
  just `merged`. The crown ties a merge to its MR without reading `prs`.
- A merged branch's `merge` reads `by: nobody, why: already merged` (18). It read `by: train,
  the train is armed and reaches this column` in REVIEW, a merge to come that never would.
- A workspace repo's `name` is `root` for the root leg (22), `worktree::leg_word` as the ticket
  page says it; the daemon keeps `""`.
- The crown's wake delta says `ahead` per leg on a branch of more than one leg (19): `ahead api
  1 → 2`, each leg that moved. `wt_agg.ahead` sums the legs, so `ahead 2 → 6` named no repository
  and matched no forge count. `Told.legs` carries each leg's count and crosses `crown.json`
  (written only for more than one leg); a baseline without it, from an older build or with a
  leg cut since, says the sum with the count (`ahead 2 → 6 over 2 repos`). One leg reads as before.
- GitLab names the job a pipeline stopped on (20): a waiting or failed pipeline is followed by
  one read of `projects/:id/pipelines/:pid/jobs`, the first `manual` (or `failed`, a job allowed
  to fail last) job's name through `forge::job_word`. The wake says `waiting on
  deploy:production !1`, not `waiting on a manual job !1`, and the failing job is named, which
  T-739 left undone. The read happens only on a waiting or failed answer, on the same cadence as
  the pipeline read; a failed read leaves the word bare.

**Tests.** Units `a_multi_leg_delta_names_each_leg_that_moved` (crownwake) and
`a_gitlab_pipeline_names_the_job_it_stopped_on` (core forge). `forge_e2e::a_folder_workspaces_leg_…`
now waits for `deploy:production` on the PR and in the crown's wake, and reads `merged_in`,
`merge: nobody` and each repo's `merged_in` through the crown's `get_ticket`; `workspace_e2e`
reads the legs as `root, api, web`. Rig F1 passed on Sonnet. The multi-leg wake has no rig
test, because the rig cuts no workspace root.

## Entry needs a passed pipeline ignores a ticket with no PR (T-750, 2026-10-13, follow-up to T-739)

**Why.** On the forge lab the crown's ticket, which has no PR and never will, ended its turn and
its `on_done` into REVIEW (`requires_pipeline`) was refused, `pipeline not read — before REVIEW`;
a person's move too, since every mover obeys the gate. T-739's `pipeline_refusal` read a ticket
with no PR set as `Pipeline::Unknown`, and unknown is never green. Its twin `requires_merge`
ignores a ticket with no branch; this one now ignores a ticket with no PR the same way.

**Why "unknown never green" stopped short of "no PR".** At a worker's turn end its PR is seconds
old and the forge is read once a minute, so "not bound yet" and "none at all" look alike at that
instant: waving every unbound ticket through would have waved the lab's A1 into REVIEW with its
pipeline running. The daemon knows a PR was opened before the forge does: `gh pr create` /
`glab mr create` print the URL in a tool result, and T-739's transcript road keeps it.

**What.** `core::forge::entry_refusal(set, opened_here)`: a bound PR (a non-empty `forge.sets`
entry) is judged by its pipeline as before; unbound with a URL opened here, or with a transcript
that could not be read, is `pipeline not read`; unbound and nothing opened passes.
`Ledger::opened_any` answers `opened_here` from the ledger's `pr_urls` and, for the race, the
tail of each of the ticket's transcripts past the pass's cursor (plus a live session's transcript
the ledger has not learned, and the subagent files beside them), read on the writer thread inside
the gate and moving no cursor: the pass folds the same lines in later. The tail is what the
30 s pass has not reached, a local file, milliseconds; past `READ_CAP` or unreadable it is
`None`, never "none opened"; a file that is gone has nothing new. The worker picked the
writer-thread read over deferring the automove to the pass's landing: `place_ticket` serves every
mover, so the hand move and `agent_allowed_columns` see the same answer with no second road.
`agent_allowed_columns` asks only when some column has the setting.

**Accepted edge.** A PR a person opens by hand on the forge has no line in any transcript: until
the next read binds it, the ticket passes; the arrival rule and the next read catch up. A `pr
create` whose result never came (an interrupted turn) is not "opened": only a printed URL is.
After a restart `forge.sets` is empty until the first read, and the ledger's persisted URLs keep
a ticket that opened its PR here held.

**Tests.** `entry_needs_a_passed_pipeline_only_where_a_pr_is_or_was_opened` (core: bound failed,
passed, running, unknown, an open PR unread; unbound with a URL, unreadable, nothing),
`a_pr_opened_in_the_unread_tail_is_seen_before_the_pass` (cost: an unlearned live transcript, a
pending create, the result in the unread tail, no cursor moved, a gone file), and `forge_e2e`'s
`a_ticket_with_no_pull_request_enters_and_one_opened_here_waits` (a checkout ticket's turn end
lands in a `requires_pipeline` REVIEW while a worktree ticket whose transcript printed a `gh pr
create` URL is held in the gate's words, hand move too, until its PR reads passed).

## A board's pull requests survive a restart (T-752, 2026-10-13, follow-up to T-739)

**Why.** On the forge lab a `U` reload took MR !1 off ticket A1's card for about 70 s. Two causes:
the sets lived in memory only, and the first pass after a start only probed (which CLI, signed
in, glab's viewer) — `queue_forge_sample` built a `RepoQuery` only for a host that already had a
`HostProbe`, so the list came one `forge::EVERY` later. Measured: daemon up 18:41:54.856, first
pass 18:41:55.284 with no `prs`, second pass 18:43:06 with `!1 merged`. The author's ask: PRs
show immediately after a restart.

**The sets persist.** `forge.json` in the state dir (`FORGE_SCHEMA` 1, `persist_forge`, barred
and quarantined on `store::load_versioned` like the other state files; the tenth): each ticket's
set in the wire's words (`PrRecord`: a word this build does not know drops that PR, not the
file) and the settled merge commits (`CommitRecord`: the terminal pipeline and the environments
reached, the old `commit_pipelines`/`deployed` maps). No time is written, so a quiet board writes
nothing; it is written after each pass through `write_if_changed`. `restore_forge` at start keeps
the sets of tickets the board still has. **A restart is not news**: the first live pass diffs
against the loaded sets, so `forge::delta`, the arrivals and the crown's forge edges (T-744) say
only what moved while the daemon was down — a PR merged in the gap is one `merged #42` line and
one arrival, every other PR silent.

**One pass probes and lists.** The repositories of a host probed on this pass ride the query as
`pending` and `forge::list_probed` turns them into `RepoQuery`s on the worker from the probe's
answer, so a board with no `forge.json` (or a quarantined one) has its PRs within the first
pass's own seconds. A host whose probe found no CLI lists nothing, as before. And a pass that finds every binding still provisioning (no
branch yet) no longer stamps the minute: it returns and the next bucket asks again, or a ticket
whose worktree was being cut at that moment waited a whole cadence (the new e2e caught it under
the full suite's load).

**A failed call keeps the last read.** `forge::carry`: a repository whose list call failed on a
pass keeps the previous read's PRs in each ticket's set; one that answered says what it says now.
Without it a timeout on the first pass after a load would blank exactly the sets the file brought
back (and, before this, any timeout blanked a live card for a pass).

**What the gates read before a live answer.** `ticket_merged` (DONE, delete, archive) and the
card's `forge_fold_legs` read a loaded set as a live one: a PR merged at the leg's tip is a fact
that cannot turn back, the tip is re-read, and the card and the gates must answer alike. The
pipeline gate (`requires_pipeline`, `pipeline_refusal`) reads **live reads only** — a set read
since this start (`State.at_ms`, which is not restored) — because a pipeline, unlike a merge, can
turn back, and a file may be a day old: before the first live pass it refuses `pipeline not
read`, which is what it said after a restart before. Beside T-750's no-PR rule: a loaded set
holding PRs refuses `pipeline not read`; a loaded empty one reads as no read, so the transcripts
decide as they did after a restart before. The train's `forge_fresh` is unchanged for
the same reason (at_ms empty: nothing fresh until a live read). An open PR from the file still
refuses `m` until the pass, the conservative side.

**Tests.** `forge_e2e::the_prs_survive_a_restart_and_the_first_pass_lists` (the cadence is a
minute, so the PR binding at all is the same-pass list; across a restart the stub `gh` holds
every call 3 s, and the first snapshot carries the PR with `sampled_at_ms` 0, a
`requires_pipeline` column refuses `pipeline not read`, and the PR merged in the gap is the one
feed line); each fix disabled in turn fails it. Units in `daemon::forge`: the same-pass list from
a fresh query, the carry, the file's round trip (no time in it, a gone ticket dropped, a load and
a save the same bytes, a newer schema refused, `{` quarantined) and a schema-1 fixture with an
unknown state word.

## A running pipeline sweeps, a waiting one is a target (T-747, 2026-10-13, follow-up to T-739)

**Why.** T-739's `glyphs::pr_mark` folded four states into two rings: `◯` for open with no
pipeline and open with one running, `◉` for passed and for waiting on a manual job. On the forge
lab a worker opened MR !1 with its pipeline running and the card read `◯!1`, nothing in
progress; a manual job a person must press read as green.

**What.** Running is a clock hand, `◴ ◷ ◶ ◵` (U+25F4–25F7, East Asian Neutral) clockwise, grey;
waiting is `◎` (U+25CE, Ambiguous, the class `◯` already ships), calm like passed. Ascii:
`' > v <` and `@`. The brief asked for `^ > v <`, but `^` is already merged + deployed on that
tier, so the up frame is the tick at the top of the cell. `pr_mark` takes the redraw clock's
frame (`App::spin_frame`), on the card's brief and the ticket page's rows alike.

**Refused: the agent's spinner, or the slow register.** A second thing moving at the spinner's
100 ms would be two things moving at one speed, and D19's motion ban bends once, for the working
agent. The slow register (400 ms) says a session is in flight. The sweep is its own, slowest
cadence, `PIPE_STEP_TICKS = 10` (one second a frame): something is happening elsewhere, and no
more. No redraw predicate was needed: the loop draws every 100 ms whatever is on screen
(`lib.rs`, T-496 writes only a changed frame), so the hand moves with no new clock.

**Tests.** `pr_marks_are_distinct_one_cell_and_the_sweep_is_the_slowest` (seven marks plus every
sweep frame pairwise distinct per tier, one cell, outside 0x2500–0x259F; clockwise; a frame holds
a whole step; the step outruns the slow register); goldens `board_prs_120` (gains a waiting MR)
and `ticket_prs_120`, at the sweep's first frame.

## A merged PR's pipeline moves the mark too (T-758, 2026-10-13, follow-up to T-747)

**Why.** On the forge lab MR !2's merge commit ran a deploy pipeline for a minute while the card
held a still `●!2`: `pr_mark` gave every merged PR `●` whatever its pipeline did.

**What.** In `glyphs::pr_mark` the `running` and `waiting` arms now sit before the plain merged
`●`, so a merged PR sweeps or shows `◎` until the pipeline settles. Order of precedence: failed,
deployed `◆` (a later pipeline on a deployed commit keeps `◆`), running, waiting, merged `●`.
Same frames, cadence and ascii as T-747; the redraw loop already ticks every 100 ms, so no
predicate was added. Test: the T-747 mark test grew the merged rows. No golden changed (none
shows a merged PR with a moving pipeline).

## An unsettled pipeline beats `◆`, and one in flight is read every 15 s (T-781, 2026-10-14, follow-up to T-758)

**Why.** Forge lab run 2: MR !5 merged, deployed to staging, its main pipeline waiting on the
manual `deploy:production`. The card held `◆` (T-758 kept a deployed PR's `◆` over a later
pipeline, calling one "unusual"; with deploy columns it is the normal case), so nothing said there
was a job to press. And the forge was read once a minute: the production job ran for seconds, the
reads went waiting → passed, and no sweep could have shown.

**Mark.** `glyphs::pr_mark` now reads failed, waiting, running, then merged-and-deployed `◆`,
then merged `●`: on a merged PR the unsettled pipeline wins whether or not it deployed, and `◆`
means the pipeline passed (or there is none) and something deployed. The card, the ticket page's
rows and `^h`'s dialog all call it. No golden changed (none draws a deployed PR with a moving
pipeline); the T-747 mark test's merged rows say the new order.

**Cadence.** `forge::State::busy` is the tickets holding an open or merged PR whose pipeline is
`running` or `waiting` (a merged PR's is its merge commit's, T-771). `Daemon::queue_forge_busy`,
asked every fourth tick, reads those tickets alone (`forge_query(Some(busy))`) when each of their
repositories was last asked `forge::busy_every()` ago (15 s, `BUSY_EVERY`;
`MESIMON_FORGE_BUSY_MS` the seam) — so only the repositories holding such a PR, and the minute
pass for the rest. It rides the turn's end's road (T-761: `burst_inflight`, `Msg::ForgeBurst`,
the minute not reset), never while a pass or a burst is out. `State::due_for` took a floor
argument (`BURST_MS` for a turn's end, `busy_every()` here), so a repository whose last call
failed keeps the minute's backoff on both. A waiting manual job nobody presses is read every 15 s
for as long as it waits (a day at most, T-771's superseded read): one list call and one
check-runs call per repository each time, far inside the forge's hourly limits.

**Tests.** Units: `pr_marks_are_distinct_one_cell_and_the_sweep_is_the_slowest` (merged +
deployed + running sweeps, + waiting `◎`, passed or none `◆`);
`a_pipeline_in_flight_reads_its_repository_every_fifteen_seconds` (`busy` takes open and merged,
not passed or closed; 14 s held, 15 s due; an error waits). E2e
`forge_e2e::a_running_pipeline_is_read_on_the_busy_cadence_and_a_settled_one_on_the_minute`: with
the minute at 6 s and busy at 500 ms, a merged PR whose commit runs is listed at least twice in
4 s and at most once after it passes; it fails (0 lists) with busy set to ten minutes.

## The crown hears the forge's edges (T-744, 2026-10-13, follow-up to T-739)

**Why.** T-739's crown heard two forge facts: a failed pipeline and a merge. With a PR open the
train never takes the ticket, so after the worker's `finished` wake the crown learned nothing more
until something else woke it (T-739's lab, scenario E3). The decisions a person wants voiced sit
on the other edges.

**What.** `daemon::forge::Edge` grows `failed`, `waiting` (the job's word), `conflict` and
`review` (per open PR, by label) beside the arrival edges, read between two forge reads like
them: a first read is a baseline, a PR newly bound brings its conflict and its review in as part
of its opening, and a review edge is only `approved` or `changes_requested` (a dismissal to
`required` is not a verdict). `Edge::news` says each in the crown's words, naming its PR:
`pipeline passed !1`, `pipeline failed #42: test-linux`, `waiting on deploy:production !1`
(`waiting on a manual job !1` where GitLab names none), `deployed to staging !1`, `conflict !1`,
`conflict cleared !1`, `review approved !1`, `changes requested !1`. Never an opening (the
worker's turn end carries it) and never the merge (the flags' merged wake). `on_forge_sampled`
joins a ticket's edges into one line per pass and calls `hear_forge` after `forge_arrivals`, so
the wake's `column` is where the arrival rule put the ticket.

**One cause, not two.** `WakeCause::Pipeline` became `WakeCause::Forge`, clause `has news from the
forge`, feed word `forge`, at the old rank (above Finished, under Merged): every edge is a decision
someone may take, and the brackets carry which. Keeping `Pipeline` for a failure beside `Forge`
would have split one table row in two for no difference in what the crown does. `Told.pipeline`
became `Told.forge`; `crown.json` reads T-739's `pipeline` spellings of both back
(`#[serde(alias)]`). **The words are edges, not a state**: `changes()` says them whenever a wake
carries them (T-739 compared them with the last told, which would have swallowed a second
`review approved` after a dismissal), and `CrownWake::fold` keeps an earlier fold's words, so a
pass and a review between two crown turns are both in the line, and a delivery folded over a
forge wake keeps the forge's words in its delta. A restart cannot say an edge twice: the sets are
memory, and the first read after it is a baseline.

**Not a cap.** The brief's "at most five over a PR's life" is the count of edge kinds, not a
fuse: a pipeline that fails, is fixed and passes again is two wakes the crown needs, and a
conflict that comes and goes is said each time. Each is one wake per pass per ticket.

**No policy.** The crown's brief (`mcp::CROWN_WAKES`) names the edges and says nothing about what
to do with them: a crown whose own brief says merge does it on the forge (`merge_ticket` refuses
an open PR in words naming the forge); one with no such instruction raises its hand as for any
step a person must take. USING.md "Pull requests" has the sentence.

**Tests.** Units: `the_crown_hears_each_forge_edge_by_its_pr` (each edge's words, a wait read
twice, a dismissal, a comment, a freshly bound PR, two edges on one pass),
`a_forge_wake_says_every_edge_and_round_trips` (rank, clause, the fold, T-739's `crown.json`).
`forge_e2e::the_crown_hears_the_forges_edges`: a crown and a worker it started; the stub PR
opens running (no wake), passes, waits on `deploy:production`, then turns conflicting and
approved on one pass, each one `forge` wake with the edge's words, and a quiet pass after says
nothing. The rig: F1 reads `woke:forge`; F2 (pipeline passes, nothing said about merging; the
`crown_hand:#42` check reads the crown's own `raise_hand`) and F3 (the brief says merge; the
worker commits; `crown:merge_ticket`) are new, with a `forge_pass` step.
On the real Sonnet (claude 2.1.296), 2026-10-13: F2 PASS in 82 s — woken `forge` on the passed
pipeline, the crown merged nothing and raised its hand: "T-2's pull request #42 … pipeline passed;
review is still required and the open P[R]…"; F3 PASS in 76 s — woken `delivered`, then `forge`,
the crown called `merge_ticket`, refused on the open PR; F1 PASS in 68 s on its second run. Its
first failed `replies:done,noted` on the rig, not the board: `forge_fail` returned at the crown's
`ask_agent` and `forge_off` restarted the daemon under the worker's `noted` turn; the step now
waits for that turn's `Stop`.

**Seen on the way, not fixed here.** In the rig a stub PR whose head is the base commit (a worker
that committed nothing) binds every worktree ticket cut from that base, since each one's reflog
holds it (`forge::binds`' `made here`): F2's pass also woke the crown for F1's ticket. GitHub
refuses a PR with no diff; GitLab opens an empty MR.

## A later PR's merge wakes the crown (T-757, 2026-10-13, follow-up to T-744)

**Why.** T-744 kept the merge out of the forge's edges: "the flags' merged wake says it". That is
half right. The flags wake the crown when they flip unmerged → merged, which happens once per
branch tip. On T-739's lab (scenario B3) a ticket whose MR !1 had merged opened !2 from
`fix/greeting`; the crown merged it on gitlab.com, the feed wrote `merged !2`, and the crown sat
70 s waiting for a wake that could not come, since the worktree already read merged.

**What.** `forge::Edge` grows `landed`: the PRs, by label, read merged that were read open
before (a first read stays a baseline). `Edge::news` says each first: `merged !2`.
`on_forge_sampled` keeps a label only where the flags will say nothing: the PR's head is not a
worktree leg's tip, and no flags wake is waiting for the tick (`crown_landed`). A PR whose head is
a leg's tip is the one `forge_fold_legs` folds into the flags (and the one the git road reads
merged by ancestry), so a first PR's merge is still said once, as `merged` with its merge step.
`merged_at` and `ticket_merged` are untouched: this is a wake, not a merge reading.

**Not the ticket's rule.** The brief said to keep the edge only where `wt_agg.merged` was
already true before the pass (or no worktree). That misses a merge the flags never flip on: once
a newer PR stands in front of a merged one, `merged_at` reads the newest PR, so a worktree whose
merge was the forge's fold alone (no fetch of the base) reads unmerged again, and the later PR's
merge, at a head that is not the tip, flips nothing. The head-is-a-tip rule says exactly what the
fold will say. What it can still double: a later PR that also carries the worktree's commits,
merged and then fetched, is said by the forge (`merged !2`) and by the flags (`merged`) in two
wakes. Both are true, and a lost merge is the worse failure.

**Tests.** Unit `a_pr_that_merges_lands_by_its_label`. `forge_e2e::the_crown_hears_the_forges_edges`
goes on: #42 merges at the tip and the base takes it, one `merged` wake and no `forge` wake; a
commit made in the worktree and stepped back from (so #43 binds by the reflog) opens as #43, no
wake, then merges: one `forge` wake with `merged #43`, and `merged #42` is never said. The rig: F4
(`forge_merge`, `forge_later` steps; `woke:merged`, `woke:forge`, `crown:ask_agent`), where the
base never takes the merge, so the flags bounce back to unmerged when #43 opens: the brief's rule
would have woken nothing there. The crown's brief (`mcp::CROWN_WAKES`) and USING.md name the
new edge. On the real Sonnet (claude 2.1.296), 2026-10-13: F4 PASS twice (the second on the final
brief, 107 s), wakes `delivered`, `merged`, `forge`, `answered`; the crown asked the worker once
and the worker said `noted`.

## The forge's edges: a freshly bound PR's state, the rebase turn's read, no phantom clear, merged before deployed (T-769, 2026-10-14, follow-up to T-744 and T-757)

**Why.** The forge lab's findings 3 to 6 (2026-10-13), all on the edge road (`forge::edge`,
`absorb_forge`, `hear_forge`).

**4. A newly bound PR says its settled state.** T-744 kept a fresh PR's conflict and review out
as "part of its opening", so a PR opened and judged between two reads said nothing (C1's !3
first read in conflict). `forge::edge` now takes `held`, every PR the ticket's reads held
before this one (`State::held`, T-767), and a PR outside it is newly bound: `opened` is that
(the caller's `&= opens` folded in), `Edge.bound` carries its pipeline where passed, failed or
waiting, and its conflict and verdict join `conflict` and `review`. `Edge::news` says the
pipeline only where the set's own edge did not already name it (another open PR passed or
failed before). A PR held before and missed by a read is no fresh PR and says nothing. B3's
`pipeline passed !2` beside a merged !1 was T-767's fix already: the merged commit's pipeline no
longer read as the set's pass.

**6. A clear follows a conflict said.** `forge::State::conflicted` keeps, per ticket, the PRs
whose `conflict` edge was said and not cleared; `State::say_conflicts` drops a second
`conflict` and any `conflict cleared` with no conflict before it. The first live read against a
set `forge.json` brought back (`at_ms` empty for the ticket) is a baseline for both directions,
for the PRs that set held; a PR bound since says its conflict. Memory only, as the brief asked.
D1's phantom was T-770's "fix read back" of a conflict the first read held and never said.

**3. Merged before deployed.** C2's `deployed to staging #1` came 40 s before `merged`:
`hear_forge` delivered its line at once, and the flags' merged wake (the same pass's
`forge_fold_legs`, heard on the tick) waited for the crown's turn on it. Now a tip PR's merge
read on the pass that reads its deployment, which the flags have not said (`wt_agg` not merged,
or a flip waiting for the tick), keeps `merged !N` in the forge's line, first, as `news` orders
every line (merged, the pipelines, deployed). `hear_forge` runs after the fold loop, so its
`Told` reads `merged`; for a worker in `crown_landed` it owes the wake as `Merged`, moves
`judged` and `told` as `hear_merges` does, and the tick's `merge_verdict` finds the merge told
and says nothing. A tip merge alone is still the flags' wake (T-757's e2e).

**5. The rebase turn is read at its end.** Checked, nothing to fix: the lab ran before T-761.
`look_after_turn` asks the ticket's own look on every `EndTurn` the train could take, the
train's rebase turn included, and a look whose `pushed` moved (the rebase's force-push) owes
the burst read. `forge_e2e::a_train_rebase_turn_is_read_at_its_end` pins it with the minute at
ten: the conflict clears seconds after the rebase turn's `Stop`, on one `pr list`. A GitLab
recompute still reading `conflict` right after the push (T-770's note) waits for the next read.

**Tests.** Units `a_freshly_bound_pr_says_its_settled_state`,
`a_conflict_cleared_follows_a_conflict_said`, `a_pass_says_merged_before_its_pipeline_and_its_deployment`;
`the_crown_hears_each_forge_edge_by_its_pr` now hears a PR bound conflicted and approved.
`forge_e2e`: `a_freshly_bound_prs_state_is_news_and_its_merge_comes_before_its_deployment` (a PR
bound passed: one `pipeline passed #42`; merged and on staging in one pass: one `merged` line
ending `merged #42, deployed to staging #42)`, no second merged wake),
`a_conflict_cleared_across_a_restart_says_nothing` (then a conflict after it and its clear are
said), `a_train_rebase_turn_is_read_at_its_end`. The first two fail with their fix disabled.
`the_crown_hears_the_forges_edges`' later PR opens with no verdict, since one bound approved is
now news. The rig: F5 (`forge_empty`, `forge_bound_passed`), on the real Sonnet (claude 2.1.296),
2026-10-14: PASS in 50 s, woken `forge` on the PR first read passed, the crown merged nothing and
raised its hand naming #42.

## A conflict said before a restart says its clear, and a wake says the column it is sent from (T-785, 2026-10-15, follow-up to T-752 and T-769)

**Why.** Forge lab run 3. D1: `conflict !12` was said, the daemon restarted, the MR read
conflicting on the first read after it and clear on a later one, and no `conflict cleared !12`
came. T-769 kept `forge::State::conflicted` (the conflicts said) in memory and made the first live
read against `forge.json`'s set a baseline both ways, so after a restart the clear had no conflict
to follow. A: the crown moved T-13 to DONE; a wake owed earlier and held for the crown's turn went
out three minutes later saying `column PROD`, while `get_ticket` read DONE.

**The conflicts said persist.** `ForgeFile.conflicts` (per ticket, the PRs by repository and
number, only PRs the ticket's set still holds) is written beside the sets and read back by
`State::restore` for the tickets it restores. `say_conflicts` lost its `baseline` argument and
`forge::Conflict` its `fresh` field: what was said is known across a restart, so the first read
after one is judged like any other. A conflict said and cleared after the restart says the clear
once, whether it cleared on a later read or while the daemon was down; a conflict never said
(D1's T-769 phantom) stays silent across it; a conflict that came while the daemon was down is
news (T-769's baseline swallowed it). No schema bump: an older build reads the file and drops the
field, which only silences a clear, and a file from before this build has no conflicts said, so
its first clear is silent, as before. **The other edges the brief named needed nothing**: a
waiting job and a review verdict are read off the PR's own fields, which `forge.json`'s
`PrRecord` already keeps (`pipeline`, `job`, `review`), so T-752's first pass diffs them against
the loaded set.

**The column is read when the wake is sent.** `CrownWake::sent_at` gives the wake its card's
column as it stands; `crown_wake_events` (the crown's sentence, the card's line, the ticket
page's pending row) reads every wake through it, and `drain_crown_wakes`, once the words are
delivered, moves each worker's `Heard::told` column there (`told_columns`), so the next wake's
delta does not say the column again. The edges stay as heard. **`merge_state` is not re-read**,
though the brief named it: a merge or a rebase between the owe and the send arrives as its own
wake (the tick's `merge_verdict`, a turn's end) and folds into the held one with its words, its
`judged` and its held delivery; re-reading the word at the send would say a merge whose own road
has not run, and its wake would then find it told and say nothing. A column move is the one change
no wake carries.

**Tests.** Units `a_conflict_cleared_follows_a_conflict_said` (through `ForgeFile` and back:
said, a restart, still conflicting, cleared, said once; cleared while down; never said; came while
down), `the_forge_file_round_trips_and_a_newer_one_is_refused` (the conflicts, a PR gone from the
set and a gone ticket not written), `crownwake::a_wake_says_the_column_it_is_sent_from`.
`forge_e2e::a_conflict_said_before_a_restart_says_its_clear_after_it` replaces T-769's
`a_conflict_cleared_across_a_restart_says_nothing`: a restart with the conflict standing, no wake
on the first read, then the clear, held behind the crown's turn while the card moves to TODO,
says `column TODO, conflict cleared #42`; the next conflict's line says no column; cleared while
down, the first read says `conflict cleared #42, after a restart`. With `restore` dropping the
conflicts it times out on the clear; without `told_columns` the next line says `column TODO`
again. The rig: F8 (`forge_conflict`, `forge_restart`, `forge_clear`), on the real Sonnet
(claude 2.1.300), 2026-10-15: PASS in 72 s, wakes `finished`, `forge`, `forge`, the crown's last
words `F8 cleared #42`. All of `forge_e2e` passes, and the whole workspace under nextest (2417).

## A board's own theme is named where it hides a pick (T-746, 2026-10-13)

The author, on the personal-life board: "it says green saved for dark and light terminals but not
actually taking effect", and "nothing said machine scope, i couldn't even set it to board using
b". The board's `prefs.json` held `amber` for both grounds (set 2026-09-30, while T-625 opened
Appearance in board scope); T-717's dialog opens on the machine's, so the pick saved to the
machine file and the board's own pick kept winning. Three faults, three fixes:

- **`b` was offered and unbound on the Theme page.** `Ctx::pref_scope_offered` held there, but
  `THEME` had no binding. It has `b` now, as `SECTIONS` does, and the `PrefScope` arm moves the
  picker's cursor onto the slot's pick in the new scope (the inherit row comes and goes).
- **Nothing named the machine's scope.** The title said `THIS BOARD` in board scope and nothing
  otherwise; where `b` is on offer it now says `MACHINE`.
- **The page and the status said nothing of the board's pick.** `App::board_keeps(slot)` names
  what the board's own picks keep of a slot; in machine scope the Theme page draws it under the
  slots (`this board keeps amber ∙ b sets this board's`) and a pick's status carries it after
  `saved for …`. The page's `●` and its opening cursor read the machine's pick wherever the board
  holds one (`kept_row`, `theme_cursor`), not the resolved theme, which is the board's.

A machine pick does not drop the board's: other boards' themes are deliberate (one colour per
board), and the board's pick is now one key away, named on the page.

**Tests.** TUI `a_board_that_keeps_its_theme_says_so_and_b_reaches_it` (the status, the cursor,
`b` both ways, the board's pick landing), `theme_picker_says_what_the_board_keeps` (the title
and the line, gone in board scope); goldens `settings_*` (the `MACHINE` word),
`theme_picker_120`, `theme_picker_board_120` (the `b` hint).

**The Theme section opens on this board's** (same day, the author: "default should be this
board for themes"). A board's look is the board's, so Theme has a scope of its own,
`App::theme_machine` (false: this board's), beside the dialog's `settings_board_scope`, and
both reset when the dialog opens or closes. `b` speaks to Theme's while the page is open or the
list's cursor is on Theme (`App::on_theme`), and to the dialog's everywhere else;
`App::scope_is_board` is what the title and `Ctx::pref_scope_board` say, so the title reads
`THIS BOARD` on Theme and `MACHINE` on Appearance in one dialog, each true of the page it heads.
T-717's "one switch for the dialog cannot flip as the cursor passes a section" still holds for
that one switch; this is a second switch, whose scope Theme alone reads. A pick lands in the
board's `prefs.json`; `inherit` returns the slot to the machine's. Tests: TUI
`the_theme_section_opens_on_this_board`; the machine-scope picker tests open through
`open_machine_theme_picker`, which presses `b`; goldens `settings_120x30`, `settings_60x20`.

## Settings reads what runs on this board, in either scope (T-751, 2026-10-13)

Seen on the forge-lab board: its default tier was `quick` (board scope, `doctor` agreed), and
Settings › Agents › Default tier read `coder`, the machine's, with the board's pick only in the
row's detail. Settings opens in machine scope (T-717), and `fill_tier_ctx` showed the machine
layer there.

- **The value column is the resolved one in every scope.** `Ctx::tier_default` is
  `Book::default_tier()` whatever the scope; the scope decides what Enter edits, not what the
  row reads. The overridable prefs already read `App::prefs` (the resolved view) in `App::ctx`;
  nothing there read `machine_prefs` but `board_overrides`' words.
- **The detail carries the other layer.** In machine scope a row this board sets reads
  `set on this board ∙ machine: <word>` before its own detail (`keymap::item_detail` for a pref,
  the Default tier row's own `detail`, which keeps board scope's `set here ∙ machine: …` and
  `inherited from the machine`). `Ctx::tier_board_uses` went with the old `this board uses … (b)`
  line. A key the machine alone keeps is untouched.
- **Enter in machine scope steps the machine's value** (`App::machine_scope_takes`). Every pref
  arm takes its next step from `self.prefs`; on a row the board overrides that was the board's
  value, so the machine's write could land where it already was and nothing moved. For the one
  dispatch the arm reads the machine's copy, the resolve follows, and the status adds `this board
  keeps <word>`; `cycle_default_tier` says the same for the tier.

**Tests.** Core `default_tier_detail_names_the_other_layer`, `scope_words_say_inherited_set_or_machine`
(the machine-scope half); TUI `default_tier_row_reads_the_boards_pick_in_machine_scope`,
`a_board_override_is_the_rows_value_in_machine_scope`; golden `settings_codex_60x20`.

## The peek keeps the agent's last words through a long tool run (T-755, 2026-10-13)

Seen on T-754's card: the pane's newest line was a progress note, and the card showed the
turn's prompt. Replayed record by record over that transcript, the reader was right about the
note at every step it could see it. After the note at 19:32:47Z came 6 m 42 s of private thinking
and tool output, more than 256 KiB of it. The note fell out of the last window
(`TAIL_BYTES_MAX`), and the walk took the `last-prompt` latch, the prompt, as the agent's words
until the next note landed. Narration was never the problem (T-604 reads it).

- **A cached read resumes where the last one stood** (`agents::read_preview_after`,
  `history::preview_after`). It reads only the bytes appended since. If they hold no reply and no
  prompt, the prior words carry forward and only the activity is renewed: nothing between the
  words and the prior end said anything, so no amount of tool traffic pushes them out. The
  `PreviewRead` mark is the offset past the last whole line, so a record half-written at one read
  is read whole at the next, plus a hash of the 256 bytes before it. A file that shrank or was
  rewritten reads afresh. Both caches resume: the TUI's `PeekCache` (card, ticket page, spoke
  scan, notifier) and the phone's `control_words`. Codex keeps the default, a fresh read.
- **A fresh read adds a 4 MiB rung** (`TAIL_BYTES_DEEP`) after 64 KiB and 256 KiB. Since every
  later read is incremental, a board opened mid-gap pays it once per transcript, not once a
  second. The census's drawer preview keeps its own two rungs.

**Tests.** Daemon `the_last_words_outlive_any_amount_of_tool_traffic` (600 KiB of tool traffic
carried, a half-written record, a fresh read 400 KiB deep, a shorter and a longer rewrite); TUI
`test_preview_pages_a_long_reply` holds the longer rewrite on the card.

## A GitLab squash reads the wrong merge commit, and a folder workspace's legs never sample (T-754, 2026-10-13, follow-up to T-739)

Seen on T-739's forge lab (`~/Documents/code/forge-lab`: a folder root with legs `api`, `web` on
gitlab.com and `gh` on github.com). The crown merged MR !1 of the api leg (a squash, under the
project's default merge method) and waited for its `merged` wake, which never came. Two faults,
one under the other.

**GitLab's merge method decides which sha landed.** Under the default "merge commit" method a
squash still lands as a merge commit whose second parent is the squash commit: the MR carries
both `merge_commit_sha` (25559fa on the lab, with the main pipeline and the staging deployment)
and `squash_commit_sha` (65f00df, no pipeline, no deployment), and what is on main is the merge
commit. `parse_glab` took the squash sha first, so the merged MR read `pipeline: none` with no
environments, and a column that arrives on a passed pipeline or a deployment never took the
ticket. Now `merge_commit_sha` first, `squash_commit_sha` second: a fast-forward or semi-linear
squash has a null merge commit, and the squash sha is then what landed. GitHub's
`mergeCommit.oid` is one field and was never the wrong way round.

**A folder root has no default branch, and every flags road gated on it.** `Daemon::base_branch`
is the root checkout's default branch, what a single-repo binding is judged against. A workspace
leg carries its own base (T-368), and a workspace whose root is a plain folder — the lab's
shape: `is_meta == false` at provisioning, no root leg — has no branch at the root for
`default_branch` to name. `refresh_worktree_flags` returned on `base_branch.is_none()`, the
tick's worker sent an empty sample that `on_worktree_flags` dropped, the train's look
(`queue_ticket_flags`), `train_could_take`, `train_takes`, `train_pass` and the crown's turn
probe (`Look::run`) all returned on the same test, and `merge_ticket` refused `no default branch
found`. So no leg of such a board was ever sampled: `wt_repos` stayed empty, the snapshot's
per-repo rows fell back to `ahead 0 ∙ merged false ∙ needs_rebase false` (nothing on the wire
told that from a clean leg), `forge_fold_legs` had no leg to fold, and the git road's patch-id
never ran. The e2e failed first exactly there: a folder root with two nested repositories, a leg
three commits ahead, the snapshot reading `ahead 0` until the wait ran out.

- `needs_root_base` says whether anything on the board is judged against the root's branch (a
  single-repo binding with a branch); `base_known_for(ticket)` is the per-ticket form (the root's
  branch, or a workspace binding's own legs). The flags pass, the train pass and the two train
  gates ask those instead of `base_branch` alone; the three worker roads fill a single-repo
  query's base where the root's is known and drop the ones left with none, so a workspace leg
  samples whichever way the root reads. `merge_ticket` takes the root's branch for a single-repo
  binding and the legs' own on a workspace (`base_word` names one for the already-merged
  sentence).
- `root_base` resolves the root's branch once and never asks git of a folder root (`.git`
  absent).
- The journal says when a pass is skipped for want of the root's branch on a board that needs
  it (`worktree flags: no default branch at <root>; single-repo bindings unsampled`).

**A leg that failed to sample is never a clean leg.** `Flags`/`RepoFlags` carry `trouble`: git's
first line when `for-each-ref` or the `rev-list` count failed (`git rev-list: not a git
repository …`; a branch git cannot count carries it too), and `not sampled` for a leg no query
reached (a workspace leg recorded with no base). `worktree_item` puts the first leg's trouble in
the row's `detail`, which the ticket page already draws beside the branch (`api ∙ git rev-list:
…`), after an init script's own detail; a change of trouble is news the sample broadcasts.
`git()`'s refusal names its verb rather than a leading `--no-optional-locks`.

**Tests.** Core `glab_json_reads_into_a_pr_and_its_pipeline_comes_by_sha` (the order, and a null
merge commit); daemon `a_folder_workspaces_legs_sample_on_their_own_bases` (two repositories
under a folder, api three ahead with its tip, web untouched, a non-repo folder's trouble),
`compute_flags_agrees_with_the_single_question_helpers` (a lost branch's trouble); e2e
`forge_e2e::a_folder_workspaces_leg_reads_ahead_and_a_gitlab_squash_lands_as_its_merge_commit`
(a `glab` stub, a folder root, legs `api`/`web` and no root leg, ahead 3, the MR merged at the
tip folding to `main (MR !1)` with the merge commit as `merged_oid` and its pipeline `passed`
while the squash commit's has none, the crown's merged wake). The lab itself is left as it was;
its daemon runs main's build until the merge.

## `^h` lists a ticket's pull requests (T-759, 2026-10-13, follow-up to T-739)

**Why.** The author, on the forge lab: "use ^h to show a dialog showing all PRs/MRs of this
ticket, including pipelines and deployments". The ticket page stops at three PR rows and folds
the rest into `+N more`; the card's brief is glyphs and numbers.

**What.** `^h` (`Verb::PullRequests`) on the board's cursor card and on the ticket page opens
`Scope::PullRequests` (`Mode::PullRequests { ticket, idx }`, `ui/prs.rs`): every PR the forge
bound, newest first, one row each — `glyphs::pr_mark` in its register (`ListRow::lead_ink`,
new, so a list's lead can carry a mark), the forge's number and the repository in columns as
wide as their widest row, then the page's words whole (`ticket::pr_clauses`, now shared by the
page and the dialog, so neither can say a PR differently). The title counts the rows and says
when the forge was last read (`ForgeStatus::sampled_at_ms`, the Usage dialog's `read 3m ago`).
The rows are read off the snapshot each frame, the summary dialog's way, so a pipeline turning
over shows in place. Enter opens the row's URL with the board's opener and leaves the dialog up
(a ticket's PRs are read one after another, unlike `^k`'s one link); `c` copies the URL; `q`,
Esc and `^h` close. The mouse: each row is a list row (T-716), and the card's brief and the
page's PR rows are `mouse::Target::Prs`, whose click is that ticket's `^h` (the cursor walks to
the card first). `board.rs::brief_at` finds the brief by matching `card::brief_spans` on the
card's second line, so the click goes only where the brief is drawn.

**The key.** `^h` is gated on `Ctx::has_prs`, so with none it is inert and unhinted, and the
dialog is never opened empty; one whose PRs go while it is open says `no pull requests ∙ the
forge binds one…`. In a text field `^h` stays delete-word beside `^w`: the keymap's
one-verb-per-key rule is per scope chain and the barriers do not reach the board. crossterm
reads 0x08 as `Ctrl('h')` and 0x7F as Backspace, so a terminal that sends 0x08 for Backspace
opens the dialog on Backspace on the board; USING.md says so, and it is not a second key.

**Tests.** `keymap::ctrl_h_opens_the_pull_requests` (both screens, gated, the dialog's keys,
Input keeps its own `^h`); `golden_ticket_prs_dialog_120` (all four PRs where the page folds
one, the cut row whole above the footer, Enter's URL, `^h` closes, the read time);
`ctrl_h_is_inert_without_prs_and_the_empty_dialog_says_why`;
`a_click_on_a_cards_prs_opens_the_dialog` (the card's brief and the page's rows).

## The hidden cursor rests in one cell (T-760, 2026-10-14)

**Report.** macOS's input-source indicator (the blue `A` / `א` bubble) stood on the board,
always at the same spot beside a working card's spinner, and went only after several layout
switches. The bubble is the system's, not ours: since Sonoma macOS draws it under the text
caret, and iTerm2 reports the caret to the text system whether DECTCEM has hidden it or not.

**Cause.** ratatui hides the cursor when a frame sets no position and never moves it, so it
rested wherever the last changed cell left it. On a board with a working session that is the
spinner, which changes every 100 ms tick: the caret moved on every tick, and the indicator,
which fades once the caret is still, stayed.

**What.** `Quiet::park`: at the end of every frame with the cursor hidden, it goes to the
bottom-right cell, the same cell every time, inside the frame's synchronized update. The
indicator then shows only when the layout changes, as in any app, below the last row, and
fades. The T-496 rule holds: a frame that wrote nothing writes no park either (`at` already
names the corner). A frame with a text field shows its cursor where the field asks, as before.

**Tests.** `quiet::a_hidden_cursor_rests_in_the_corner_whatever_the_frame_wrote`;
`the_cursor_is_told_only_what_it_was_not_told_last` now expects the park after the hide. Not
measured against the real indicator in this ticket: the person's board is the check.

## A refused automove leaves a trace on the ticket page (T-749, 2026-10-14)

**Why.** On the forge lab a worker's turn ended in IN PROGRESS, the `on_done` move to REVIEW was
refused by `Entry needs a passed pipeline`, and the only sign was the feed's `movement_decision
refused: pipeline not read — before REVIEW`. The person asked why the ticket had not moved.

**What.** `place_ticket` keeps the last refusal of an **automation** per ticket
(`movegate::HeldMoves`, in memory like the move gate): the column rules' words (merge, pipeline,
summary boxes — `Daemon::column_gate`, factored out of `place_ticket` so the refusal and the
re-check are one function) and the move gate's (no undo, depth, fuse). A person's refusal is not
kept (their dialog said it), nor an agent's (`move_ticket` answers it). Any successful column
move clears it. It rides the snapshot as `AutomationStatus.held` (`HeldMove { ticket, words,
at_ms }`, `#[serde(default)]`, left off the wire when empty) and `get_ticket` as
`automove.held`, which its description now names (below). **A column rule's line
stands only while the rule still refuses**: `held_items` asks `column_gate` again for each
entry as the snapshot is built, so a pipeline that passes clears the line with the card still
where it was; the move gate's line stands until the ticket moves. The words shown are the
refusal's as it happened, never re-read: a pipeline that went from running to failed keeps
`running` until the next automove is refused in its own words.

**The page.** `ui/ticket.rs::held_row`: one grey (`dim2`) row under the PR rows, `held: <words> ∙
2m ago`, the words through `scrub_cells` (a forge's job name rides them). No card line: the
card's second line is the brief's. The golden is `ticket_held_move_120x30`, since
`ticket_held_120x30` already named T-544's held ask.

**Tests.** `movegate::a_refused_automation_move_is_held_until_the_ticket_moves` (an automation's
kept, a person's and an agent's not, the latest replaces, a passing rule clears a rule's line
and not the gate's, off the board draws nothing, a move clears); `golden_ticket_held_move_120`
(the row under the PRs, the age, an escape in the words drawn inert, another ticket's not
drawn); `forge_e2e::a_ticket_with_no_pull_request_enters_and_one_opened_here_waits` now reads
the held line on the snapshot and in `get_ticket`, keeps it through the person's refused
`MoveTicket`, and sees it go when the forge reads the pipeline passed.

**Rig H1, and what it took.** REVIEW gated (`gate_pipeline`, reset on every lay), a running PR,
a worker's second turn ends held in IN PROGRESS. Asked a bare `Why did your ticket not move to
REVIEW?`, Sonnet answered `I don't know` without calling a tool in three runs — twice citing the
rig brief's `read no file and run no command`, once with that rule scoped to its first turn,
offering to look instead. `get_ticket`'s description named no automove at all, so it now says
`the board's moves and why it last held it (automove)` (816 → 820 bytes after trimming
`mesimon`, `the ticket's` and two parentheses), against the brief's "the field, not the
description". Asked `Find out why …, and say why in one line` (no tool or field named), the
worker tailed `daemon.log` (this repository's CLAUDE.md names it), then called `get_ticket` and
answered `held because this ticket's pull request #42 has a pipeline still running`: PASS. Not
measured: whether that run needed the description's new words.

## Doctor and USING.md say why a folder workspace asks to trust every worktree (T-762, 2026-10-14)

Seen on the forge lab: every ticket's agent stopped at Claude Code's "Quick safety check". Claude
Code keeps the trust answer per exact folder (`~/.claude.json`, `projects[path]`) and carries a
trusted checkout's answer to its git worktrees. A repository board's worktree is one; a folder
workspace's is a new folder holding git worktrees, so each ticket asks. mesimon answers no startup
modal and writes no `~/.claude.json`, so the way out is the person's: `git init` the root, commit a
README and a `.gitignore` naming the nested repos, run `claude` there once and accept.
`doctor`'s `workspace` line carries that as a second advice paragraph where the root has no
`.git`, and USING.md says it beside the worktree init script. No behaviour change.

## The train reads the forge at a turn's end, and not at all when nothing was pushed (T-761, 2026-10-14, follow-up to T-739 and T-753)

**Why.** T-753 asked why T-752 took 4 min 9 s from REVIEW to merged: 1 min 45 s of it was
`forge_fresh` (T-739) waiting for a forge reading. The train acts on a ticket only once the
forge was read after its agent's last turn end, since that turn may have opened a PR, and the
forge is read once a minute on the 10 s sweep: 0 to 70 s per turn end, two turn ends per rebase
cycle. Measured on T-749 and T-758 the same day: 36 s each before the rebase ask, up to a minute
again before the merge. The rule stays; the wait goes.

**No read when nothing could have changed.** A PR the forge would show and the last read did
not is one a push or a `pr create` made since, and both leave a local trace. Every forge read
now records its **basis** per ticket before any list call (`forge::Basis`): what the legs had
pushed (`forge::pushed`: every `refs/remotes/*` ref pointing at a commit in a leg's HEAD reflog,
`<repo> <ref> <oid>`, sorted; one `for-each-ref` per leg beside the reflog the binding already
read) and the ledger's PR URLs the query carried. The turn's end's own look (T-678's
`look_after_turn`, already a worker at the `Stop`) now reads the same `pushed` and whether a
transcript tail past the cost ledger's cursor holds a `pr create` (`cost::opened_in_tails`,
factored out of `opened_any`), into `forge::Local`. `forge::State::fresh` (the old `forge_fresh`
body, moved so it is unit-tested) answers true when the look began after the turn's end, both
`pushed` agree and are known, the tail held no `pr create`, and the ledger has no URL the read
lacked. All on the writer from memory; git runs only on the look's worker. A look from before
