the turn's end, or `None` anywhere (git or a tail unreadable), proves nothing. The basis and the
look are memory only: after a restart the first read sets them, so no schema moved.

**A read at the turn's end otherwise.** A look that proves nothing marks the ticket **owed**
(`forge.owed`, with the look's time) and `queue_forge_burst` reads that ticket's repositories
alone (`forge_query(Some(only))`, the minute's builder with a ticket filter; it probes no host,
so a host never probed waits for the minute), under a floor of one read per repository per
`forge::BURST_MS` (10 s, `forge.asked` stamped by both roads; a repository whose last call
failed waits for the minute's backoff). A floor or a read already out holds it to the next
tick. It lands as `Msg::ForgeBurst`, absorbed by the minute's code (`absorb_forge`), which
replaces only its repositories' errors and leaves the minute's clock alone. A read begun at or
after the owed time answers it. Two reads out at once is now possible, so a set is never
replaced by one read earlier than the set on hand. **The train now runs on every forge read**,
changed or not: a read that only made a ticket current used to wait for the next 10 s sweep.

**Measured** (`forge_e2e`, the minute set to ten): a turn that pushed nothing merges 1.9 s after
its `Stop` with no `gh` call (1.5 s of it the attention settle before the turn reads ended); a
turn that pushed (its tracking ref moved) merges 9.4 s after, the floor from the first pass just
before, with exactly one `pr list`. Every mesimon-board ticket today pushes nothing, so the first
half alone takes the forge out of the train's wait there; the second is the lab's shape and
costs one CLI call per turn end that pushed.

**Not done.** The base branch's own tracking ref moving (a fetch, the person pushing main) also
changes `pushed` when it points at a reflog commit: a read is owed where none was needed. Safe
side, one call. A PR opened from a browser leaves no local trace; the minute still finds it.

**Tests.** `forge::the_forge_is_current_with_no_forge_after_a_read_or_on_a_look_that_found_nothing`
(no forge; never read; no look; the look agrees; a new URL; that URL in the basis; a `pr create`
in the tail; an unreadable tail; pushed then a read at the turn's end; a look before the turn's
end; git unknown), `forge::the_floor_holds_a_repository_read_inside_the_burst_and_one_that_failed`,
`forge::a_push_moves_what_a_ticket_pushed_and_a_commit_alone_does_not` (a real repository: a
commit moves nothing, `update-ref` of a tracking ref does, a ref at a foreign commit does not);
`forge_e2e::a_turn_that_pushed_nothing_merges_on_its_look_with_no_read` and
`forge_e2e::a_turn_that_pushed_is_read_at_its_end_not_on_the_minute` (the stub `gh` logs its
calls). Each e2e fails with its half disabled: `unchanged` forced false reads once, the burst
off never merges. They sit in `forge_e2e` rather than `merge_train_e2e`, which has no `gh` stub.

## Dead rig boards are cleared, and a rig worktree seeds no target/ (T-765, 2026-10-14)

**The leak.** `ci/rig.py` keys its board on the ticket worktree it runs in, so its state dir
(`~/.local/state/mesimon/<proj16>/`), its worktrees, their `msmn/T-N-t-…` branches and at times
a `tmux -D` server outlived that worktree: the main board archives the ticket, nothing touches the
rig's. On 2026-10-14, 14 such boards held 71 worktrees and 71 branches in this repository, and
T-734's tmux server had run for two days. `du` read ~1.2 TB for them; it counts every APFS
clone whole. Every rig worktree's `target/` was a clone of the checkout's with **0 bytes rebuilt**
after it (rig workers never build); what they really held was the build output the checkout had
since replaced, 21 GB across all of them (a file's (path, mtime, size) absent from the checkout's
`target/`, counted once). The by-hand clear freed 13 GB; the rest is shared with live
main-board worktrees.

**Not in the daemon.** A teardown of nested boards on archive was proposed and refused: it is
this repository's own workflow, not a user's. Both halves are dev tooling.

**The fix.** `.mesimon-worktree-init.sh` exits before the clone when the checkout is on a `msmn/`
branch (a rig worktree's checkout is a ticket worktree). `ci/rig.py` writes its checkout's path
to `<state>/rig/parent` on every run and, before anything else, sweeps each board whose checkout
(that record, else a `sessions.json` cwd whose proj16 is the dir's name) is a
`<state root>/<proj16>/worktrees/<name>` path that no longer exists: its daemon and tmux server
SIGTERMed by `pgrep -f` on their argv (no client of a build that may be gone), its worktrees
`git worktree remove -f -f`, their branches `branch -D`, its state and runtime dirs removed. A
board with a worktree of another repository is left alone. `--stale` lists and removes nothing.
A board whose checkout exists is never touched, so a rig run never clears a sibling ticket's rig.

**Tests.** By hand: a dry sweep of the real state dir found the two live rig boards' checkouts
present and one dead board (a T-215 board, 52 KB); a fabricated dead board with a registered
worktree, a branch and a live tmux server was listed by the dry pass untouched, then cleared
whole; a board found by its `rig/parent` record alone was cleared; the init script skips for a
ticket-worktree checkout and seeds for a `main` one.

## The composer's workspace row drops `(default)` (T-766, 2026-10-14)

The new-ticket card's workspace row said `⎇ worktree (default)` while the pick was the column's
own workspace default (T-117's readout, kept when T-117's ring went to two explicit stops). The
author asked for the tail to go: the row now names the pick alone, on every column, and the
`shift+tab` hint takes the room the tail held. `render_workspace_selector` no longer takes the
column's default. The multi-line composer dialog never spelled it. Golden
`composer_column_default_120x30` reminted; its test asserts no `(default)`.

## A column can take no new tickets, and `o` there files next door (T-764, 2026-10-14)

**The ask.** Nothing is ever started in IN PROGRESS or REVIEW: a ticket reaches them by moving.
`o` on such a column should open the composer in the nearest column that takes new tickets, the
left side first, then the right; with none at all, the footer flashes red to say why.

**The setting.** `ColumnSettings::refuses_new`, the column dialog's `New tickets here: yes/no`
row. `#[serde(default)]`, no `COLUMNS_SCHEMA` bump: a build that drops it only lets a mint in
again, which narrows nothing. The template seeds it on IN PROGRESS and REVIEW; DONE stays open
(a person may log finished work there). `seed_template_settings` runs on a fresh board only, so
**an existing board keeps every column open** until a person sets the row: no migration.
`Board::set_column_settings` refuses to close the board's last open column, so `o` always has a
place to file; the red flash is for a board that got there anyway (an older file, a delete).

**One rule, every road.** `Board::filing_column(name)` is the rule (itself, else nearest left,
else nearest right, else `None`) and `landing_column` goes through it, so a board default that
is closed lands where `o` on it would, and the phone's `default_column` follows. `mint_full`
refuses a mint that names a closed column, in words that name the open one (`REVIEW takes no new
tickets: file it in TODO`): an agent's `create_ticket`, the phone's file, an import and the CLI
are refused rather than redirected, because the phone's `FileTicket` is authorized per column
and a redirect after the check would land it where it was never allowed. The TUI resolves
before it opens the composer, so the composer opens in the column the ticket will land in. An
adopted external session mints in the first column's `filing_column`. `DuplicateTicket` copies
beside its source and is not gated: a copy is not a new ticket in the sense the ask meant.

**The flash.** `App::refuse_flashing` sets the status and `status_flash` (the words and the
instant); the footer draws a status in the layout pause's delete-row/err treatment while lit,
on the same 400 ms × 3 cadence, and only while the status still says those words.

**Open.** The phone's New ticket sheet still lists every column; a closed one comes back as the
daemon's refusal. Hiding it needs the column's flag on the phone's board reply.

**Tests.** `a_closed_column_files_into_its_nearest_open_neighbour` (core),
`o_on_a_closed_column_composes_in_the_nearest_open_one` (TUI), the store round-trip, and
`mcp_e2e` asserts an agent's `create_ticket` into REVIEW is refused naming TODO. Five e2es and
`ci/state-lab.py` minted straight into IN PROGRESS/REVIEW; they open the column first
(`TestClient::open_to_new`) or mint and move.

## The train asks once per forge conflict, and a restart remembers what it asked (T-770, 2026-10-14, follow-up to T-635 and T-739)

**Why.** Forge lab 2026-10-13, scenario D1 (lab log findings 16 and 17): T-7's worker opened MR !4
on `api`, and the train asked it to rebase three times: 23:32:14, 23:40:09 and 23:40:40 (IDT), the
last two about 6 minutes after the forge reported the conflict the crown pushed. The lab log read
the first ask as made on a stale local main with no conflict on the forge, and the train as acting
on the local `needs_rebase` alone.

**Measured, from the board's feed, its journal and the worker's transcript.** The first ask was
owed. T-7's worktree was cut from the checkout's `api` main, which did not hold the MRs the lab
had merged on GitLab, so !4 conflicted from its first read. The worker resolved `hello.txt` and
force-pushed 7b478a9 at 23:32:35. The "phantom" `conflict cleared !4` at 23:33:25 was that fix
read back. Since T-739 the train asks on the forge's conflict alone while a PR is open. The 39 s
from the turn's end to that ask was `forge_fresh` waiting on the minute, which T-761 removed. The
6 minutes broke down like this:

| IDT | what | where the time went |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 23:33 | crown pushes 6be3497 to GitLab's main | |
| 23:35:47 | a forge read says `conflict !4` | ~1.5 min: the minute's cadence and GitLab's recompute |
| 23:35:47–23:39:59 | the train is silent | the memo: the ask was keyed on the local base tip, and `api`'s local main never moved (the forge merges), so `asked == base_tip` held. Without a restart it would never have asked |
| 23:39:59 | SIGTERM (a rebuilt binary); re-armed 23:40:00 | |
| 23:40:09 | second ask | the restart forgot the settled ask: T-635 kept open asks only |
| 23:40:23 | the worker force-pushes ce60ad0; its turn ends at 23:40:25 | |
| 23:40:34 | `U` handover | |
| 23:40:40 | third ask; the worker answers "Already up to date" | forgotten again, and the forge's last read (before the push) still said conflict |

**Built: one ask per conflict.** `train::lane` with a PR open owes the rebase on `pr_conflict`
and `!conflict_asked`. A new `Input::conflict_asked` / `Reading::conflict_asked` replaces the
base-tip memo there: a forge merge never moves the checkout's base, so the local tip can neither
say a conflict is new nor that it was asked about. Without a PR the rule is unchanged: once per
base tip. `AskRecord::conflict` records whether the forge reported a conflict on the ticket's PR
when the ask was delivered (`merge_to_agent`, by train or by hand). `absorb_forge`, on every read,
clears it for a ticket whose open PRs show no conflict (`Train::conflict_cleared`), so the next
conflict is owed one ask. A stale conflict read after the rebase's push, the 23:40:40 shape, is
the same conflict and asks nothing. The crown's `train_takes` reads the same memo.

**Built: the memo survives a restart.** `train.json` keeps `settled` beside `asks` (same
`KeptAsk` shape plus `conflict`). `restore_train` brings a settled ask back settled, and brings an
open ask whose ticket has no working or re-deriving agent back settled too (it used to be
dropped). The schema stays 1: an older build reads `asks`, ignores `settled` and drops it on its
next write, which is the pre-T-770 behaviour (one repeat), and nothing widens.

**Not built: "no ask on a stale local base".** The premise was the first ask, and that ask was
owed. With a PR open `needs_rebase` is not a reason (T-739). Without one, `needs_rebase` and the
base tip are about the checkout's own base branch (`worktree::compute_flags`), which a fetch never
moves, so "read since the last fetch" has nothing to wait for. A base that moved locally asks, as
before.

**Not done.** GitLab's `detailed_merge_status` can read `conflict` while `has_conflicts` is false
during a recompute (lab, 23:41), and `forge::parse_glab` ORs the two, so a card reads conflict
for a read or two after a fix. The memo stops that from asking. A read of `checking` (no conflict)
between two stale `conflict` reads would clear the memo and ask once more. Not seen; the fuse caps
it. A worktree cut from a checkout base that lags the forge starts behind its PR's target. That is
the first conflict's cause, and it is outside this ticket.

**Tests.** `train::a_pr_conflict_is_asked_once_whatever_the_local_base_says` (core: a clean local
base asks; asked at this local tip but not about this conflict asks; asked about it, silent, also
after the local base moves; a clean PR behind its base is the forge's; no PR keeps once per base
tip; `plan` reads the memo). Daemon: `train::the_asks_round_trip_open_and_settled` (settled with
its conflict; a pre-T-770 file reads as before) and
`train::a_conflict_asked_about_holds_until_the_forge_clears_it`.
`forge_e2e::a_pr_conflict_is_asked_about_once_and_again_only_when_it_returns`, on the stub `gh`: a
clean PR asks nothing and is never merged here; the flip to `CONFLICTING` asks once, in words
ending `so PR #42 updates`; the rebase turn ending under the stale conflict asks nothing; the flip
back asks nothing; a second conflict at the same local base asks again; a restart, then a person's
turn, asks nothing. The e2e fails in each half's absence: the old base-tip memo times out on the
second conflict's ask, and a restore without `settled` asks a third time.
`merge_train_e2e::a_rebase_turn_open_across_a_restart_still_holds_the_next_ask` now reads B's
settled ask under `settled` rather than gone. There is no rig test: the words to the agent are
unchanged, and only when they are sent moved.

## The train never merges a ticket whose work goes through pull requests (T-778, 2026-10-14, follow-up to T-739 and T-770)

**Why.** Forge lab run 2, 2026-10-14 17:52 (`~/Documents/code/forge-lab`, its T-9). T-9's work went
to GitLab as MR !5 (merged), !6 (closed) and !7 (merged, from `fix/greeting-r2`). At 17:52:24 a
forge read said `merged !7`. One second later the train fast-forwarded T-9's `msmn/` branch into
the lab's local `api` main (`merge_train_merged`). GitLab had already merged that work as merge
commits, so local main and `origin/main` diverged 4 and 4, and the next pull would have merged
duplicates. The train held a ticket only while a PR was open (`pr_open`, T-739). Once every PR was
merged or closed nothing held it. The branch's tip was no PR's head, so `forge::merged_at` did not
fold it merged, and the local base had not moved, so the branch read `ahead`.

**Built: a PR bound is the forge's merge.** `train::WtFlags::pr_open` became `has_pr`: any PR in
the ticket's set, open, merged or closed, on any repository (`forge::State::has_pr`). `train::lane`
never puts such a ticket on the merge list. A rebase is owed only on the forge's conflict (T-770's
memo), never on `needs_rebase` alone. `pr_conflict` is about open PRs only, so a ticket whose PRs
are all closed or merged is asked nothing. The crown's `train_takes` reads the same flag, so a
delivery of such a ticket wakes the crown rather than waiting for a train that will not come.

**Built: the words.** `get_ticket`'s `merge` reads `by: "forge", why: "its work goes through pull
requests"` for any ticket with a PR bound, after the merged clause (a merged branch still reads
`nobody`) and before the mode and the train: the forge merges it in either crown mode.
`forge::merge_refusal` is the one refusal: the open PR's sentence while one is open (T-739's
`open_refusal`), else `its pull requests carry the merge — merge on <forge>`. `merge_ticket` (a
person's `m`, the crown, the train's pass) refuses with it after the already-merged check, and
`crown_merge_refusal` says it with the key in front, before a `needs_rebase` refusal that would
ask for a rebase the forge does not need. `CROWN_WAKES` names the fourth merger.

**Not built.** The lab's recovery: its crown reset the local main. A ticket that went through a
PR and should now be merged here (its PR closed unmerged and the work wanted locally) has no road
on the board but git. The ticket asked for no exception, and a closed PR is still the team's
decision about that work.

**Tests.** `train::a_ticket_with_a_merged_pr_is_never_the_trains_to_merge` (core: ahead or behind,
nothing; the same branches with no PR are the train's), `train::an_open_pr_is_the_merge_and_a_stale_verdict_holds`
and the T-770 test on `has_pr`, and `forge::an_open_pr_on_a_merged_ticket_holds_the_merge` for
`merge_refusal`'s three answers. `forge_e2e::a_ticket_whose_work_went_through_a_pr_is_never_the_trains`,
on the stub `gh` with the train armed: PR 42 merged at a head the branch is not at, the branch ahead
in REVIEW; after several passes there is no `merge_train_merged`, no rebase ask, the local main has
not moved, and the snapshot's pending list does not hold the ticket. The agent's `get_ticket` reads
`forge`, and `m` is refused in the new words. A ticket beside it with no PR is then merged by the
same train. With the lane's flag forced off, the e2e fails on the pending list: the train tries the
merge and only `merge_ticket`'s refusal stops it. Rig F7 (real Sonnet): a crown asked to land such
a branch "if landing it is the crown's to do" reads `merge`, lands nothing and answers forge.

## The armed column flashes like an armed card (T-775, 2026-10-14)

The first `d` on a column's header armed the delete with a footer sentence alone, while the
first `d` on a card flashed it red. Now the header row takes the doomed card's treatment from
the first `d` to the second or the stray key that cancels: `Theme::delete_row` (the diff's
deleted-line ground) under an `err` name, on `Theme::delete_lit`'s 400 ms phase. `App::column_doomed`
is the column's twin of `App::doomed`; nothing new in the theme, so the one-saturated-colour law
is untouched. A header being renamed does not flash.

**Tests.** `ui::tests::test_armed_column_delete_flashes_the_header`: at rest no header cell is
tinted, after `d` the row is and the name is in `err`, a stray key clears it.

## The guided tour (T-763, 2026-10-14)

**The ask.** A walkthrough for newcomers, in the Esc menu for now: a big dialog, the concepts
down the left, an animated board on the right showing the one under the cursor with a
description, and Enter to do it yourself on that board where that makes sense. Named **Guided
tour** (the menu row, the frame's title).

**The practice board is the board.** The right pane is a second `App`
(`App::practice`) on a toy daemon (`tour/toy.rs`): a `Transport` whose world is in memory and
answers the wire the way the daemon does for the commands a lesson reaches (create, rename,
move, tag, notes, archive, delete, duplicate, columns, tiers, crown, merge, adopt, spawn). It
writes no file and starts no process; anything else is refused in words saying it belongs to a
real board, and the refusal is recorded (`World::refused`). `ui::tour` draws that `App` with the
very `ui::draw` that draws the board, onto a `TestBackend` canvas the pane's size, and lays its
cells into the pane; its dialog frames join the outer frame's record, so the L1 laws read its
composer's border as a frame. The practice board is drawn under the board's 60x20 floor
(`App::is_practice`). Its mouse hints are stashed around its draw (`mouse::stash_hints`), so the
outer frame's survive.

**A lesson is keys on a clock** (`tour/lessons.rs`): a seed world, then `Step`s, `Key` (900 ms
to see it land), `Type` (70 ms a letter), `Wait`, `Say` (the line under the board) and `Do`, the
world moving by itself where an agent, a forge or the train has the part (a turn ending, a
pipeline passing, a branch merging). The toy applies `core::automove` on a session's state
edge, so a start moves its card as on a real board. Because the animation presses the real
keys, it cannot drift from them: `every_lesson_plays_to_its_end` plays all 23 and fails on a
lesson whose keys no longer do what its try asks for, or that reaches past the practice board.
Each lesson replays after a 3 s hold; `r` replays at once.

**Trying it.** Enter (where the lesson has an `ask`) resets the world and hands the practice
board every key, Esc and its menu included, since two lessons go through the menu. **q gives
them back**: on the practice board the board's quit is the way back to the lessons, its hint
reads `back to the tour` and the menu's last row `Back to the tour` (`Ctx::practice`); the
practice menu offers no tour and no Sharing. A lesson's `done(&World, &App)` turns its row's
tick on and the line under the board to `✓ done`. Copying during playback copies nothing; a
person's own `c` while trying does (`App::practice_copies`), and an opener only says what it
would open.

**The 23 lessons**, in five groups: Tickets (create, rename, describe and pictures, checklists,
tags, copy the title, duplicate, archive, delete), Moving (`> >`, `HJKL` and `.`, automatic
moves), Finding (search, links), Agents (quick start, start an agent, tiers, worktrees, the
merge train, pull requests, the crown, adopt a session), The board (columns and their
settings). Watch-only: automatic moves and the merge train.

**Plumbing.** `App::tick` split into `pump` (everything but the terminal read) and the read; the
practice board is pumped by the tour's own tick, never reads the terminal. `UpdateWatch::inert`,
`ReleaseWatch::inert` and a first `refresh` (the machine's tiers ride the snapshot, not `new`)
in `App::practice`. `Scope::Tour` (jk, enter try it, r replay, esc close), `Verb::Tour`,
`Mode::Tour` with the state in `App::tour`.

**Open.** The mouse picks nothing in the dialog yet (no `Target::Row` on the lessons, no clicks
into the practice board). The crown lesson does not strike its lightning. The lesson words are
first drafts for the author to tune.

**Tests.** The tour's own (`tour::tests`, `tour::toy::tests`, `tour::lessons::tests`), goldens
`tour_140x40` and `tour_narrow_90x30`, the tour with a practice-board dialog open in
`test_no_drawn_structure`, `trying_hands_the_practice_board_the_keys_and_the_real_board_keeps_its_own`.
`MESIMON_TOUR_DUMP=<n> cargo test -p mesimon-tui dump_a_lesson -- --nocapture` prints lesson n
beat by beat: how a lesson is written against what the board really does. Menu goldens reminted
for the new row.

## A turn's end's crown wake waits for that turn's forge read (T-773, 2026-10-14, follow-up to T-744 and T-761)

**Why.** Forge lab 2026-10-13, finding 1: the `finished`, `answered your ask` and `delivered`
wakes reached the crown before the board had read the MR the turn had just opened, and
`get_ticket` showed no PR row for 30 to 90 s (A1 ~30 s, B3 ~90 s, C1 ~40 s). T-761 now reads
the forge at a turn's end that pushed or opened something; the wake did not wait for it.

**What.** `crownwake::owe_turn_end` is the one road a turn's end's wake takes out of
`judge_probe` (both the look's and git's `Unknown`). Where `forge::State::awaited` says a read
is coming, the wake is held in `Heard::forging` (in `crown.json`, beside `stepped`; feed word
`crown_wake_deferred:forge`), folding a second turn's end into it. `awaited` is: a forge reads
the board, and either the ticket's own look is out with a forge half (`State::looking`, set in
`queue_ticket_flags`, cleared when the look lands: the look may yet find a push) or the look
owed a read none has answered (`State::owed`, T-761). `hear_forged` lets it go when
`awaited` turns false (the look found nothing to read, or a read begun since the turn's end
landed, `State::answer`) or `FORGE_WAIT_MS` (15 s) pass, on the look's landing, on each forge
read and on the tick. It enters the wake without draining, before `hear_forge`, so a forge edge
the same read brings (a PR bound passed) folds into the one line. The ticket's id in the brief
was `Msg::ForgeSampled`'s; T-761's own read lands as `Msg::ForgeBurst`, and either answers.

**The look runs for the crown, train or not.** T-761's look was asked only where the train
could take the ticket (`look_after_turn`); with the train off, a turn's end owed no read and
the hold had nothing to wait for. `look_after_turn` now also takes it for a worker the crown
hears (`crown_hears_turn`), without the person's banner hold (`awaiting_looks` stays the
train's).

**The opening is said.** `forge::Edge::opened` became the labels, and `Edge::opening` says them
(`opened !2`). T-744 kept the opening out of `news` because the turn's end carried it; now it
does: `absorb_forge` hands each ticket's openings to `hear_forged`, which puts them first in a
held wake's forge words, or keeps them (`Heard::opening`, memory) for a turn whose probe is
still out. An opening found with no turn's end to ride (a PR opened from a browser, a read past
the 15 s) still wakes no one by itself. The crown's brief (`mcp::CROWN_WAKES`) and USING.md
say it.

**Not re-judged at release.** The wake is the one `due` gave at the look, as `hear_stepped`
does: a turn begun in the 15 s folds its own end into it.

**Tests.** Unit `a_turn_end_waits_for_its_forge_read_only_where_one_is_owed` (no forge; the look
out; nothing pushed; pushed, a read begun before answers nothing, the 15 s, the read; the
opening first in the line beside a bound PR's edge). `forge_e2e::a_turn_end_wake_waits_for_the_turns_forge_read`:
the stub's `pr list` takes 2 s from the turn on; the worker pushes and #42 appears; one
`finished` wake, at least 2 s after the `Stop`, saying `opened #42`, the crown's `get_ticket`
at that moment listing #42, and no `forge` wake. With the hold off it fails on `get_ticket`.
`crown_e2e`, `merge_train_e2e`, `pr_merge_e2e` and all of `forge_e2e` pass. The rig: F1 on the
real Sonnet (claude 2.1.296), 2026-10-14: PASS in 44 s, wakes `finished`, `forge`.

## Forge wakes per PR on a multi-repo ticket (T-782, 2026-10-14, follow-up to T-757 and T-773)

**Why.** Forge lab run 2, 2026-10-14. C1 (two repositories): web's !2 merged while api's !8 was
open, and the crown heard neither `merged !2` nor `waiting on deploy:production !2`. Its
`delivered` line said `merge_state ahead` with no repository. A pass said `waiting on
deploy:production !7, deployed to staging !7`, the deployment after the wait it came before. A1:
the first turn's `delivered` did not name `opened !5`, though `get_ticket` listed it.

**The first merge of a multi-repo ticket.** T-757 left a merge to the flags wherever the PR's head
is a leg's tip. On a ticket with another leg unmerged no flag flips: the ticket reads merged only
once every judged leg does (`worktree::aggregate`), so that merge was said by no one.
`absorb_forge` now asks `forge_lands_all`: the legs with this read folded in as
`forge_fold_legs` will fold it. A tip PR's merge is said by the forge unless the flags carry it
(a flip waiting for the tick, already said, or this read flips them), and under T-757's rule
otherwise (said first where the same read reads its deployment). The second leg's merge is the
flags' `merged` wake, and `merged !2` is not said again.

**A merged PR's wait is its own.** `Edge::waiting` was `pipeline_of(set)`'s, which is the open
PRs' worst while any is open: a merged PR's merge-commit wait beside an open PR was never seen.
`waiting` is now the open PRs' alone, and `Edge::stopped` holds each merged PR whose pipeline newly
stopped on a job (newly merged, or read merged before at another pipeline), said per PR like
`reached`. `failed` keeps its set-wide reading; nothing in the lab asked for it per PR.

**The order.** `Edge::news` says merged, the pipelines (failed, passed, a bound PR's), deployed,
then waiting (the open set's, a bound PR's, each merged PR's). T-769 had waiting before deployed.
Conflicts and reviews still come last.

**`ahead` per repository.** T-772 made a moved `ahead` per leg; the first word, `merge_state
ahead` with nothing heard before, still named none. On a branch of more than one leg it is now
`merge_state ahead api 1, web 1`, the legs ahead by their word (`crownwake::changes`).

**The opening mid-turn.** T-773 kept an opening for a turn whose probe was out, else dropped it.
If the minute's read binds the PR while the turn that opened it is still running, the look after
the turn finds the push it read (`State::unchanged`), so no read is owed, nothing is held, and the
opening was already dropped. Two holes, both closed: `hear_forged` also keeps an opening for a
worker the crown hears whose turn is open (`turns_open`), and a ticket's first read, a baseline
for every other edge, still yields its openings (a PR the ticket's reads never held), for a first
turn that opens one before any read of the ticket. An opening with no turn to ride still wakes
no one. A forge first probed while a worker is mid-turn on an old PR would call it opened: rare,
and accepted.

**Who merges on the forge.** `CROWN_WAKES` said a forge's PR "is merged on the forge by a person".
That is not the board's to say (T-744): a crown whose brief says merge merges there itself. It
now says "is merged on the forge, and merge_ticket refuses it". `merge.why` (`its work goes through
pull requests`) and `forge::merge_refusal` named no one already.

**Tests.** Units `a_merged_prs_wait_is_its_own_beside_an_open_one`,
`a_pass_says_merged_before_its_pipeline_and_its_deployment` (the new order),
`a_merged_commits_pipeline_passing_is_no_pass` (a merged wait is `stopped`),
`a_multi_leg_delta_names_each_leg_that_moved` (the first word), and the brief's test.
`forge_e2e::a_two_repo_tickets_first_merge_and_its_wait_are_said`: a folder workspace, an MR on
api and on web; the `delivered` line says `merge_state ahead api 1, web 1`; web's !2 merges and
the crown hears `merged !2` and `waiting on deploy:production !2` with no `merged` wake; api's !8
merges and the `merged` wake comes, `merged !2` said once, no `merged !8`. Without the change it
times out on `merged !2`. `forge_e2e::an_opening_read_mid_turn_rides_the_turns_wake`: the read
binds #42 between the turn's `UserPromptSubmit` and its `Stop`; the `finished` line says `opened
#42`, once. Without the change the line says `nothing new to merge` alone. All of `forge_e2e`
passes, and the whole workspace under nextest (2408).

**A refused crown merge is fed again.** T-778 moved the forge's refusal into
`crown_merge_refusal`, which answered before any feed line, so the rig's F3 counted
`merge_ticket×0` while the crown had called it twice and been refused in the forge's words. Every
`crown_merge_refusal` refusal now feeds `merge_ticket refused`, as the merge road's own refusal
does; `crown_e2e::the_crown_merges_where_the_train_will_not` counts the supervised one.

**The rig**, on the real Sonnet (claude 2.1.300), 2026-10-15: F1 PASS in 44 s (wakes `finished`,
`forge`, the crown's `ask_agent`, the worker's `noted`). F3 failed `crown:merge_ticket` on the
feed gap above, the crown's transcript showing both refused calls; with the feed line, PASS in
49 s: woken `delivered` then `forge`, and the crown, its brief saying merge, called
`merge_ticket`, refused on the open PR.

## A worktree that cannot be cut says why, and the crown hears it (T-777, 2026-10-14)

**The words.** A repository with no commits read on the card as `precheck: git
--no-optional-locks failed: fatal: ambiguous argument 'HEAD': …`, cut mid-sentence. The cause
was `default_branch`'s last rung, `rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD`, which refuses an unborn HEAD; the
precheck's own `base branch main has no commits` was never reached. The rung now asks
`symbolic-ref --short HEAD` first (it names an unborn branch), so the precheck says
`no commits on main yet — make a first commit, then start again` (`worktree::no_commits_yet`); a
detached HEAD with no main/master/trunk says `DETACHED_HEAD` instead of `base branch HEAD …`, and
a workspace leg says `api has no commits on main yet — …`. The card's detail
(`worktree::error_words`) drops the stage word for a precheck, whose message is always mesimon's
sentence; a later stage (`add`, `mark`, `include`) keeps `stage: git's words`, because the
stage is what places them.

**The crown.** `start_agent` on a ticket whose tree is still to be cut answers `session_started:
false`, and a provision that then failed dropped the parked spawn in silence: the crown waited
on a worker that would never come. `on_provisioned`'s failure now owes the crown a wake when
the parked spawn was the crown's (`PendingSpawn::started_by`) or the parked wake was of a
worker it started: `WakeCause::Unstarted`, the strongest cause (no agent exists, so nothing
else about the ticket is news), said `T-12 "…" could not start (its worktree: <the card's
words>)`, with the reason on `CrownWake::unstarted` (serde default; crown.json's schema stays 1,
as T-739's `Forge` did). `get_ticket` carries the same words as `worktree_error` while the
binding is in error. `CROWN_WAKES` tells the crown that a fix outside the brief is the person's,
by `raise_hand`, and that `start_agent` tries again once it is made.

**The root's failure takes the same road.** `queue_provision`'s `ensure_root` failure set
`Error { stage: "root" }` and returned, leaving its parked spawn parked for good and the queue
behind it unstarted; it now goes through `on_provisioned`'s failure arm like any stage's.

**Not done.** A later stage's git text is still git's own, behind its stage word.

**Tests.** Unit `provision_refuses_an_unborn_or_detached_base_in_plain_words`.
`crown_e2e::a_crown_start_whose_worktree_cannot_be_cut_wakes_the_crown_with_why`: a repository
with `git init` alone, the crown's `start_agent` on a worktree; the crown's pane reads the
`could not start` line, the card's detail and `get_ticket`'s `worktree_error` are the sentence,
no agent started. The rig: U1 (new; `hold_branch` makes the ticket's branch before the start, so
the precheck refuses; an `until = { woke = … }` for a step with no worker) on the real Sonnet
(claude 2.1.299), 2026-10-14: PASS in 30 s, wake `unstarted`, and the crown, told nothing of
what to do, raised its hand naming the branch that already exists.

## A card shows what went between it and the crown (T-783, 2026-10-15, "when messages received through crown communications show the message in the preview below title of ticket like normal agent message does")

**What.** A card the crown spoke to said `♛ sent` (or `♛ answered`) for a beat and nothing of what
was sent; the crown's card said `♛ woke` and nothing of why. The words now take the resting
card's line under its title — the T-720 new-reply row, same fade, same quiet ink: on a worker's
card `♛ <the crown's ask or answer>`, on the crown's card the wake's news bare (`T-5 delivered
(commit 1a2b3c4)`). Agreed with the author before building: both directions, on the receiving
card, gone as a new reply goes.

**The record.** `Snapshot.crown_said` (serde default), one `CrownSaid { ticket, words, at_ms }`
per receiving ticket, the latest, in memory like the touches; whitespace-flattened and capped at
`CROWN_SAID_BYTES` (240) by `Daemon::crown_said`. Written where the words provably went, never at
`asked`: `send_queued_ask` for a crown's ask (sent now, immediately, or by a person's `^y`),
`drain_queue`'s crown arm for one sent at the agent's idle, `crown_answer_settled` for an answer
whose keys went in, and `drain_crown_wakes` on a delivered wake, from `crown_wake_news` — the
wake sentence's events without the template and without the titles, which the board already
shows on each worker's card. `start_agent` carries no words of the crown's, so it records none.

**The card.** `App::card_news` picks the line: the crown's words while unseen and newer than the
agent's last reply (`Spoke::since_ms`), else the T-720 reply. The cursor resting on the card
acks both (`ack_spoke`, `crown_said_seen`); `New replies` off turns both off. A board opened
later than the words still shows them (the daemon keeps the latest per ticket until a newer one
or a restart); a reply already on the transcript when the board opens reads as newer, as T-720's
first sight does.

**The ink** (the author, after the first build: "indicate it's crown communication, maybe using
the blue colored text, but with a slight opacity since it's not a title"). The line settles in
`Theme::crown_quiet` — the crown's tint (`pip(5)`) mixed `CROWN_QUIET` (0.7) over the ground —
through `Theme::crown_reveal`, the reply's fade with another ink; a reply keeps `rest.dim2`. Below
an RGB ground it is the tint itself. The bolts were already there and stay as they were: the
crown's ask strikes worker-ward on `asked`/`sent`, and the turn that answers it owes the crown a
wake, whose `woke` touch strikes crown-ward.

**Tests.** `app::crown_words_ride_the_card_until_seen_or_answered`,
`ui::a_resting_card_shows_what_went_between_it_and_the_crown` (golden
`board_crown_said_120x30`), and `crown_e2e`'s sent, answered and delivered-wake steps assert
`crown_said`.

## T-788 — the card's pull-request line wears the card's band (2026-10-15)

The author: "the MR line below ticket title has a different background than the rest of the
ticket". The T-739 brief's line 2 was pushed with no line style, so under the cursor it sat on
the board's ground between a banded title row and banded accordion rows. Line 2 — the brief, or
a reply sharing it — now takes the accordion's `acc_style` (the cursor band, or the delete row),
hoisted above it; never the needs-you row's, which stays one row. Test:
`ui::the_cursor_cards_pr_line_wears_the_cards_band`.

## T-789 — an open card draws its pull-request line last (2026-10-15)

First built as "an open card names neither its key nor its tier; the hover row names the tier",
merged, and reverted the same day on the author's word ("revert this, I changed my mind"): the
open card names its key and tier as before.

What shipped instead, in the author's words: "if there is a PR line on the ticket, when peeked,
show it last and reduce the max preview lines and summary lines by one". An open card (`p`, `P`
or the pointer) draws the T-739 brief as its last row, after the reply and the summary rows, and
not on line 2; the reply's cap goes from `PEEK_ROWS` (4) to 3 and the summary's from
`SUMMARY_ROWS` (3) to 2 while it does, so the card grows by at most the row it moved. A closed
card keeps it on line 2, beside a new reply. The board finds the brief's click spot on line 2 or
the card's last line (`Group::prs_at` carries its row). Test:
`ui::an_open_cards_pr_line_comes_last_and_the_rows_above_give_way`.

## T-793 — a provision cut before a restart is adopted, not refused (2026-10-15)

T-792's start failed with `precheck: branch msmn/T-792-… already exists`. The spawn queued a
fresh provision, the daemon was asked to shut down 6 s later (the `U` handover) while the
worktree init script ran, and the tree was already cut and marked. `queue_provision` persists a
fresh binding blank (no path, no branch) until the provision reports, so on restart
`reconcile_interrupted` read it as "nothing landed" and dropped it; every later spawn then
provisioned fresh and precheck refused the branch the first one had cut. `provision` now adopts
a tree at its own directory whose ownership marker names the same ticket and which stands on
the ticket's branch: `Attached`, `base_oid` the merge-base with the base branch, and the init
script runs again (it is idempotent: `[ -e target ] && exit 0`). A tree marked for another
ticket, or none, is refused as before. A workspace provision (T-368) still refuses its
container in that case. Test: `worktree::provision_merge_teardown_roundtrip`.

## T-794 — the pull-request line says what the newest PR is at (2026-10-15)

The author: "show more information on PR line — if pipeline running, show the current job
that's running with a slow shimmer; make use of the free space there unless there's a message
preview rendered right now and user is not peeking". The T-739 line held only marks and
numbers, right-aligned, with the room left of them blank. Where no new reply holds that room
(a resting card's T-720 row), it now carries `card::pr_words`: about the newest open PR, else
the newest — the leftmost mark — its pipeline in fewer words than the page (`build-linux`
alone while it runs, `failed: test-linux`, `waiting: deploy`, `passed`), then the page's
conflict, review and deployed clauses, then `draft`, the one state no mark spells (a merged
PR's `●` says merged). Cut against the marks like a reply; under `PR_WORDS_MIN` cells the marks
stand alone. An open card's last-row line (T-789) carries the words too, since its reply is
drawn whole above. The words are the line's click as well (`board::brief_at` widens the span
leftward to them).

**A running pipeline names its job.** `Pipeline::Running` carries a `String`, as the wait and
the failure do. GitHub's rollup names the first check `IN_PROGRESS`, else the first queued one;
GitLab's `named_job` reads the pipeline's jobs for a `running` one, one more call per read of a
running pipeline (every 15 s, T-781). The name rides the snapshot's existing `job` and
`forge.json`'s, so no wire or schema change; an older TUI ignores it. `get_ticket`'s
`AgentPrView` drops it on purpose: an agent's `job` stays a wait's or a failure's, and the
crown's edges never turn on a running job's name.

**The shimmer** (`Theme::pr_shimmer`): a crest five cells wide eases across the words in
2.4 s, then rests 1.6 s, lifting the row's `dim2` toward its `dim1` — grey on grey, so the
one-saturated-colour law stands. Below TrueColor it steps; mono holds still. It rides the
100 ms frame, never `animating()`'s 16 ms. Tests: `ui::a_cards_pr_line_says_what_the_newest_pr_is_at`,
`theme::a_running_pipelines_shimmer_crosses_slowly_then_rests`, `forge::the_rollup_folds_to_the_loudest_word`,
and `forge_e2e::the_crown_hears_the_forges_edges` (the snapshot names the check, `get_ticket`
does not).

## T-795 — who merges a working ticket is read where its turn ends (2026-10-15)

The author, watching two tickets land while the crown waited on them: "It might be a bug that
the board told you you are responsible to merge it. Merge train was on the whole time".
`merge_by` (T-613) read the train's reach off the column the card sat in, so a worker working in
IN PROGRESS (reach: rebase asks) read `merge: crown` with the train armed; its turn's end moved
the card to REVIEW and the train merged it. A working ticket is now read in the column it
delivers in, `automove::delivers_in`: the column rules a turn in flight will apply at its end
(`on_working` then `on_done` for one still spawning; `on_done` for a running turn, a mid-turn
dialog or background tasks), the card's own column otherwise. The why names it ("the train is
armed and reaches REVIEW, where this turn's end puts it"). The delivered wake's word is
unchanged: at delivery the turn has ended and the card moved. Tests:
`automove::a_turn_in_flight_delivers_where_its_end_lands`, `crown_e2e`'s
`the_crown_merges_where_the_train_will_not` step 2.

## The fourth simplify pass, and the forge's bug hunt (T-795, 2026-10-15, "simplify")

The author: "run simplify since last simplify run and also try to hunt for bugs or issues
introduced especially with the github PR and gitlab MR integrations". Range `870c00ae..71b64b01`
(everything since T-688, 142 commits). Four review angles (reuse, simplification, efficiency,
altitude) and two bug hunts (the forge's daemon side; its core, wire and TUI side), each finding
checked against the code before it was applied.

**Applied, simplify.** The forge's `gh`/`glab` api calls through `RepoQuery::api`/`project`; one
`failed_words`; `Edge::any` as `!= Default`; one parse of GitLab's pipelines answer;
`State::pr_conflict` for `open_of`; `fold_set` under `forge_fold_legs` and `forge_lands_all`;
`set_ticket_agg` for both writers of `wt_agg`; `launch_forge_burst`; `agent_allowed_columns`
through `column_gate`; `Heard::land`; `PrItem::forge_kind`/`label` (the TUI spelled `!`/`MR` by
hand four times); `Remote::candidates`, `Remote::key`; `Count::of_marks`;
`Board::filing_refusal`; `State::remote`, `State::keep_tickets` (the forget missed
`conflicted`); `Daemon::live_transcripts`; `forge::iso_ms` through `usage::rfc3339_ms`;
`App::pr_mark`, `flash_running`/`flash_lit`, `pr_state_clauses`; the tour's toy applies the
`Board`'s column methods and stamps `state_changed_at` in ms (it stamped seconds: practice
agents read decades old). Dead: `State::cli_for`, `Row::is_task`, `typing_now`. Efficiency: the
snapshot's held lines read the merge clause off the cached flags (`gate_with`), the burst checks
its floor before building a query, an arrival reads its tip once.

**Applied, bugs.** A forge read that did not hear every repository of a ticket reads nothing of
it (`forge::read_whole`): before, a failed `pr list` stamped the ticket current with the PR its
turn had just opened unbound, and the train fast-forwarded the branch
(`forge_e2e::a_failed_read_after_a_push_holds_the_train` failed on the old code). `carry` keeps
the old PRs of every repository that did not answer (failed, unlisted, a host no CLI reads),
not only a failed one's, and an open PR whose pipeline read failed keeps the last one at the
same head; `pipeline_of` reads an unread open PR `Unknown` where the fold would be green or
none. Smaller: a PR's page is kept only as an `http(s)` address; a GitLab fast-forward merge
without squash lands its head; `canceling` reads failed, `requested_changes` changes requested;
GitLab environment names and project paths are percent-encoded; `pipeline failed` names the
open PRs failing; `pr_urls` cuts a JSON-escaped newline; the forge advisory scrubs its key; the
`news` fingerprint covers the job, conflicts, the review and deployments.

**Skipped, and why.** Dropping `ForgeStatus.present`/`trouble` (unread, but a public wire
struct the relay builds against). One `text_field` list (the three differ by mutability and by
what a field is). `sanitize_environment` through `job_word` (they would agree, but the column's
name is drawn, and `job_word` keeps box glyphs). The larger redesigns, each a ticket of its own:
one `train::lane` → `Result<Lane, Skip>` behind `merge_by`, `train_takes` and
`train_could_take`; one speaker per merge (the flags' `merged` or the forge's `merged !N`, never
both, which removes T-757/T-769/T-782's dedupe clauses); one flags sample per turn end
(`probe_turn` and `look_after_turn` each sample); a `MergeState` enum for the stringly
`merge_word`; `forge::State`'s seven per-ticket maps as one struct; the pref arms stepping the
layer they write (T-751's swap of `App::prefs`); one `Seen<K>` for the three unseen stores; one
fenced child-process runner (`forge::run`, `gitstatus::fetch`, `modroad::run_bounded`); one
remote ladder; `Pr::item` for the three projections of a PR; `get_ticket` reading each note once.

**Found and left open** (the forge's, each needing a decision): a new worktree's HEAD reflog
holds its cut commit, so under GitLab fast-forward merges a ticket cut right after a merge binds
that MR and reads merged by the forge; `ticket_set` drops closed PRs, so `has_pr` (T-778's "open,
merged or closed") never sees one, and an opened-here URL whose PR closed holds a
`requires_pipeline` column at `pipeline not read`; a probe that fails (offline at start) is
believed for 6 h and reads the host as having no CLI; a PR merged with a head past the local tip
(a review-suggestion commit) never lands the leg; a fork-as-origin PR is keyed on the wrong
repository; a cancelled merge-commit pipeline settles as failed; "newest merged PR" orders by
`updated_at`, not merge time; a `STALE` GitHub check reads passed and a merge commit's commit
statuses are never read; one failing repository backs off the whole board's minute; a list
capped at 100 drops an older bound PR; an SSH host alias is never a forge.

## A lost forge sign-in is asked again on the backoff (T-798, 2026-10-15)

Closes T-795's "a probe that fails (offline at start) is believed for 6 h". `probe_host` now
keeps the CLI's words when a binary is there and `auth status` fails (`HostProbe::lost`), and
the writer keeps them (`State::take_probe`) only for a host the board reads: one whose probe
had a CLI or was lost before, or whose host a live ticket's PRs are on. Such a host is
`stale()` after `backoff()` (5 min, `MESIMON_FORGE_BACKOFF_MS`) rather than `PROBE_FOR`, is
the advisory row's first line (`trouble()`: `<host> sign-in: <the CLI's words>`), and is not
"no forge" (`reads_nothing`, read by `none()` and `read_whole`'s closure), so its tickets wait
for it as for a repository that failed, while `carry` keeps their known PRs on the cards.

**Kept as it was:** a host with no `gh`/`glab`, or one whose CLI was never signed in and holds
no PR, still reads as no forge and flows through the train.

**`--active`:** gh's `auth status` fails when *any* account on the host has a stale token;
`--active` checks the one gh uses. gh older than it (2.52 here) says `unknown flag: --active`,
and the probe asks again without it. glab has no such flag.

**Not done:** a first probe that fails on a board that has never held a PR on the host (no
memory of a CLI across a restart, nothing on the cards) is still believed for 6 h: nothing
local separates "offline" from "never signed in" without parsing the CLI's prose.

## The card's `passed` is news for a beat; a deploy reads `in <env>` (T-803, 2026-10-15)

The card's PR line (T-794) said `passed` for as long as a pipeline stayed passed, and
`deployed: staging, production`, both of which pushed the words into the `~` cut. Now the card
says `passed` only for `PR_PASSED_MS` (5 s) after the board saw that PR's pipeline turn passed
(`App::pr_passed`, by ticket, repository and number, recorded in `App::take_prs` from `absorb`,
timed on the injected `App::now`), and its mark says it alone after that. A PR first seen
passed — the board opening, a PR that arrives already passed — is not news: only a PR the last
snapshot held at another pipeline word counts. `failed`, `waiting` and a running job are
unchanged. Every tick already renders, so the word leaves on the 100 ms tick with no
`animating()` frame.

The merge's environments read `in production` on the card, the last one `PrItem.deployed`
names (it is in the order it happened, `forge::deploy_order`), and `in staging, production` on
the ticket page's rows and in the `^h` dialog, which still say `pipeline passed`. The crown's
wake words and `get_ticket`'s `deployed` field are unchanged.

## T-800 — the forge's misreadings: forks, cancels, stale checks, aliases (2026-10-15)

Eight of the T-795 bug hunt's "left open" findings, each answered as its brief proposed.

**A cancelled run is its own word, `cancelled`, never green and never failed.** GitLab's
`canceled`/`canceling` and GitHub's `CANCELLED` read failed before, and `merged_reads` settled a
merge commit's failure for good: GitLab's auto-cancel of a redundant pipeline, or a deploy
workflow's `cancel-in-progress`, woke the crown with "pipeline failed" and left a ✗ on the card
forever. `Pipeline::Cancelled` ranks between a pass and a run (a cancel beside a run reads
running; beside a pass, cancelled), so a `requires_pipeline` column refuses it ("pipeline
cancelled"), no edge fires on it, the card says `cancelled` under the hollow ring, and a GitLab
cancel names no job (every job of a cancelled pipeline is cancelled). A merge commit's `Failed`
or `Cancelled` is read again while its merge is under `SUPERSEDED_READ_MS` old and settles after,
so a main pipeline retried green reads passed; a pass still settles at once. Refuted: reading a
cancel as passed (nothing was judged) or as failed (that was the bug).

**GitHub's checks: `STALE` is no pass, and commit statuses count.** `gh_rollup`'s
`("COMPLETED", _, _)` arm read any completed run passed, `STALE` included (GitHub marks a run
left incomplete for 14 days stale). A pass is now `SUCCESS`, `NEUTRAL` or `SKIPPED` by name;
`STALE`, `CANCELLED` and a conclusion this build does not know read `cancelled`. A merge commit
read only `check-runs`, so CI that reports commit statuses (Jenkins, older CircleCI) read "no
pipeline ran": `commit_pipeline` also reads `commits/{sha}/status` and takes the worse of the two
(`forge::gh_commit_pipeline`); one of the two reads failing leaves the commit unknown, never the
other's green. One more call per unsettled merge commit per pass. An open PR's
`statusCheckRollup` already carried both.

**The rest.** A fork's leg matches a PR under every remote's path on its remote's host
(`forge::Remotes::paths`, `State::repo_paths`): `merged_at`, the fold, `pipeline_head_unread` and
the reflog binding, so a PR opened against the upstream lands the ticket. The upstream is not
*listed*: a stale `upstream` remote would fail every read and hold its tickets unread, so such a
PR reaches the set by the URL `pr create` printed. `remote_of` reads `git remote -v` (git's
`insteadOf` already applied) and resolves an SSH host through `ssh -G` (`~/.ssh/config`'s
`HostName`); `ssh.github.com` and `altssh.gitlab.com` are their forges; a host that could be an
option never reaches `ssh`. `doctor`'s forge line asks the CLI's `auth status` for that host and
warns where no account is signed in. "The newest merged PR of a repository" is by `mergedAt`/
`merged_at` (`Pr::merged_ms`, kept in `forge.json`; an older file's PR falls back to
`updated_ms`), never by `updated_at`, which a comment moves. A failing repository backs off
alone (`State::backing_off`); the minute reads the rest, and an error stays until that
repository is read again or no ticket reads it. A list that comes back full (`LIST_LIMIT`, 100)
and leaves out a PR the ticket held has that PR read by itself (`gh pr view`, GitLab's single
MR read), its last reading kept where the read fails; a list with room to spare that leaves one
out has said it is gone. A GitHub deployment counts where any of its statuses is `success`
(`statuses?per_page=100`): `auto_inactive` marks a superseded success `inactive`.

Tests: `forge::a_cancelled_or_stale_run_is_neither_green_nor_failed`,
`the_newest_merged_pr_is_the_last_to_merge_not_the_last_touched`,
`an_ssh_remote_names_the_host_ssh_would_reach`, the fork case in
`the_set_is_newest_first_without_the_abandoned`; the daemon's
`a_failed_merge_pipeline_is_read_again_while_young`, `a_pr_a_full_list_cut_off_is_read_by_itself`,
`a_forks_remotes_name_the_upstream_beside_origin`, `an_ssh_alias_resolves_through_ssh_config`,
the backoff in `the_state_is_due_on_its_cadence_and_backs_off_after_trouble`; `forge_e2e`'s
`a_pull_request_binds_pipelines_gate_and_the_forges_merge_lands` (a Jenkins status fails the
merge commit whose check runs passed, then a retry green reads passed). No rig test: the rig
has no forge, and `cancelled` is a new word in `get_ticket`'s `pipeline`, not new behaviour of an
agent's.

## T-799 — a PR merged with its head past the local tip lands the leg (2026-10-15, from T-795's bug hunt)

A reviewer commits a suggestion on GitHub, so the PR's head is one past the worktree's tip, and
the PR is squash-merged. The forge's fold landed a leg only where a merged head *was* the tip
(`merged_at`), the git road had no fetch or a squash whose patch-id is not the branch's, and the
ticket read unmerged for good: DONE refused `worktree unmerged`, `m` said the PRs carry the merge,
the crown heard `merged #42` and could not place the ticket. The way out was a `git pull` in the
worktree that nothing suggested.

**The rule.** A merged PR lands a leg's tip when its head is that tip **or carries it**
(`Pr::lands`). Carrying is asked only of a PR from the ticket's own branch (`head_ref` equal to
the binding's), merged, its head and the tip both full commit ids and different
(`forge::merged_past`), and only for a leg whose tip has left the commit it was cut at: every PR
descends from that one, so an untouched leg would read merged by any of them. A PR from another
branch still lands only at its head (T-786). A commit made after the merge is not carried, so it
reads unlanded as it did. Open PRs are T-780's `head_unread`, unchanged. A leg's PRs are the ones
naming any of its repository's paths (`LegQuery::repo_paths`, T-800), so a PR opened from a fork
against its upstream is asked too.

**How it is read**, on the forge pass's worker (`forge::landed_reads`), never the writer's: git
first, `merge-base --is-ancestor <tip> <head>` in the leg (`carries_here`), which answers exactly
where the head is here (a fetch brought it, or it was the worktree's own commit, as when the
worker committed after the merge) and exits 128 where it is not; `--no-optional-locks` and
`GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1`, so a partial clone never writes a pack for the missing head (promise 1).
Else the forge: GitHub's `pulls/:n/commits`, GitLab's merge request `commits`, through
`RepoQuery::api`, a page of 100 at a time up to GitHub's 250 (`pr_carries`); an answer that is not
a list is no answer. A tip the head carries goes on the PR (`landed_tips`), so `merged_at`, the
fold, `ticket_merged` and `forge_lands_all` read it with no change, and so does the crown's "who
says the merge" clause in `absorb_forge` (the flags say a merge they flip on).

**Asked once.** Each answer, yes or no, is kept per ticket by (repository, head, tip) in
`forge::State::landed` and rides the next query: both are commits, so the answer never changes. A
whole read replaces the ticket's answers with the ones it stood on (a tip the branch left drops
out), a partial read adds to them, and a failed call keeps none and is asked again. `landed_tips`
rides `forge.json` (`PrRecord`, skipped when empty, no schema bump: an older build drops it and
reads the ticket as it always did) and seeds the answers on restore, so a restart neither asks
again nor reads a landed ticket unmerged until the first pass, which would wake the crown with a
second landing.

Tests: `forge::a_merged_head_past_the_tip_lands_the_tip_it_carries` and
`a_prs_commits_read_off_either_forge_and_an_error_page_is_none` (core);
`forge::a_merged_head_past_the_tip_is_asked_of_git_then_once_of_the_forge` and
`a_carried_tip_round_trips_and_is_not_asked_again` (daemon); `forge_e2e`'s
`a_merged_pr_whose_head_carries_the_tip_lands_and_one_that_does_not_holds_done` — the card reads
`main (PR #43)`, `m` says already merged, DONE admits it, and a sibling whose head does not carry
its tip stays unmerged and refused; each PR's commits asked once. It times out on the old rule.

## A closed PR stays a ticket's (T-797, 2026-10-15, follow-up to T-778 and T-795)

**Why.** T-795's bug hunt: `forge::ticket_set` dropped every closed PR, so `has_pr` (T-778's
"open, merged or closed") never saw one. A ticket whose PR #42 the team closed unmerged had an
empty set, and the train fast-forwarded its branch into local main; `m` did too, and `get_ticket`
said the train or the crown merges it. If #42 was later reopened and merged, local main diverged
from origin, T-778's lab incident by another road. And the pipeline gate refused forever: the
ledger keeps the opened URL for good, so `opened_any` said `true` against an empty set and a
`requires_pipeline` column answered `pipeline not read` to every mover, a person's hand
included. The same forever-refusal held for a checkout ticket that ran `pr create` (no forge
query asks about a ticket with no branch) and for a PR on a host no CLI reads.

**Decided: a closed PR is the team's decision, and the merge stays the forge's.** The set keeps
closed PRs; `ticket_set` reads a closed PR's pipeline, conflict and review as none, so no fold,
edge or mark reads them. `has_pr`, the train's lane, `merge_by`, `crown_merge_refusal` and
`merge_ticket` see it: the train and `m` land nothing of a ticket whose PRs are all closed.
`forge::merge_refusal` says `PR #42 closed unmerged — reopen it on GitHub` (the newest closed
PR) where no PR is open or merged; with one merged, T-778's words stand. `get_ticket`'s merge is
`by: forge`, why `its pull requests were closed unmerged on the forge` (`forge::merge_why`). The
road back is reopening the PR on the forge; landing it locally stays git by hand, as T-778 left
it. Not chosen: basing `has_pr` on `State::held` (every PR ever bound), which would have needed
`held` in `forge.json` and left the card, the gates and the train reading two different sets.

**The pipeline gate.** A closed PR has no pipeline to pass: `forge::pipelined` (an open or a
merged PR in the set) decides whether the set is judged, so a set of closed PRs alone reads as
none bound, live or loaded. An opened-here URL now holds only while a read still owes it
(`Daemon::opened_unread`, `Ledger::opened_unread`): the ticket is one a forge read asks about (a
worktree binding with its branch, not tearing down), the URL's host is one the board's legs reach
(`forge_hosts`, or unknown while a leg's remote is unparsed) and its probe did not find no CLI
(`forge_reaches`), and, once read live, the ticket's reads never held its PR in any state
(`State::held_url`, by number and path in any case, or the same URL). Anything else falls back to
T-750's no-PR pass. The tail reader returns the URLs it finds (`urls_in_tails`) so a URL already
read is dropped there too. A ticket with a PR to judge is judged by its pipeline as before; the
transcripts are not read for it. `forge_query` now parses every ticket's leg remotes before it
judges any printed URL's host, so a URL on a host another ticket's leg reaches is listed
whatever order the tickets come in: the gate waits on exactly the hosts the query reads.

**What changed beside.** The `merged` edge (`Arrives here when: merged`) is one merged PR and
none open, so a closed PR beside a merged one waits for nothing. The feed's `closed #42` line in
`forge::delta`, unreachable while closed PRs left the set, now fires. A closed PR is `⊘` (ascii
`-`), grey whatever its pipeline was (`glyphs::pr_mark`), with no clauses past `closed` on the
page and in the `^h` list. The card's line (`App::card_prs`) leaves closed PRs out while one is
open or merged, and on a ticket whose PRs are all closed shows them with the word `closed`: there
it is why the board merges nothing. `forge.json` now holds closed PRs; no schema bump, since
`closed` was always a word the file's readers knew. A closed PR a full list cut off is read by
itself like any held PR (T-800's `unlisted`), so a ticket keeps it past a hundred newer PRs and
the train does not take the branch then.

**Tests.** Core: `the_set_is_newest_first_closed_included`,
`entry_needs_a_passed_pipeline_only_where_a_pr_is_or_was_opened` (a closed set alone enters, a
URL still owed holds it, an open one beside is judged), `a_printed_url_names_its_pr_by_number_and_path`,
and `an_open_pr_on_a_merged_ticket_holds_the_merge` for the closed words and `merge_why`.
Daemon: `a_closed_pr_stays_and_waits_for_nothing` (the feed line, the `merged` edge, `held_url`)
and the ledger's `a_pr_opened_in_the_unread_tail_is_seen_before_the_pass` with a read URL.
TUI: `a_closed_pr_is_on_the_card_only_where_every_pr_is_closed` and the glyph test. `forge_e2e`:
`a_ticket_whose_work_went_through_a_pr_is_never_the_trains` gains a ticket whose PR #43 closed
at its tip (off the train's list, `m` refused in the closed words, `get_ticket` by forge); with
`has_pr` blind to closed PRs it fails on the train's pending list.
`a_ticket_with_no_pull_request_enters_and_one_opened_here_waits` gains a worktree ticket whose
turn printed #44, read closed, entering a `requires_pipeline` REVIEW, and a checkout ticket whose
turn printed #45 entering it too; each fails with its fix taken out. Rig F9 (real Sonnet): a
crown asked to land a branch whose PR is closed reads `merge`, lands nothing and says it was
closed.

## A ticket's PRs are the ones its worktree wrote (T-796, 2026-10-15, follow-up to T-795)

**Why.** T-795's bug hunt left it open. `forge::binds`' "made here" matched any commit in a
worktree leg's HEAD reflog, and that reflog starts with the commit the worktree was cut at; a
rebase's start adds the upstream tip it rebased onto. Under GitLab's fast-forward merge method a
merged MR's head is the base's new tip, and T-779 cuts a new worktree at the fetched upstream, so
a ticket cut right after someone's ff merge bound that MR. Its card read ⎇✓ by the forge's fold,
`ticket_merged` agreed, the crown was woken `merged` for a worker that had done nothing,
`merge_by` said nobody, `get_ticket` listed the MR, and after the first commit `has_pr` kept the
train off the ticket and `m` refused it as the forge's. T-744's rig run saw the same with a stub
PR whose head was the base commit.

**The rule.** A commit is the ticket's when its worktree wrote it: a reflog entry binds only where
its move wrote the commit it moved to (`forge::wrote_commit` over `%gs`, `<action>[ (<step>)]:
<words>`). A commit of any kind, a merge commit, a cherry-pick, a revert, an `am` and a rebase's
pick, reword, squash, fixup or edit wrote one. The cut (`git worktree add` records no words, then
`reset: moving to HEAD`), a checkout or switch, a reset, every fast-forward (a merge's and a
pull's `Fast-forward`, a rebase's and a cherry-pick's `fast-forward`) and a rebase's start,
finish, abort and reset moved to a commit that already was. An action the rule does not name reads
as a commit, as every entry did before, so an unknown tool fails toward today's binding and never
loses one. The `commit` family binds whatever its message says: a commit titled "fast-forward…"
stays its author's. The unit test's table is the subjects git 2.54 wrote in a worktree for each of
those moves.

**Not the other road.** The ticket offered "the commits reachable from the base at the cut". It
reads the cut out but not a later upstream tip a pull or a reset brought in, and it needs the cut,
which is the `base_oid` T-740's `rebase_on_tip` moves. Any filter by ancestry from the base also
unbinds a ticket's own PR once the base took it, since the PR's head is then on the base. Only the
subject says how HEAD got to a commit: a ff-merged own head and a pulled foreign head both sit on
the base afterwards.

**The second guard.** `RepoFlags::fold_forge_merge` folds nothing into a leg whose tip is its
`base_oid`, and `ticket_merged`'s forge clause asks the same: a branch with no work lands nothing,
which is what the git road (`compute_flags`) already says of it. A PR from the ticket's own branch
at its cut (GitLab opens an empty MR) still binds by the branch and never reads the ticket merged.
T-799's `landed_reads` already skips a leg at its cut when it asks whether a merged head carries
the tip; this guard covers the head that is the cut itself. The written commits fill T-800's
per-leg facts beside the leg's fork paths, so a commit written in a fork's checkout still binds
the upstream's PR.

**Kept.** `pushed` (T-761's basis) still reads every reflog commit. A remote ref at the cut there
only owes a read where none was needed, which is safe, and narrowing it would change when a
turn's end reads the forge. A commit whose entry fell past the 2,000 newest still binds nothing,
as before.

**Tests.** Core `a_reflog_entry_wrote_its_commit_only_where_git_made_one` (the subjects table).
Daemon `a_worktree_wrote_its_commits_and_never_its_cut_or_its_rebases_base` (a real worktree:
cut, commit, a rebase onto a moved base, a reset, an ff merge) and an untouched leg in
`the_forge_names_a_merge_the_git_road_found_first`.
`forge_e2e::a_ticket_cut_at_a_fast_forward_merge_binds_nothing_of_it` on a glab stub: alpha's commit merged
fast-forward as !1 from `fix/alpha` (so only its reflog binds it) with `origin/main` taken there;
beta, cut at !1's head, binds nothing, reads unmerged, and `get_ticket` lists no PR and names no
forge or "nobody" merger; alpha keeps !1, landed as `main (MR !1)`; after beta's first commit
nothing binds and `m` fast-forwards main to it. It failed on the old code with beta holding !1.
USING.md says a commit the worktree started from or pulled in binds nothing.
## The pull requests dialog is a table as wide as its rows (T-805, 2026-10-15)

The `^h` dialog (T-759) was one sentence a PR in the 64-cell list every dialog keeps, so a
failing PR under review ended `changes req~`, the repository was cut to `o/r`, and the whole
sentence came only for the cursor's row, above the footer, on the marquee. The author picked
layout A of three proposed (a table; two lines a PR at 64; a list beside the cursor's details)
with the optional title and age.

**The table** (`ui/prs.rs::table`): one column per fact under dim headings, PR, REPO, TITLE,
STATE, PIPELINE, REVIEW, REACHED, UPDATED, aligned by spaces (no rule inside the frame, the L1
law). The dialog is as wide as its rows, up to the screen less the usual margins; this is the one
dialog past `dialog::MAX_W`, and never narrower than it. A column no row fills is dropped; REPO
is dropped when every PR is in one repository, and the title edge names it. STATE carries the
merge commit's seven characters and `, conflicts`; REVIEW now says `required`, which the wire
always carried and no surface drew.

**Nothing is cut; a row grows instead.** Past the room the title gives way to 32 cells, then the
columns of words (state, pipeline, review, environments) wrap inside themselves down to their
longest word, widest first (`squeeze`), then the title to 20. At 120 columns with two
repositories every such column wraps and a row is two or three lines; with one repository there
is room for the title. Below even that, each PR is a head line (the title wrapped under the
number) and its facts labelled and wrapped under it, at 64 (`stacked`). The row above the footer
is the cursor's link, what Enter opens and `c` copies, since the row itself is whole. The
list's scroll window is `dialog::window`, shared with `dialog::list`, over rows of any height.

**Title and age ride the wire.** `GH_FIELDS` (gh's list and view) asks for `title`, glab's MR JSON already
had it; `forge::Pr::title` is scrubbed at the parse (`str_of`), `PrRecord` keeps it in
`forge.json` (no schema bump: an absent title is no title, and an older build dropping it widens
nothing), and `PrItem` carries `title` and `updated_ms`. The TUI scrubs both again before drawing.
`get_ticket`'s `AgentPrView` is unchanged: an agent is told nothing new.

## A usage limit needs you, and the crown hears it (T-802, 2026-10-15, "quota issues doesn't read in mesimon as \"needs you\"")

**Seen.** Four workers on the author's board stopped on `You've reached your Fable limit. Run
/usage-credits to continue or switch models with /model.` The words sat under each card's title
and nothing else said so: no needs-you, no notification, and the crown that had started one of
them was never told. The feed shows why: the `StopFailure` came with class `rate_limit`, which
mapped to `Throttled` (rank 10, outside the attention set), and `Throttled` was built to wait for
Claude Code's quota auto-resume (`quota_auto_resume_fired` back to `Running`, `_stale` or
`_disabled` to `RequiresAction{QuotaResume}`). No such notice appears anywhere in the board's
feed, so the card waited, in grey, on an event that never came. Each one left only on a person's
prompt.

**Built.**
- `StopFailure{RateLimit}` enters `RequiresAction{QuotaResume}` (rank 6, the card's `QUOTA`,
  in the attention set): needs-you, the notification, and the limit's words kept as the detail.
  `Overloaded` stays `Throttled`; it is the server's and passes. A prompt leaves on the usual
  1.5 s settle, and a prompt that hits the limit again inside that settle is the same wait
  (no second notification). `docs/state-scenarios/rate-limit.json` now pins this, and
  `overloaded.json` keeps the throttle's 5 s leave.
- **It does not go stale while it is true.** The 15-minute stale clock would have taken QUOTA off
  the card (and its words with it) while the agent was still stopped. The recovery adapter restates
  it the way T-363 restates a held dialog: once a minute, while the transcript's last word is the
  limit's error row (`tail::api_error` with class `rate_limit`), it sends the same `StopFailure`,
  which re-arms the clock. A prompt that got through writes past the row, so a lost clearing frame
  still demotes.
- **The crown hears it.** `WakeCause::Limited`, `T-12 "…" hit a usage limit`, on the edge into
  QUOTA, whatever the crown mode, for a worker the crown started or a ticket it watches. A
  limit ends no turn, so without it a crown waits on a worker whose turn will never end. It ranks
  between an answer (the answer's turn is the one the limit cut) and a raised hand. crown.json stays
  schema 1, as with `Forge` and `Unstarted`. `CROWN_WAKES` tells the crown that `get_ticket`
  carries `needs_you: quota`, and that no word of the crown's resumes the worker: the person does.

**Kept.** A QUOTA agent is `is_working` as every `RequiresAction` is, so queued words, including the
crown's asks, wait instead of hitting the limit again, and the merge train's seat holds as it does
for a question. `sleep` still refuses it (only idle sessions sleep), as it refused `Throttled`.

**Tests.** `cargo ut`: the class routing and `a_usage_limit_holds_until_a_prompt_runs`
(attention), `a_usage_limit_is_restated_off_the_tail_while_it_is_the_last_word` (recovery),
`a_usage_limit_wakes_the_crown_on_its_edge` (crownwake), and the crown's words (mcp).
`crown_e2e::a_usage_limit_needs_you_and_wakes_the_crown_that_started_the_worker` on both roads.
The rig's L1 (new; rig step `limit` sends the `StopFailure` through the real hook binary, since
no account is made to hit a limit) on the real Sonnet (claude 2.1.300), 2026-10-15: PASS in 43 s,
wakes `finished` then `limited`. The crown, told nothing of what to do, sent the worker no words.

## The column dialog reads as a Settings page (T-806, 2026-10-15)

**What shipped.** The column settings dialog was twelve `Label: value` lines with no groups:
every value started where its label ended (cell 16 to 43), four vocabularies (`yes/no`,
`on/off`, `nothing`, `stay`) said one idea, and the `Agent behaviour` door sat mid-list looking
like a setting with its value missing. It now draws as a Settings page (T-717) does: a name
column, the value beside it through `settings::row_line` and `keymap::Value` (a switch is
`● on`/`○ off`, a short choice shows every option), and the rows under headings — LOOK, NEW
TICKETS, COMING IN, GOING OUT, FINISHED TICKETS, then the door alone with its `›` and what is
behind it (`mode auto ∙ tools full ∙ sleep off`). The agent page is LAUNCH (mode, Codex's two,
tools) and IDLE (sleep). A design was approved as an artifact before any code.

**Decisions.** The card's own moves on an agent's turn (`on_working`, `on_done`) left the agent
page for GOING OUT, right under COMING IN, at the author's ask: every way a card enters or leaves
the column is one screen, and the door keeps what is about the agent itself. Labels are names
alone and the heading carries the context (`Needs boxes ticked`, not `Entry needs every summary
box ticked`); `Sort now` is `Sort once`, an action kept under LOOK. `keymap::column_group` is
the section table and `column_value` the values, reached through `value` after the Settings
verbs. Option columns line up within a section, not across the dialog: across, the Workspace and
Offer choices collapsed to their chosen word. The dialog is 82 wide (`TABLE_W`), the Offer row
whole; at 120×30 the gap above the detail line is the first thing given up, and a shorter screen
windows the rows around the cursor as Settings does. The Name row (a new column, a rename) keeps
`draw_dense`: it stands alone, a field. The Description and `deployed to` fields take the
value's place, the name column saying which. Nothing on the wire or on disk changed.

**Tests.** `every_column_row_has_a_value_and_one_section` (no label spells its value, no section
split, GOING OUT beside COMING IN); `the_sort_row_owns_h_and_l` reads the new rows; the four
column goldens reminted and `golden_column_settings_60_scrolls_to_the_cursor` added.

## A stop on a usage limit is a turn that has ended (T-808, 2026-10-15, "agent stopped on a usage limit is considered running")

**Seen.** T-801's deep-tier worker hit the weekly Fable limit and sat `Throttled` (a record from
before T-802) for hours. The crown could neither park it (`sleep_agent`: "agent still awake — only
idle sessions sleep") nor move it to another tier (`^n` waits for an idle that never came), and
`start_agent` rightly refused a second agent on the held seat. Only a person's `x` freed it. T-802's
QUOTA had the same gaps, plus `is_working`, which read every `RequiresAction` as a turn in
progress: the train's seat, the shared checkout and `turns_open` stayed held by an agent sitting at
its composer.

**Decided: one predicate, not a new state.** `SessionState::stopped_on_limit()` (board.rs) is true
for `RequiresAction{QuotaResume}` and `Throttled`, and is the one place that says which states
those are. `sessions.json` is unchanged: no new variant, no schema bump, and an older build reads
every record as it did. A new `Idle{UsageLimit}` was refused because the attention set, the card's
QUOTA, the notifier and T-802's crown wake are all keyed on `RequiresAction{QuotaResume}`, and
an `Idle` in the attention set would have broken `is_attention`'s single rank table. `Throttled` is
in the set because it is what every limit read as before T-802, and an overload's stop has ended
its turn as well.

Who reads it:
- `quiet::is_working`: a stop on a limit is quiet, so the train, the shared checkout,
  `turns_open`, the crown's `pending_on` turn and `train::plan` all see a finished turn.
  `apply_change` now calls `turn_ended(_, false)` on the edge into QUOTA. That drops the turn's ask
  and settles a rebase hold, with no probe and no `finished` wake: `Limited` is the wake.
- `quiet::holds_against_words`: still true, by its own clause. Words would only meet the limit
  again, and a person resumes it. `session_takes_words` needed `Idle` anyway.
- `quiet::sleep_eligible`: an agent sleeps from it. That covers `z`, `x`, `sleep_agent` and
  the reclaim offer. `SessionRecord::autosleep_due` takes it too, so a column's `sleep_after_minutes`
  parks it (High confidence, as for any idle).
- `quiet::at_rest` (new): idle at the prompt or stopped on a limit, and not working. The daemon's
  `session_at_rest` reads it for the tier switch (`drain_tier_switches`, `relaunch_with` without
  plan, a tier-owed seat's queued ask and send) and the TUI's `^n` line reads it as well. A
  relaunch onto another tier is the way past the limit, and it carries any queued words there. A
  plan relaunch keeps `session_idle` (strict): it pastes the words on the same tier.
- `automove::delivers_in`: no turn in flight, so the card delivers where it sits. `automove`
  already fired nothing on `RequiresAction`, so no done move happens.

**The crown's words.** `CROWN_WAKES` now says the limit ended the worker's turn: `sleep_agent`
parks it with its conversation kept, and `start_agent` naming another tier then wakes it there.
Otherwise the person resumes it. `sleep_agent`'s description says "once idle or stopped on a
usage limit" (≤820 bytes kept).
