**Not done.** A `Throttled` record from a rate limit is not re-read as QUOTA. The recovery
restate reads only an attention record (`abort_only`). It is parkable and switchable, which is
what T-801 needed.

**Tests.** `cargo ut`: `a_stop_on_a_limit_is_a_turn_ended_that_holds_its_words` (quiet), the
StopFailure arms (attention), `a_usage_limit_is_not_done` and `delivers_in` (automove),
`autosleep_due` (board), and the crown's words (mcp). The T-802 crown_e2e goes on to a second
limit: the worker is not working but holds its words, does not move to REVIEW, is parked by
`sleep_agent`, and is woken by `start_agent` on a board tier `deep` with `--model opus` on its
argv. Rig L2 (new; the rig lays a second board tier `rig-alt`, check `tier:<name>`): the person
asks the crown to carry the limited worker on with rig-alt, without naming a tool. Run on the real
Sonnet (claude 2.1.300), 2026-10-15: L2 PASS in 45 s (the crown called `sleep_agent` and then
`start_agent` on rig-alt, and the worker resumed). L1 PASS beside it: told nothing, the crown still
sent the worker no words and did not park it, and the card stayed QUOTA.

## A deploy of a later commit deploys every merge it carries (T-801, 2026-10-15, forge lab run 4)

**What was wrong.** A PR read deployed to an environment only where a deployment's commit was
exactly its own merge commit (GitLab: one of the environment's last 20 successful deployments
naming the sha; GitHub: `deployments?sha=`), and the ticket arrived where each repository's
newest merged PR was (T-768). Batched deploys broke both: in lab run 4, !13 and !15 (forge-lab
T-19) merged with `deploy:production` manual and never run, production then ran !14's merge
commit `ddc16d7f`, which carries both, and T-19 stayed in STAGING for good.

**The rule** (`forge::deployed_after`). An environment holds a merge commit where its latest
successful deployment is that commit, or carries it: `merge-base --is-ancestor` on the forge
worker, in the repository's checkout, `--no-optional-locks` and `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH`
(`carries_here`, T-799's), writing nothing. Git's yes is deployed; git's no is not, a rollback or
a deploy of another branch; where git cannot say (either commit not here), the PR's own
deployment, seen in this read or held before, stands. A board that fetches nothing therefore
keeps a PR's own deployment as before, and the Settings row for fetch says so while it is off.
Git's answers are kept in memory by repository, merge and deployed commit (`State::carried`:
the minute's pass replaces them, a burst adds), never in `forge.json`; a restart asks git again.

**The read.** Per environment, once per repository per pass, not per merge commit
(`forge::environments`): GitLab's `deployments?environment=&status=success` page, the latest
being the one that *finished* last (`parse_gitlab_env`), since a manual job created with an older
pipeline runs after a newer one's; GitHub's `deployments?environment=` newest first, the first
whose statuses hold any success (T-800's `inactive` rule), at most 10 walked. A status read that
fails leaves the environment unread rather than an older deployment read as the latest, which
would read a merge it lacks as a rollback. Only environments a column names are read, as before.
GitHub's read sees only the latest commit, so a PR's own deploy superseded between two passes is
caught by ancestry alone.

**The ticket.** `arrived_envs` is every merged PR deployed there, none open (a closed one waits
for nothing). This replaces T-768's "each repository's newest merged PR", which took an older
merge being in the newer one's history on trust. On a board without fetch, a ticket with two
merged PRs now arrives only where each PR's own commit was deployed: the brief's choice, an
unknown history not being deployed by ancestry.

**Rollback.** A PR's `deployed` is the last read's word, not a sum: `State::deployed` and
`forge.json`'s `commits[].deployed` are replaced for every ticket a pass answered, an older
read never overwriting a newer one's. The card does not move back: `forge_arrivals` moves a
ticket forward on an edge, a lost environment is no edge, and a person moves the card. A
redeploy after a rollback is an edge again, said and arrived on again.

**What did not change.** A merge commit's pipeline reads as before: a waiting manual job is
`waiting on deploy:production !15`, and ancestry never invents a passed job. `SUPERSEDED_READ_MS`
now gates pipelines alone; every merged PR's deployments are judged on every pass a column asks
for one, since a batched deploy can come days after an old merge. No schema bump: `deployed`
keeps its shape. Refuted: inferring ancestry from merge order (T-768's trust), and fetching to
answer it (fetch stays the person's opt-in, promise 1).

Tests: `forge::an_environment_runs_the_deployment_that_finished_last`,
`a_merge_is_deployed_where_the_latest_deploy_is_it_or_carries_it` (exact, ancestor, not here,
seen, held, rollback, order); the daemon's `a_batched_deploy_brings_every_merged_pr_it_carries`
(the lab's !13 and !15, unfetched, half there, rollback and redeploy),
`each_merged_pr_keeps_its_own_pipeline_and_deployments`, `a_ticket_arrives_as_its_least_advanced_pr`;
`forge_e2e`'s `a_later_deploy_carrying_every_merged_mr_moves_the_ticket_to_prod` (glab stub:
production runs a commit carrying !13 alone, then !14's, then a rollback). No rig test: the
crown hears the same words as before (`deployed to production !13`) on new occasions, and the
rig has no forge.

## The crown's residue sits before the worktree mark (T-807, 2026-10-15)

A card the crown touched keeps a quiet crown mark until the cursor has rested on it (T-411's
`CrownMark::Residue`). The mark was drawn between the worktree mark and the age, so that card's
worktree glyph sat two cells left of every other card's. It is now drawn before the worktree
mark (`[fill][residue][wt][editor][age]`), and the title gives up the cells as it did before.
Test: `the_worktree_glyph_holds_one_column` gains the residue case.

## A relaunched agent at its composer is a free seat for the train (T-809, 2026-10-15)

Seen on T-801: its agent ended its turn in REVIEW, and 25 ms later a tier switch the person had
asked for with `^n` relaunched it on its conversation. The relaunch's `SessionStart` put it at
`Idle{Unknown}` High, and `train::seat` read every state but `Idle{EndTurn}` at High|Medium (the
2026-09-04 rule) as busy, so the train never planned the merge and the crown merged it by hand.
Every road that brings a live agent up on its conversation lands there: a tier switch, a wake
(`c`, `start_agent`), the mod road's relaunch on the hook set.

**The rule.** `train::seat` reads an agent at its composer as `Seat::Idle`
(`train::at_composer`): `Idle{EndTurn}` at High|Medium as before, or `Idle{Unknown}` at High
with no `unsent` launch words. The owed Enter (`pending_submit`) was already busy through
`quiet::is_working`. New: `seat` takes `words_owed`, from the daemon's `owed` ledger
(`Daemon::train_seat`, `Input::owed`). A ticket the daemon is pasting words to is busy at
any state, since a turn is about to start on them. That is what holds a brand-new spawn whose
brief is still waiting for its composer: it sits at `Idle{Unknown}` High from its own
`SessionStart` until the paste is acknowledged. It also holds an `Idle{EndTurn}` seat while a
queued ask is in flight to it, which the old rule let the train merge under. A restart's
re-derived `Idle{Unknown}` is Low and still holds (T-663).

**Refuted: carrying the ended turn's state across the relaunch.** Landing a tier switch's or a
wake's `SessionStart` at `Idle{EndTurn}` would reach far past the train. `on_done` and the
crown's delivered wake fire on the edge into `Idle{EndTurn}`, so every relaunch would deliver
again. And a wake from `Sleeping` has no ended-turn state left to carry.

**One answer.** `Seat::lets_merge` (`Empty | Idle`) is what `train::lane` merges past, and
`Daemon::merge_by` reads the same `train_seat`. A parked agent reads `by: crown`, "its agent is
parked, which the train leaves alone", since the train never merges past a parked seat. A busy
seat in the column it delivers in reads `by: train`, "the train is armed and reaches this column;
it waits for its agent's turn to end". A seat still working in another column keeps T-795's
words. T-795's `lane → Result<Lane, Skip>` was not taken: `merge_by` reads no worktree flags, so
the seat is the only clause the two had to share.

Tests: `train::a_relaunched_agent_at_its_composer_is_a_free_seat` (Unknown at High, Medium and
Low, with `unsent`, with `pending_submit`, with words owed, an end of turn with words owed);
`merge_train_e2e::a_relaunched_agent_at_its_composer_does_not_hold_the_train` (a delivered
REVIEW ticket relaunched by a tier switch: armed while it is still starting, nothing merges and
`get_ticket` says the train waits; its `SessionStart{resume}` lands it at `Idle{Unknown}` and the
train merges it. It fails with the `Idle{Unknown}` arm removed). No rig test: no rig step holds a
worker busy in REVIEW or parks one before the train lands it, and the crown's tool text is
unchanged.

## The snapshot leaves an archived ticket's parked records out (T-804, 2026-10-15)

The author's board stalled on every push. It had 674 tickets, 648 of them archived, and 629
session records, 614 of them parked records of archived tickets: 1.52 MB per snapshot, 1.02 MB
of it those records, which nothing on the board draws. The TUI fetches the snapshot on its UI
thread after every `BoardChanged` (~14 a minute with one agent working) and after every
mutating key, and the daemon serializes it on the writer thread. Measured on the dogfood debug
build: a round-trip of 98–161 ms at p50 and 380–730 ms at p90 (822 ms max), against 0.3 ms for
`gate_status`; offline, the debug build parses those 1.5 MB in 26–72 ms and serializes them in
33–156 ms (release: 3–24 ms and 1.5–7 ms). Build load on the machine stretches all of it past a
second.

**Now:** `Daemon::snapshot` calls `Board::drop_archived_records`: a record with no pane on an
archived ticket (a snooze included) stays off the wire; one with a pane always rides. The new
read `Command::TicketSessions { ticket }` → `Response::Sessions` returns one ticket's records,
decorated as the snapshot's are (`Daemon::decorate`). The TUI asks it for the archived ticket on
screen: the ticket page, or the picker's preview (`App::shown_archived`, `App::poll_held` in
`pump`), once when it comes on screen and again after each snapshot, and `absorb` lays the held
records into every board meanwhile (`App::lay_held`), so the rail and the preview never draw
empty for a frame. Closing the page drops them. An older daemon answers an unknown command, and
its snapshot still carries every record. On the author's board the snapshot drops to ~0.5 MB.

**Refuted:** dropping `argv` from the snapshot's records (proposed beside this). After the cut it
is 11 KB, and ~80 e2e assertions read a live record's launch flags off the snapshot.

**Not done:** the archived tickets themselves are ~420 KB of what remains (their `notes`
metadata 160 KB), and the fetch still blocks the UI thread; that move is its own ticket.

## A board merges into main or through pull requests, never both (T-810, 2026-10-15, the author: "Worktree merge to main and PR are two different workflows I don't believe people would mix. Is the train responsible for the PRs workflow or is the train specifically to merge to main?")

**Why.** The forge integration (T-739 onward) never shipped, and it mixed the two workflows
ticket by ticket: a ticket with a PR bound merged on the forge, one without was fast-forwarded
into main by the train. Mixing is what made the train wait for a forge read after every turn
that pushed (`forge_fresh`, T-752/T-761): it could not otherwise rule out a PR. A board where
`gh` was signed in but nobody opened PRs held its train while GitHub was unreachable (T-795).
The author chose a per-board workflow over a plain forge on/off, which supersedes the
"Pull requests: auto / off" switch T-795's crown proposed.

**The setting.** `Board::merge_into` (`MergeInto::Main | PullRequests`), `#[serde(default)]`
main, a scalar in `columns.toml` beside `crown_mode`, no schema bump (a build before it reads
every board's forge, which widens nothing an agent or a spawn gets). `Command::SetMergeInto`,
local only (`agent_allows`: who merges is the team's workflow). Settings › Behaviour › Merge
into, under its own `MERGE` heading above the fetch row; board state like Agent tools, so no
`PrefKey`. `doctor` prints `merge into` beside `merge base`. No migration: the author's
forge-lab boards switch by hand.

**Main is the board before T-739.** `Daemon::through_prs` is the first question of every road
to the forge: the minute's pass, the turn's end's burst, the busy cadence and a turn's look
(`look_legs`) ask nothing; a read that lands after a switch is dropped; `forge.json` is not
loaded at start and not written (`persist_forge`). Switching to main drops `forge::State`
whole (the cards, the gates, the train and `get_ticket` read no PR) and leaves the file as it
was; switching to pull requests loads it back and the next tick reads. `doctor` asks no CLI
either. The PR-only rows say why they are inert (`keymap::PRS_INERT`: Pull requests on cards,
Moves in when, Needs passed pipeline), and `pipeline_refusal` passes every ticket.

**The train reads the mode, and `forge_fresh` is gone.** `train::Reading::merge_into`. Into
main: the merge and rebase lanes as before T-739, `has_pr` unread. Through pull requests: no
merge lane, and the rebase lane is the PR conflict alone (T-770's once per conflict). Neither
mode needs the forge's freshness: main reads nothing, and a pull-requests train makes no merge
a read could have to rule out, so `WtFlags::forge_fresh` and `learn_remotes` (which existed to
learn freshness early) are deleted. The turn's end's read stays for what else waits on it: the
crown's wake (T-773) and the cards.

**Decided: a branch with no PR yet, behind its local base, is asked nothing** on a
pull-requests board. The base its PR will target is the forge's; the forge says whether the PR
conflicts once it is open, and the train asks then. Asking on the local base would spend a turn
the forge may never need, and would bring `forge_fresh` back (the train would have to rule out a
PR the turn just opened, T-739's very wait).

**Who merges.** `merge_by` says `forge` for every worktree ticket of a pull-requests board,
whatever the crown's mode and the train: the bound set's why where there is one (T-778, T-797),
else `this board merges through pull requests`. `merge_ticket` (`m`, the crown, the train)
refuses every worktree branch there, after the merged check, in `Daemon::prs_refusal`: the set's
sentence, else `forge::open_one_refusal` (`this board merges through pull requests — open a PR
from its branch and merge it on GitHub`; `an MR … GitLab`, the forge the root leg's host was
probed to be; `GitHub or GitLab` before any probe). `crown_merge_refusal` says it with the key in
front. The DONE gate still admits a branch the forge merged (`ticket_merged`'s forge clause).
Shared-checkout tickets are unchanged under either mode (T-797).

**Decided: the upstream counting follows pull requests only** (T-779's cut, T-786's count,
T-787's fetch words). On a board that merges into main the train lands a branch in the local
main, so that is where a branch starts and what it is counted against: a branch cut at a
fetched `origin/main` ahead of local main would carry the upstream's commits into the person's
main on its fast-forward, and counting against the upstream would understate what that lands.
`worktree::provision` and `provision_workspace` take `upstream` (the daemon's `through_prs`);
the flag queries set `RepoQuery::forge` only under pull requests, and the fetch words follow
`counted`. `doctor`'s cut words print only there.

**The crown.** `CROWN_WAKES`: the forge's merge is every worktree ticket's on a board whose
Merge into is pull requests, and nothing is the forge's on one that merges into main. Rig M1
(`ci/rig/tests.toml`, new check `crown_line:<prefix>:<word>`, new step `prs_board`): one crown,
asked who merges a delivered ticket under each mode, naming no tool. On the real Sonnet,
2026-10-15, PASS: `M1 main: the crown merges it, because the train is off.` and `M1 prs: the
forge merges it, because this board merges through pull requests.` The first run answered right
and failed a `!forge` check (`… so the forge does not merge it`), which was dropped; the second
put each answer under its prefix line, which the check now reads to the reply's end. Every
`forge_*` rig step that starts the stub sets pull requests, and `forge_off` sets main back;
F7 passed on that change.

**Tests.** Core: `train::a_board_merges_into_main_or_through_pull_requests_never_both`,
`a_board_through_pull_requests_is_never_the_trains_to_merge` (T-778's, on the mode), the T-770
test under pull requests, `board::merge_into_defaults_main_and_pull_requests_is_kept`,
`keymap::pull_request_rows_are_inert_on_a_board_that_merges_into_main`, `open_one_refusal` in
the T-774 forge test. Daemon: `store::merge_into_is_main_unless_the_file_says_pull_requests`, the
T-779 cut test (a main board cuts at the local base). TUI:
`merge_into_setting_toggles_through_board_command`; goldens `settings_behaviour_*` reminted (the
`MERGE` row). `forge_e2e`: every test sets pull requests but
`a_board_that_merges_into_main_never_calls_the_forge` (`gh` signed in on a github.com remote, the
train merges a turn that pushed, the stub's log stays empty, no `forge.json`; pull requests then
starts the reads), which replaces T-761's two freshness tests and T-795's
`a_failed_read_after_a_push_holds_the_train` (nothing left to hold); T-778's test now shows a
no-PR ticket off the train with `m` asking for a PR, and T-796's `m` asks beta for an MR.
`crown_e2e::the_crown_merges_where_the_train_will_not` reads `forge` and a refused
`merge_ticket` under pull requests before the crown's merge. `worktree_e2e`'s T-779 test sets
pull requests, and under main a second ticket cuts at local main while the first counts 5 ahead
of it.

**Kept.** The cost ledger still notes a `pr create` URL in a transcript under either mode (local
reading, no forge call); Mesophon reads the snapshot's empty `prs` under main.

**Addendum: the backfill** (the author: "Add to backfill but it should be in background and not
cause hiccups"). The cost ledger's cursor never goes back, so a `pr create` a session ran before
T-739 looked for one is in no `pr_urls`, and a PR it opened from another branch binds to nothing.
`cost::Cursor::backfilled` marks a transcript every `pr create` of which is in its ticket's URLs: a
transcript learned from now on is born marked (the pass reads it from its start, a subagent's and a
rewritten one's too), and a pass that ran beside a backfill keeps the mark (`apply`). On a board
that merges through pull requests, at the switch and at start, `Daemon::queue_backfill` sends the
worktree tickets' unmarked transcripts to a worker (`cost::backfill`: one at a time, `read_until`
line by line, `forge::pr_create_line` only on a line that can hold one), which lands as one
`Msg::Backfilled`; `Ledger::apply_backfill` marks each and keeps each new URL as the oldest of its
ticket's, never past `PR_URLS_CAP` and never pushing a newer one out, with no cursor or count
moved. Once marked, a board switched back and forth reads nothing again. **No noise:** each URL
the backfill added waits in `forge::State::quiet`, and the read that first finds its PR takes it as
held and as the last read's too (`State::baseline`): no `delta` line, no opening, no edge, so no
crown wake and no arrival. **Left open:** a backfilled PR merged at the leg's tip can still flip the
flags' `merged`, whose own wake is the flags' road, not the forge's. Tests:
`cost::the_backfill_finds_the_pr_creates_a_passed_cursor_never_read` (Claude's escaped and block
results, Codex's output, a last line with no newline, the oldest-first keep, once, a pass beside
it), `forge::a_backfilled_url_binds_its_pr_as_a_baseline_once`,
`forge_e2e::a_pr_opened_before_the_ledger_looked_binds_quietly_after_the_backfill` (a crowned
worker's set read empty and kept, `costs.json` set back to a pre-T-739 cursor across a restart,
the PR listed from then on: it binds with no feed line, no `forge` wake and TODO's `Moves in when:
PR opened` taking nothing; with `baseline` turned off the crown is woken).

**Addendum 2: a forge nobody can read is trouble, never silence** (the author: "if pr workflow
fails for some reason (glab needs login or something else), will the board let the user know?").
T-798 kept a failed sign-in only for a host that had a CLI or held PRs, and a host with no CLI on
PATH read as no forge, said by nothing. On a board that merges through pull requests, the only
one that probes, every worktree's host is one the person means read: `take_probe` keeps every
failed sign-in, and the writer records a host with no candidate CLI as lost too, both in words
with their fix (`forge::sign_in_trouble`: `github.com sign-in: <the CLI's words> (gh auth login
--hostname github.com)`; `forge::missing_trouble`: `gitlab.com: no glab or gh on PATH (install
glab, then glab auth login --hostname gitlab.com)`), asked again on the backoff. The advisory row
says `pull requests not read — <that line>` (`forge_unreachable`, only under pull requests; the
"merge train holds its tickets" clause went, since that train merges nothing), `doctor`'s forge
line warns in the same words, and `ForgeStatus.trouble` on the snapshot carries the line for the
header mark a later ticket adds. The words cannot tell a host never signed in from one offline,
so the fix is offered either way. A repository with no forge remote at all is still no forge.
Tests: `forge::a_host_nothing_reads_is_trouble_never_no_forge` (replaces T-798's
`a_failed_sign_in_is_lost_where_the_host_had_a_cli_or_holds_prs`) and
`forge_e2e::a_cli_never_signed_in_is_trouble_with_its_fix` (`auth status` failing from the start:
silent under main, then the advisory row and `forge.trouble` name the host and the fix).

## The board's top row names its workflow and lights when it acts (T-811, 2026-10-15, the author: "we also need some indication on top of the board of the workflow currently in power (pr workflow / merge train), and have that light up when anything related to it happens. Like remote control")

**Reverses the 2026-09-04 silence.** The board header had no train word since a day of ` ∙ train`
and an hour of ` ∙ auto-merge` (the train touched only attached worktree tickets, so a board-wide
clause claimed too much). T-810 made the workflow the board's — main or pull requests, never both
— and the author asked for it named. `chrome.rs::workflow_mark`, after the awake and Remote
Control marks, **on the board alone** (Remote Control's mark rides every screen; the workflow is
the board's own fact, and its light on a ticket page would be noise): ` ∙ train` on a main board
while the train is armed (`AutomationStatus.merge_train`), nothing with it off; ` ∙ pull requests`
on a pull-request board whatever the train; ` ∙ pull requests offline` while `ForgeStatus.trouble`
holds (T-810's addendum 2), the advisory row keeping the sentence and the fix. A row too tight for
the whole word (the 60-cell minimum with a long repo name) says `PRs` / `PRs offline`, swapped
whole once everything but the offer and the git clause is placed: those two give way first.

**A chip** (`HeaderChip::Workflow`, last in `ALL`): `h`/`l` reach it from Remote Control's, Enter
and a second click open Settings at the Merge into row (`return_to_settings(Verb::MergeInto)`),
and `settle_header` hands the cursor back when it goes. The mouse target and the T-681 step-down
spot ride the header's `cells` like the others; the ` ∙ ` is the gap, not the chip.

**The light.** Two stamps on the snapshot, memory only in the daemon (a restart lights nothing):
`AutomationStatus.acted_at_ms`, set in `train_pass` on a merge, a new refusal it holds and a rebase
ask delivered (a fuse trips on that ask, so it is covered); and `ForgeStatus.acted_at_ms`, set in
`absorb_forge` when a read finds an `Edge` on any ticket or a first read's opening, which also
broadcasts. The TUI lights the word for `theme::WORKFLOW_LIT_MS` (4 s) on its injected clock
(`App::workflow_lit`): the train's stamp on either board (under pull requests it asks a conflict's
rebase), the forge's on a pull-request board only. Grey ramp: `dim2` at rest, `dim3` offline,
`base` lit; `attn` stays needs-you's. It is not `animating()`: the board's 100 ms frames carry it.

Tests: `keymap::header_workflow_chip_is_the_last_and_opens_merge_into`,
`app::workflow_chip_opens_merge_into_and_leaves_with_the_train`, `ui::golden_workflow_mark_120`
(train, pull requests, offline goldens), `ui::golden_workflow_mark_focused_120`,
`ui::workflow_mark_shortens_on_a_tight_row`, `ui::workflow_mark_lights_after_an_act_and_settles`
(every flavour), `ui::a_click_on_the_workflow_mark_opens_merge_into`; the three `train_*` goldens
now carry ` ∙ train`. `merge_train_e2e::the_train_merges_asks_to_rebase_once_and_stops_with_its_board`
reads the stamp after the merge, `forge_e2e::the_crown_hears_the_forges_edges` after the opening and
the pipeline's pass.

## A bounded native Codex rig beside the Claude crown rig (T-815, 2026-10-16)

`ci/rig.py --provider codex --live` runs real Codex through the production daemon,
sequentially, in supervised disposable boards. `--lay` lists the selection without
starting anything; `--only` selects cases and `--failed` includes inconclusive and
unattempted cases. The Claude crown/worker rig keeps its existing board and road.
Codex prints each board's external-terminal watch command and retains verdicts,
snapshots and native evidence under `target/rig/codex`, then reaps the fixture.
It does not leave a persistent board or use Claude's stale-board sweep.

The smoke cases are completion/automove, scoped MCP, additive brief/exact wake,
queued prompt ordering, sleep/resume across a provider switch, and daemon handover.
Extended cases reuse the native gate, plan, interruption, child and lifecycle
checks. A Codex question or plan remains the person's: the runner exercises native
dialogs, not unsupported crown dialog automation. This is a provider-specific
adapter over the existing native fixtures, not a translation of Claude mod checks.

Every case checks authenticated, paginated `model/list` before any scenario turn;
the exact selected model and effort must be advertised and later appear in native
turn contexts. The default is `gpt-6-luna`, low effort, with no model fallback.
MCP/brief fixtures offer read-only board tools. Other than the explicit child
case, model-created children are disabled. Turn allowances include the child,
Stop continuation and compaction where requested; observed total tokens include
cached input. Per-case deadlines and the bounded runner own cancellation. Native
usage is delayed and may omit overhead, so the stop threshold is not a hard
token or dollar cap. A failure stops subsequent cases; cleanup and missing
evidence never become a pass. Reports preserve each run separately.

Codex 0.163.0 changed the folder-trust and hooks-review screens used by the old
0.153.4 fixtures. The driver now recognizes their current labels, still verifying
the isolated configuration, repository and exact allowed hook definitions before
trusting them. These are fixture changes, not changes to production trust policy.
The historical compatibility manifest remains version-scoped; a new smoke run
does not certify every entry of the old acceptance matrix for a new CLI.

The native runs also caught two fixture assumptions: entering `/plan` chose
medium effort despite the ordinary low-effort setting, and child creation now
uses discovered native spawn tools and `subAgentActivity` records. The fixture
pins `plan_mode_reasoning_effort` and child defaults separately. A modern child
identity is correlated with its actual completed spawn result in owned native
history; a `started` activity alone does not certify a completed spawn. The
live-child checkout-hold assertion remains required. Interruption waits for
native model activity before cancelling, so its model/usage audit is meaningful.

Runner usage and the case matrix are in `ci/rig/README.md`; offline budget,
selection, history containment and trust checks are in `ci/codex_rig_test.py`.

Validation on Codex CLI 0.163.0 with `gpt-6-luna` at low effort passed all fourteen
native cases across focused runs, each with clean fixture teardown. The six
successful smoke cases recorded 220984 total tokens including cached input;
that is observed usage, not a price estimate or the total spent on failed fixture
development attempts. Earlier failed and inconclusive captures remain retained,
not relabelled as passes. All 35 Python harness tests passed, including the 15
new offline rig tests. `cargo ut` passed after removing the CLI environment's
inherited `NO_COLOR`, which otherwise suppresses escape sequences required by an
existing underline-colour assertion; no rendering code changed.

The one full-workspace nextest run stopped at an unrelated worktree-init timing
assertion (`failed ∙ exit 2 ∙ 1 s` versus the test's exact `0 s`): 697 passed,
one failed, three intentionally skipped, and 1787 not run after fail-fast. Its
fixture audit was clean; the unchanged `worktree_init_e2e` binary passed alone
with clean teardown. This is not recorded as a passing full-suite run. The three
skips are the timing benchmark, the live-release network check, and a subprocess
helper exercised by the restart-skew tests.

The mod-road integration pass that fail-fast prevented was run separately under
`MESIMON_TEST_ROAD=mod`: all 208 tests passed, with only that subprocess helper
skipped as a standalone test, and a clean fixture audit. Python syntax checks,
the existing six offline native-driver self-tests, and `git diff --check` passed.
Linux and manual TUI checks were not run for this Python-only harness change.

## A card's move plays out, and a card's dialog hangs from its card (T-817, 2026-10-16, the author: "when cards move it's instant and can be missed easily by the user" and "when opening card dialog using ^hjk it's hard to know which card was this opened from")

Proposed as a live simulation first and shaped by the author's answers: no landing light (it
"can be misread as cursor moved to the card"), no gutter dot, no arc ("too aggressive"), and no
italic, which SGR 3's ban kept off the board anyway.

**A move plays (`glide.rs`).** `App::absorb` diffs the snapshot against the board it replaces:
a ticket on the board in both, in another column, both columns drawn, is a move. It plays unless
this board sent it (`req` stamps every `MoveTicket` in `own_moves` for `OWN_MOVE_MS`, 10 s: the
cursor rode it), unless the crown did (its `moved` touch keeps the T-544 bolt), and only with
**Settings › Appearance › Card moves** on (`Prefs::card_moves`, machine-only like the lightning,
on by default). Three phases along the direction of travel, 1.5 s in all: **out** (450 ms) — the
card fades along the move, left to right for a move right, down to a ghost that keeps 30 % of
its ink; **trail** (600 ms) — a grey braille stretch, 40 % of the path, travels from the ghost to
the new slot in straight runs through the gaps alone (`glide::route`: out of the card's end into
the gutter beside its column, along the gutter, along the empty row under the headers when a
column lies between, down the target column's gutter, in); **in** (450 ms) — the card fades in
along the move, its slot held blank until then. The ghost is the T-544 trail's place
(`App::gliding_out`, `Place::Glide`) drawn as the card itself, since the fade does the dimming.
Several in one snapshot start `STAGGER_MS` (150) apart, at most `MAX_PLAYED` (4); the rest are
simply where they went. The trail is braille, so the ascii tier plays the fades alone.

**Then it shimmers until seen.** `unseen_moves` keeps each played card and its landing; the row
wears the pipeline's crest and clock (`theme::shimmer_crest`, T-794's numbers, shared) until a
keypress leaves the cursor on it (`ack_woke`, the crown residue's rule). A card the cursor rode
is seen at once. **A shade, not a lift**: the preview lifted grey toward white, but a resting
title is already the ramp's top (graphite's E9E7E1 has nowhere to go), so `Theme::move_shimmer`
takes the crest's letters 55 % toward the ground and back. A card whose pipeline words already
shimmer does not shimmer twice. Grey on grey; `attn` stays needs-you's.

**A card's dialog hangs from its card.** `App::dialog_card` names the card a board dialog is
about — links (`^k`), summary (`^j`), pull requests (`^h`), the merge dialog — on the board alone.
That card is drawn selected under its dialog (it collapsed before, the cards under it jumping
up), the board records its whole rect (`Spots::about`), and `dialog::placed` hangs the dialog one
row under it, centred on it and kept on the screen, or over it when it sits low, or centred when
neither fits. `dialog::notch` turns the edge cell nearest the card's middle into `┴` (`┬` from
above, `+` ascii) — a frame cell on the recorded perimeter, which `test_no_drawn_structure` now
sweeps. `board::recede` takes every other cell of the columns (not the header row) to 40 % of
its colour toward the ground (`Theme::recede`; mono has no step and keeps its own).

Tests: `glide::tests` (the front, the route through the gaps, the travelling stretch, a trail that
never covers a letter or a painted cell, the ghost's life),
`app::a_move_from_elsewhere_plays_and_shimmers_until_seen`,
`app::own_moves_reorders_renames_and_the_switch_do_not_play`,
`app::a_burst_of_moves_staggers_and_is_capped`,
`ui::a_moved_card_leaves_a_ghost_and_a_trail_in_the_gutter`, `ui::an_unseen_moved_card_shimmers`,
`ui::the_board_recedes_behind_a_cards_dialog`, `prefs::card_moves_default_on_and_round_trip`; the
links, summary and picture-link goldens hang from T-3 now, and the Appearance goldens carry the
row.

## Codex tickets have an API-price estimate in the dollar view (T-815, 2026-10-16)

The ledger already counted Codex rollout tokens, but the price table contained
only Claude models, and a card with no priced tokens left its `$` corner blank.
Verified OpenAI model rates now price GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 Sol, GPT-6
Luna, and GPT-5.6 Sol/Terra/Luna. Exact model IDs and dated snapshots match;
unverified aliases, Spark and unknown model variants remain unpriced instead of
inheriting a different model's rate. An unpriced card now says `unpriced`, matching
the Usage dialog, rather than silently disappearing from the cost view. A ticket
with nothing counted still has a blank cost corner.

Rates are standard, short-context API USD per million tokens, verified on
2026-10-16 against [OpenAI's pricing table](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing)
and the model pages for
[GPT-6 Sol](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-6-sol),
[GPT-5.6 Sol](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.6-sol),
[GPT-5.6 Terra](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.6-terra) and
[GPT-5.6 Luna](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.6-luna).
GPT-6.1 Sol's cached-input rate differs from GPT-6 Sol's; they are separate entries.
Codex's cached input is subtracted from input before pricing, and reasoning tokens
are already part of output, so neither is charged twice. OpenAI's single cache-write
rate is shared by the ledger's two write-lifetime fields; Codex's existing rollout
reader does not infer cache writes absent from its token counters.

This remains a standard-rate estimate, not a subscription bill or an exact API
invoice: hourly totals cannot reconstruct request-level long-context thresholds,
service-tier changes or regional surcharges. The stored token buckets are priced
when the snapshot is built, so existing histories gain estimates without a schema
change, migration or another model call after the rebuilt daemon is handed over.
Regression tests cover verified rates, unknown variants, cached-input arithmetic,
ledger growth and the `$` card/ticket views. The cost-corner golden deliberately
adds the `unpriced` label; no other layout is intended to change.

Validation: focused core/ledger checks, `cargo ut`, the full TUI suite (1028
passed, one existing ignored test), formatting and the rebuilt binary passed;
the single changed golden was inspected. The bounded four-worker workspace run
passed all 2488 tests with three intentional skips. Its automatic mod-road pass
ran all 208 tests: 207 passed and the unchanged worktree-init elapsed-time
assertion again observed `1 s` where it requires `0 s`; its standalone subprocess
helper was skipped. The cost integration tests passed on both roads and fixture
cleanup was clean. This does not fix or claim a pass for that unrelated timing
assertion. Linux, manual TUI and paid model runs were not repeated for this
pricing/rendering change.

## Integration checks observe outcomes, not scheduler speed (T-815, 2026-10-16)

The pre-merge workspace run exposed an existing worktree-init assertion that
required a failing shell to finish in less than half a second (`0 s` after
rounding). Under suite load the same exit-2 result correctly reported `1 s`.
The integration test now parses the single init feed row for each ticket,
checks its exact success/failure/timeout status and whole-second duration,
and requires the journal and agent's ticket view to report that same outcome.
The 1500 ms timeout still requires at least two rounded seconds, but not exactly
two; the existing core unit test checks deterministic duration formatting.
Script ordering, exit codes, timeout reporting and agent startup remain checked.
No production timing or timeout policy changes.

The rebased full suite also caught the restart board-tool test taking a snapshot
before its prompt hook reached the daemon's state writer. Hook subprocess exit
is not an acknowledgement that the state transition has been applied. Both
remaining immediate pre-restart checks now use the existing bounded `await_state`
helper, like the other restart scenarios. The post-restart unknown-state and
board-call recovery assertions stay unchanged; no production ordering changes.

The mod-road rerun then caught a permission-hold plugin test calling its initial
no-op `release` after a fixed 20 ms sleep, before the mocked approve process had
installed the actual resolver. It now awaits an explicit start signal from that
mock before releasing it. The pending-dialog and final personal-decision checks
are unchanged; neither the plugin nor its permission behavior changes.

Validation after rebasing onto main: `cargo ut`, `cargo build --workspace`,
formatting and `git diff --check` passed, as did the focused init, restart and
plugin tests. The final bounded six-worker workspace run passed all 2500 tests;
its mod-road pass passed all 208 integrations, with a clean 411-owner fixture
audit. The existing live-network check, timing benchmark and subprocess helper
remain intentionally skipped (the helper is exercised by its parent tests).
One earlier default-concurrency run timed out waiting for the provider test's
provisioning hook. It passed five isolated repetitions and both final suite
passes without a code change; that timeout was not reproduced or claimed fixed.
Linux, manual TUI and paid-agent runs were not repeated for these test-only fixes.

## Remote Control follows Codex's continued rollout (T-815, 2026-10-16)

Codex 0.163.0 was observed continuing the same thread in a new native rollout:
the selected thread's original file held startup context, while a later
`rollout-…-<thread>_<segment>.jsonl` held the conversation. The session record
still named the original file, so Remote Control read an empty or stale chat.

The transcript worker now resolves a newer native rollout before reading its
page. Discovery stays bounded at the existing native sessions depth and entry,
file and byte limits; candidate filenames narrow the read, but matching metadata
identity and working directory decide whether the file belongs to this history.
The shared directory walk skips symlinks. Unknown or unreadable histories retain
the original path. No conversation is modified, and history remains display
evidence, never authority for an agent's state or checkout ownership.

The page's conversation token names the resolved file, so a changed rollout
resets the browser's tail cursor rather than applying an old byte offset to it.
The same reader supplies the offline shelf. Codex's shelf pages are checked on
each scheduled shelf build and keyed by the resulting page, so rotation is
noticed even when the original file is unchanged, without resending identical
pages. Claude's metadata cache, the wire format and authorization stay unchanged;
no browser or relay deployment is needed. The rebuilt host daemon needs its
normal handover before the new reader is in use.

Regression tests cover cross-day rotation, matching metadata, unrelated files,
incremental and older pages, cursor resets, unchanged native files and stable
shelf keys. A shelf key also includes the agent session, so replacing the session
refreshes its copy even when the conversation's page is identical.

Validation: the three focused regressions, `cargo ut`, workspace build, daemon
Clippy with warnings denied, formatting and `git diff --check` passed. The final
bounded six-worker run passed 2503 workspace tests and all 208 mod-road tests;
fixture cleanup was clean for all 411 owners. The existing live-network check,
timing benchmark and subprocess helper remain intentionally skipped. An earlier
verification run was deliberately stopped for the shelf-key correction, not
counted as a pass; its retained `runner-lost` owner had no fixture sockets or
repositories, and its processes and temporary directory were confirmed gone.
Linux, live-phone and paid-model checks were not repeated for this read-only host
change; live-phone verification awaits the rebuilt daemon's normal handover.

## Setup asks a new board how its person works (T-816, 2026-10-16, the author: "quick-start first time opening mesimon ∙ ask important questions, let to skip. propose first with an artifact ∙ auto accept the system prompt ∙ worktree default by default, remove the board default")

**Proposed first, as a clickable simulation, three rounds.** The first draft's questions were
mesimon's own words (train, worktree, forge) and its previews were prose; the author asked for
plain questions ("how do you usually work?"), the technical choice as a follow-up step of the
plain answer, and a preview that is the board and grows with the answers rather than changing
under them. The author's answers: the brief on for new boards with promise 3 reworded; a
multi-repository folder asks, worktree preselected; three templates; no re-run from the menu
(Settings is the way back); named Setup, since the tour already has a Quick start lesson; and no
"Nothing" for an agent's tools, which breaks mesimon.

**When.** `Board::setup_pending`, set by the store on a repository with no `columns.toml` and
nowhere else, so every older board and every board a test builds reads as set up (absent key,
skipped when false, no bump). The TUI opens Setup on a snapshot that says so, once
(`App::setup_applied` until the next snapshot), armed in `lib.rs::run` after the prefs and the key
probe, never on a practice board or a board joined from someone else. Quitting mid-way applies
nothing, and the next open asks again.

**The pages** (`tui/src/setup.rs`): how you work (on my own · with pull requests, in the forge's
words, GitHub's or GitLab's from `forge::setup_probe`, which reads `origin` and asks `gh`/`glab`
off the draw thread), then merging into main (auto merge on or off) or bringing a PR that fell
behind main up to date (the same switch under pull requests, with the sign-in's state under the
question), the board (`board::Template`: Kanban; Pull requests: TODO, IN PROGRESS, PR/MR OPEN on
`arrives_on: PR opened`, MERGED on `merged`; and that plus PRODUCTION on `deployed to production`,
a person widening to more environments from the column's settings), a worktree per ticket on a
folder of two or more repositories, what an agent may do on its card (Everything · Write notes and
ask you · Only read it, written to every column's `agent_tools`), and the brief, `brief::TEXT`
verbatim on its own lines. `s` keeps a page's default, Esc all the rest's, `h` goes back; the last
page opens the board or the tour, and its Enter is the only way out: `Scope::Setup` is a barrier
(no parent, so no Settings, reload or suspend reaches past it), with its own `?`; `q`/Esc are
`Back` before the last page and unbound on it (the author: "don't allow to exit the setup").

**The preview is the tour's practice board** (`tour::toy`), a scene per page laid from the
answers given and the one under the cursor: the ticket's journey, a PR's marks, a sibling's merge
leaving this PR conflicting and its agent rebasing, two agents in their own worktrees, an agent
finding a bug and the person's Shift+Enter ask filed, refused with a raised hand or refused, and
the brief's first words. Two seams made it possible: the toy answers `PromptSession`, and a card's
peek reads a practice agent's words from `PeekCache::stage` (`World::says`), since a practice
board has no transcript. `ui::tour::lay_board` is the blit both use.

**Applying.** `Command::ApplySetup` (local only, `agent_allows` no): the template's columns while
the board has no ticket, `merge_into`, every column's tools, `Board::workspace`, the brief on,
`setup_pending` off, in one writer turn (`set_merge_into`'s own road where the workflow changes,
so the forge state follows). Auto merge off is this board's `merge_train` override, written by
the TUI.

**Worktree by default.** `Board::workspace` stamps a ticket at mint when its composer and its
column left it alone (`create_ticket`), `None` the shared checkout as before, so a board before
Setup and every test board mint as they did. Setup writes a worktree unless the person chose the
shared checkout or the folder has no repository (`Daemon::has_repo`: `.git` at the root, or the
census). Settings › Behaviour › Worktrees (`Command::SetBoardWorkspace`, under a TICKETS heading;
a switch, since two long choice words widened the page's value column past the fetch row) changes
it after; a column's Workspace row lost `board default` and shows the board's answer where the
column says nothing.

**Promise 3** now says Setup shows the brief and turns it on; a board from before Setup keeps it
off. No rig test: the brief's text and delivery are T-224's, unchanged, and when it is on is
board state `setup_e2e` reads. Measured once on the real Sonnet all the same: a worker on a board
with the brief calls `get_ticket` first (past Claude Code's `ToolSearch`), and a ticket whose
description says "read no file and run no command" is obeyed over the brief, with no call at all.

Tests: `board::every_template_is_a_valid_board`, `a_template_is_refused_once_a_ticket_exists`;
`setup_e2e` (both); `setup::every_page_plays_to_its_end` (both workflows, both forges, a folder of
projects, every answer: the toy refused nothing), `the_pages_follow_how_you_work`,
`skipping_everything_is_the_defaults`, `the_answers_become_the_outcome`; `app::setup_applies_its_
answers_in_one_command`, `setup_esc_twice_is_the_defaults`; goldens `setup_work_120x30`,
`setup_fix_120x30`, `setup_brief_120x36`, `setup_ready_80x24`, and the Behaviour and column
goldens reminted. `MESIMON_SETUP_DUMP=<page>[,<cursor>[,team]] cargo test -p mesimon-tui
dump_a_page -- --nocapture` prints a page's scene beat by beat.

**Addendum (T-816, same day, the author: "remove 'tell agents to read the ticket' suggestion. it
should be on by default ∙ the dialog should be entirely full screen, and its title should be
mesimon -> setup {folder name}").** The brief is on by default on every board, not only on one
Setup made: `Board::system_prompt` defaults on, and since `columns.toml` always wrote the switch,
an off reads as on unless `claude_md_ignored` says a person answered (`store::brief_on`: turning
it off in Settings and the old offer's "never" both stamp it), doctor reading the same. The
offer is gone from the TUI: no header chip, no menu row, no `i never ask again` in the dialog,
which the Settings row still opens before turning it back on. The daemon still answers
`ClaudeMdStatus.offer` and `IgnoreBriefOffer` for an older TUI. Setup takes the whole screen,
edge to edge, titled `mesimon › setup <folder>`, its keys on its own bottom edge. Tests:
`store::an_unanswered_off_reads_as_on_and_an_answered_one_stays`, `ui::the_brief_is_never_offered`;
`brief_offer_e2e` and `setup_e2e` read the brief on from the first snapshot.

known price. This meets the requested three-character maximum for that marker
without shortening the title unnecessarily. Usage retains its explicit
`unpriced` label; priced amounts and tickets with nothing counted are unchanged.
The cost-corner regression and its golden cover the compact marker and the
restored full title.

Validation: the full TUI suite (1040 passed), `cargo ut`, formatting and
`git diff --check` passed; the sole golden diff was inspected. The existing
live-network check and timing benchmark remain ignored. Integration, Linux and

## A moved card is marked by a bold glyph, and moves as one row (T-817 addendum, 2026-10-16, the author: "it's not good that the shimmer doesn't stop, because it reads as ticket still working. instead of shimmer, use bold glyph" and "the target card before the trail reaches it sits ghosted and is very bulky")

**Refutes the shimmer.** Anything moving on a card reads as its agent working, and the shimmer ran
until the cursor came, so a finished card looked busy. `unseen_moves` now marks the card still:
`card::render`'s `moved` makes its state glyph bold (`App::moved_unseen`, from its landing until a
keypress leaves the cursor on it), and a card with no glyph — a TODO card a phone moved — wears a
bold title instead. `Theme::move_shimmer` and the `quiet` hook in `glide::draw` are gone;
`shimmer_crest` stays the pipeline's own.

**A card on the move is one row.** An open card (the cursor's, `P`, a summary) held its whole
height blank in the new column while the trail ran, a block nothing explained. `board.rs` now
truncates the ghost to its title row and the landing card to `App::landing_rows`: one row until it
lands, then one more every `glide::ROW_MS` (60 ms). A glide is kept `SETTLE_MS` (2 s) past its
landing for the opening (`Glide::settled`, which `absorb_moves` prunes by and `gliding` asks for
the fast frames); past that the card is whole whatever its height.

Tests: `ui::an_unseen_moved_card_wears_a_bold_glyph` (glyph, title fallback, still frame to frame),
`ui::a_moving_card_is_one_row_and_opens_once_landed`; `app::a_move_from_elsewhere_plays_and_is_marked_until_seen`
renamed from the shimmer's.

## A landing card's tag bar comes in muted, not missing (T-817 addendum, 2026-10-16, the author: "the target ticket tag box looks black until filled. it should be just slightly muted original colored tag")

`glide::fade` cleared every cell the fade-in had not reached, a painted one to `Color::Reset`: the
landing card's tag bar sat as a black hole in its column until the front came. The bar's cells
(the card's first `BAR_WIDTH`) now keep at least `BAR_KEEP` (75 %) of their colour from the start
and come up to their own as the front passes; the rest of the card still arrives with the front,
and a cleared painted cell takes the theme's ground rather than the terminal's. The ghost's bar
still fades with its card. Test: `glide::tests::a_landing_cards_tag_bar_comes_muted_not_missing`.

## A moving card's ghost shrinks as the card grows (T-817 addendum, 2026-10-16, the author: "just like the target card is growing gradually, the source should shrink gradually")

The ghost was drawn as a crown trail is, title alone, so an open card (`P`, a reply line, its
pull requests) lost its rows in one frame and the column under it jumped. `push_card` now draws a
glide's ghost as the card looked (`bare` is the crown trail alone: the ghost keeps `open`, `fresh`
and `brief`), and truncates it by `App::ghost_dropped`: one row every `glide::ROW_MS` from the
move's start, down to its title row, while it fades out. The landing side is unchanged. Test:
`ui::a_moving_cards_ghost_shrinks_a_row_at_a_time`.

## The card the cursor rode away shrinks from what was on screen (T-817 addendum, 2026-10-16, the author: "it doesn't shrink gradually")

The shrink above was right for a `P` card and wrong for the common case: an agent's card moves on
its turn's edge while the cursor sits on it, the cursor rides it away (`follow_ticket`), and its
ghost was drawn unselected — the accordion that listed its agent, its shell and the peek gone in
the first frame, nothing left to shrink. A glide now records `was_cursor` (the card the snapshot's
cursor held), and its ghost renders with `selected` (the accordion, the peek rule) while
`card::render`'s new `ghost` keeps it from looking like the cursor (`cursorish` off: no band, no
cursor bar, rest ink). It then gives up its rows at `glide::ROW_MS` as before. Test:
`ui::the_cursors_card_leaves_an_open_ghost_that_shrinks`.

## The summary fold spells its key after the count (T-819, 2026-10-16, the author: "switch \"^j summary\" with ^j next to the N more")

The open cursor card's summary fold row read `[✓] 2 more` with `^j summary` right-aligned across
the card. It now reads `[✓] 2 more ^j`: the count already says what the key opens, so the key
stands alone, bold, one space after it. `chrome::key_spans` draws a binding's key without its
word and notes it with `mouse::note_key`, so the lone `^j` is clickable as a spelled hint is
(T-716). Tests: the `board_summary_120x30` golden, `ui::the_summary_folds_key_alone_clicks`.

Addendum (2026-10-16, the author: "it's too white, add bullet before it and keep same color as the
rest of the text before it"): the row reads `[✓] 2 more ∙ ^j`, the bullet and the key in the
count's faint ink, not bold. A scraped hint needs a bold first cell to tell it from running text;
`note_key` records `∙ ^j` with that check off, the bullet doing the telling.

## The links list reads latest first (T-820, 2026-10-16, "links order")

The ask: "latest first (transcript originated links is always latest)". `App::ticket_links`
now lists the agent's latest words first, then every note and pull request by when it last
changed (a note's `edited_at`, else `created_at`; a PR's `updated_ms`), newest first. A tie
keeps the notes' order, so an untouched ticket still reads description first. Inside one body
the order stays the document's: the words were written together, and reversing them would
scramble a sentence. A target listed twice keeps its latest place, so a URL the agent repeats
from the description rises to the top. `^K` (Ctrl+Shift+K) opens the first row, which is now
the agent's latest link, not the description's.

Tests: `the_agents_latest_words_are_links_too`, `the_newest_note_lists_its_links_first`.

Addendum (2026-10-16, the author: "inside links render ticket references as the ticket ID instead
of 'ticket' and also when hovering a referenced ticket flash it on board (if it's there)", then
"make sure the table is aligned"): a ticket row's first column is its key (`T-2  Decay
treatments`), no longer the word `ticket` and the key again. That column is as wide as its widest
entry, every row padded to it, so the bodies start in one column whatever the keys' lengths; the
old fixed six cells cut a URL that now fits. The row the pointer rests on, else the cursor's row,
names a ticket (`App::link_hovered`); on a board, that card blinks out of the recess
(`board::recede`): lit for 400 ms, receded with the rest for 400 ms, on the MOVE ghost's
cadence, for as long as the row is chosen. It takes no new colour, so the
one-saturated-colour law holds. A card scrolled off its column, the ticket page (no board under
it) and an archived ticket flash nothing.

Tests: `a_ticket_links_row_flashes_its_card_on_the_board`; goldens `links_120x30`,
`picture_link_unavailable_120x30`.

## A worker mid-turn says what the train does after it (T-822, 2026-10-16, "no train pending merge / rebase indication")

The ask: T-816's card showed no train mark or row, where it "used to be". It had shown them

0.6 s after the turn ended. `train::lane` needs a free seat for either list, and a ticket whose
own agent is mid-turn is on neither, so the snapshot had no row for it. That has been so since

`train::Plan` now has a third list, `after_turn`. A ticket the two lists skip because its own

`merge_train_e2e::a_worker_mid_turn_says_what_the_train_does_after_it`, and the row assertions in
