## Codex startup trust reaches the person on the board (T-824, 2026-10-16)

Codex 0.163.0's folder disclosure starts `Trust this folder? Codex can read, edit, and run
files here…`, followed by `Trust and continue`. The production probe only knew the older
`Do you trust` heading and `Hooks need review`; the native rig had already learned the new
wording. The probe now recognizes the new paragraph and choice together, including a wrapped
paragraph, while a live composer still rules out startup attention. Older folder and hook
review dialogs remain supported.

A detected trust stop carries `Codex needs your trust decision ∙ open its pane` through the
normal authorized state transition. It enters the existing attention queue and needs-you
notification path. No keystroke answers trust: initial title/description delivery still waits
for both structured readiness and the native composer, and a resumed session still receives
no fresh prefill. The integration regression covers an actual provisioned worktree, the
notification, consecutive folder/hook dialogs with no input, and one original submission
after the composer returns. Unit cases also reject historical text above a live composer.

Repeated folder trust has a native one-time route, documented in USING.md: trust the main
repository checkout in Codex. Codex 0.163.0's `resolve_root_git_project_for_trust` resolves a
linked worktree to that checkout; its config loader falls back to that trust entry after a
worktree's own entry. A non-Git folder containing several repositories cannot inherit this
way. Hook review is separate: native trust is keyed to the hook definition, and Mesimon's
session-flag hook source and commands are already stable across ticket worktrees. No trust
configuration is written or overridden and no bypass flag is added. Evidence: the versioned
upstream `codex-rs/git-utils/src/trust.rs`, `codex-rs/config/src/loader/mod.rs`,
`codex-rs/hooks/src/engine/discovery.rs`, and `codex-rs/tui/src/onboarding/trust_directory.rs`.

Validation: the focused worktree regression, `cargo ut`, `cargo nextest run --workspace`
(2525 passed), and the mod-road integration pass (211 passed) passed. Nextest noted an
output-handle leak in the unchanged `approve_bridge::a_wait_the_daemon_closed_ends_the_hold`
on the mod road; the outer fixture audit was clean for all 423 owners. Intentional skips
were the timing benchmark, the live-release network test, and the restart-skew subprocess
helper (the mod pass skips only that helper). Formatting and `git diff --check` passed.
An initial unit run hit the already-recorded `NO_COLOR` underline assertion; the unchanged
isolated test and the complete rerun passed with `NO_COLOR=`. The initial sandboxed
integration attempt could not bind its socket or inspect processes; its two retained
fixtures were cleaned through their inspected ownership records before elevated reruns.
No live-model rig was run: this changes board observation, not agent instructions or turn
submission policy. Native dialog spelling and trust inheritance were checked against the
installed CLI version's upstream source, not asserted as a new live Codex acceptance run.

## Games share the live board's empty space (T-823, 2026-10-16)

Board Breaker and Ticket Snake are opt-in TUI state, opened by `ctrl-g` or
Games in the menu. They share the existing snapshot and event loop; no game
sends commands, changes tickets or persists scores. `Scope::Arcade` owns its
keys without inheriting board/global mutations; Esc returns to navigation.
Mouse hints use the same bindings, and a card click or wheel exits first.

The original disappearing-card Breakout proposal was changed to preserve
readability: cards remain solid, readable bumpers, with small removable bricks
in unused cells. Snake travels between cards. The renderer protects the whole
card footprint and every other nonblank cell, leaves the header and advisory
alone, and uses neutral ink. A layout change re-seats pieces and pauses,
preserving score and Breaker's lives. New attention is detected by ticket
identity, not a count; it pauses even if another attention item vanished in
the same snapshot. Focus loss and disconnection also pause. Slow ticks never
catch up a backlog of game steps. A board without enough room offers a resize
instead of hiding work or launching an impossible round.

The engines cover buffered Snake turns, reachable food, growth and collision;
Breaker covers aimable paddle rebounds, three lives, card bonuses, combos and
waves. Tests exercise the games through board rendering and key dispatch,
including all themes and terminal profiles, unchanged card cells, live updates,
input isolation, help and clickable exit. Shin's Garden is a separate planning
and design ticket, T-825; seeds and a persistent personal world are outside this
arcade's scope.

### Card movement preserves an arcade round (T-823 follow-up, 2026-10-16)

The live-board layout pause above interrupted normal play: every changed card
rectangle, animation trail or nonblank cell called `place`, recreating Snake's
body and Breaker's ball, targets and combo before pausing. Preserving only the
score and lives still felt like a restart, as the person reported.

Terrain synchronization now keeps the round running. Unaffected pieces and the
step clock stay unchanged. A covered Snake moves as a whole to the closest fitting
position, retaining its length, direction and buffered turns; a newly blocked
next step receives the same protection. Covered or disconnected food moves to a
reachable cell. Breaker retains its paddle lane when it still fits and moves only
a covered paddle, ball or unreachable target. The remaining target count, ball
velocity, launch state, combo, card-hit history, wave, lives and score survive.
Cards and animation trails remain protected from game ink on every frame.

If there is no safe placement, the game holds its existing pieces and progress
until room returns, without requiring a fresh launch. Explicit pauses, attention,
focus loss and disconnection still hold; terminal resizing pauses but also
preserves the round. Tests cover repeated terrain updates, every card-glide phase
in both games, covered pieces, next-step protection, paddle-lane changes, temporary
crowding and zero-size resize recovery. The narrow Snake golden now shows the
preserved body and the resize-specific pause message.

## Column auto-sleep includes Codex (T-828, 2026-10-16)

The column timer still required `SessionKind::Claude`, so a confirmed idle Codex session
never reached the daemon's ordinary sleep path. `SessionRecord::autosleep_due` now accepts
both agent providers. Codex additionally requires no observation hold, pending observation,
unacknowledged submit or runtime cleanup; shells remain excluded. The existing idle-state,
confidence, elapsed-time, pending-input, ownership, conversation-identity, attached-client
and queued-work guards still apply. Sleeping and waking use the provider's existing path,
which retains the Codex thread and resumes it exactly.

The core timer test now runs its state and clock cases for both providers and covers each
Codex hold. `provider_e2e::column_autosleep_parks_codex_only_when_observed_quiet_and_resumes_its_thread`
uses the synthetic runtime through the real daemon and tmux to check opt-in, held and working
sessions, automatic cleanup, the automation feed, exact-thread wake and sleeping again.

## Correction: main-checkout trust does not settle Codex's remote folder check (T-824, 2026-10-16)

The one-time route described above was incomplete. Codex 0.163.0's ordinary config loader
resolves linked worktrees to their main checkout, but Mesimon launches the native terminal
with `--remote unix://…`. Codex classifies an explicit remote endpoint as a remote workspace,
including a Unix socket on the same machine. Its startup `check_directory_trust` therefore
calls `read_remote_project_trust` with `ProjectTrustHost::Remote`. That lookup does not resolve
local Git roots. With no project config layers supplying trust evidence and no saved entry
for the worktree itself, it asks for that folder even if the main checkout is trusted.

The user's main checkout already had `trust_level = "trusted"`, explaining why an ordinary
`codex` launch there offered no dialog. Repeating that launch cannot settle the separate
worktree check. USING.md now describes this limitation and directs the person to the native
dialog in the ticket's pane. The shipped board-attention fix remains valid; repeated trust
for new worktrees is not solved by it. No trust setting or launch behavior is changed here.

Evidence: the installed CLI version and its versioned upstream `codex-rs/tui/src/lib.rs`
(`AppServerTarget`), `codex-rs/tui/src/onboarding/directory_trust.rs`, and
`codex-rs/tui/src/config_update.rs` (`read_remote_project_trust`), compared with Mesimon's
`agents/codex/runtime.rs` launch arguments. This corrects documentation only; `git diff
--check` passed. Runtime tests were not rerun and no native trust decision was submitted.

## Bounded runs in independent worktrees overlap (T-830, 2026-10-16)

`ci/test-run.py` held one lock per OS user (`/tmp/msmn-test-command-<uid>.lock`, from T-235)
for the whole run, pruning included, so a ticket's `cargo ut` waited behind another ticket's
full suite, its mod-road pass and minutes of `prune-deps`. The lock now follows what actually
conflicts.

**What is shared, checked before narrowing.** Fixture roots (`mkdtemp`), the runtime and state
dirs (keyed on a fixture's unique repo path), tmux sockets, the audit registry
(`/tmp/msmn-test-run-*`, one per run) and the command supervisor (it reaps only its own
children's trees and leaves nested fixture supervisors to theirs) are all per run. The Rust
tests' fixed `/tmp/…` names are uuid-suffixed or never written. What two runs can genuinely
share is **build output**: one Cargo target or `build-dir`, by `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, `build.
target-dir`, `build.build-dir` or `--target-dir`. A rebuild there swaps binaries under a
running suite, and the `suite-passed.json` stamp lives there. The rest is machine load, which
only the release gate is timed against. Not covered by this lock: the Claude rig's fixed
`/tmp/msmn-rig-phone.sock` (`ci/rig.py` never enters the runner, and never did).

**The model.** Locks live in `/tmp/msmn-test-locks-<uid>/` (private, owned, checked like the
audit root; `MESIMON_TEST_LOCK_DIR` moves it for the runner's own tests). Each run resolves its
build directories the way cargo does (`cargo metadata`, resolved paths; a non-cargo command
gets its checkout's, since a script may build) and takes one exclusive flock per directory, in
sorted order. Every run holds `machine.lock` shared; `--exclusive`, which `ci/release.sh` now
passes, takes it exclusively behind a `machine.gate` turnstile so new runs cannot starve it.
Waiting is bounded by the run's `--timeout` and spends none of the supervisor's deadline; past
it the run is "not started" (exit 2). A run inside a run inherits `MESIMON_TEST_HELD` and does
not wait on its parent. Lock fds are close-on-exec, so a leaked child never holds one.

**Saying whose turn it is.** Each held lock has a JSON note (pid, checkout, command, phase,
since), rewritten at every phase and removed before the lock is let go. A waiting run prints
`== waiting (not testing yet): build output <dir> is in use by pid N in <checkout> (running
tests since 22:07:05): <command>` once per change of holder or phase; the phases are `running
tests`, `running the mod road's pass`, `auditing its fixtures` and `pruning the build cache`.
The run itself prints `== tests:` and `== pruning the build cache in …`.

**Pruning.** Still after the audit and still under the run's lock on that build directory,
which holds off only runs sharing it: they would wait on cargo's lock anyway and now say why.
`prune-deps.py` gets the build directory the run used (`--target-dir <build-dir>/debug`), not
the cwd's `target/`. It takes every `.cargo*lock` in the profile dir, all or none per attempt:
Cargo 1.98 holds `.cargo-build-lock` and `.cargo-artifact-lock` exclusively for a whole build
and `.cargo-lock` only shared, and a separate `build-dir` keeps its own `.cargo-build-lock`
(measured with a sleeping `build.rs`). It says when it waits (`--wait`, default 30 s), and
skips the `nm` scan when `deps/`'s mtime equals the one stamped in `debug/.msmn-pruned` after
its last prune: a run that linked nothing no longer pays minutes of scan (211 s on a 42k-entry
worktree `deps/`).

**Tests** (`ci/test_run_test.py`, real runs over throwaway Cargo packages): two independent runs
each wait for the other's start marker; shared output by `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, `build.target-dir`
and `build.build-dir` takes turns with the holder named; a run cancelled with SIGINT or failing
while another holds a nested fixture leaves the other's sleep alive and both audits exact (the
cancelled run's two owners `runner-lost`, none of them the other's); a pruning holder blocks
only its own build output; `--exclusive` waits for a running run and holds a new one off; a
nested run does not wait on its parent; `prune-deps` steps aside under a held
`.cargo-build-lock` and skips an unchanged `deps/`. CI's Python step now discovers
`test_*_test.py`, so the runner's tests run beside the supervisor's.

An older runner in a not-yet-rebased worktree still takes the per-user lock among its own kind;
the new runner ignores that file.

## A Codex turn survives a `U`; the rebase turn keeps holding ready merges (T-827, 2026-10-16, the author: "turn end didn't register until I opened it" ∙ "it was asked to rebase \"after its turn\" while mid turn" ∙ "T-816 is waiting until T-824 is merged even though T-816 could have been merged already" ∙ "it means that train can cause redundant rebases, no?")

**The Codex card.** T-824's record read `Unknown{DaemonRestarted}` (grey, "unavailable") from the
18:15:16 handover to the end of its turn at 18:22:38, while its row said `rebase ask ∙ after its
turn`: the card looked finished and the train looked stuck. `on_codex_snapshots` restored a
handed-over record only from a snapshot without `observation_hold`, and a turn's own pending work
(a long `exec`) is a hold, with no state change to move the sequence. A snapshot at `Running` or
`RequiresAction` is now restored under a hold too; an `Idle` behind a hold stays as it was, which
is what the guard was for. The turn's end was heard 2 s after Codex wrote it: the "until I opened
it" was the grey card, not a missed end. T-823, named in the title, had every turn heard in 2 s.

**The hold, tried and refuted.** T-816 sat in REVIEW from 18:28:54, one commit ahead of main and
none behind, while T-824's rebase turn (asked 18:22:38) ran its tests; T-824 merged at 18:39:00
and T-816 then owed a rebase. `train_pass` returns while `train_busy` holds, and `train_busy`
holds T-435's rebase turn for merges as well as asks. Splitting the gates (a merge waiting only on
the root checkout's workers) was built, tested, and reverted on the author's question. With
ff-only merges the second of two tickets rebases either way, so the count does not move, but
merging past the rebase turn throws away the turn in flight: its tests ran on a base that just
moved, and the same agent is asked again. A slow rebaser can be passed by one ready ticket after
another, asked again each time, until its fuse (6 asks in 2 h) trips. Under the hold every ask
ends in a merge and no agent is asked twice for one base; the waiting ticket's row already says
`auto-merge ∙ after T-824`. The wait is the price, not a bug.

The day's feed was also read for wasted rebases: from 18:22, four tickets (T-826, T-824, T-816,
T-823) for three asks, the ff-only floor of N−1. T-817's four merges and T-822's three each
followed a person's prompt and a new commit, not the train; the merged notice between them was a
13–25 s turn.

Test: `provider_e2e::daemon_handover_restores_a_codex_turn_held_by_its_own_work` (fails without
the restore: `Unknown` past 15 s).

## The open card reads in one order, and its summary is the boxes (T-829, 2026-10-16, the author: "it's a mess right now … make sure everything is in the RIGHT place")

The open card grew a row per feature, each where its ticket put it: the tags and key under the
title (T-410), a held ask's keys on a row of their own under its words (T-551), the sessions
listed two rows deep above the reply, the reply four rows, the step running now, the summary's
plain line and boxes, and the pull requests last (T-789). The merge train's ask shared the owed
row with a queued message at the top, so a ticket held one or the other, never both, and a
shipping fact sat at the opposite end of the card from the pull request it was about.

The author picked layout A of a proposal (an artifact with "today", A "sorted" and B "compact",
toggles for what is going on), with two reply rows and the tags at the bottom, after two changes
on the way: the checklist above the step running now, and plain summary lines gone. The order is
now one place per kind, top to bottom: what waits on the person (snooze preset, raised hand, the
crown's answer, the owed row with its keys right-aligned on the same row), the reply (two rows),
the boxes (three rows, the fold row included), the step running now, every other session on one
row (`✻ claude ⠋  $ bash ◦`, each name capped at 10 cells, the rest counted, ages left to the
page), where the work goes (the merge train's `rebase ask ∙ …` / `auto-merge ∙ …` before the
pull request's words, its marks under the age), and last the tags and key.

- `App::card_owed` splits `pending_row`'s words by kind: a merge or rebase action (or
  `auto-merge ∙ off`) goes to the pull-request row, everything else stays at the top. The ticket
  page reads `pending_row` whole, unchanged.
- A held ask's row drops its own `∙ you send` when `^y send` fits beside it; a key too wide for
  the words' row (`shift+enter resend`) takes the row under them, as every key did before.
- The pull-request row is no longer last, so `board.rs` finds its click by scanning the card's
  rows for the brief instead of reading line 2 and the last line.
- The summary is the boxes everywhere: `summary::extract` drops every non-box line, `Row.done`
  is a `bool`, and so is the wire's `AgentSummaryRow.done` (a reader of the old optional field
  reads the same JSON). The note keeps its plain lines; the page draws them as markdown. The
  `^j` dialog lists boxes only. `card_rows(n)` shows every box when they fit in `n` rows, else
  `n - 1` and the fold.
- `mcp::SUMMARY_ABOUT` now says "Only the boxes reach the card; any other line there stays the
  note's" in place of T-743's "a plain line takes a card line … waits for a person's ask". Rig S1
  and S2 no longer count plain rows.

Golden: `board_open_card_order_120x30` is the whole card in order.

## Codex worktrees expose the main checkout's existing trust (T-824, 2026-10-16)

Codex 0.163.0's config loader records a project layer for an existing `.codex/` directory
even without `config.toml`. The loader resolves that layer's trust through the main Git
checkout; the remote terminal's folder check accepts the enabled layer as trust evidence.
An isolated native app-server/terminal probe confirmed that main-checkout trust alone still
prompts, while an empty worktree `.codex/` reaches the composer without saving worktree
trust. Without main-checkout trust the layer remains disabled and the folder prompt remains;
an explicit untrusted worktree also disables its project layer. Approval and sandbox policy
and saved trust entries were unchanged. No model turn or native trust answer was sent.

The Codex adapter now attempts that single directory creation before both fresh starts and
exact resumes. The daemon supplies eligibility from an attached binding with a root Git
leg, matching the session cwd directly under its owned worktrees root. Shared checkouts,
external directories and plain folder containers are excluded. A single `create_dir` leaves
existing files, directories and symlinks alone; failure falls back to native onboarding.
There is no trust override, user configuration edit or generated project configuration.
Hook trust is still a separate native decision, and remaining dialogs still hold the
queued prompt and surface `TRUST` on the board. This supersedes the preceding limitation
for managed Git worktrees, including those provisioned before this change.

Regression coverage exercises fresh starts, missing directories on exact wake, existing
configuration and symlinks/files, clean Git status, and shared-checkout/folder exclusions
through the real daemon and synthetic Codex runtime. The existing trust-attention test
continues to cover folder and hook prompts that still require the person.

Validation: bounded `cargo ut`, all 21 provider e2es, all 2,553 workspace nextest tests,
and all 215 mod-road integration tests passed. The first mod pass hit an extra-wake count
in the Claude forge/crown test; it passed both alone and in the complete mod rerun without
code changes. That rerun reported an approval-bridge output-handle leak warning; its isolated
rerun passed without the warning. Every fixture audit was clean. The existing timing probe,
live-release network test and indirectly exercised subprocess helper remain excluded from
ordinary discovery. Optional object-cache pruning was stopped after the audits to release
the runner lock. Formatting and `git diff --check` passed. No live-model rig was run: this
changes Codex filesystem preparation, not model instructions or turn submission.

## The tag bar is one cell until a ticket wears two tags (T-821, 2026-10-16, the author: "single tag if no 2 tags attached on any ticket currently in board … half the width of the tag box right now (also on columns)")

The bar was one cell until 47102fec (2026-09-09) widened it to two so two tags could each take a
`▉`. On a board where no ticket wears a second tag, that second cell was ink beside one colour.
The width is now the board's, worked out on every frame (`tags::bar_width`, `App::bar_width`):
`BAR_WIDE` (2) when any ticket on the board wears two tags or more, `BAR_NARROW` (1) otherwise.
Archived tickets are not on the board and do not count; the draft being composed does, so the
phantom card (and the grown editor's stripe) widens the board on its second `^t` pick.

- One width for the whole board, never per card: a column's titles must start in one column, so
  an untagged card and the column header move with the two-tag ticket.
- `CardCtx.bar` carries it into the card; the column header, the dialog's stripe and lead
  (`editor.rs`), the glide's fade, the crown's bolt and the settings sample read
  `App::bar_width`.
- `bar_spans` at one cell paints a single tag whole. Handed two tags at one cell, which
  `bar_width` never allows, it paints the first.

Goldens: every fixture without a two-tag ticket went narrow; `board_tags_*` keep the wide bar.
`a_second_tag_on_any_ticket_widens_every_bar` pins the flip.

## The fifth simplify pass, a bug hunt off the diff (T-838, 2026-10-17, "simplify")

The author: "bug hunt as well, try to look for areas where last 2 simplify runs may have failed to
catch. focus on performance and bugs". The last four passes reviewed diffs, so this one split in
two: three reviewers over the 63 commits since T-795 (`71b64b01..`) and three over code the
diffs never reached — the daemon's tick, snapshot and hook paths read whole, the TUI's frame
path read whole, and a workspace scan for the panic classes a diff review never sees (byte
slicing, index arithmetic, casts, locks, serde defaults). Each finding was checked against the
code before it was applied; the goldens are unchanged.

**Applied, bugs.**
- **A subscriber that stops reading no longer stops the daemon.** `broadcast` wrote each
  `board_changed` line into the subscriber's socket under its mutex with no timeout, and the
  reply writer wrote whole board answers under the same mutex; a TUI under Ctrl+Z filled its
  8 KiB send buffer after ~300 pushes and the writer thread blocked for good (no tick, no hook
  frame, no other client). `Command::Subscribe` now sets a 5 s write timeout on the socket
  (`SUBSCRIBER_WRITE_TIMEOUT`, per socket so the reply clone takes it), and a write that times
  out drops the subscriber and ends its loop; the client reconnects as after any dropped line.
- **A hand-edited `order` cannot kill the writer thread.** `fracindex::idx` was an `expect` on a
  byte off the base-62 alphabet, and `between` took `Ticket.order`/`Column.order` straight
  from disk: one `order = "a.0"` in a `ticket.toml` panicked the daemon on the next filing or
  move beside it, and the respawn died again. A foreign byte now reads as the lowest digit;
  the minted key is valid and may sort beside the foreign one rather than between.
- **The merged pipeline is each repository's newest merge.** `forge::pipeline_of` took the first
  merged PR in set order (`updated_ms`, which a comment on an older PR moves), while
  `merged_reads` reads a live pipeline onto the newest-merged per repository alone: a comment on
  a superseded PR with a settled failure turned a passed merge into "pipeline failed" on the
  card, in the gate and to the crown. It folds `newest_merged` now, so a ticket with legs in
  two repositories reads both merges.
- **`ticket_set` keeps one record per PR whatever sat between its readings** (`dedup_by` drops
  adjacent twins only); `Remote::parse` refuses a local path with a colon as `ssh_alias`
  already did; a move the daemon refused no longer stamps `own_moves`, which claimed the next
  mover's move of that card inside 10 s as the cursor's.
- **Two clocks on one animation**: the glide readers and `glide::draw` read `App::now`, as
  `absorb_moves` stamps them, so a test's injected clock governs both ends.

**Applied, performance.**
- **The snapshot's pipeline clause reads nothing of git or the disk.** `held_items` judged
  every standing held line through `gate_with` → `pipeline_refusal` on every broadcast, and
  that forked `git rev-parse` per leg with an open PR (`pipeline_head_unread`) and read every
  transcript tail of the ticket (`opened_unread`) — the twin of the merge clause T-795 took off
  git. `Reading::{Fresh, Cached}` names the road: a move reads the tip and the tails now; a
  snapshot reads the flags' tip and the ledger's URLs (`Ledger::opened_owed`), a held line at
  most one cost pass late.
- **`ssh -G` has a 3 s deadline** (`SSH_TIMEOUT`): it runs on the writer thread once per SSH
  alias and evaluates `Match exec` blocks of the person's own config, under a CLI call's 20 s.
- **A snapshot clones only the records it sends.** `Board::without_archived_records` builds the
  copy from the kept records; the daemon cloned every record (641 parked, over a megabyte of
  argv on the author's board) per snapshot and dropped them.
- **One tmux fork per list.** `activity` and `pane_facts` ran `list-sessions` before every
  `list-panes` (every 1 s and 2 s); the liveness fork is asked only when the list failed, so
  a dead server still reads as no panes.
- **Smaller:** the Links dialog no longer asks 16 ms frames (its blink is on the spinner's
  100 ms step; `link_flashing` is gone); the arcade rasterises each card once instead of asking
  `card_at` of every cell against every card per frame; `pr_fingerprint` is a summed hash per
  card instead of a formatted, sorted, joined line; the column dialog values each section once
  (was per row); `scrape_hints` runs only with the mouse on; a card group's lines move into
  the column instead of cloning; `pr_passed_news` scans without a key clone;
  `poll_agent_recovery`'s retain is a set lookup (was records²); `unprompted_hint` stats last;
  `drain_queue` and `service_plan_accepts` rank nothing on an empty queue;
  `forge::State::keep_tickets` prunes `commit_pipelines` and `deployed` to the merge commits a
  kept set names (they grew by every PR ever merged, written whole and copied into every
  query); a deleted ticket's attention machines go when its grace expires; the TUI's
  `pr_seen`, `crown_residue` and `summaries` are pruned on absorb; `tags::painted`'s no-op
  sort, `Ctx::theme_name` (filled per frame, read by nothing) and Setup's `col` twin of `nth`
  are gone.

**Checked and kept.** The train's seat stays `Busy` for an agent stopped on a usage limit
(T-808): `lets_merge` passes only a seat the train can speak to, as a parked seat is off the
train; T-808's "the train sees a finished turn" is the shared-checkout hold, not the seat.
`merge_refusal`'s `find(Merged)` names the forge only. The `ps axo` scan while a Claude sits
idle feeds a park decision (`foregrounds`, T-707), not only a glyph, so it is not gated on a
reader.

**Found and left open (each a decision or a structure change):**
- `sessions.json` is serialised whole (1.3 MB pretty JSON, 470 KB of it parked seats' argv) on
  every changed tick and compared as text; a dirty flag, or a parked seat that keeps no argv
  (a wake rebuilds flags from `LaunchContext`; `resume` replays the stored argv today).
- 684 archived tickets ride every snapshot; serving the drawer by ask is a wire change.
- Every shelf build (30 s while an agent is busy) re-reads every Codex transcript and walks
  `~/.codex/sessions` whole (`shelf.rs`'s `everywhere` skip is off for Codex).
- `archive_held` reads every note of every un-archived ticket in a `requires_ticked` column on
  the bucket after any broadcast; a per-ticket open-box count keyed on note revs.
- The phone's `control_awareness` is tickets × records per push; `persist_crown` serialises the
  ledger every second to learn nothing changed; `cost::save` clones the 2 MB ledger to set one
  field; `refresh_panes` broadcasts inside the tick and the tick broadcasts again; a Codex seat
  at a dialog is captured four times a second; `Msg::ForgeBurst` carries no `gen`.
- The TUI renders one full frame per terminal event (a trackpad sweep is ~200 frames);
  coalescing motion in `tick` touches the one-event-one-draw handover `lib.rs` relies on. The
  ticket page's description excerpt is parsed as markdown per frame (the zone's document is
  cached, the band's excerpt is not); `ticket_summary` allocates per card per frame, twice;
  `needs_you_count` is computed three times a frame; `Board::ticket` is a linear scan over
  archived tickets too, asked several times per card.
- A practice board skips the 60×20 floor, under which five `u16` subtractions in the ticket
  page, search, editor and settings can underflow (debug builds only); the tour opens none of
  those screens.
- `HostProbe::reads_nothing` is effectively dead on a live board (every stored probe carries
  `cli` or `lost` since T-810); `set_board_workspace` stores `None` for the shared checkout
  where `apply_setup` stores `Some(SharedCheckout)`, read alike everywhere; OpenAI's `Price`
  carries an invented cache-write rate nothing bills yet.

## Python bytecode is ignored (T-832)

Four `.pyc` files under `ci/__pycache__/` and `ci/rig/__pycache__/` were tracked since T-588 and
T-744: the root `.gitignore` was written for Rust and never named Python. `-B` on the CLI does not
reach a module loaded through `importlib` (`ci/test_run_test.py` loads `test-run.py` that way), so
a test run rewrote tracked bytecode and every ticket worktree carried a stray diff. The files are
untracked and `.gitignore` names `__pycache__/` and `*.pyc`.

## A column can collapse when empty (T-837, 2026-10-17, the author: "Add another mode \"when empty\"")

The column dialog's `Collapsed` row was a switch; it is now three choices Enter cycles: `off`,
`always`, `when empty` (`board::Collapse`). A `when empty` column is a spine while no
un-archived ticket stands in it and opens the moment one lands; the cursor in it expands it as
it does an `always` column, and the launch and a refresh skip it while it is folded
(`leave_pinned_column`).

- On disk it is two switches, `collapsed` (always, as before) and `collapsed_when_empty`, read
  as one mode by `ColumnSettings::collapse`/`set_collapse`. No schema bump: a build that drops
  the new one shows the column open, which narrows nothing, and an old `collapsed = true` still
  reads `always`.
- `Board::column_pinned` is the one predicate; the board and the composer's dialog geometry ask
  it through `App::pinned_columns`, never `settings.collapsed`.

`collapse_modes_round_trip_and_when_empty_follows_the_tickets` and
`a_when_empty_column_folds_only_while_empty` pin it; `column_settings_120x30` shows the three.

## A pointer sweep is one frame (T-841, 2026-10-17, from the T-838 simplify pass)

`lib.rs::event_loop` draws once per `App::tick`, and a tick took one terminal event, so with the
mouse on a trackpad sweep across a 200-column board (a `Moved` per cell crossed) was ~200
complete `ui::draw`s for a hover that only wanted its last spot. `App::next_event` now takes the
`Moved` reports already queued (`poll(Duration::ZERO)`) as one, at the last position. The first
other event ends the run and waits in `App::queued_event` as the next tick's, ahead of the poll,
so every key, click, paste and focus report keeps its own tick and frame in arrival order — the
handovers after a tick rest on that, and a click hit-tests against the frame its moves drew.

- Only `Moved` coalesces. A `Drag` stays one event per frame (the selection it paints is read
  back by the draw), and a held key is never merged: each repeat is a press that acts.
- The hover targets a queued sweep crossed on the way are skipped, so a card crossed and left
  inside one burst of reports does not restart the peek clock. Nothing on screen differs: the
  goldens are unchanged.
- `tick` is `next_event` + `on_event`; `next_event` takes the terminal as a `read(timeout)`
  closure, which is how `a_pointer_sweep_draws_one_frame_and_a_click_inside_it_lands_in_place`
  drives it with a queue: forty moves are one frame, and a click inside a sweep is its own two.

## The fifth pass's daemon leftovers (T-840)

Six of the costs T-838 found and left open, each behaviour-preserving: no schema bump, no wire
change, nothing the board says moves. Like T-688 was to T-682.

- **The shelf remembers where a Codex conversation is written.** Every build (30 s while an
  agent is busy) walked `~/.codex/sessions` for each Codex seat on Now, read the page, and
  serialised it to key it, because the slot's stat key named the seat's own rollout and not a
  continuation (T-815). `Shelf::rollouts` keeps each seat's walk (the rollout it found, its
  size, when); while that file grows or the walk is under a minute old, the slot is keyed off
  its stat and skipped where every browser holds it, as a Claude slot is. A seat whose file
  stopped growing a minute after its walk is walked again on the reader. On the author's
  machine (266 rollouts, 439 MB) a walk is 0.8 ms warm and 2.3 ms cold, against a 13 µs stat,
  before the page's read and parse. A continuation is seen at most a minute and a build late.
  The slot key is the stat's for Codex too, so a growing rollout is sent each build as a
  growing Claude transcript always was.
- **The archive offer keeps each ticket's open-box count** (`open_box_counts`) under a hash of
  its notes' `(id, rev, edited_at)`, and reads the notes only when it moved; `write_note` drops
  the entry besides. The gates (`requires_ticked` at a column's door and on `a a`) still read
  the disk every time, and refresh the count.
- **A turn's end's forge read carries the forge's `epoch`** (`Msg::ForgeBurst(epoch, _)`),
  bumped only when `set_merge_into(Main)` lets the forge go. `gen` moves with every minute's
  pass, which a burst outlives, so it could not be the guard. A stale landing returns before it
  clears `burst_inflight`, which by then belongs to a read the restored forge has out.
- **A Codex seat at a dialog, or one whose composer was not seen yet, is captured once a
  second**, not every 250 ms tick; one with launch words waiting (`pending_prefill`) still every
  tick. `drive_codex_inputs` is unchanged.
- **`control_awareness` indexes the agents by ticket once per push** (the first of the lowest
  rank, as `min_by_key` kept it) instead of filtering every record per un-archived ticket.
- **One broadcast per tick.** `refresh_panes` returns `Panes { changed, repaint }`; a foreground
  change is a `repaint`, folded into the tick's broadcast without persisting the sessions.
  It broadcast on its own before, and a tick with any other change broadcast again: two
  snapshot round-trips for every TUI.

## Persist only what changed: `Tracked`, a borrowed costs body (T-839, 2026-10-17)

Three state-file writes on the writer thread did the whole serialisation to learn nothing moved
(T-838's "left open"). `sessions.json` and `crown.json` now skip the build when no field they are
built from was reached for writing; `costs.json` is serialised from a borrowed body. No schema
bump, no wire change: every byte on disk and on the wire is the same.

- **`mesimon_core::tracked::Tracked<T>`** wraps a value and sets a mark in `DerefMut`, so every
  `&mut` (a `push`, an `iter_mut().find`, an `entry`, a field assignment through an index) marks
  it, and the compiler routes every mutator through the mark: no call site has to remember it,
  which about 76 record mutation sites and 55 crown-ledger ones made the only safe shape (a
  hand-set dirty flag is one forgotten site from a lost write across a restart). It reads, iterates
  and serialises as the value; a new, cloned or deserialised one starts marked, so the first save
  after it is never skipped. The mark over-approximates (a `get_mut` that changes nothing marks),
  so a marked value still goes through the old text comparison: never more work than before.
- **`Board::sessions` is `Tracked<Vec<SessionRecord>>`.** `persist_sessions` returns at once while
  it is unmarked (skipping `started::fold`'s key per record too: a conversation key changes only on
  a record), and marks it clean after a save that succeeded or a barred one. `sessions_written` and
  `persist_sessions` as the single write path are unchanged.
- **The crown ledger's six fields** (`crown_wakes`, `crown_heard`, `turns_open`, `turn_asks`,
  `lingered`, `crown_watched`) are `Tracked`, and `crown_written_for` is the crown the last write
  was for, since a change of hands moves no field. `persist_crown` builds `ledger()` only when one
  is marked or the crown changed.
- **Two tick stages took `&mut` every tick and changed nothing**, which would have kept the mark
  set: `refresh_panes` walked the records with `iter_mut` (now by index, writing only a title that
  moved) and `hear_lingering` called `lingered.retain` every bucket (now only when an id is gone);
  the Codex orphan `retain` runs only on orphans. The other tick-time sites mutate only on an event.
- **`cost::save`** serialises `{schema_version, tickets: &ledger.tickets}` instead of cloning the
  2 MB ledger to set its version; its round-trip test asserts the bytes equal the owned ledger's,
  so a field added to `Ledger` and not to the borrowed body fails there.

**Measured** (ignored tests `how_long_a_big_sessions_save_takes` and
`how_long_a_big_crown_ledger_check_takes`, run with `--ignored --nocapture`): 655 generated records
(`sessions.json` 1.21 MB) and a ledger that heard 650 workers (233 KB). An unchanged
`persist_sessions` took 20.3 ms in a debug build (0.8–1.2 ms release) and now takes ~10 ns; an
unchanged `persist_crown` took 5.2 ms debug (0.64 ms release) and now ~10 ns. The crown figure is
`ledger()`'s work replayed on the fixture, since no unit test builds a `Daemon`. A real change of
one record still pays the serialisation and `write_atomic`'s fsync (30 ms debug, 9–11 ms release).

**Left as it was:** a parked seat keeps its `argv` (T-838's separate decision); a real record change
still writes the whole file.

## A Codex seat held past its turn says why, and the idle audit lets it go (T-843, 2026-10-17, the author: "Codex remote control is bug … It's reported as running, and in remote control it looks like it's 'replying' indefinitely")

**What was found.** T-34 on the axiom board (Codex 0.163.0, `gpt-6-astra`, guardian auto-review
on, Playwright MCP, two sub-agents, a mid-turn compaction, two dev servers left running) ran one
turn from 17:22:23Z. Codex's own rollout wrote `task_complete` for that turn at 17:53:12Z, and
Codex's log shows the app-server sent `turn/completed` to the runtime's one connection at that
second. An hour later the record still read `running` with the same `codex_turn_id`, the runtime's
snapshot sat at sequence 15 with `observation_hold: true`, the preview's activity was the last
`item/agentMessage/delta`'s "replying" (what Remote Control shows while the state is Running), and
a prompt sent from the phone at 17:29Z was still `pending_submit` — nothing presses Enter into a
seat the snapshot calls held. Replaying the runtime's own idle audit read-only against the same
socket (`thread/loaded/list`, `thread/list ancestorThreadId`, `thread/read` each) found the
parent and both sub-agent threads idle and every item of the turn terminal: the audit would have
passed. It never ran, because `poll_audit` runs it only while the ledger is clean
(`can_reconcile_work`: no started-and-uncompleted item, no hook run, no unknown request id), and
the hold was exactly such bookkeeping. Which bucket held is not on disk: Codex's log keeps event
names without payloads in a bounded ring (the first 19 minutes of the turn were gone), the rollout
records no `item_started`, and the ledger lives in the runtime's memory. The state was `Running`,
not `RequiresAction`, so no approval request or active flag held it; `turn/completed` was
delivered, so the terminal outcome was set; what remained was an item, a hook run or a request id
the ledger never saw close. The same shape, for a compaction, was T-398.

**What shipped.**
- `Snapshot.hold` (`codex::Hold`): the ledger's buckets by count and the pending items' kinds
  (up to eight), `turn_closed`, the native requests the audit waits on, `since_ms` and
  `closed_since_ms`. Written on every heartbeat, never a sequence bump. The next such seat is
  read off `cdx-<sid16>.json`.
- `Ledger::closed_but_held`: the turn closed (`turn/completed` seen), nothing asks a person on
  this thread or a known descendant, no capacity loss, and bookkeeping or late work still holds.
  It asks for the audit (`needs_work_audit`), and a passing audit (`reconcile_work`: the parent
  idle, every loaded and descendant thread idle, nothing changed during the walk) clears the
  items, hooks, unknown request ids and the known children's same, then projects the turn's end
  as it would have — `TurnEnded{Completed}` once, `published_completions` as before. Requests and
  flags are never cleared: `closed_but_held` is false while one stands. A running turn is never
  "closed", so the audit's cadence during a turn is unchanged.
- `Snapshot.releases` / `last_release`: counted and worded by the runtime; the daemon's journal
  says `codex <sid16>: released a turn held past its close — <reasons>` once per release, and
  `codex <sid16>: held N s past its turn's close — <reasons>` once per turn after a minute. The
  count is seeded on first sight, so a daemon restart repeats nothing.

**Not done, on purpose.** The ledger learns a child only from a `collabAgentToolCall` item's
`receiverThreadIds`; Codex 0.163 names a child in a `subAgentActivity` item's `agentThreadId`
(T-815 saw the rename), so a 0.163 child is never in `children` and a child outliving its
parent's turn does not hold the seat. Teaching it is one line in `observe_item`, but it adds a
hold source and the audit's cadence during every child turn, and the rig's child case is the
test — a ticket of its own. The audit's gate on *any* in-flight native request
(`native_requests.is_empty()`) is unchanged and now visible in `Hold.native_requests`; if a
TUI request ever stays open, the held line will say so.

**The live seat.** The running runtime keeps the old ledger; a sleep and wake of the agent builds
a fresh one from an audit and is the workaround until main carries this and the daemon restarts.

Tests: `observation::tests::{a_closed_turn_held_by_stale_bookkeeping_releases_only_through_the_audit,
the_audit_never_releases_a_closed_turn_that_asks_a_person, a_running_turn_is_never_a_closed_one}`,
`runtime::tests::a_closed_turn_held_by_a_stale_item_is_released_by_the_idle_audit_and_counted`,
`provider_e2e::a_codex_seat_held_past_its_turn_and_its_release_reach_the_journal`.

## A Codex steer goes into the running turn (T-845, 2026-10-17, from T-843's finding: a steer sent at 17:29Z on the axiom board's T-34 "Sending… Awaiting delivery" for the whole turn)

**What was wrong.** Remote Control's Steer (and the board's plain send) reaches a Codex seat through
`paste_at`, whose Codex branch parked the words for `drive_codex_inputs`, which pastes only into an
idle seat. The phone's "Goes in now, mid-turn." waited for the turn's end, and a new turn by hand
(`ack_owed`) or a wake dropped the words unsaid.

**What Codex does.** Codex 0.163's TUI sends what is entered during a turn as `turn/steer`
(`{threadId, input, expectedTurnId}` → `{turnId}`, from `codex app-server generate-ts`); its
queue is a separate key. Measured on the rig (`--only steer`, `gpt-6-luna` low): the steer did
not stop a running `sleep 15`. The model read it at the turn's next step, a tool yield 0.85 s
after the send and 14.7 s before the command ended. The same turn then replied to it. So the
phone's line for a Codex seat says **"Goes into this turn at its next step."**, Claude's keeps
"Goes in now, mid-turn.", and Queue's is "Waits for the turn to end." for both
(`queue.js::modeHelp`).

**What shipped.**
- The runtime counts `turn/steer` requests on the foreground thread whose answer carries no error
  (`Snapshot.steers`, serde default, written on the heartbeat, no sequence bump). A steer the
  server refuses (the turn ended under it) or another thread's is not counted.
- `paste_at` on a Codex seat in `Running` whose count the daemon has read (`codex_steers`) takes
  `codex_steer`: the box must read as a box (`codex::input_ready`; a dialog hides the cursor and
  is refused with `ANSWER_IN_PANE_FIRST`, T-568), then bracketed paste, and an `Owed` with
  `steer: Some(count at the paste)` whose Enter `settle_owed` presses a cadence later
  (`press_steer`). The Enter repeats only while the box still holds text
  (`codex::composer_holds_text`: the cursor off the prompt's start; the placeholder sits in the
  same cells, so the cursor is the one sign) and never at `RequiresAction`. An empty box means
  the words went; the presses run out either way (`SUBMIT_ATTEMPTS` × `SUBMIT_RETRY_MS`) and a
  steer never counted is `prompt_submit_gave_up`, the phone's `unknown`. The ack is the count
  passing the paste's (`codex_steered`, then `ack_owed`'s `prompt_submitted`), or a new turn if
  the turn ended and the Enter started one.
- The phone's receipt for a Codex steer is `awaiting_delivery` until that ack, then `submitted`;
  a second steer while one is owed is refused ("a prompt is already waiting"), not a cancel of
  the first.
- Any other Codex seat (idle, spawning, at a dialog, unread count) keeps the parked road.

**Not done.** A daemon handover forgets an owed steer (the `Owed` ledger is memory): its words are
in Codex's box or its turn, and the phone's receipt reads as the restart left it. The count can
be raced by a steer a person typed in the pane between the paste and the Enter; that acks ours.
The parked road's drop on a hand-typed turn or a wake is unchanged.

Tests: `runtime::tests::a_steer_counts_when_the_server_takes_it_on_the_foreground_thread`,
`codex::tests::a_running_turns_composer_is_a_box_and_its_cursor_says_whether_it_holds_text`,
`provider_e2e::{a_steer_goes_into_a_running_codex_turn_and_is_acked_by_the_runtime,
a_codex_dialog_refuses_a_steer_in_the_boards_words, an_unacked_codex_steer_is_pressed_once_and_given_up}`,
the Codex rig's `steer` case, `state.test.js`'s help-line test and the UX suite's Codex seat.

## The trust dialog is accepted from the board and from a phone (T-844, 2026-10-17, the author: "allow users to accept remotely since they are running inside mesimon and consent was explicitly given anyway. right now, users of mesimon remote control are stuck and there's no way out unless they return to their computer")

**Why.** Claude Code asks whether to trust a folder before it works there for the first time,
and the question comes before any hook fires: `SessionStart` lands only once it is answered.
A seat on it read SETUP at the 10 s startup probe (`SpawnProbe`: bytes, no title), its launch
words were abandoned as `unsent` (`pressable()` is false on any `RequiresAction`), and the one
road out was the pane. A phone saw "needs attention" with nothing to tap. T-762 had documented
the way out (trust the root once); T-824 had given Codex's folder dialog a TRUST card and the
words "open its pane". Both left the person at the keyboard.

**What shipped.**

- **The dialog is read off the pane** (`trust_dialog.rs`, the daemon's `probe_claude_startup`,
  one `capture-pane` a second for a Claude seat at `Spawning`, `StartupModal` or `Trust`, the
  cadence `probe_codex_startup` already pays). Claude Code 2.1.302 spells the dialog in its
  binary: the `Accessing workspace:` heading, the `Quick safety check` paragraph,
  `cancelFirst`, `focus: "cancel"` and `hideIndexes`, so the cursor opens on `No, exit` and the
  rows carry no numbers; the 2.1.28x shape the lab drivers answered (`❯ 1. Yes, I trust this
  folder` first) reads too, and so does Codex's `Trust this folder? › 1. Trust and continue`.
  The reader wants a heading, both rows as whole rows by their exact labels and at most one
  marker: a conversation quoting the words, a heading with one row, or the composer is `None`.
  A recognised dialog is `Signal::Attention { Trust }` (TRUST on the card, detail `Claude Code
  asks to trust this folder`; Codex's folder dialog now says `Codex asks to trust this folder`,
  its hook review keeps `open its pane`), and a composer seen in its place is `Ready`, as
  Codex's `input_ready` is. A startup modal this does not recognise reads SETUP as before.
- **The brief waits.** `settle_owed` holds a Claude seat's parked words while it stands at
  `Trust`: `next_press`, `ready_by` and, on the mod road, `bridge_by` are pushed each pass, so
  the composer and the bridge get their whole waits once the dialog goes, and the words go in
  as any launch's do — answered in the pane, from the board or from a phone. Nothing is
  marked unsent on this dialog; `relaunch_silent_mods` and `rescue_silent_mods` never saw it
  (both want `Spawning`, and the first wants a composer).
- **The accept is the dialog's own keys**, on Remote Control's dialog road: the daemon
  projects the dialog as `DialogContent::Trust { folder }` (`control_offer_trust`, a request
  minted since no hook names one), a `DialogAnswer::Accept` walks it (`trust_step`: Down or Up
  toward the Yes row, Enter on it, the screen read before every key, a cursor on neither row
  sends nothing), and the edge is `SessionStart` (`dialog_edge`), or the seat leaving `Trust`
  with no hook to say so (Codex, or a composer seen first). No refusal road: `No, exit` ends
  the agent and stays the pane's (`dialog_plan` gives a `Reject` on a trust dialog nothing).
  A walk that sent no key puts `could not accept the trust dialog ∙ answer it in its pane` on
  the card.
- **The phone draws it from `Agent::trust`**, a field of its own (`api::Trust { request,
  folder }`), never a `dialog` kind: a browser from before this ticket would have thrown on
  `dialog.questions.map` for a kind it did not know, and it draws nothing for a field it does
  not know. The ticket page and the Now card show the folder and one button, `Yes, I trust
  this folder`, whose answer is `Request::Dialog { Accept }`; the list reads `asks for trust`.
- **The board's `w`** (`Verb::AcceptTrust`, `Ctx::ticket_trust_ready`, `Command::AcceptTrust
  { ticket }`), overlay-only: the cursor card's owed row asks `trust folder?` with
  `w confirm` beside it (`App::pending_row`, `TRUST_ROW`; the key through `ask_keys`, the
  T-551 road), and the ticket page's owed row says the same, while the subject's agent stands
  at `Trust`; inert, unhinted and rowless otherwise. It shipped first as `w trust workspace`
  in the footer, and the author: "it should say it directly on the card itself or users won't
  be able to understand what to do". `w` was free on every screen and the dialog's own
  heading is `Accessing workspace:`. The daemon runs the
  same walk under `Deliverer::Board` (`Principal::Local`), with `trust_accept` and its outcome
  in the feed and the card's state for a receipt; `agent_allows` refuses it to every agent.
  The ticket page's clause reads `it cannot start until the folder is trusted ∙ accept it here
  or in its pane`.

**Not done.** The crown gets no accept: whether one agent may trust a folder for another is a
policy question nobody asked. Claude Code's dialog on a folder that pre-approves permissions
(`No, continue without these permissions`) reads and walks the same, unmeasured live. The
phone offers no `No, exit`.

**Measured.** `cargo ut`; `trust_accept_e2e` (a Python stub painting 2.1.302's dialog with the
cursor on `No, exit`: TRUST with its words before any hook, the brief still owed past a 3 s
composer wait with no key sent, `Command::AcceptTrust` → `Down`, `Enter` and nothing else, the
composer painted, `SessionStart`, the brief pasted, `trust_accept ∙ answered` in the feed);
`provider_e2e::worktree_trust_calls_for_the_person_before_delivering_the_queued_prompt` with
the new Codex words; the phone's `ux.test.js` trust case (chromium). Tests:
`trust_dialog::tests::*`, `mesophon::tests::a_trust_dialog_walks_to_yes_and_takes_no_refusal`,
`keymap::tests::w_trusts_the_workspace_only_while_the_dialog_stands`.

## A Codex 0.163 sub-agent holds the seat until the audit reads it idle (T-848, 2026-10-17, from T-843's "Not done")

**What was wrong.** The ledger learned a child thread only from a `collabAgentToolCall` item's
`receiverThreadIds` (Codex 0.153). Codex 0.163 names one in a `subAgentActivity` item
(`{type, id, kind: started|interacted|interrupted|completed, agentThreadId, agentPath, model?,
reasoningEffort?}`, camelCase, from `codex app-server generate-json-schema` and the rig's own
parent turns; the activity's `completed` lands on the parent's turn as a second item). So
`children` stayed empty and a child outliving its parent's turn was never named in the hold.

**What shipped.** `observation::child_ids` reads either shape, and both the parent's
`observe_item` and a child's own `ChildWork::item` (a grandchild) go through it, so a 0.163
child is known, `discover_descendants` walks it, `needs_work_audit` asks for the audit, the
audit must read it (`apply_audit`'s coverage), and `Snapshot.hold.children` says so. Any `kind`
names the child; an activity's `completed` is a hint like `agentsStates`, never a release.
A child-only hold released by a clean audit is the ordinary road, not counted in `releases`
(that count is T-843's bookkeeping releases).

**The rig did not bite, and now does.** The child case passed on the old code: on 0.163 the
seat was held by luck (the TUI's open `native_requests`, below, outlast a four-second child), and
the case checked only that the seat was held. It now reads the runtime's own `hold` beside each observation and fails
when the parent's turn has closed under a live child and the hold does not name it — measured:
the old reading fails in those words, this branch passes (`gpt-6-luna` low, Codex 0.163.0).

**The audit's cadence, measured.** No backoff: with the child running, the audit was not even
attempted (one audit in the whole run, passing), and the isolated app-server's log stayed empty.

**Not done, measured.** The release comes 15–27 s after the child goes idle, on the old code
too: Codex 0.163's TUI sends `plugin/list` four times at startup and each stays open ~27 s, and
`poll_audit` waits for `native_requests` to empty — any request, read-only included. That is
T-843's gate, visible as `Hold.native_requests`; loosening it to mutations is a ticket of its own.

Tests: `observation::tests::{a_sub_agent_activity_names_a_child_that_holds_the_closed_turn_until_audited,
a_childs_own_sub_agent_activity_names_a_grandchild}`,
`runtime::tests::a_sub_agent_outliving_its_parents_turn_holds_until_the_audit_reads_it_idle`,
the Codex rig's `child` case.
## Codex questions and approvals answerable from the phone and the crown (T-846, 2026-10-17)

**What was wrong.** A Codex approval (`item/commandExecution/requestApproval`,
`item/fileChange/requestApproval`, `item/permissions/requestApproval`, an MCP elicitation with
`codex_approval_kind: mcp_tool_call`) or question (`item/tool/requestUserInput`) reached the
board as `needs you` with the right reason, and nothing but the terminal could answer it. Remote
Control's cards were filled from Claude's hook stream alone (`control_observe_dialog` off the
`AskUserQuestion` payload, `control_permission_wait` off the `PermissionRequest` hook); a Codex
stop drew no card. The crown's one rule, `CrownMode::takes_stop`, said a codex has no dialog the
board answers, so `asks_the_crown` never woke the crown for one and `answer_agent` refused it.
The runtime saw the whole request on the WebSocket and threw its content away, keeping only the
id and the reason.

**What shipped.**
- `codex::Ask` on the runtime's snapshot (`Snapshot.request`): the open request's content, by its
  id — a question's words, header and options (`AskKind::Question`), or an approval's kind in a
  word (`command`, `edit`, `permissions`, `mcp_tool`), its command, folder, reason and the
  decisions Codex offered (`AskKind::Approval`). The command comes off the request where it
  carries one, else off the started `commandExecution` item the request names by `itemId`
  (`PendingItem.command`). Bounded (four questions, eight options, a thousand chars a field,
  sixteen asks), never a reply's text; a secret question is carried marked `secret`; a form
  that is not Codex's one-tool approval carries nothing. The ledger keeps the asks beside its
  `requests` (`Ledger.asks`, a known child's too) and `serverRequest/resolved` drops the one it
  names; an idle reconcile drops them all. `Update.ask` reports the oldest open one on every
  update, so the snapshot mirrors the ledger.
- The daemon projects it (`control_codex_ask`, after each snapshot pass): a question into
  `control.dialogs` as the hook stream's `AskUserQuestion` lands there, so the phone's card,
  `get_ticket`'s `needs_you` and the crown read the same thing; an approval into
  `control.permissions` as `api::Permission { tool: <what>, input: {command, cwd, reason} }`,
  where a phone is paired to answer it; the plan a Codex seat stopped on into `control.dialogs`
  as a `Plan`, off `Snapshot.plan`. The request id changing is its resolution: the projection
  goes and the dialog's edge reads `Answered` — the confirmation a walked answer's receipt waits
  for, where Claude's waits for the `PostToolUse` (T-567). A secret or a form projects nothing.
- `PermissionWait.road`: `Hook { stream, renews, closed }` (Claude's `mesimon approve`) or
  `Codex`. A phone's allow or deny on a Codex approval is an `ApprovalDelivery`, walked one key a
  tick (`control_deliver_approvals`) to the first `Yes` row or the one `No` row and Enter
  (`codex_approval_step`), the receipt `awaiting_delivery` → `answered` on the request's
  resolution, `input_sent` past `DIALOG_CONFIRM`, `unknown` with its reason. Each key is bound
  to the request the phone answered, not to the rows alone: the screen must show the request's
  reason, or without one the end of its command (the item spells `/bin/zsh -lc '…'`, the dialog
  the words inside), and the wait's standing is re-read from the projection each key — a dialog
  that replaced the answered one between the tap and the key gets nothing (`label_not_found`).
- The dialog walk knows the harness (`dialog_step_for`, `dialog_shape_for`, by the record's
  `kind`): Codex's question dialog as measured on 0.163.0 (`codex_dialog_step`), rows `N. label
  description` with the cursor `›`, a `None of the above` row Codex adds, the footer `tab to add
  notes | enter to submit answer | esc to interrupt`; its approval dialog (`codex_approval_step`):
  `1. Yes, proceed (y)`, `2. Yes, and don't ask again …(p)`, `3. No, and tell Codex what to do
  differently (esc)`, the footer `Press enter to confirm or esc to cancel`, the heading not read
  so an edit's and a permission's dialogs are covered by their rows; its plan dialog the T-420
  press (`codex_at_default`). `numbered` and `dialog_rows_to` take `›` beside `❯`.
- What a Codex dialog takes from the board (`codex_takes`): one question's one choice, a refusal
  (Esc, which Codex reads as an interrupt) and a plan's accept. Words typed into its notes row,
  several questions, several choices and a plan sent back are unmeasured and refused in words
  — the phone's "this dialog shape is not verified", the crown's "a codex, whose dialog takes one
  choice of one question". `dialog_answerable_for` says so in `needs_you.answerable`.
- `CrownMode::takes_stop` admits an agent's question or plan (`kind.is_agent()`): a codex's wakes
  the crown as a claude's (`asks_the_crown`, `notify::scan`), and `answer_agent` and
  `accept_plan` reach it through the same road (`crown_accept_plan` and `crown_plan_allowed` take
  any agent). A permission stays the person's for both.

**Measured on Codex 0.163.0 (2026-10-17), the real rig.** A deny on the command dialog
("No, and tell Codex what to do differently") interrupts the conversation: `turn/completed`
`interrupted`, the composer back — so a phone's deny is an interrupt, as the terminal's would be.
Codex's `requestUserInput` dialog numbers its rows and adds `None of the above`; the first row is
the cursor's. The approval dialog's second row wraps across three lines at 80 columns, which
`dialog_rows_to` joins as it joins Claude's descriptions. Two more things the runs found:
- Asked to "use request_user_input once", Luna in plan mode sometimes calls
  `request_user_input_async` instead: the question arrives with `isBlocking: false`, the pane
  shows it under `Queued follow-up inputs … ⇧← to answer` while the turn keeps working, and the
  ledger leaves it as no stop, as it did before (the board shows `working`, not `needs you`). The
  rig's prompt now names the blocking tool and forbids the async one. Whether a non-blocking
  question should reach the board is a question of its own, not decided here.
- A crowned Codex seat launched with the board's tools on called `merge_ticket` instead of
  running the `sleep` it was asked for, and stopped on the one-tool MCP approval — which the
  snapshot carried as `what: mcp_tool`, `command: mesimon`, the reason naming the tool, so the
  projection held up on a real one. The rig launches the crown's seat before the tools go on.

**Not done, on purpose.** The phone's approval road is proven by unit tests on the captured
screens and by the fake runtime, not on the real rig: no Local principal walks a dialog, and the
rig has no relay. The rig's question case goes through the crown's road instead (below). A Codex
plan's reject from the phone, free words into a question and several questions at once stay the
terminal's until measured. A form (`Reason::Elicitation`) stays the terminal's.

**The rig.** `python3 -B ci/rig.py --provider codex --live --only question` is three turns now:
a crowned Codex seat kept busy on a `sleep` turn (so the question's wake queues behind it and no
model turn answers the board's words), the worker it starts in a worktree (`agent_start_ticket`
over the lab's new agent road, `lab.Client.agent`), `/plan` and the question; `get_ticket`
lists the carried question as answerable, `answer_agent` presses Enter on the chosen row and
reads `answered` on the request's resolution, the turn completes on the chosen colour, and the
snapshot has dropped the request. `ci/codex-approval-e2e.py` asserts the snapshot carries the
approval's command, reason and decisions and drops it on the native refusal.

Tests: `board::tests::takes_stop_admits_a_claude_s_and_a_codex_s_question_or_plan_alone`,
`observation::tests::{a_question_s_words_and_options_ride_the_update_until_it_is_resolved,
a_secret_question_is_carried_as_secret_and_an_unidentified_one_not_at_all,
an_approval_carries_its_item_s_command_and_the_decisions_on_offer,
a_known_child_s_question_is_carried_and_a_reconcile_clears_asks}`,
`runtime::tests::the_snapshot_carries_the_open_request_and_clears_it_when_resolved`,
`mesophon::tests::{a_codex_question_walks_its_rows_by_label_and_description,
a_codex_approval_walks_to_yes_or_no_and_confirms, a_codex_plan_takes_the_accept_at_its_yes_row_alone,
a_codex_question_is_projected_within_the_phone_s_bounds,
a_codex_approval_s_wait_has_no_run_and_is_never_renewed}`, `crownwake::tests`,
`provider_e2e::a_codex_question_is_carried_to_the_board_and_answered_by_keys_until_resolved`,
