`docs/codex-compatibility.json` under `0.163.0` (`crown_answers_native_question`,
`native_approval_carried`; the approval's `availableDecisions` there read `accept, cancel`).

## Plan mode on a Codex launch (T-847, 2026-10-18)

**What was missing.** `^p` and `plan: true` (T-434) start Claude with `--permission-mode plan`;
a Codex seat refused them (`plan_refusal`, `AgentProvider::has_plan_flag`), because Codex has no
launch flag for its plan mode.

**What Codex does, measured (0.163.0, real binary, no model turn).** `/plan` typed into the
composer switches the thread: the native client sends `thread/settings/update` with
`collaborationMode: {mode: "plan", …}`, the server answers with `thread/settings/updated`
(`threadSettings.collaborationMode.mode`), the footer ends `… Plan mode`, and a second `/plan`
leaves it in plan mode (idempotent). Nothing names the mode at thread start; every `turn/start`
carries it (an accepted plan's implementation goes back to `default` there, with no settings
notice).

**What shipped.** A Codex start, wake or idle pane asked in plan mode sets
`SessionRecord::codex_plan_owed` (persisted, serde default, skipped when false).
`drive_codex_inputs` then types `/plan` into an empty composer, presses Enter 400 ms later, and
withholds the title, the brief and the words until the thread is seen planning: the runtime's
new `Snapshot::collaboration_mode` (from the server's `thread/settings/updated` and the native
`turn/start`, foreground thread only) or `codex::plan_mode_shown` (the footer below the cursor,
for a status line that keeps it). Unseen after 5 s it is pressed again once; unseen twice, the
words go into the box **unsubmitted** (feed `codex_plan_unconfirmed`, a journal line) — never
into a default-mode turn that would do the work it was asked to plan. A live pane is not
relaunched: `deliver` routes a Codex pane's plan to `codex_park`, which never steers; mid-turn
it is refused sent now and waits its idle queued, as Claude's is. `plan_refusal` and
`has_plan_flag` are gone; the TUI offers `^p` on every seat and composer, and a Codex pane's
receipt says `asked in plan mode` / `agent plans next` instead of `restarts`. The accept road is
T-420's, unchanged. A column's `claude_mode = plan` stays Claude's (not asked for here).

Tests: `provider_e2e::{a_planned_codex_start_types_plan_first_and_its_words_wait_for_the_mode,
a_codex_pane_asked_in_plan_mode_waits_its_idle_and_types_plan_without_a_relaunch,
a_parked_codex_seat_wakes_into_plan_mode_before_its_words,
a_codex_plan_mode_never_seen_leaves_the_words_unsubmitted}` (the synthetic runtime answers a
typed `/plan` on its snapshot, its footer, or not at all);
`runtime::tests::the_foreground_threads_collaboration_mode_rides_the_snapshot`;
`codex::tests::plan_mode_is_read_off_the_footer_and_nowhere_else`;
`app::tests::ctrl_p_on_an_idle_codex_pane_asks_in_plan_mode_without_a_restart`; and the Codex
rig's `plan-launch` case, passed on `gpt-6-luna` low: the planned start stopped on its plan with
`codex_plan_mode` fed before the title, and the board's accept moved the same thread on to a
turn of its own. `plan_mode_e2e` stays Claude's: its stub harness has no Codex runtime.

## Codex parity leftovers: Sleep after, handed-over words, prices (T-849, 2026-10-18)

Three places T-843's sweep found where a Codex seat got less than a Claude seat.

**Sleep after shows on every board.** The column dialog's `Sleep after` row was hidden where no
tier used Claude (`Ctx::claude_unused`), from when nothing parked a Codex agent; column auto-sleep
has parked Codex since T-828, so the row is gated on `!col_new` alone, and the `Agent behaviour`
door's Codex spelling carries the sleep word as Claude's does (`sandbox … ∙ tools … ∙ sleep …`).

**A Codex seat's unpasted words cross a restart.** T-722 kept a Claude launch's parked words as
`unsent` on the way out and left Codex dropping its own. On the Codex road the owed entry's
`parked` is exactly what no box holds — `drive_codex_inputs` pastes title, brief and words in one
go and clears `parked` with the prefill — so `hand_over_owed` now writes it onto a Codex seat with
a pane too (directly, not through `mark_unsent`, whose other callers are Claude's give-ups and
must not start marking a Codex steer). The reconcile's Codex arm still drops `pending_submit`
without `codex_submit_sent`, and hands a record with `unsent` to `resend_after_restart`, whose
Codex branch (`repark_codex_after_restart`) parks the words again as a launch and puts the hold
back: the next idle edge the runtime proves pastes them, the title too while `pending_prefill` is
owed, with one Enter. Unlike Claude's resend it does not require a seat that never took a
prompt: the Codex road waits on the runtime's own idle and a cursor in the composer, and a turn
the runtime reports begun while the daemon was down is the person's prompt, whose ack drops the
words as it drops any ask (`ack_owed`). Words already pasted, or already entered
(`codex_submit_sent`), are unchanged — never reconstructed. A seat whose pane died meanwhile
loses them with a journal line. Feed `prompt_resent`, by `daemon`.

**Codex prices: no "est." marker.** T-815 already prices Codex rollouts at OpenAI's API rates, so
a Codex card's `$` corner is the same kind of figure as a Claude card's — both are mesimon's
API-price estimate. The author chose no Codex-only marker, which would have read Claude's figure
as exact; `docs/USING.md`'s stale "Codex shows its tokens instead" line now says how a Codex
ticket is priced.

Tests: `keymap::tests::the_sort_row_owns_h_and_l` (a Codex-only board lists `Sleep after` and the
door says the sleep), `provider_e2e::daemon_handover_keeps_unpasted_codex_words_and_sends_them_once`
(replaces `…_abandons_unpasted_volatile_words_…`, which pinned the old drop).

## The snapshot leaves archived tickets out, and the list asks for them (T-842, 2026-10-18)

**The cost.** After T-804 took the parked records off, the archived tickets were what remained
of the author's snapshot: measured over the socket on the release build, 0.1.0-beta.7, idle,
716 tickets, 690 of them archived:

| | bytes |
|---|---|
| whole snapshot | 567,179 |
| `board.tickets` | 446,762 |
| the 690 archived tickets | 428,031 (their `notes` metadata 162,608) |
| the 26 live tickets | 18,732 |
| sessions (14 records) | 23,320 |
| `costs`, the next largest | 78,631 |

Three quarters of every push, serialised per subscriber on the writer thread and parsed on the
TUI's UI thread, and drawn by nothing on the board: only the Esc menu's `Archived tickets` list,
the picker's archived half, a page on an archived ticket and a note's link to one read them. The
round trip was 28 ms at p50 and 37 ms at p90 on that build with the board idle — T-804's
98–161 ms was a debug build under load — so the cost was bandwidth and the parse, growing by
one ticket per ticket shipped.

**Now.** `Board::for_snapshot` (the daemon's copy, replacing `without_archived_records`) and
`Board::drop_archived` (in place) leave out every archived ticket and, as before, every paneless
record of one; an archived ticket with a pane still open rides, so a record on the snapshot
never names a ticket it lacks. `Response::Board` carries `archived`, the count, `#[serde(default)]`.
The new read `Command::ArchivedTickets` → `Response::Tickets` returns them whole, newest archive
first, the order `Board::archived_tickets` gives; `Command::meta` reads, `agent_allows` refuses.
Measured with this build on a copy of that board: `board.tickets` is 20,553 bytes (29 live
tickets, the board having moved on); the whole snapshot computes to ~139 KB against the 567 KB,
`costs` and the records untouched.

**The TUI holds them while something shows them**, T-804's mechanism grown to tickets:
`App::wants_archive` is the archived list open, the picker with its archived half on, the links
list open (a note's `T-n` may name an archived ticket), or the page on a ticket the snapshot
lacks or carries archived; `poll_archive` (in `pump`, before `poll_held`, whose `shown_archived`
reads what it lays) asks once when wanted and again after every snapshot while it stays, and
lays the tickets into `board.tickets` (`lay_tickets`: those the board lacks), where
`archived_tickets()`, `Board::ticket`, the dialog, the search, the page and the restore key read
unchanged. `absorb` lays the held set into each new board first (`lay_archive`), and when the
page's ticket left the snapshot that very pass with nothing held — archived under it by `a`
there, the crown or a phone — asks right there, or `clamp_screen` reads it as deleted and leaves
the page. Opening the list, the picker and the links list ask at once, so their first frame is
whole. `App::archived_count` is the daemon's count or what the board carries (an older daemon
sends them all and answers the ask with an error, which the TUI takes as "the board has them");
it gates the menu row, the picker's total and the list's closing. `undo_target` reads an archived
ticket as absent-and-not-in-grace, since `x` takes it off the next snapshot rather than marking
it; `unarchive`'s status says `restored` when the column is not at hand. The crown's burn plays
on a copy the board keeps (`App::burnt`, filled in `absorb` from the touched cards as they were,
dropped with their strikes), as the next snapshot no longer carries the card.

**What did not move.** `archive_all`, the reclaim offer's candidate set, the crown's
`archive_ticket`, the phone's `sent_archived` and board sharing all read the daemon's own
`self.board`, never the snapshot; the phone's board reply is built daemon-side. The relay's
runtime deserialises no `Response::Board` (it imports `mesimon_team` alone); its half is one
assertion in `relay/tests/board_e2e.rs`, on `msmn/T-842-archived-tickets-off-the`. The shape is
serde-additive both ways: an old TUI on a new daemon shows an empty list and no menu row until
the `U` handover the build-skew notice already asks for; a new TUI on an old daemon reads the
board it is sent. The tour's toy daemon serves the same shape and the same ask.

**Refuted:** ids or keys of the archived tickets on the snapshot beside the count (~20–30 KB,
one sixth of what remains) so every id-keyed reader stays exact; the count plus "absent and
not in grace" was enough, and the ask decides the one case that matters (the page). Paging the
ask: one answer of 428 KB when a list opens beats 428 KB on every push; a `since`/`limit`
field can come later as `#[serde(default)]`.

Tests: `board::tests::the_snapshot_drops_only_paneless_records_of_archived_tickets` (the ticket
cut, the pane exception and the count), `archive_e2e` (off the snapshot, listed, counted),
`TestClient::{archived, ticket_any, is_archived}` for every e2e that read an archived ticket
off the snapshot, `app::tests::{archived_tickets, archived_ticket}` for the TUI's; the goldens
with an archived ticket on screen call `poll_archive` as the loop does.

## Setup holds still, and asks only what a newcomer can answer (T-850, 2026-10-18, the author: "no moving cards on preview … the current is overwhelming and user won't be able to understand what the heck is going on" ∙ "remove brief section … it's in the README" ∙ "add (recommended) next to recommended things" ∙ "remove agents section, they should do everything anyway")

**The preview is a still board.** T-816's scenes (beats, keys pressed on the practice board,
cards arriving, a typed Shift+Enter ask) are gone with their player: each page lays a fresh toy
world from the answers (`Setup::lay`) and nothing moves. A page shows the card or two its
question is about, where the answer under the cursor puts them, with the agent at work or done
and its peek saying one short line an agent would say there ("main moved on; updating PR #412.").
Sessions are pushed by hand (`setup::agent`), never through `World::session`, whose automove
would move the card. The lines are short enough for a card's two peek rows at 110 columns. The
preview is drawn one row taller than shown (`tour::lay_board`'s `crop`), so the practice board's
key footer falls off: its keys are not Setup's.

**The pages.** How you work has a third answer, I'm not sure, which is on your own (straight into
main, no PRs). On your own asks about merging and stops; with pull requests asks about falling
behind, then the board, which offers only the two pull request templates (Kanban is what on your
own gets, unasked). A folder of projects still asks about worktrees. The Agents page is gone:
every board Setup makes gets `AgentTools::Full`, sent by `finish_setup` (`Outcome` lost the
field; the wire's `ApplySetup.agent_tools` is unchanged). The Brief page is gone, and with it
`Ctx::setup_single`. Each question's default is its recommended answer and is marked
`(recommended)` (`Opt::recommended`); how you work and the last page recommend nothing.

**The brief lives in the README.** Promise 3 now points at the brief below it, shown in a
`text` block, and `brief::the_readme_shows_the_text` holds the README to `brief::TEXT`. PROMISES,
USING, the site and the CLAUDE.md boundary line say the README shows it.

**Settings › About** (`SettingsSection::About`, not board-scoped): the version over one row,
Project page, whose value is the repository (`keymap::PROJECT_PAGE`, `CARGO_PKG_REPOSITORY`) and
whose Enter opens it (`open_outside`). The section sweep's goldens mask the version in its own
width so a release bump drifts nothing.

Tests: `setup::every_page_holds_still_and_speaks` (no card arrived from anywhere, every agent
says something, nothing refused, every page, answer, workflow and forge),
`the_pages_follow_how_you_work`, `the_default_is_the_recommended_answer`,
`not_sure_goes_straight_into_main`, `skipping_everything_is_the_defaults`,
`the_answers_become_the_outcome`; `app::about_opens_the_project_page`,
`ui::settings_about_shows_the_version_and_the_project`; goldens `setup_board_120x30`,
`setup_merge_120x30`, `settings_about_*` new, `setup_brief_120x36` removed, the other setup and
Settings goldens reminted (one row, About, in the section list). `setup_e2e` green. No rig test:
nothing an agent is told changed.

**Addendum (T-850, same day, the author: "can't quit setup without applying. ctrl+c not
working (and there should be an easier way too, q for example)").** T-816's "don't allow to exit
the setup" is reversed. `q` and `Esc` (one binding, as the q-pops law asks of every scope) leave
Setup on any page with nothing applied: the board as it starts, `App::setup_done` (was
`setup_applied`) keeping it closed for this run, and `setup_pending` still on, so the next open of
the folder asks again. `^c` is `Verb::Quit` there as on the board, overlay-only. Esc's "skip the
rest" went with it (`Setup::skip_rest`): at two to four pages, `s` does the same. Setup is still a
barrier for every board key. Tests: `app::setup_q_and_esc_leave_with_nothing_applied`,

## A refused credential pairs again (T-852, 2026-10-18)

**What was wrong.** A browser keeps its relay credential in IndexedDB. When the relay no longer
knew it (its database reset), `/control` closed the socket with no frame, which the page reads
as a network loss: `Connection::connect` retried the same credential three times on a code and
said "Pairing did not complete", and a fresh code never helped. Only clearing the site's data
got out.

**Shipped.** The relay says the refusal: `Wire::Error { code: control::DENIED }` before any
`Authenticated`, for a credential it does not know or a registration of a key it already holds;
a fault (`Unavailable`) stays a bare close. The page's `connect` reads `denied` only before
`authenticated` and only when it sent a credential: it deletes the credential, saves, and the
next attempt registers with the same seed, so the device id is unchanged and a host that lists
it (after the reset, on its next publish) reaches the same boards. The line is authentication,
never a board: an `error` after `authenticated` (an away host, a removed grant, which the relay
deliberately does not tell apart) keeps the credential and the boards as before. A host reads
any first frame but `Authenticated` as a failed connect, as it read the close; the mailbox
socket ignores every frame before `authenticated`. The relay half is on
`msmn/T-852-pairing-hangs-on-pairing-when` in `mesimon-relay`.

**Not done.** A registration the relay refuses after the credential was dropped (a known key)
is left to the old retry and its message: no browser device is disabled or deleted at the relay
today, so minting a new seed there would orphan the store's sealing keys for a case that does
not occur.

Tests: `ux.test.js`'s `refusedFlow` (the fixture relay forgets a credential; a code pairs at
once, the refused credential sent once and then a registration; a valid credential and one whose
host is away kept across reloads), `control::tests::the_page_reads_the_denied_word` (the page's
literal is the wire's), and the relay's `an_unknown_credential_is_refused_in_words`.

## Pictures go with the words to an agent (T-853, 2026-10-18, "pictures inside ask agent prompt")

**Asked.** "currently sending pictures is not possible when using shift+enter to ask the agent
or from remote control send message. should 'just work'."

**Measured first.** Claude Code 2.1.302's mod submit takes text alone: `$.prompt.submit`
answers "takes text alone; attachments cannot be submitted" (the engine's `CJo` destructures
`attachments` only to refuse a non-empty one), and the paste road is a bracketed paste of
text. So no road carries image bytes into a turn. What every road, Claude and Codex, hook set
and mod, already carries is the ticket's pictures through `read_attachment` (T-402, T-629).

**Decided: the picture is the ticket's, and the words name it.** A pictured ask goes as a note
does: the picture is uploaded (the desk's `UploadAttachment` chunks, the phone's `Upload`
pieces), `PromptSession` and the phone's `Prompt` and `Start` carry `uploads`, the daemon keeps
each picture at `attachments/<id>.png` beside the ticket's notes BEFORE the words go (an agent
may read it the moment it has the words), and the words reach the agent as
`[Image #N](mesimon-attachment:<id>)`, which `read_attachment` serves; its tool text now names
a prompt as a place such a link appears. A send the daemon refuses lets the pictures go again
(`Daemon::with_pictures`, one helper under both the desk's dispatch arm and the phone's
`control_pictured`), and an upload the words do not name is refused ("the words do not name
that picture") before anything is kept. Promise 3 holds as it does for a note: the person put
`[Image #N]` in the words, and the link is the picture's own address, nothing of mesimon's.

**Desk.** The ask room is the note editor (T-380), so `^v` there is the note's clipboard read
(`image_paste`), gated by `Ctx::ask_ticket`: a ticket's ask, never a column's, which has no
ticket to keep a picture. The one-line field's `^v` grows into the room and reads the clipboard
there (`Verb::EditorPaste` in `INPUT`), so a picture never needs the room opened first.
`Editor::new` unpacks an ask's links too, so a taken-back ask shows `[Image #N]` and folds back
into the field with its link whole (`fold_ask` packs). `upload_draft` takes the body's limit
(`EditorPurpose::body_limit`: a prompt's 4 KiB, a note's 32 KiB), and `editor_send` uploads,
sends, then discards the staging as `write_note` does.

**Phone.** The composer gets the note sheet's picture road (`PicturePick`, the icon alone beside
the arrow, and `PictureList` under the words), on a host that says `ask_pictures`; the pictures
go up first (`sendPicturedPrompt`), then the words linked, on `prompt` or on `start` from the
same field. The receipt keeps the draft's own words, so a refusal gives them back with the
pictures still held, and a taken prompt drops them (`sessions::dropPictures`). The caret marks
on input too: the earlier draft's caret put the token mid-word in the first run.

**Tests.** Core: `Request::Prompt`/`Start` parse and skip `uploads`; `a_ticket_ask_takes_a_picture_and_a_column_ask_does_not`
(keymap). TUI: `a_picture_pasted_into_an_ask_rides_the_prompt_as_an_upload`. E2e:
`attachments_e2e::a_prompt_with_a_picture_keeps_it_with_the_ticket_and_links_it_in_the_words`
(the unnamed upload refused and kept nowhere, the linked words in the pane, the picture read
by the desk and by the agent's shim). Page: the tier flow picks a picture on the composer,
sends, and reads the upload for the ticket and the linked words on the prompt. Rig: `P6`
(`picture_ask`, a solid red PNG: `tools:read_attachment`, `reply:red`), run once on Sonnet.
**Owed:** a CHANGELOG line at the next bump — **Added:** a picture can go with the words you
send an agent, from the board's ask (Ctrl+V) and from Remote Control's composer.

## A slow daemon is said as slow, and the board keeps drawing while it reconnects (T-856, 2026-10-18, "mesimon became extremely slow on my work computer")

The author, on their work machine, a board that merges through pull requests: "often it says
'daemon unreachable reconnecting' and hangs for a long time (30 second) and I can't do anything
while it's that way. happens every minute or so, happened since last update (jumped 2
versions)". Half an hour later: "looks like it is better now … i was on a zoom call while it
happened so maybe it's related".

**What the words meant.** `Conn::request` waits 10 s for the writer thread's answer and then
drops the connection, and `App::note_daemon_down` said "unreachable" for every failed request.
A reconnect ran on the loop's own thread: `open_current` → `connect_or_spawn` (connects at once
when the daemon is up — its listener thread accepts while the writer is busy) → `hello` → a
`Hello` and a `Subscribe` of 10 s each against the same busy writer, every 2 s. So a writer
turn of S seconds froze the board for S plus a handshake per cadence, said as an outage: a
20 s turn read as 30 s of "unreachable". The daemon was up the whole time.

**What stalls the writer.** Every tick forks `tmux` (`pane_facts`, the recovery captures), `ps`
(`refresh_rss`) and, on the slow bucket, `git` (`upstream_base`, `reclaim_archived` →
`ticket_merged`: one to three forks per leg, more on a PR board where the forge's word is asked
at the tip), all synchronous on the single writer. This machine's own journals show the same
stages at 1–8 s whenever something else loads the box (the e2e suite, 2026-09-16 and
2026-10-17: `refresh_titles 7783 ms`, `refresh_rss 8029 ms`, `refresh_panes 3397 ms`). A Zoom
call is that load on a work laptop: a fork that takes 50 ms idle takes seconds, the tick's
dozen forks add up past the board's patience, and the slow bucket and the forge minute stack
on top — "every minute or so". The version jump reads as coincidence: nothing in beta.7 or
beta.8 adds a per-minute writer fork, and beta.8's T-838 took git and the transcript tails
*out* of the snapshot. The forge's own reads (`gh`, `glab`, the probe) were already on a
worker and never blocked the writer; the one writer-side forge fork is `ssh -G`, once per
repository, under 3 s.

**Applied.**
- **The status row tells slow from gone.** `client::ResponseTimeout` is the typed error of a
  request the daemon took and did not answer in `RESPONSE_WAIT`; `client::outage` reads an
  error as `Slow`, `Gone` or `Dialing`, and `note_daemon_down(outage)` says
  `daemon slow ∙ <what> took <n> s ∙ <stage> ∙ reconnecting` from the journal's newest `slow
  turn` of the last ten minutes (the turn before this one — a line is written when a turn
  ends), `daemon slow ∙ reconnecting ∙ doctor names its slow turns` with none, and
  `daemon unreachable ∙ reconnecting` only when the daemon hung up or is not there. A reopen
  still dialling changes nothing said. A key's refusal (`App::req`) carries the row's words.
- **The reconnect runs off the loop.** `Client::reopened` spawns `open_current` on a thread and
  answers `Reopening` until the connection lands; the dial, a spawn, a handover wait, the
  handshake and a skew restart all happen there, and the board keeps drawing with the last
  snapshot. A daemon that is slow now costs one `RESPONSE_WAIT` on the request that found it,
  not that plus a handshake per 2 s. `legacy_daemon` is left alone while a reopen is in
  flight, so an older daemon's `U upgrades` does not flicker to `unreachable` between
  attempts. The observer's road (`open_existing`) and `Shutdown` on a dropped connection are
  unchanged; `Client::connect` at launch still blocks, under its `LateWord`.
- **`doctor` lists the slow turns.** `Journal::slow_turns(path, since_ms, n)` reads the lines
  back as `SlowTurn { what, took_ms, stage }` (the `iso_utc` stamp orders as text, so the
  floor is a string compare); the daemon section prints the last 24 h's three newest, newest
  first, as a `WARN` with the advice that each is a writer turn past 1 s and the stage is
  where the time went. `ok ∙ none in the last 24 h` otherwise.
- **The archive reclaim forks nothing for a queued teardown.** `reclaim_on_archive` asked
  `ticket_merged` (git) before checking `pending_teardown` and `tearing_down`; the free checks
  come first now, and `process_teardowns` judges the tree again where it lands, as it did.

**Left open, the structural fix:** the tick's forks belong on a worker, as the git sample, the
worktree flags and the forge already are — `refresh_panes`/`pane_facts`, `refresh_rss`, the
recovery captures and `reclaim_archived`'s `ticket_merged`. The journal names which stage a
given machine pays for; the author's work machine's `daemon.log` has that answer for the Zoom
case and was not read here. A follow-up ticket per stage, each with its slow-turn line as the
brief.

**Tests.** `journal::slow_turns_read_back_newest_first_above_the_floor`;
`app::a_slow_daemon_is_said_as_slow_not_unreachable` (a transport that times out reads
`daemon slow`, a dial in flight leaves it, a hang-up reads `unreachable`, a key's refusal
carries the row); `restart_skew_e2e` drives the real client's connect and observer roads
unchanged. **Owed:** CHANGELOG lines at the next bump — **Changed:** when the daemon is slow to
answer, the board says `daemon slow` with what it was doing, keeps drawing and reconnects in
the background; it said `daemon unreachable` and froze. **Added:** `mesimon doctor` lists the
daemon's slow turns of the last day.

## The tick's tmux, ps and git forks ride a worker (T-857, 2026-10-18, the structural fix T-856 left open)

T-856's "Left open": every tick forked `tmux` (`pane_facts`, the startup and activity probes,
the Claude and Codex startup screens, the composer reads for owed words, `server_alive`, the
folder probe) and `ps` (the RSS figure, the bash-mode foreground) on the single writer thread,
and `reclaim_archived` asked git (`ticket_merged`) every bucket for an archived tree still
standing. Under load a fork that takes 50 ms idle takes seconds, and every hook frame, client
request and other board waited behind the tick.

**Measured, before** (`slow_tmux_e2e` against the unchanged daemon: `MESIMON_TMUX_BIN` a
wrapper that sleeps 2 s before the real tmux, one Spawning stub): `tick took 4068 ms ∙ slowest
stage refresh_panes 2033 ms`, `tick took 6102 ms ∙ slowest stage probe_spawning 4052 ms`,
`tick took 8155 ms ∙ slowest stage refresh_rss 4083 ms`, `tick took 4072 ms ∙ slowest stage
guard_server 2037 ms`, and `tick took 2036 ms ∙ slowest stage probe_spawning 0 ms` — the
unnamed 2 s was `probe_claude_startup`, which ran outside a `stage!`. A `Snapshot` round-trip
hit the test client's 10 s read timeout, and so did the reconnect's `Hello`.

**Applied: the pane sampler (`daemon/src/panes.rs`).** The same shape as the git sample, the
worktree flags and the forge. The writer builds a `panes::Query` from its state over the ticks
(`want_panes`, `want_rss`, `want_recovery` for the startup and activity channels,
`want_claude_startup`, `want_codex_startup`, `want_owed_screens`, `want_guard`,
`want_server_access`); `queue_pane_sample` hands it to one worker thread when none is out
(`TmuxBackend` is `Clone` now; the worker runs `panes::take`); the answers land as
`Msg::PaneSampled` carrying the time the reads began; and `on_pane_sampled` runs each stage's
absorb under the stage's own name (`refresh_panes`, `refresh_rss`, `probe_spawning`,
`probe_activity`, `probe_claude_startup`, `probe_codex_startup`, `guard_server`,
`recheck_server_access`), so a slow absorb is still journalled as the probe it is. A bucket that
comes round while a sample is out adds to the query rather than skipping: the read is late,
never lost.
- **Time is the sample's.** Every observation is fed `sample.at`, never `now()` at absorb
  (`core/src/attention.rs` is time-injected on purpose): a silence is as long as it was when
  tmux was asked; a startup probe is dated when the pane was read.
- **A result that lands after the session moved on is dropped.** Each absorb re-reads its
  candidates off the board as it stands: `absorb_startup` only for a record still `Spawning`;
  `absorb_activity` against `needs_poll`'s activity arm again (stateless: `Running`, not
  observe-only); the startup probes against their state filter; the guard only for a pane whose
  `state_changed_at` is not after the read (a pane spawned or woken since stands on a server the
  read never saw).
- **`needs_poll` stays on the writer** (`recovery_candidates`): the startup channel's stage
  advances when it says yes, so a candidate is asked exactly once and its answer comes back
  through the sample. `feed_recovery` is the one road every channel's sample takes into the
  adapter and the machine; the status-file and transcript channels read files and stay on the
  tick as they were.
- **The composer read is off the sampler's newest screen.** `settle_owed` consults
  `Daemon::screens` (the newest `InputScreen` per pane, with its sample's time) and asks the next
  sample for another, so the next cadence reads fresh; `want_owed_screens` asks every bucket for
  every pane with words parked, so the screen is at most a second old when the words are due —
  the fork it replaced was no fresher under load. `Owed::screen_after` is the stamp a screen
  must postdate: the entry's birth (a wake reuses the pane's name, and the old pane's screen must
  not paste into the new one before it asks for bracketed paste, T-570) and the one Ctrl+C of a
  resend. An older screen reads as no composer, and the `COMPOSER_WAIT_MS` clock still bounds
  the wait.
- **`refresh_rss` reads its pane process groups off the same `pane_facts`** the titles use
  (`snapshot()` was a second fork for the same three fields), and the `ps` runs on the worker;
  the no-pane clear stays on the writer and forks nothing.
- **`reclaim_archived` passes the sample's verdict** (`reclaim_on_archive(id, Some(true))`: its
  filter already requires `wt_agg.merged` and no open PR), and `process_teardowns` makes the one
  fresh `ticket_merged` where it tears down, as it did. A person's archive (`archive_one`) still
  asks git once (`None`).
- **The journal says what tmux costs**: `slow pane sample: N tmux/ps forks took M ms, off the
  writer thread`, at most once a minute, when a sample passes `journal::SLOW_TURN`. It is the
  author's work machine's answer to "how slow is tmux here" with the board no longer paying for
  it.

**Measured, after** (the same e2e): 67 `Snapshot` round-trips over 17 s, the slowest 14–20 ms;
no slow turn in the journal; `slow pane sample: 1 tmux/ps forks took 2022 ms, off the writer
thread`.

**Still forks on the writer, and why.**
- The actions — `paste_text`, `send_enter`, `clear_input`, `kill_session`, `spawn`,
  `send_text`: a delivery or a kill is one fork at an edge, not a probe per tick, and its order
  against the record's state is the point (T-5's separate Enter; one Ctrl+C, never two).
- `drive_codex_inputs` and `press_steer` capture a screen and act on it in the same breath (a
  paste into a box seen ready, an Enter into a box seen holding): a Codex seat with words
  pending, a steer in flight — short windows, and the read-then-act pair belongs together.
- `park_inactive`'s `client_quiet_secs`: one `list-clients` for a session already due to park.
- `sweep_codex_orphans`' `panes()`: only with an orphan candidate, every 15 s.
- `probe_server_access` at the launch-death edge (T-690), once; `on_shell_env`'s
  `set_path`/`publish_path` at startup, once (the e2e waits for it before slowing tmux).
- `focus_start`'s `pane_title`, `focus_quiet`, `pane_tail`/`terminal_tail`: a person's request,
  one fork, as the `pane_tail` comment argues.
- `on_worktree_flags`' `upstream_base` on landing, once per leg per fetch: T-216's own road.

**Tests.** `slow_tmux_e2e` (above; a marker file turns the wrapper's sleep on after the spawn
and after the shell env landed, so what is measured is the tick's own forks; a round-trip the
client gives up on counts as its 10 s and reconnects);
`panes::tests::a_query_counts_its_forks_and_asks_each_pane_once`; `hook_e2e` and `prompt_e2e`
(the recovery and composer roads) and the full suite once, green. **Owed:** a CHANGELOG line
at the next bump — **Changed:** the board stays quick on a loaded machine: what it reads from
tmux and the process table runs beside the daemon's writer, not in its way.

## Every step that is a person's is a hand on the crown's card (T-862, 2026-10-19, "crown just say on the transcript but not notifying with a hand so i miss it sometimes")

The crown's wake words (`mcp::CROWN_WAKES`) named `raise_hand` four times, each for one case:
a fix outside the brief a worktree cut needs (T-777), a supervised merge (T-744), a plan the
crown would change (T-582) and a question that is a person's (T-569). Nothing said the rule
those are instances of, so a crown at the author's work that needed the person to rotate a
key, approve a thing or run a step ended its turn saying so in its pane, where nobody reads: the
person watches the board and its attention count, and the card read `idle`.

**Applied.** One clause, `mcp::PERSONS_STEPS`, ends `CROWN_WAKES` after the plans' and the
questions': whatever is a person's to do — a step no tool of the session takes, a fix outside a
brief, a decision the crown leaves to them, a merge or an archive that is theirs — is raised
with `raise_hand` on the crown's own ticket before the turn ends, naming the ticket and the step
in one line, with the reason a model can act on (the person reads the cards, not the pane; a
turn that only says so ends unheard and reads as done) and the hand's mechanics (one per ticket,
the reason replaced by the next, down when the ticket is opened or prompted, which is what
`agent_raise_hand` does). The four named cases stay where they were. `docs/USING.md`'s crown
section says the same to the person. The tool's own description is unchanged: it already names
"a blocker a person has to settle", and the 820-byte cap holds.

- Unit: `the_crown_is_told_every_person_s_step_is_a_hand` (the wake words end on the clause,
  its phrases, the lint). Rig: `N1` — the worker goes idle, then the crown is told in plain
  words, naming no tool, that the ticket waits on the person's vault; the check is
  `crown_hand:vault` and no `ask_agent`.
- **Not done**: nothing on the daemon's side raises a hand for the crown. A turn of the crown's
  that ends with words and no hand is not read for intent — the words are the crown's and
  mesimon classifies no transcript (promise 3's spirit: no token added, none read as a command).

## `dark and light` is a pick of its own, and the last pick is worn (T-863, 2026-10-19)

The author: "theme settings 'light and dark' overriding dark / light … if either is changed the
other shouldn't take effect anymore". `dark and light` wrote the same flavor into both slots, so
it destroyed the two picks; and a `dark` pick after it left `light` on the shared flavor, so
`dark and light` kept applying to the ground nobody touched.

**Three picks, the last one worn.** `prefs.json` gains `theme` (`PrefKey::Theme`, board
overridable): `Prefs::both` / `BoardPrefs::both`. While it is set both grounds wear it
(`for_ground`), and `dark`/`light` stay in the file, unworn. `set_both` leaves the slots alone;
`set` / `set_flavor` (a ground's pick) removes `theme`, so the other ground goes back to its own
pick. On a board the inherit row on a ground clears `theme` too, and inherit on `dark and light`
clears all three. `overlay` flattens: the view's `dark`/`light` are what each ground wears (the
board's `both`, else its slot, else the machine's wear) and it carries no `both`.

**The picker opens on the state worn**, a ground while two themes follow the OS, `dark and
light` while one covers both (T-625's "both first" holds wherever one theme is worn). Tab onto a
ground lands on that ground's own pick, kept under `both`. The `●` on `dark and light` marks the
`both` pick, or two equal slots an older build wrote (`Prefs::pick`/`BoardPrefs::pick`); with two
themes and no `both` pick nothing is marked there.

**Older builds** read only `dark`/`light`, so they wear the kept slot picks while `theme` is
set, and their merging save keeps `theme`. Pre-v0.1; not migrated.

**Tests.** TUI `tab_cycles_the_state_a_pick_is_for` (rewritten around the ticket's case: a
`dark` pick after `both` puts `light` back on its own pick, on the machine and on a board),
prefs `the_last_of_both_and_a_ground_is_worn`; the opening-state picker tests now open on the
ground where the defaults (graphite, chalk) follow the OS. Goldens unchanged. **Owed:** a
CHANGELOG line at the next bump — **Fixed:** in Settings › Theme, a theme for dark and light no
longer overwrites the separate dark and light themes, and picking a dark or light theme
afterwards stops the shared one from applying.

## A raised hand comes down when somebody deals with the agent (T-861, 2026-10-19, "relax raise hand persistence")

**Seen.** The author stepped into a worker's pane from the board, read the question there, came
out, and the card kept its `!` and the reason: board Enter never visits the ticket page, and the
page's departure was the hand's only road down on the person's side. Parking the agent kept it
too, and a crown told of a worker's hand left two cards lit for one question — the worker's and,
once the crown escalated, its own.

**Shipped.** Six more erasers for `Ticket.raised`, all `lower_hand_on`'s, none new in kind: the
hand comes down when somebody deals with the AGENT and not only with the card.

- **In and out of the pane**: `focus_start` lowers it as it hands the attach over, and the
  `FocusEnd` arm lowers it again on the way out, for a hand raised while the person sat inside.
  Both broadcast, since neither command is a mutate on its own.
- **A park of a person's or the crown's**: `SleepSession`, the crown's `sleep_agent`, and
  `park_on_exit` (Ctrl+C, `/exit`, Ctrl+D are a person leaving from inside). `lower_hand_of`
  is the session-keyed spelling for the roads that name a session.
- **The crown told**: `crownwake::lower_told_hands`, in `drain_crown_wakes`' sent arm, lowers
  every delivered wake whose cause IS `Raised`. The crown holds the question from there — its
  `ask_agent` would have lowered the hand anyway through `UserPromptSubmit`, and its own
  `raise_hand` is the one card that should be lit. A question or a plan folded over the hand
  (`WakeCause`'s order) comes down with its dialog instead (T-611); a hand folded over a delivery
  is still the hand. The ticket offered a crown tool to lower it as the alternative; automatic
  needs no tool text, no rig run, and no judgement the crown could forget.

**Kept up, on purpose.** An autosleep (`autosleep_due`), a bulk reclaim, the Esc menu's restart
park and a tier or plan relaunch all go through `sleep_one` and lower nothing: nobody dealt with
the question, and a mark that vanished with a timer is one the person learns to distrust (T-107's
own argument). The board CURSOR still lowers nothing. `train::plan`'s clause is unchanged: the
train takes the ticket once the crown has been told, as it did the moment the crown answered
before — the gap between the telling and the answer is new, and a worker whose branch the crown
should hold off the train is the crown's `merge_ticket`/mode to settle. The tool's description
("until the ticket is opened or its next prompt arrives") is not reworded: nothing the agent is
told changed, so no rig run.

**Tests.** `raise_hand_e2e::a_raised_hand_comes_down_when_the_person_steps_in_or_parks_the_agent`
(FocusStart, FocusEnd with a hand raised inside, SleepSession, the file agreeing), both roads.
`crown_e2e`'s two hand passages now assert the hand is down once the wake landed, where they
used to send `LowerHand` by hand.

## Remote Control's card is the TUI card's order, and no word breaks (T-855, 2026-10-19)

The author, with a phone screenshot: "remote control match cards layout with how terminal renders
them … right now it's a mess and too many items are overflown". The card's second line held the
tags, the crown's word with its age, the column, the worktree mark and the key in one flex row;
`.ticket`'s `overflow-wrap: anywhere` let every item shrink, so `watched · 9m`, `IN PROGRESS` and
`T-853` each broke over two lines on a 390 px phone.

**The face (`lists.js::Face`) is a grid in the TUI card's order:** the agent's mark in a slot of
its own before the title (the TUI's state glyph), the title, and in the corner the worktree mark
and the agent's age (the TUI's `[wt][age]` against the right edge). Under the title, starting
where it does: the tags with `column · key` at the right; the agent's words with the crown's word
beside them (the crown touches what the agent does; it was in the key's strip); the headline.
The age left the agent's words (`claude · working`, no `· 22m`). The phone has no
`column_since`, so a card with no agent has no age — the TUI's age is time in column, a wire
field this ticket did not add.

**No word breaks.** Every strip item is `white-space: nowrap`; the tag line and the agent line
wrap whole items, so on a narrow card `column · key` drops under the tags, right-aligned. The
tags stay named chips, not the TUI's colour bar: a phone has room for the names and nothing
else says them on a list.

**Tests.** `ux.test.js`'s card block: the agent's words without the age, `.card-age` beside, and
a card carrying two tags, the column, the key, a worktree mark and a long title has no text node
with more than one line box. The README's Remote Control picture (`assets/demo/remote.png`) is
re-shot (`npm run shot:remote`). **Owed:** a CHANGELOG line at the next bump — **Changed:** in
Remote Control, a ticket card reads as it does in the terminal: the agent's mark before the
title, the branch mark and age at the right, and no label splits across lines.

## `^g` finds VS Code, and the editor is a Settings row (T-864, 2026-10-19)

The author: "right now it uses vim / nvim. is there a way to know user is using vscode instead
and suggest it? maybe also configure in settings?" `^g` ran `$VISUAL`, else `$EDITOR`, else `vi`.
A bare `EDITOR=code` lost the edit without a word: `code` returns at once, the file read back
unchanged, and it was deleted under the open tab.

**The ladder (`external::Editors::find`, once per process in `lib.rs::run`):** `$VISUAL`,
`$EDITOR`, git's `core.editor` (read with `mesimon_daemon::git::git` from the repo, so a repo's
own setting counts), the editor whose built-in terminal the board runs in, `vi`. That host step
reads `TERM_PROGRAM` (`vscode` for VS Code and every fork, `zed`) and tells the forks apart by
`__CFBundleIdentifier` (macOS names the app that started the process) or Cursor's
`CURSOR_TRACE_ID`; it counts only where that editor is installed. Git's own order puts
`core.editor` first; it is third here because `$VISUAL`/`$EDITOR` are the general answer and
`core.editor` is git's, and the Settings row overrides all of it anyway.

**A table of known editors (`external::KNOWN`)** says how each takes a line (`+N`, `file:N`, `-g
file:N`) and, for a window editor, its wait flag and where its command sits inside its macOS app
— the app is often installed while `code` was never put on PATH, so "installed" checks PATH,
then `/Applications` and `~/Applications`, and the command is the quoted path. A window editor
named without its wait flag gets it (`code` runs as `code --wait`); a link to a file opens in
one detached (`App::pending_open`), at its line and without the flag, and the board stays up.
While `^g` waits on a window editor the given-back terminal says `editing in code ∙ close its tab
to come back to the board` instead of standing blank.

**The Behaviour row `Editor`** (`PrefKey::Editor`, `prefs.json`'s `editor`, machine-only) cycles
`auto`, then each known editor the machine has. `auto`'s detail names what the ladder found and
where (`code, from git's core.editor`). A name the table does not know reads as `auto` and
survives in the file, the week's rule. `mesimon doctor`'s `editor` line names the program and
whether Settings or which rung chose it.

**Refuted:** suggesting VS Code from "installed" alone — installed is not preferred, so the
installed list only fills the row and never picks.

**Tests.** `external.rs`: the ladder's five rungs, the wait flag, a pick running the installed
command, PATH before the app, the host table, and links in both kinds of editor. `app.rs`:
`the_settings_row_picks_the_editor`, `a_file_link_opens_where_its_editor_lives`. `prefs.rs`:
`the_editor_pick_defaults_to_auto_and_round_trips`. Behaviour goldens reminted for the new row.
**Owed:** a CHANGELOG line at the next bump — **Added:** an `Editor` row in Settings ∙ Behaviour
picks what `^g` and file links open; `auto` now also finds git's editor setting and VS Code, Cursor
or Zed when the board runs in its terminal. **Fixed:** VS Code, Cursor, Zed or Sublime set as the
editor without its wait flag no longer lose the edit, and a file link opens in such an editor
without taking over the board.
