## A pull request the ticket named is read by itself, and a reviewed one is the ticket's too (T-859, 2026-10-19, the author: "MRs sometimes not registered ∙ happens when MR repo is outside this repo ∙ also when an agent reviews an MR, it should also be registered given the review posted a comment / commit ∙ gate in settings on by default ∙ maybe ride on summary for MRs references? with duplicates handling and no checklist item on the ^j list")

**Why MRs went unregistered.** Four holes in T-739's road, each measured in the code. A ticket
with no worktree was never asked about: `forge_query` walked `self.worktrees`, `forge_hosts`
too, `queue_forge_sample` returned on an empty `worktrees`, and `opened_unread` answered a
checkout ticket "owed nothing" (T-797 even leaned on it). An agent on the checkout, or one that
`cd`'d into a sibling repository, opened an MR that nothing read. A PR not in the account's own
list (`pr list --author @me`) was never read at all: `binds` matched a printed URL against the
lists alone, so a PR someone else opened reached no set however the agent acted on it, and a
`pr create` the list lagged behind (GitLab's does, by minutes, T-784) waited a pass. Nothing but
`pr create` was a fact. And a URL on a host no leg reaches is dropped by design (the security
rule), which stays.

**Decided: every address a ticket names is read, and a reviewed PR is shown and followed,
never judged.** Three roads name a PR beside the two facts T-739 kept (a commit the worktree
wrote, the ticket's own branch): the `pr create` result (`opened here`), **an act the agent ran
through the CLI** (`acted on here`: `forge::pr_act` reads `gh pr review|comment|checkout|
merge|close|reopen|ready|edit|lock|unlock|update-branch` and `glab mr approve|revoke|note|
checkout|merge|close|reopen|rebase|update|subscribe|unsubscribe|todo` off the tool call, a read
such as `view`, `diff`, `checks` or `list` naming nothing; the subject is the URL the command
names, else its number after the `-R`/`--repo` it names, else a bare number, read only where it
stands right after the verb, last on the command, or after a flag that takes no value — the
short forms that mean a value under one verb and a switch under another (`-m -s -r -c -t`) are
left out; and the result's own address wins where it printed one, since `gh pr comment` and
`glab mr note` print the comment's, which is the PR's with a fragment `pr_urls` now cuts), and
**an address on a line under a note's `Summary` heading** (`summary::pr_urls`, a box or a plain
line, each once; the author's "ride on summary"). An act whose result was an error (Claude's
`is_error`, Codex's `metadata.exit_code`) names nothing: a review the forge refused was no
review; `gh pr review` prints nothing off a tty (its source: `!IsStdoutTTY → return nil`), so the
entry stands on the command alone. A bare number names the working directory's repository: it
resolves on the ticket's one repository (`Daemon::ticket_repo`: the single leg's remote, or the
checkout's; several legs name none) and is dropped where the command changes directory first
(`cd …&&`), since Claude Code's Bash resets its cwd after every call and a `cd` in the same
command is the one way the number is another repository's. The ledger keeps the acts as
`costs.json`'s `pr_acted` beside `pr_urls` (`cost::keep_named`, the same cap), the cursor's
`pending_act` as `<id> <entry>`, and `named_on` reads both; the backfill stays `pr create`'s.

`Daemon::named_prs` is the one list: the opened URLs, then the acts' (`forge::acted_url`) and
the Summary's (`summary_prs_of`, cached under `notes_key` so a note is read again only once a
write moved it), each once by `same_url`; `TicketQuery.opened` carries it all (so T-761's
basis, `fresh` and `unchanged` see a new Summary line or act as they saw a `pr create`) and
`TicketQuery.theirs` the part that is not a `pr create`'s. `forge_query` asks about every
ticket that names a PR, legs or none, learns the checkout's own remote first (`forge_hosts`
counts it), and the host rule stands: a URL binds only on a host a leg's or the checkout's remote
reaches. In `sample`, an address no list of the pass holds is read by itself (`read_one`: `gh pr
view`, GitLab's single MR read); found that way and not a `pr create`'s, it is `Pr.reviewed`
(`forge.json`'s `PrRecord.reviewed`, `#[serde(default)]`, no bump: an older build reads it as the
ticket's own, which holds a merge this build would not and widens nothing). A read that says
there is no such PR (gh's "Could not resolve to a PullRequest", GitLab's 404: `Missing::Gone`)
puts the address in `Sample.unfound` → `State.unfound` (memory), and `held_url` reads it as
answered, so a deleted PR or a wrong number holds no `requires_pipeline` column forever; a call
that failed (`Missing::Failed`) keeps the last reading where one is held and stays owed where
none is, T-750's hold as before.

**Shown and followed, never judged.** `forge::own(set)` is every PR but the reviewed, and it is
what `holding`, `merge_refusal`, `merge_why`, `merged_at`, `pipelined`, `entry_refusal`,
`head_unread` and `State::has_pr` judge: an open reviewed PR holds no DONE and no `m`, a merged
one lands no leg, its pipeline passes no gate, and a ticket whose PRs are all reviewed reads as
one with none bound (`merge` by the board's T-810 answer, "open a PR from its branch"). The
reviewed PR is on the card's line, the page (`reviewed here` among its clauses), `^h`, `^k`,
`get_ticket`'s `prs` (`reviewed: true`) and the snapshot's `PrItem.reviewed`; its merge, pipeline
and deployment edges fire a column's `Arrives here when` and the crown's wake as any PR's do, so
a review ticket follows the MR it reviewed; it is no `opening` (`Edge.opened` skips it: the
worker reviewed it, it did not open it), and the feed says `open !7 bound, reviewed here`, on a
first read too (a turn's end's read is often the ticket's first). Why a reviewed PR must not
judge: a review ticket whose DONE waited for a colleague's merge, with `m` saying "merge it on
GitLab" of a PR the agent cannot merge, would have been the visible wrong.

**The switch: Settings › Behaviour › Reviewed pull requests**, under Merge into, on by default
(`Board::reviewed_prs`, `#[serde(default = "yes")]`, a scalar in `columns.toml` beside
`crown_watches`, no bump on the same argument; `Command::SetReviewedPrs`, local only in
`agent_allows`: whose PRs a ticket carries is the team's workflow as `SetMergeInto` is; inert
under main like every PR row, `PRS_INERT`; `doctor` prints `reviewed pull requests` under `merge
into`). Off, `Query.others` keeps the acts' and the Summary's addresses to the lists alone, so an
own PR named there still binds (the "outside this repo" case) and someone else's never does, and
`opened_unread` owes nothing on those roads; the next read drops every reviewed PR (`carry`
keeps only what the answered repository's read names), and on again they return. Why a person
turns it off: a board where review tickets should carry nothing of the MRs they review, or where
a bare number read on the ticket's repository is a risk the team would rather not take.

**The agent is told.** `SUMMARY_ABOUT` (every `get_ticket`) and `write_note`'s description say a
pull request's address on a plain line under `Summary` names it as the ticket's; the tool's
description lost "over 32 KiB is refused" (the refusal says itself) and a word of the plan
clause to stay under `MAX_TOOL_BYTES`. The line is no box, so `^j`'s list and the card's count
are untouched ("no checklist item on the ^j list"); a URL inside a box binds all the same, and
the box stays what the card counts. USING.md has the rule, the number's caveat and the switch.

**Refuted.** Listing every open PR of a repository to find reviewed ones: a stranger's PR from a
branch named like the ticket's would bind by `head_ref`, T-739's security finding, and a busy
repository's 100 newest would still miss one. Verifying an act on the forge (the account's
review, comment or approval read back): two more calls per reviewed MR per pass on GitLab, and
the act's own result already says whether it went through. Resolving a bare number through the
transcript's `cwd`: the entry's `cwd` is the process's, never the shell's. A reviewed PR judged
like the ticket's own (simplest to build): the review ticket's DONE waits on a merge the agent
cannot make. A `pr create` URL the forge answers nothing for staying owed (today's rule for a
transferred PR): a wrong number from an act would hold a pipeline column for good.

**Tests.** Core `forge::an_act_names_its_pr_and_a_read_names_none` (the command table, the
`cd` guard, the flag positions, `shell_words`), `an_acted_entry_is_an_address_on_the_tickets_repository`,
`an_act_and_its_result_name_the_pr_and_a_failed_act_names_none` (Claude's and Codex's shapes,
the fragment cut, `is_error`, `exit_code`), `a_reviewed_pr_holds_no_merge_and_no_gate`;
`summary::the_summary_names_its_pull_requests_and_the_rest_of_the_note_does_not`;
`board::reviewed_prs_default_on_and_an_off_is_kept`; the keymap's inert-row and detail tests;
`mcp::the_summary_convention_is_in_the_tools`. Daemon `cost::an_act_on_a_pr_in_the_transcript_names_it_on_the_ticket`
(the pending act, the owed tail, the round trip); TUI `reviewed_prs_setting_toggles_through_board_command`;
the `settings_behaviour_*` goldens reminted for the row. `forge_e2e::a_reviewed_pull_request_is_read_by_itself_shown_and_never_judged`
(a `gh pr review 43 --approve` with an empty result binds #43 reviewed off `pr view` alone; `m`
says open a PR; `get_ticket` says reviewed and the board's merge answer; the feed's line; a
checkout ticket's Summary line binds #46 while a mention of #99 binds nothing; the switch off
drops both, on returns them) and `a_ticket_with_no_pull_request_enters_and_one_opened_here_waits`'s
checkout ticket, whose `pr create` is now read by itself and answered gone. Rig F10 (the worker
approves PR 43 through the stub gh by its path: a pane's PATH is the person's, never the
daemon's) and F11 (the worker is told the ticket reviews a PR and puts it on the ticket), each
with a `forge_reviewed` step that waits for the bind before `forge_off` drops the forge, and a
`reviewed:<n>` check on the feed's line (the snapshot is back on main by then): on the real
Sonnet, 2026-10-19, both PASS in 47 s — F10's worker ran the stub's `pr review 43 --approve`
and F11's wrote the address under `Summary` with nothing but `get_ticket`'s sentence to go on;
the first run of each failed only because the check read the snapshot after `forge_off`.
## Two crowns on one machine reach each other (T-733, 2026-10-19, "crown to crown communication over shared boards": "right now what I do is I paste asks from one crown to another (ctrl+tab). it should work just like the crown to tickets communication and needs a proper indication (maybe a lightning bolt targeting the board on title bar …)")

**Proposed first, as an artifact, built as proposed** (the author: "build it as proposed").
Local machines only, on a person's say-so; the shared-board half waits for Teams (T-653).

**The link.** One machine-wide file, `~/.local/state/mesimon/links.toml` (`store::LINKS_SCHEMA`
1, `[[pairs]]` of two canonical repository paths, `core/src/boardlink.rs`), read by every
board's daemon at each command through a `stat` cache (`server/peer.rs::MachineLinksCache`,
`tiers.toml`'s shape). One link reaches both ways, a board closed when it was linked is linked
when it opens, and either side unlinks for both. A person makes it in **Settings › Crown ›
Reaches boards** (`Verb::CrownLinks`, a door; `Scope::Boards`, `Mode::Boards`): the list is the
linked boards, the boards whose daemon is up right now — the TUI walks `/tmp/mesimon-<uid>/*/
orch.sock` off the draw thread and asks each `Hello`, which now carries `repo_root` and `crown`
(`tui/src/boards.rs`; the seam `App::board_scanner` is set in `lib.rs::run`, so a test app lists
nothing) — and a folder row for a board that is not open. No registry exists to list a closed
board: the state root holds hundreds of `proj16` dirs that do not name their repository. A board
is named by its directory (`boardlink::board_name`), the breadcrumb's rule; two of one name are
told apart by path, and `find` says so.

**The road.** `ask_board { board, text }` (crown only, `Command::AgentAskBoard`, top rung) finds
the partner, connects to its `orch.sock` as `Principal::Peer { board }` — a new principal
`authorize` denies everything to; the daemon admits it for exactly `Command::PeerAsk` and judges
that against the file — and sends the words synchronously with short timeouts (an edge action,
a fork on the writer; a daemon not listening refuses at once and reads `is not open`). The
receiving daemon parks the words on its crown's card by `park_ask` (`QueuedAsk::from_board`,
`Daemon::peer_parking`), through the board's **Board ask** template (`AgentPrompt::BoardAsk`:
the asking board's name, its crown's key and title, the words, and that `ask_board board=…`
replies); `sends` follows `crown_mode` — autonomous goes at the crown's idle, supervised holds
for `^y` — and a person's queued words go first. A reply is the same tool back: a daemon that
holds an open ask from a board (`asks_out`/`asks_in`, in memory) reads the next words it sends
there, or gets from there, as the answer (`Board reply` template, `reply: true` on both
receipts). Refused in words the crown relays: not linked (naming the setting), no crown (`^o`),
no agent, at a dialog, a person's words first, not open. The feed carries the roads
(`ask_board` with the road, `board_ask_received`, `board_ask_sent`), never the words.

**What the board shows.** The header names each linked board after the merge word, dim. A
`BoardTouch` on the snapshot (`sent`, `replied`, `received`, `got_reply`, `refused`, ten
seconds in memory) lights that name with what happened in the crown's tint for `LINK_LIT_MS`
(4 s; a refusal in the plain ink with its why) and strikes T-544's bolt between the crown's `♛`
and the name: up for words that left, down for words that came (`strike::LinkStrike`,
`Spots::links`, `strike::draw` now takes the header rect). The author's "blue" is the crown's
tint: a saturated blue would break the one-saturated-colour rule, and the crown's words already
wear it (T-783). The crown's card says where its words went (`→ relay: …`) and the receiving
crown's card says whose they were (`relay: …`), on T-783's line.

**The crown is told** (`CROWN_WAKES`): linked boards are `list_board`'s `linked_boards`,
`ask_board` reaches their crown, the answer arrives as its next prompt beginning with the
board's name, a reply is `ask_board` naming the board that asked, and work that belongs to the
other repository is asked of its crown rather than done from here.

**Tests.** Core: `boardlink` (pairs, names, `find`), `mcp` (twenty tools, the tier, the never
list, the lint over the clause), `prompts` (six templates), keymap (the Crown section's five
rows, the Boards scope). TUI: `reaches_boards_door_links_and_unlinks_through_board_commands`,
`a_board_touch_lights_the_header_word_and_strikes_once`,
`ui::the_header_names_linked_boards_and_lights_the_one_words_went_to` (golden
`board_links_120x30`; `settings_crown_*` and `agent_prompt*` goldens reminted for the new rows).
E2e `boardlink_e2e`: two daemons sharing one HOME, link from one side listed on both, the ask
landing in the stub pane through the template, the reply read as one on both sides, supervised
holding for `^y`, no crown and not open refused, unlink for both, the feeds without the words.
Rig `X1`–`X3` (`ci/rig.py --only X1,X2,X3`, each passed on Sonnet, claude 2.1.303): a
`peer_board` step lays `target/rig/rig-peer` with its own daemon and a stub crown and links it;
the peer goes with its test, link and daemon. X1: the crown, asked in plain words to have the
relay released, calls `ask_board` once naming `rig-peer` (`crown_board:ask_board`,
`peer_fed:board_ask_received`), and its `X1 replied:` line repeats the words the peer's crown
sent back (`peer_reply`). X2: the peer's crown asks first and the rig says nothing to the
crown; the Board ask template alone has it answer with `ask_board` naming the asking board,
and the peer's daemon takes the answer. X3: the peer's daemon is stopped with the link kept
(`peer_stop`); the crown's `ask_board` is refused `is not open`, it does no relay work here and
raises its hand naming `rig-peer` (`crown_hand:rig-peer`, T-862's rule).

**Owed:** a CHANGELOG line at the next bump — **Added:** Settings › Crown › Reaches boards links
two mesimon boards on one machine so their crowns can ask each other; the header names the
linked boards and lights with what went between them.

## The snake comes out on its own, and nothing opens it (T-870, 2026-10-19)

T-823's two games, their menu row and the board's `^g` are gone. What remains is Ticket
Snake, and it is a screensaver: after an hour with no key, paste or click (`App::last_input`,
stamped in `on_event` for everything but focus and resize; `App::idle_after`, an hour unless
`lib.rs::run` read `MESIMON_IDLE_SNAKE_MS`), on a calm board — nothing needs you, the daemon
answers, the terminal is focused and not under `MIN_W`x`MIN_H` (`App::too_small`, set by
`ui::draw`), the board screen with no dialog, no tour, no practice board — `App::drive_arcade`
seats an `Arcade` and the cpu plays it. **An agent working is not the person at the keys**:
the clock reads input alone, so a board whose tickets are busy still gets its snake.

**The cpu** (`Snake::cpu_dir`): the shortest path to the snack when the snake can still
reach its own tail after eating there (the walk is simulated, head first, and the tail
checked from the new head), else the step that leaves the longest way round to the tail,
else any free step. The neck is in every blocked set, so it never reverses. Tests: 4,000
steps on an open 60x20 field without a loss and past 100 points; 3,000 around four cards. A
lost round stays two seconds (`REPLAY_AFTER`) and starts over at zero; the best survives.

**Holds and stops.** The cpu's snake stops outright — the board is the board again — the
moment a ticket needs you or the daemon is down (`drive_arcade`, before `observe`), and does
not come back while that holds. It pauses, and resumes on its own, while the terminal is
unfocused (`App::focused`, from the focus events), too small, or under the help card
(`Arcade::drive`'s `hold`). A person's snake keeps T-823's pauses, every one waiting for
`space`. `esc`/`q`, a card click and the wheel stop it as before.

**`^g` is the handover**, both ways, inside `Scope::Arcade` only (`Verb::GameTake`; the
Board binding and the menu row are deleted, `Verb::Games`/`GameBreaker`/`GameSnake`/
`GameRestart` with them). The steering keys and `space` are gated on `Ctx::game_human`, so
they are inert and unhinted while the cpu plays; the footer reads `^g you play ∙ esc stop ∙
? keys`, and `^g cpu plays` once taken. A person's lost round offers `space for another`.

**The switch** is `PrefKey::IdleSnake` (`idle_snake`, on by default, machine-only: whether a
person wants their board to play while they are away is theirs), the Behaviour row `Snake
while idle` beside `Keep this machine awake`; off also stops a snake that is out. The row
makes Behaviour one longer, so at 120x30 it scrolls by one (`settings_behaviour_120x30_end`).

**Breaker is deleted**, not kept behind a key: with nothing opening the arcade by hand it had
no road, and the user chose Snake. `arcade.rs` lost its half, `Kind`, and the breaker tests;
the `arcade_breaker_120x30` golden is gone. Help goldens lost the `^g games` row; the menu
goldens the Games row.

**Tests.** `arcade`: the handover, the cpu's survival on open and carded fields, no reversal,
the replay, a person's lost round, holds, the path walker. `ui::tests`:
`the_snake_comes_out_idle_on_a_calm_board_and_nowhere_else` (the hour, the menu, focus,
daemon down, a lit ticket, a ticket lighting mid-round, a key resetting the clock, `esc`, the
switch) and T-823's tests rewritten for one game. Keymap: `arcade_keys_are_local…` says `^g`
on the board is nothing and the steering keys are the person's alone. No e2e and no rig: the
daemon, the wire and what an agent is told are untouched.

## The sixth simplify pass (T-867, 2026-10-19, "Simplify")

Four reviewers (reuse, simplification, efficiency, altitude) over the 36 commits since T-838
(`7bbc5b42..`, T-837 to T-870 and T-733), 65 findings, deduped to about 40 applied. Each was
checked against the live code before it was applied; the goldens and the wire are unchanged
(every state file and every JSON byte reads as before). Clippy, `cargo ut` and one full
`nextest` run are green.

**Applied, structure.**
- **One machine-file road.** `store::load_machine_file`/`save_machine_file` over a
  `MachineFile` trait (schema, name, what) replace the twin loaders of `tiers.json` and
  `links.toml`, and `server::tiers::MachineFileCache<T>` replaces `MachineTierCache` and
  `peer::MachineLinksCache` (the stat-stamp cache was written twice). Every notice's words are
  unchanged.
- **One envelope round trip.** `mesimon_daemon::oneshot::one_shot` is the connect, timeouts,
  write-line, read-line and parse that `peer::call_peer`, the TUI's `boards::hello`,
  `doctor::daemon_hello` and the shim's `ask` each spelled; each keeps its own timeouts and
  its failure words.
- **`park_ask` takes its asker.** `Asker::{Person, Agent(crown), Board(from)}` replaces the
  `by: Option<Ulid>` argument plus the `peer_parking` field T-733 smuggled `FromBoard` in
  through (the eighth argument clippy refuses is why the field was there).
- **`BoardTouch.action` is a `TouchAction` enum** (`snake_case`, `#[serde(other)] Unknown`):
  the five words were string literals written in `peer.rs` and matched in the TUI.
- **`NoteFacts<T>`**: the archive offer's open-box count (T-840) and the forge's `Summary`
  addresses (T-859) were two hand-rolled `RefCell<HashMap<Ulid, (notes_key, T)>>` caches with
  the same get-or-read; `write_note` forgets both. The addresses are an `Arc<[String]>`, so a
  hit no longer clones the list.
- **`NamedPrs`**: `named_prs` returns one struct (`all`, `theirs`, `repo`, `summary`), so
  `opened_unread` no longer calls `ticket_repo` and `summary_prs_of` again after it, and
  `forge_query` names each ticket's PRs once per pass instead of twice (three times for the
  checkout tickets); `entry_url` is the entry-to-address fold that was written twice.
- **Codex's open requests are one list**: `observation.rs` kept `requests: BTreeMap<id,
  Reason>` and `asks: Vec<Ask>` in lockstep at five paired sites in `Ledger` and `ChildWork`;
  `OpenRequest { id, reason, ask }` in insertion order is both (the oldest ask was the first
  with content already; `attention_reasons` folds by rank, so map order never mattered).
- **`stage!`** is defined once, taking `self`, instead of twice (`on_tick`, `on_pane_sampled`).
- **`set_board_switch`** is the one barred-check-compare-persist for the three board switches.
- **Smaller:** `plan_dialog::menu_row` is the one native-menu row parse (`❯`/`›` marker, `N.`
  number, label) for the plan, trust and phone dialog readers (four copies, two of them
  patched for `›` in T-846); `trust_dialog(id)` for the four Trust lookups in `mesophon.rs`;
  `grant_pictures` for the three picture prologues; `walk_reason` for the dialog walkers'
  "; cursor moved"; `text::sh_quote` (three copies of the single-quote shell quoting);
  `mcp::text` (the third `requires a text string` parse); `prefs::both_of` (the "two equal
  slots read as `both`" rule, twice); `expand_home` (the `~/` arm, twice); `gitlab_mr` returns
  `Result<_, Missing>` and `read_one` calls it; `peer::fresh` for the touch window;
  `ask_archive`/`hold_archive` under `poll_archive` and `lay_archive`; `mark_unsent` gates on
  the pane alone, so T-849's Codex hand-over is a call to it; `session_kind` replaces
  `is_codex`; `forge::act_id`/`act_entry` parse the `"<id> <entry>"` act once for core and `cost.rs`.
- **Dead code gone:** `Board::drop_archived` (test-only reader after T-842), `Tracked`'s
  `into_inner` and `PartialEq` (its `FromIterator` stays: `for_snapshot` collects through it),
  `take_unfound` (a four-line wrapper of one `extend`), the no-op `drop(spawned)`, the
  unreachable `PermissionRoad::Codex` arm in `control_permission_answer`, the redundant
  `links.refresh()` in `link_board`/`unlink_board` (`handle` refreshed already; the agent road
  keeps its own, it returns before that line), `pr_create_line` under `#[cfg(test)]`.

**Applied, performance.**
- **A Codex report that moved nothing marks nothing.** `on_codex_snapshots` took
  `iter_mut().find` on every seat on every observer report — every tick while a Codex seat is
  live — and `Tracked`'s `DerefMut` marked the records dirty before the sequence check, so
  `sessions.json` was serialised and compared again (T-839's 22 ms) to learn nothing moved. It
  finds by index and takes `&mut` only past the sequence check and in the lost arm only on a
  change; `probe_codex_startup`'s plan arm the same. The snapshot's request is `take`n, not
  cloned.
- `State::fresh` takes `opened` as a closure, asked only in its third clause: the tick priced
  every owed ticket's named PRs for the clause it rarely reached.
- `drive_arcade` tests its cheap bools before `needs_you_tickets()` (every frame since T-870);
  `pinned_columns` is a `Vec<bool>` filled in `reindex_columns`, not a sort plus a ticket scan
  per frame; the two `want_*` stages iterate instead of collecting a `Vec<String>` to iterate;
  `named_on` no longer allocates a `String` per pending act per transcript line.

**Checked and kept (the reviewers' own verdicts, or mine).** `entry_refusal`'s clone of the
own set stays: moving `own` into `pipeline_of` cut reviewed PRs from the card's and the
feed's fold too, and cutting only its open branch let a reviewed merge's passed pipeline
stand in for the own merge's failed one (the commit's security review caught it; the test
now pins the merged case). `save_note_with_attachments` is
not `with_pictures`: it matches links against the raw note text under the note limit, the
other against `sanitize_prompt`'s cap, and their refusal words differ. `startup_attention`'s
`folder_trust` is wider than `trust_dialog::codex` on purpose (heading plus "Trust and
continue" alone, a wrapped Quit row included). The two dialog walkers share only
`walk_reason`: the dialog's key block handles seven steps and mutates `pending.walk`, the
approval's three arms are eight lines, and one body needed an `Option<&mut Walk>` and a
second refusal path. `mesophon::Agent.trust` beside the dialog's Trust content (older
browsers) and the TUI's reading of the journal for `daemon slow` are design. `grant_pictures`
reads an unknown upload before an invalid ticket where both are wrong (one message, both a
client's bug).

**Found and left open (each a behaviour, wire or design decision):**
- **A Codex seat's trust dialog is projected and refused.** T-846 routes every dialog through
  the harness split before the content check, and the Codex arm has no Trust (`codex_takes`,
  `codex_dialog_shape`), while `probe_codex_startup` still offers a Codex trust dialog to the
  phone and the board's `w`: the accept answers `shape_unrecognised` and the projection drops.
  The fix is to dispatch on `DialogContent::Trust` before the harness; `trust_accept_e2e` has
  no Codex case, so one goes with it.
- **Two per-tick forks on the writer thread** after T-857: `drive_codex_inputs`
  (`capture_input_screen` every tick) and `press_steer` on `settle_owed`'s cadence, where the
  Claude roads ride the pane sampler's `want_*`/`self.screens`. A sample-old screen changes
  the Codex e2es' timing.
- `ApprovalDelivery` mirrors `DialogDelivery` with a second walk loop and settle; a Codex
  approval as a `DialogDelivery` with an answer enum merges two receipts.
- `TicketQuery.theirs` is a subset of `opened` carried beside it, re-derived per address in
  `forge::sample`; two disjoint lists, or `(address, reviewed)` pairs.
- `Response::AgentAskedBoard` mirrors `Response::PeerAsked` (wire names).
- `lower_hand_*` is remembered at each deliberate park road; a `Park::{Deliberate,
  Automatic}` on `sleep_one` would lower it in one place.
- The Codex plan is cloned into `asks` per report whatever the seat's state (the consumer
  reads the state after the loop, so a pre-check would drop a plan arriving with its stop).
- The twelfth per-file `create`/`spawn` e2e helper pair (`boardlink_e2e`) and the hand-typed
  `UserPromptSubmit`+`Stop` turn want `TestClient` helpers in `common`.

## The shin wakes up out of משימון, once per machine (T-869, 2026-10-19, the author: "Mesimon starting animation in terminal showing the shin emerging from משימון … Should appear after installation or when starting board for the first time ∙ Think like pixar starting animation with the lamp" and "this needs to run a single time per installation (not including updates) … if they already installed, show them the next time they run mesimon, and that's it")

**What plays** (`crates/mesimon-tui/src/intro.rs`, about 13 s): the word comes up out of the
ground right to left, the ש stirs and shivers, then breathes in and fills out into the medium
shin. The morph is a blend of two distance fields (the letter's and the shin's silhouette, one
stage), the bottom rows leading, so the stems swell, the gaps close from the bottom up and the
arms slide into the shin's; past 1 the body alone swells a pixel (the arms' heads ran together
when they swelled too). A wipe was tried first and refuted by the author ("could be more
seamless"): the arms snapped at its last row. The face then arrives on the finished body, eyes
shut, and the closing lines come with it ("can mesimon be ready right after the morph?"): it
wakes, looks at each neighbour, at you, blushes, waves twice, hops with the calm sparkles and
rests. The letters are drawn in the shin's weight and lit by `creature::light` (the rim light,
lifted out of `compose` so the letters and the morph share it); the shin's poses are
`creature::pose` over the engine's own eyes, mouths and inks. Only משימון ships (the author
picked it over the English version, where the m flips into a ש).

**Where, and once.** `~/.local/state/mesimon/welcomed` (at the state root, beside
`prefs.json`) is written as it starts, so quitting halfway counts as seen. `install.sh` runs
`mesimon welcome` after a successful install on a UTF-8 terminal, keys from `/dev/tty` because
the script itself arrives on stdin: exit 0 means it played inline (ratatui's inline viewport,
24 rows) with "mesimon is ready" and the `next:` lines in it, and the script then prints
neither its picture nor its own `next:` lines; exit 1 (seen, too small, no colour) keeps
today's picture and lines. The script asks `--help` for the command first, so a pinned older
release never gets an unknown command. A board run on a machine with no marker plays it
fullscreen before its first frame (`intro::before_board`, after `init_terminal`), then waits
for a key on the seat's invitation ("enter opens your board"). An update, `U`'s re-exec and
`brew upgrade` write nothing and ask nothing: the marker outlives the binary. A key during
play skips to the end; the hint "any key skips" holds the place of the next words, then of the
prompt. Keys go through `osc::ReplySwallow` first, so a late colour reply skips nothing.

**What waits.** Below 88 columns, or 22 rows on the board (26 under the installer), or on mono,
nothing plays and nothing is marked: the first terminal that fits plays it (the author chose
this over a small-shin version). The demo recorder's sandbox HOME is seeded with the marker so
the README GIFs never show it.

**Tests.** `intro::tests`: goldens `intro-board-end.txt`, `intro-install-end.txt`,
`intro-morph.txt`; the morph is exactly the letter at 0 and the shin at 1; the words come on
the first beat after the morph; every frame fits `MIN_COLS`; `install.sh` prints the same
`next:` lines and runs `mesimon welcome`. Watched by hand in a scratch tmux on a scratch HOME:
inline play, a key skipping it with nothing left typed, exit 0 then 1 on the second run; the
board's fullscreen play, a key opening the board, and no intro on the relaunch. Found that way
and fixed: the board's rest pose was computed eagerly (`unwrap_or`) and overflowed before the
end.

**Owed:** a CHANGELOG line at the next bump — **Added:** a short animation the first time
mesimon runs on a machine, after the installer or on the first board: the ש in משימון wakes up
as the shin. Any key skips it, and it never plays again.

## The header counts the linked boards (T-878, 2026-10-21, "Crown connected boards should show N boards": "Instead of the literal list of boards. Only when messages flow, show the relevant board in blue with what happened like now")

**What changed.** T-733's header wrote every linked board's name after the workflow word
(` ∙ relay ∙ site`). It now writes their count, ` ∙ 2 boards` (` ∙ 1 board`), in the same quiet
ink, and only while words go between the crowns does the count give its place to what happened
with the one board, as before: `↯ sent ask to relay` in the crown's tint for `LINK_LIT_MS`, a
refusal in the plain ink. The names stay in `Settings › Crown › Reaches boards`.

**The bolt.** With one word on the row there is one end: `links_mark` records every linked
board's name at that word's cell, so `strike.rs`'s lookup by name is unchanged and a bolt for
any board lands on the count or on the lit words. A lit board that is no longer linked lights
nothing, as before.

**Tests.** `ui::tests::the_header_counts_linked_boards_and_lights_what_words_did` (renamed from
`…names_linked_boards…`): the count, no names, `1 board`, every board's end on the same cell,
the lit words in the tint, the refusal in base, the lit words dropped on a 60-column row; the
golden `board_links_120x30` reminted (one header line). The quiet count always fits: the board
draws from 60 columns, and the row needs 52.

**Owed:** a CHANGELOG line at the next bump — **Changed:** the board header shows how many
boards this one is linked to, instead of their names; a board's name shows there only while its
crown and this one are exchanging a message.

## ask_agent's receipt says the words woke a parked agent (T-880, 2026-10-21, the author: "Tell the crown queueing words to agents woke them up ∙ They attempt to start_agent after ask_agent. Ask agent response should let the crown know it was successful and woke the agent so that the crown would stop doing it")

**What was wrong.** Words for a parked worker are its wake (`QueuedSeat::Wake`): the queue, or
a `deliver now`, resumes the agent in its conversation with them. The receipt said only
`road: queued` (or `sent_now`), which a crown read as "delivered later, agent still asleep",
and it called `start_agent` after the ask. That start either met `already has an agent` or,
while the words still waited on a busy checkout, woke the agent without them.

**What shipped.** `Response::AgentAsked` carries `wake: Option<AskWake>` (`#[serde(default)]`,
absent for a pane): `woken` when the words already went and the seat is no longer asleep (or
its resume waits on the worktree), `when_sent` while they wait (for the checkout, the budget,
or a person's `^y`). A wake that failed says neither; the feed's `queued_wake_failed` has it.
The shim renders `wake` plus `wake_about`, a sentence naming the ticket that says start_agent
is not needed. `CROWN_WAKES` gains one clause next to the start_agent-wakes sentence: ask_agent's
words to a parked agent wake it as well, as they are sent, so no start_agent follows them.

**Tests.** `an_ask_receipt_says_the_words_woke_a_parked_agent` (render);
`the_crown_sends_its_asks_to_the_agents_it_started` asserts `when_sent` on the budget-held and
checkout-queued asks, `None` on a pane, and a new block: a parked worker asked with `deliver
now` reads `woken`, is awake at once, and a `start_agent` after it is refused. Rig R8 (bare
ask to a parked worker, `crown:start_agent=1`, a new exact-count form of the `crown:` check)
passed on Sonnet, claude 2.1.305: one start, one sleep, one ask, the worker answered from its
conversation.

## Words wait for a mod seat's bridge instead of being pasted (T-879, 2026-10-21, "Crown to crown communication sometimes uses paste instead of plugin path … I think it happens when the main board sends a message")

**What the feeds showed.** No linked boards had ever carried an ask on this machine, so the
"message from the main board" was the board's own crown wake. Every crown wake and queued ask
in the boards' feeds was checked for its road (a `prompt_by_mod` beside the `*_sent` line, or
none: a paste). Hook-set crowns aside, the one mod-road paste was forge-lab's crown on
2026-10-14: a tier switch relaunched it (`sleep_session`, `resume_session`), the new pane's
`SessionStart` landed, and 2.3 s later a crown wake for a merged PR went with no
`prompt_by_mod`, into the composer by paste.

**Why.** `mod_speaks` is true only once the bridge has polled from the record's own pane. A
pane's `SessionStart` comes in through the mod's relay, and the bridge starts after the mod
has registered its tools, so a fresh pane can read idle while no bridge has polled yet. The
same gap opens after a daemon restart, which forgets every bridge until it polls again (at most
2 s with the bridge's backoff). Launch words already wait for both edges (T-575). The queue and
the crown wake checked only `session_takes_words`, so anything due in that gap went by paste:
a person's queued ask, the crown's wake, the crown's asks to a worker, a linked board's ask.

**The fix.** `session_takes_words` (the readiness the queue and `crown_wake_blocked` read) is
false while `bridge_awaited`: a Claude record on the mod road with a pane, no bridge up, and
less than a bridge wait (`MOD_BRIDGE_WAIT_MS`, 10 s) since the pane's launch. A pane the daemon
inherited is timed from the daemon's start. `ModRoad::awaited` is stamped at the three
pane launches (`spawn_session`, `resume_session_with_cleanup_ack`, `wake_session`) and dropped
by `mod_forget`. When the bridge polls, the next tick sends the words by `submit`. When it
does not, the paste road takes them after the wait, as it does for launch words. A prompt sent
on the spot (`PromptSession` not queued, a send-now) is unchanged: a person who types into a
pane that is a second old has chosen the moment.

**Tests.** E2e `mod_turns_e2e::a_queued_ask_waits_for_a_late_bridge_and_goes_down_the_mod`
(the stand-in engine's new `mod-late` switch holds its bridge 2.5 s): a queued ask to an idle
mod seat is not typed during that gap and goes down as a `submit` once the bridge polls. With
the gate removed it fails, the words pasted. Both roads of the whole suite are green. No rig
run: the words and the tools the crown is told about are unchanged, only when the same words
go and by which road.

**Owed:** a CHANGELOG line at the next bump — **Fixed:** a crown's wake or a queued message
that came due just after its agent restarted could appear typed into the agent's input box;
it now waits a moment and arrives as its own message.

## The search finds words and note lines, in any case (T-882, 2026-10-21, user: "the search is not really finding things ∙ I'm trying to find the promo codes precreated for friends. (it's on a note on a ticket already archived) but I can't find it. i think it's also case sensitive which it shouldnt be and also it scores things wrongly.")

Three complaints, three causes, measured on the author's board (749 tickets, 703 notes,
19,000 lines) before anything was changed:

- **Not finding it.** The codes were on two note bodies (T-514, T-515) whose titles say
  "access codes" and "registration gate", and T-349 searched the row alone — key, title,
  column, tags — and recorded "note BODIES are not searched" as deliberate. `promo`, `friends`
  and `codes` could not reach them from the picker at all.
- **Case sensitive.** Smart case: a capital anywhere in the query made it case-sensitive, so
  `Promo` returned 8 rows and `promo` 224, two different searches for one word. A title's
  capital is not something a reader remembers.
- **Scoring wrongly.** Fuzzy by default. `promo` matched 224 of 749 cards on scattered
  letters and ranked "Design Shin's Garden: grow a personal world…" first at 87; `codes`
  matched 262. fzf's v2 scoring is right for a file path typed as an abbreviation and wrong
  for a board whose reader types words: a word either is in the title or it is not.

**The grammar is now fzf's `--exact` mode** (`search::atoms`): a bare word is a substring,
`'word` is the one that goes fuzzy (fzf's "unquote"), `^`, `$` and `!` keep their meaning,
and every atom is `CaseMatching::Ignore` with `Normalization::Smart` (`cafe` finds `café`).
`nucleo-matcher` stays: its `Atom.kind` is public, so the parse is its own with the default
kind flipped, and the indices, the scoring among substring hits (word-boundary bonus, so
`friends` ranks "friends computer…" over "share this project with friends") and the row
split are unchanged. After: `promo` 8 hits, `Promo` the same 8, `codes` 11.

**Notes are searched by the line, and the line is drawn.** A ticket whose row does not match
is a hit when one line of one of its notes holds the whole query — grep's rule, two words on
two lines are not a match — and the `Hit` carries that line as an `Excerpt` (which note, the
line, the indices). The picker draws it as a second row under the ticket's: the title column's
indent, the rail's note mark, the line lit the way a title is, opened near its first match
behind `…` when it is long (`Field::windowed`, so what lit is on the screen), and the preview
bolds that note among the ticket's note rows. The row's own fields stay unlit — nothing in
them matched. Inside a tier, row hits rank above note hits: the ticket's name outranks a line
somebody wrote under it. `!foo` alone asks nothing of the notes (every line lacks something).

**The bodies ride one wire command, once.** `Command::ReadNotes { notes: Vec<NoteRef> }` →
`Response::Notes` (each body with its `rev`; a ref naming no ticket, note or file is left out,
never an error). The picker's `Corpus` (`App::poll_bodies`) asks on the first keystroke for
every note of every ticket it ranks — the archive too while `tab` has it in — and on every
snapshot after only for the notes whose `rev` moved, dropping the ones whose ticket left the
board; a note the daemon left out is held empty at the rev asked, so it is not asked again
until it changes. One round-trip for a board's worth (1.7 MB here), and a keystroke never
waits on the wire — T-349's "no index, no wire" holds for the ranking. An older daemon
refuses the command and the picker searches rows alone, asking again after 30 s. Agents may
not send it (`agent_allows`); the e2e is in `notes_e2e`.

**The precheck is the matcher's own fold.** Every line is kept beside a copy folded through
`nucleo_matcher::chars::to_lower_case` then `::normalize`, and so is each positive contiguous
needle; a line whose folded copy does not `contain` every needle is refused before the matcher
is asked, which is a necessary condition under exactly the flags the atoms carry. Debug build,
the author's board, per keystroke: a miss was 155 ms through the matcher alone and is 5 ms
with the precheck; `the` (484 hits, every one scored) 42 ms; release 10 ms before the precheck.
`how_long_the_notes_take` prints the synthetic figures beside `how_long_a_big_board_takes`.

Goldens: `search_120x30` and `search_80x24` moved from `ac` to `en` — `ac` fuzzy-matched
"Gr-a-pheme trun-c-ation" and now reaches "accent" alone, which lost the two-tier picture the
golden is for; `en` is in "treatments" and "accent" and nowhere else. New: `search_note_120x30`
(a title hit, a live note hit with its line, an archived note hit with a long line opened near
the match). The T-349 block above stands as the record of what fuzzy and smart case were
chosen for; this block is why they went.

Not done: a query whose words fall on different lines of a note, or across a note and the
row, is not a hit (one line is what the picker can show, and the rule is one sentence); the
note names on the snapshot are not searched apart from their bodies (the name is the body's
first line, so it is covered); the phone's search is unchanged.

## Remote Control queues a prompt while the terminal is away (T-881, 2026-10-21, "Allow to queue messages from remote control if offline ∙ Maybe add a popup so user will understand")

**Built: a third letter kind.** A prompt written while the terminal is out of reach is sealed
for the relay's mailbox as T-497's tickets and T-532's note edits are: the letter's JSON says
`"kind": "prompt"` with `ticket`, `session` (a hint only) and `text`
(`mesophon::MailPrompt`, `Letter::Prompt`). No crypto, Wasm or relay change: the relay keeps
it under the same caps and cannot read it. An older host reads it as a ticket with no title
and refuses it, and the page sends one only to a host whose last handshake said
`mail_prompts` (offered beside `mailbox`, remembered on the identity's board entry as
`mailPrompts`). Prompts go through the mailbox only while the terminal is away; live, the
live op with its steer, tiers, pictures and receipts is unchanged.

**Decided: it is a Queue, never a steer, and only on an awake agent.** On collection the host
parks the words as the ticket's queued ask (`park_ask`, `QueuedSeat::Pane`, `Asker::Person`)
on the ticket's pane agent, and only when it is the session the page wrote to
(`mail_prompt_seat`, as the live prompt's `control_target` binds it; a wake keeps the id),
authorized as `PromptExisting` on that session. Words for one conversation never land in
another: a ticket whose agent was replaced since refuses them, and the page gives them back
for review ("Session changed"). As the live Queue, words still going into the pane
(`parked`, `steering`, `pending_submit`) refuse it, and words already queued on the ticket
are replaced with the receipt saying whose. A parked agent or none is refused too: a wake
from a letter would launch hours later with nobody watching. (The session binding and the
going-in refusal were added after a review of the first commit; not a permission gap, since
a paired browser may prompt any agent on the board, but a wrong-conversation delivery.) The page offers the road only where the remembered
board shows an agent not sleeping.

**Exactly once:** the answer goes in `Stored.noted` (the ring T-532's note letters use, now
`control_answered`/`control_keep_answer`) before the queue drains, so the words reach the
pane only after the ring says so. A crash before that replays the letter, and a pane ask is
memory-only, so nothing goes twice; a crash after it can lose the queued words, never repeat
them.

**The page** (`letters.js`, `PromptMail`; kept at `prompts:<grant>` in IndexedDB beside
`notes:`, dropped by revoke and forget): one letter per ticket, a clock in this browser, one
tick at the relay with **Take back** (the mailbox's `withdraw`), and on the host's sealed
receipt gone (the queued row now shows the words) or refused (`Sessions::retain` puts the
words back, beside a newer draft). A letter the relay lost reads "Delivery unknown" with
**Dismiss**, since it may have arrived. **The popup asked for is the away sheet**
(`AwaySheet`): the first send while away explains in three lines where the words wait, when
they reach the agent and that they can be taken back, Cancel sending nothing; it is said
once per browser (`localStorage`, a per-viewer convenience). After that the composer's own
line and placeholder say it. The away hero now says messages wait when the host takes them.

Tests: `a_letter_is_a_note_only_when_it_says_so` (core, the prompt's kind),
`a_mailed_prompt_queues_only_on_an_awake_agent` (daemon), a state test for `PromptMail`, and
the UX suite's `mailPromptFlow` in Chromium and WebKit at three sizes (the sheet and its
Cancel, sealed with the session, one per ticket, Take back beside a newer draft, kept across
a reload, queued on return with the queued row showing it, given back for a parked agent).
**Not verified:** the relay's acceptance tests (no relay change; letters are opaque to it), a
physical phone, the hosted relay.

**Owed:** a CHANGELOG line at the next bump — **Added:** Remote Control can send a prompt
while your terminal is out of reach: it waits sealed at the relay, and is queued for the agent
when the terminal is back. The first time, a sheet explains where it goes.

## The snake waits to be asked (T-884, 2026-10-21, "Stop games from running automatically")

T-870's idle snake was on by default, so every board started a game by itself after an idle
hour. **`Snake while idle` is now off by default**: the board starts no game unless the person
turns that row on. Everything T-870 built behind the switch is unchanged.

**The key moved, on purpose.** `Prefs::body` writes every flag on every save, so any save from
v0.1.0-beta.10 or .11 wrote `"idle_snake": true` whether or not the person touched the row; a
flipped default alone would have left the snake on for all of them. `PrefKey::IdleSnake`'s
JSON name is now `snake_while_idle`, `"idle_snake"` is never read, and a save removes it
(`IDLE_SNAKE_RETIRED_KEY`). A person who had turned it off loses nothing; one who wants it
turns it on once more. A downgrade reads the dropped key as absent, which there is on.

**Tests:** `idle_snake_defaults_off_and_round_trips` (the old key ignored and dropped, an on
round-trips); `the_snake_comes_out_idle_on_a_calm_board_and_nowhere_else` first proves no snake
with the switch untouched and an expired clock, then seeds it on. TUI-only: no e2e, no rig.

**Owed:** a CHANGELOG line at the next bump — **Changed:** The idle snake no longer starts on
its own; turn it on with `Settings › Behaviour › Snake while idle`.

## A card has no agent words (T-886, 2026-10-21, "Don't render \"claude * working\" on remote control tickets")

Remote Control's card drew `claude · working` (or `· idle`, `· needs approval`, …) under the
tags, while its mark (spinner, idle dot, needs-you dot) and the needs-you card's ink already say
the state. **The card's agent words are gone in every state**: a first cut kept them for every
state but `working`, and the author's answer was that the card's mark and style say the others
too. The `.card-agent` line now carries the crown's touch alone, and only when there is one;
what the agent is on stays in the headline below. The ticket page's screen-reader word, the
needs-you list's `need-line` and the dialogs are unchanged.

**Tests:** the UX suite asserts the mark instead of the words (the spinner on a working card,
`mark-idle`, a needs-you card's `mark-attn`) and no `.card-agent` without a crown touch.
Mesophon-only: no e2e, no rig.

**Owed:** a CHANGELOG line at the next bump — **Changed:** Remote Control's cards no longer
spell the agent's state ("claude · working"); the card's mark shows it.

**Follow-up, the crown's word on the key's line (2026-10-21).** With the agent's words gone,
`.card-agent` held only the crown's touch (`moved · 2m`), a whole line for one word. The
author asked for it beside the key: it now opens `.ticket-meta`, `moved · 2m · T-3` (the
column between, where the list shows it), and `.card-agent` is gone from the page and the
stylesheet. The meta line does not wrap, so the UX suite's no-wrap card now carries a crown
touch too and checks that the key's line stays inside the card at every size.

## A raised hand is read whole on the board (T-888, 2026-10-21, "Hand raised should be shown on board")

The card cuts an agent's `raise_hand` sentence to its column (T-865), and in the pane the words
sit inside an MCP call, so a long ask was read nowhere. **The cursor card's hand now has rows of
its own above the row that names the card** (`chrome::hand_lines`, between the columns and the
advisory row): `!` and the sentence in the needs-you colour, wrapped to the frame, at most three
rows (a reason is capped at 160 bytes). The board gives up rows only while there is a hand to
show, and only at rest, under the same conditions as `hover_line`.

**A lowered hand keeps its words for five minutes** (`LOWERED_HAND_MS`), behind `¡` (ASCII `i`)
in `dim2`, never attn and never counted: a hand comes down the moment someone deals with the
agent (pane entered, prompt sent, page left, T-861), which is often before the words were read.
The memory is the TUI's alone (`App::lowered`, filled by `note_lowered_hands` on every absorb by
comparing the old board with the new): no wire or schema change, and a TUI restart forgets it,
which costs at most five minutes of a quiet line. The clock starts when the board saw the hand
go, not when the daemon lowered it.

**Tests:** `the_cursor_cards_hand_is_read_whole_above_its_name` (every word across the wrap, attn,
no row off the card), `a_lowered_hand_stays_quiet_on_the_hand_row` (no attn, no `!1`, gone after
the window), and `a_raised_hand_survives_the_board_and_is_lowered_by_leaving_its_page` now walks
the absorb road into `App::lowered`. `board_raised_120x30` reminted with the new row. TUI-only:
no e2e, no rig.

**Owed:** a CHANGELOG line at the next bump — **Added:** When an agent raises its hand, the
board shows its whole message above the selected card's name; after the hand is lowered the
message stays, greyed, for five minutes.

**Follow-up, same day (the author, on the shipped row: "it's truncated as well down there … when
the hand is down it's not reading as 'used to be' raised hand").** Two changes:
- **`RAISE_REASON_MAX_BYTES` is 400, was 160.** The row wrapped what it got, but the daemon had
  already cut the sentence at 160 bytes. 400 is a short paragraph, at most six rows on an
  80-column board (`HAND_ROWS_MAX` 6); the card still cuts to its column. Older builds read a
  longer reason unchanged. The banner backstop (`notify::MAX_FIELD`) rose to 440 so the whole
  reason still fits behind `needs you ∙ `. `raise_hand`'s description is unchanged.
- **A lowered hand is the needs-you colour faded half way to the ground** (`Theme::attn_faded`,
  `LOWERED_KEEP` 0.5), never attn itself; with no RGB ground to fade into it is `dim2`, as before.

## The newest release is the highest tag, not the first listed (T-877, 2026-10-21, "Update check and install.sh offer the release GitHub lists first, not the newest")

v0.1.0-beta.10 shipped on 2026-10-19 and no Mac saw it: the board offered no update and
`install.sh` installed beta.9. **Cause:** `GET /repos/<dist>/releases` orders by a release's
`created_at`, which is the date of the commit its tag names, not when it was published, and
`ci/release.sh` ran `gh release create` (tag on the releases repo's main head) *before* syncing
`install.sh` and the site there. With nothing changed in that repo since the last release, the new
tag landed on the previous one's commit (beta.9 and beta.10 both on `3116ed33`) and GitHub broke
the tie with beta.9 first: the listing read beta.9, beta.8, beta.10, beta.7, beta.6. beta.11 sits
on beta.10's commit too, and is listed first only by that same tie-break.

**Every reader picks the highest version, never the first entry.** `release.rs::latest_tag` takes
the max by `semver::Version` over the non-draft tags (a tag that is no version is passed over);
`install.sh` reads every `"tag_name"` with `grep -o` and keeps the highest through a POSIX awk
semver compare (`highest_tag`). Not `sort -V`: busybox may lack it, and GNU's ranks `v0.1.0`
below `v0.1.0-beta.1`. The old `grep -m1 | sed` had a second bug the test found: on a one-line
JSON body its greedy `.*` took the *last* tag.

**Each release names a commit of its own**, so readers already in the field (who still take the
first entry) see it first. Syncing `install.sh` before the create would not have been enough:
beta.10's case was exactly a release where nothing in the repo changed. So `release.sh` commits
`LATEST` (one line, the tag) to the releases repo's default branch first, refuses if that branch's
head is still the commit the first-listed release names, creates the release with `--target`
that commit, and then asks `releases?per_page=3` (five tries) for the new tag first, reporting
a wrong order at the end with exit 1 rather than stopping the syncs. Pages serves `LATEST` at
mesimon.dev/LATEST as a side effect; nothing reads it. A dry run prints this order.

**Tests:** `the_newest_published_tag_is_the_highest_not_the_first` (the real listing, and a
release above its prereleases with a non-version tag in between), `a_draft_is_never_the_newest`;
`ci/test_installer.py`'s `InstallerVersion` installs beta.10 from that listing in pretty and
one-line JSON (red on the old script: beta.9 and beta.6) and installs nothing from `[]`. The
awk was run on macOS's bwk awk only; busybox's and mawk's ride `ci/test-linux.sh` when Docker is
back. The publish half cannot run outside a real release (it needs the tag at HEAD and writes to
GitHub); its dry-run block was run alone.

**Owed:** a CHANGELOG line at the next bump — **Fixed:** The update check and the installer now
pick the newest release even when GitHub lists an older one first.

## A `!` line from the phone or the ask field runs in Claude Code's shell (T-876, 2026-10-21, "`!` shell commands sent from Remote Control arrive as plain text")

**Asked.** On the beta.10 release ticket the author sent `! cd ~/Documents/code/mesimon-relay &&
deploy/ship.sh all` from Remote Control to a Claude agent; it reached the agent as a sentence,
the agent tried to run it with its Bash tool and auto mode refused it. A denial only a person at
the terminal lifts (a production deploy, self-modification) had no road from the phone.

**Measured first, in a scratch Claude Code 2.1.306 under a private tmux.** The ticket's leads
were half right. (1) The mod road is the bug: `$.prompt.submit` refuses only a text beginning with
`/` (the engine's own words name the slash alone, and list "bash mode" among the inputs that
never go through `prompt.submit`), so a `!` line goes down as a prompt the model reads — which is
what the author saw, their board on the mod road. (2) The paste road already works: a bracketed
paste of `!echo x` into an empty box switches it into bash mode (the row reads `! echo x`, the
footer `! for shell mode`) and a separate Enter runs it, for a short line, a 1,200-character
line (a `[Pasted text #1]` chip, still run) and a two-line paste (both lines run). No separate
`!` keypress is needed. (3) Mid-turn, Enter and the send-now keys alike queue the line (`Press up
to edit queued messages`) and it runs when the turn ends. (4) As T-707 measured on 2.1.295: no
`UserPromptSubmit` for the line; the transcript gets `<bash-input>` and `<bash-stdout>` rows when
it ends, and a model turn on the output follows, ending in a `Stop` (3 s after a quick `echo`).

**Built.** `road::is_command` now reads a leading `!` as it reads a leading `/`
(`road::is_shell`), so a shell line keeps the paste road on every Claude session — the mod's
`submit` and its `fill` both skip it — and the keys are the ones every prompt gets: the paste,
then the Enter. What changed around the keys: **the receipt.** A pasted shell line is owed as a
paste is (`Owed.shell`), but no hook will ack it, so `settle_owed` asks the sampler for the pane's
screen each cadence and acks when a sample stamped `SHELL_RENDER_MS` (300 ms) after the Enter
reads the composer empty (`composer::read` now knows the `!` glyph of a box in bash mode, so the
line still in the box reads `Holding`, never `Absent`). The ack is the entry's own word
(`prompt_submitted`, `queued_ask_delivered`); the paste itself is fed `shell_sent`. A pasted
shell line is **never kept unsent**: on the wake road the presses that run out, or a pane that
stops being pressable, drop the entry with `paste_unacked`, since the line may well be running
with its echo scrolled off — the person's screen says, the board cannot. And a shell line into a
box that holds a draft is refused (`the prompt box holds text ∙ a `!` line runs only from an
empty box`): `!` switches the mode only from an empty box, and after a draft the line would ride
to the model as the draft's tail, the failure this closes by another door. The screen is read
once at that edge (a fork, as `codex_steer`'s), and a screen that cannot be read refuses nothing.

**Refuted.** A `!` keypress of its own before the paste (the ticket's lead): the box reads the
`!` off a paste, measured. Acking off the `Stop` of the output's turn: it comes minutes after a
long command and, pasted mid-turn, the running turn's `Stop` would ack a line merely queued; the
screen says it in a second. Re-pressing Enter into a box still holding the line on the idle-pane
road: a prompt's paste has no retry there either (T-5 measured the separate Enter reliable), and
parity keeps one road.

**Tests.** `road.rs`: `a_shell_line_is_words_the_box_runs`. `composer.rs`:
`a_box_in_bash_mode_is_the_composer`, from the measured screens. `shell_line_e2e`: the ask
field's `!` line reaches the stub as one line with no mod `submit` (the mod pass records every
frame), is fed `shell_sent` and acked off the screen with no hook sent and no `paste_unacked`;
queued, the same; to a parked agent it wakes it, goes in at the composer, the presses stop on the
screen's ack and the seat never reads unsent; and a box holding a draft refuses it while a prompt
rides the draft as before. `mod_turns_e2e` has the shell line beside the slash command on the
explicit mod road. The rig's **P7** sends `!echo mesimon-rig-876` to an idle Sonnet worker on
the mod road (rig step `shell`, checks `shell:` and `shell_out:` off the transcript's
`<bash-input>`/`<bash-stdout>` rows); its first run passed on 2.1.306 and found that the output
turn's `Stop` wakes no crown — no prompt began the turn, so the record never left idle and the
`Stop` is no finished-turn edge, the same as T-707's "the state does not move". `docs/USING.md`
says what a `!` line is from the ask field and the phone.

**Closed after the merge, on the security review's finding: a shell line is a person's alone.**
The first cut read any `!`-leading text as a shell line, whoever wrote it, which handed an agent
principal a shell in another pane with no permission check — the worker's classifier never sees
a `!` line, and the crown's own never saw it either. The hole was older on the hooks road (a
crown's `ask_agent "!…"` was pasted there before this ticket, and a crown's `create_ticket` title
beginning with `!` is typed into the box by the composed spawn), and this ticket had widened it
to the mod road. Closed at every agent road: the crown's `ask_agent` (`AgentAskTicket`), a
linked board's ask at both ends (`agent_ask_board`, `peer_ask`) and the queue's `park_ask` for
any asker but a person refuse a `!` line with `road::SHELL_LINE_REFUSED`; an agent's
`create_ticket` and `rename_ticket` refuse a title beginning with `!` with
`road::SHELL_TITLE_REFUSED`. And `road::is_shell` skips no blank: a person's words arrive
trimmed (`sanitize_prompt`), a brief's description rides under a blank line, so a description
beginning with `!` is words (it goes down the mod as a submit, where the model reads it), never
the shell's. A slash command from the crown stays as it was (T-575; the rig's R6 sends `/exit`):
it stays inside Claude Code's own box and dialogs, where a `!` line is the person's shell.
`shell_line_e2e::an_agent_s_shell_line_and_shell_title_are_refused` pins the five refusals and
that a person's queued `!` line still goes; the rig's **P8** has the crown try one and relay the
refusal. **The review's second pass found a validator differential in the title checks**: they
read the raw title where the board stores `sanitize_title`'s, and the scrub removes a format
hazard (`\u{200B}!rm` stored is `!rm`) and turns a tab into a blank. Now one predicate,
`board::shell_title`, reads the STORED form (`trim_start`, as a start types the title and as
`launch_words` leads with it), in `mint_full` for every non-human principal and in the agent's
rename; and the backstop is the start itself: `spawn_session` refuses a Claude start on any
ticket whose title begins with `!`, whoever set it (a person's `!!! urgent` would otherwise run
`!! urgent` in their shell), and the two wake roads that retype a title skip one. The e2e's
titles carry the zero-width space.

**Owed:** a CHANGELOG line at the next bump — **Fixed:** A message that begins with `!`, sent
from Remote Control or the board's ask field, now runs as a shell command in Claude Code's
prompt box (its bash mode) and the agent reads the output; it used to reach the agent as a
sentence, which auto mode then refused to run. Only a person can send one: the crown's
`ask_agent` refuses it.

## A pull request on a ticket with no agent is the crown's to hear (T-890, 2026-10-22, "crown not notified when pull request of a ticket it ran got merged")

**Why.** On the author's work board the crown did a ticket's work itself, opened the PR and put
it on the ticket; nobody started an agent there. The forge read the merge and the card updated,
and the crown heard nothing. Every crown wake makes one claim, `crown_hears` (T-712): the
worker was started by THIS crown (`started_by_crown`, which reads a record that holds the
agent seat) or the crown watches the ticket. A ticket with no agent record passes neither, so
`hear_forge` dropped the forge's `merged !N` and `hear_merges` (a tip PR's merge, the flags'
road) judged it `started: false`. The same hole took a worker whose seat went before its PR
landed (a crash, a kill): `holds_agent_seat` is false on an `Exited` record. The two e2es
written first for the suspected roads (a parked worker's squash merge, awake and across a
restart) passed and stay as `forge_e2e::a_parked_workers_squash_merge_*`.

**The clause.** `crownwake::unattended_pr`: the ticket is not the crown's own, `crown_watches`
is on, the crown is worn, `Board::live_agent` finds no record (a parked one holds its seat, so
its ticket is still heard by provenance), and the ticket carries a PR (`forge::State::carries_pr`,
own or reviewed: a PR the crown opened and named under the ticket's `Summary` is read by itself
and binds reviewed, T-859, and its edges are the ticket's). `crown_hears` is the one claim, so
`hear_forge`, `hear_merges`, the restart's look and the hold for a merge step all take it. The
switch is the watch's (T-732, on by default; "guards the crown's turns"): off, nothing is said,
and an edge read while off is not said later. A merge the crown never heard of reads as a first
line (`merge_state merged` in the state, a `delivered` or `forge` cause), as a watched ticket's
does. No new state, nothing in `crown.json`.

**Words.** `CROWN_WAKES` gained one sentence after the watch's; USING.md's forge paragraph names
the case. No rig test: the wake's words and roads are unchanged, only who receives them
(T-816's rule).

**Tests.** `forge_e2e::a_pull_request_on_a_ticket_with_no_agent_wakes_the_crown`: a Summary-named
PR on a ticket with no agent is a baseline on its first read and its merge one `forge` wake
(`merged #42`); a worktree ticket's PR binds unheard while a person's agent holds the seat, the
agent killed and the row off its merge is nobody's, and the row on its deployment is one `forge`
wake carrying `merge_state merged` and the arrival's `column DONE`.

## A card's reply rows draw words, not markdown (T-893, 2026-10-22, "transcript preview on ticket should not renders MD decorators")

**What was seen.** A card's two reply rows read `Run this to ship: ``` ! cd ~/Documents/…`:
the fence's backticks spent a sixth of the rows. And a session whose brief was pasted at launch
showed `> Title <pasted_content id="19e3"> …` until its first reply, the wrapper Claude Code
2.1.287 puts round a paste (T-588's trap) taking a third of both rows.

**The wrapper** is gone where a prompt's words are read: `adopt::user_prompt` drops an opening
`<pasted_content …>` line, the blank lines under it and the closing `</pasted_content>` line.
Only a tag on a line of its own is the wrapper; the same words inside a sentence are the
person's and stay. That one function feeds the peek (card and ticket page) and Mesophon's
transcript rows, so all three lose it. The `last-prompt` latch never carried it.

**The markdown** comes off on the card alone. The ticket page renders the reply (`rich.rs`), so
`peek::sanitize` keeps the source; the card draws `peek::card_words`, which is `rich::plain`:
the page's own parse, each block's runs as text — no fence, `#`, emphasis delimiter, code-span
backtick or bullet; an ordered item keeps its number, a link its label (not its target), a
quote its `> ` (the card's mark for the person's words), a fenced block its lines as words.
The card's new-reply row reads the same. Only the first 4 KiB is parsed, because a card is
asked for per frame; a reply longer than that ends in ` ~` so `wrap` still marks the cut.

**A Summary box's label** too (the same screenshot: ``[ ] Ship it: `cd ~/…``): the card's box
rows and the `^j` list draw `rich::plain_inline`, the inline parse alone, because a label is one
line and its own `# ` or `- ` is words, not a block. The box mark stays the card's. The ticket
page draws the Summary note through `rich` already; the `^j` ask quotes the label raw to the
agent, which reads markdown.

**Tests.** `adopt::user_prompt_drops_the_pasted_content_wrapper`,
`rich::plain_takes_the_markdown_off_and_keeps_the_words`, `rich::plain_inline_reads_a_box_label`,
`peek::card_words_drop_the_fence_and_mark_a_long_reply`,
`ui::tests::test_summary_rows_draw_a_code_span_as_words` (card and `^j`). No golden moved.

## A deploy edge never moves a card left, and the right-most column of equals wins (T-891, 2026-10-22, "a deploy wake told the crown a column the ticket had already left")

**What was wrong.** `forge_arrivals` (T-739) ranked the columns a pass's edge satisfied, excluded
the column the ticket was in, and among equal ranks took the last in board order (`max_by_key`;
the comment said the first). On the author's work board (GitLab, dev → staging → production) a
merge commit reached all three environments within minutes, production's read first — a direct
deploy of the merge commit needs no git answer, where an earlier environment running a later
commit waits on ancestry (T-801) — and the card went to production. The next pass's edge for
dev and staging found PROD excluded and took STAGING, the last of the rest: the board moved the
card back, and the wake the crown's turn held said `column STAGING`, which was where the card
then was. The crown read the board faithfully; the board was wrong. The e2e reproduced it on the
old rule: `movement_decision` PROD → STAGING one pass after REVIEW → PROD.

**The rule** (`board::arrival_dest`, pure, over `Arrival`'s new `Ord`, which is the stage order):
the furthest stage; among equals the right-most column in board order, said now rather than
left to `max_by_key`; and a deploy column left of the ticket's own never takes it — a later
environment's column never yields to an earlier one's, the author's "right-most column wins",
and from DONE no deploy edge moves a card. A merge or an opening may still take a ticket back,
as a follow-up PR on a shipped ticket does (T-774's road): its new work is not deployed.

**No column setting.** The ticket asked for one if the board could still move a ticket back on
a deploy edge. It cannot, so there is nothing to switch, and a switch that is never off would
be a row that says nothing (T-677's rule for rows).

**The sentence was cleared.** `CrownWake::fold`, `sent_at` and `told_columns` (T-785) were the
first suspects. The e2e reads the one line a crown's turn held across both passes: `column
PROD, deployed to production !1, deployed to dev !1, deployed to staging !1`, the edges kept as
heard and the column as the card stands when the line goes out. No word to the crown changed,
so no rig test (T-816). The work board's exact sequence was not recovered: a second PR on the
ticket read open (T-890's, opened by the crown) empties `arrived_envs` and its merge fires every
environment at once, which is one road by which the card reached production again after the
crown read staging; the board's `movement_decision` lines say which it was.

Tests: `board::an_arrival_takes_the_right_most_of_equals_and_a_deploy_never_moves_left` (three
on one pass, two from production, from DONE, a stage over board order, a merge back, nothing);
`forge_e2e::a_deploy_to_an_earlier_environment_never_moves_the_card_back` (glab stub, three
environment columns after REVIEW, production first while the crown's turn runs, dev and staging
a pass later, the card in PROD, no move to STAGING or DEV in the feed, and the held line).

## One dialog walker: a Codex approval is a `DialogDelivery` (T-873, 2026-10-22, "One dialog walker on the phone's control road")

Found by the sixth simplify pass (T-867). `server/mesophon.rs` walked a phone's Codex approval
(T-846) in a loop of its own, `control_deliver_approvals`/`control_settle_approval` over
`ApprovalDelivery`, beside `control_deliver_dialogs`/`control_settle_dialog`: the same ready
set, the same `allowed` gate, the same key send (a subset), the same `steps`/`confirm`/
`walk_reason` bookkeeping and the same receipt tail.

**The merge.** `DialogDelivery.response` is now `answer: DeliveryAnswer`, `Dialog(api::DialogAnswer)`
or `Approval { allow }`, and an approval rides `dialog_deliveries` with `by: Deliverer::Phone`.
`delivery_standing` returns the request while it stands, as `Standing::Dialog(dialog, answer)`
off `dialogs` or `Standing::Approval(projection, allow)` off a Codex wait in `permissions`, and
`dialog_step_for` takes that `Standing`, so an approval goes to `codex_approval_step` and a
mismatched pair cannot be spelled. The four places the two loops differed are match arms in
the one loop: the confirm (an approval is confirmed by its wait leaving the snapshot, a dialog
by its hook edge), the phone's gate (`ApproveExisting` and a `Permission` stop, against
`PromptExisting` and `dialog_waiting`), the mod's `answer` frame (dialogs only), and the settle
(an approval's wait dropped once keys went in, feed `mesophon_permission_answer`). The 12 keys
and 8 s an approval and a one-row dialog share are `ONE_WALK`. `control.approvals`,
`ApprovalDelivery` and both functions are gone.

**No behaviour change, and no receipt changed shape.** The ticket expected two receipts to merge
into one; both were already `Reply::Delivery { status, reason, replaced: None }`, and each feed
word stays its own. One map now holds both, so a dialog answer and an approval on one session
refuse each other as `input is already pending`; a session stops on one of them at a time, so
that was never reachable.

Tests: `a_codex_approval_walks_to_yes_or_no_and_confirms` also walks through `dialog_step_for`;
`provider_e2e`, `trust_accept_e2e`, `approve_bridge` and `crown_e2e` green. No e2e in this
repository drives a phone's approval; the relay's browser tests do.

## A compaction is painted, and moves nothing (T-894, 2026-10-22, "indicate compaction in progress")

The author's board: a seat compacting its conversation read idle — Claude Code compacts an idle
session before its prompt cache expires (T-728), and the card wore the finished turn's `✓` through
the minute or two of it. The other two shapes were wrong the other way: a person's `/compact` at a
finished turn put the seat at `Running` (2026-09-09's "exposes Running during compaction"), which
`on_working` moved to IN PROGRESS, `on_done` moved back at `PostCompact`, and the crown heard a
turn end that was no turn; an automatic compaction inside a turn spun the working spinner, which
says the agent is working when it is the engine summarizing. T-728's `quiet_compaction` held only
the idle automatic case, and `manual_compact_prior` restored a state the machine should never have
left.

**A compaction moves nothing, and the window is a fact on the record.** `Machine::compacting_since`
opens at any `PreCompact` (a duplicate keeps the first clock) and closes at `PostCompact`, at
anything that says the conversation moved on (a prompt, a turn's start or end, a top-level `Stop`,
a `SessionEnd`, a pane death, a new conversation's `SessionStart`), and at `COMPACT_STALE_MS`
(ten minutes, the daemon's tick) — a vetoed compaction fires `PreCompact` alone, and `mesimon hook`
fails open, so a `PostCompact` can be lost. No frame of the window moves the state: `PreCompact`
and `SessionStart{compact}` are inert everywhere (the start may land after the end, both being
relayed on their own; 2.1.266 was seen sending it late), and a `PostCompact` with no window open —
a restart between the frames — keeps its old meaning: automatic continues the turn, manual leaves
the seat at the prompt at Low. The two manual scenarios now expect the state and the column kept,
and every compaction scenario asserts the window (`expect.compacting`). The daemon broadcasts a
window edge that moved no state (`on_hook`'s `announce`), decorates `SessionRecord::compacting`
onto the snapshot only (the machine holds it; a restart's machine starts with none), and the
auto-park gate waits on it where it waited on the manual prior.

**The card paints it.** `glyphs::compacting`, the cell pressed down and let go (`⠿ ⠶ ⠤ ⠶`;
ascii `# % _ %`) on the slow cadence: distinct from the spinner, which never draws a full cell or
a lower square, grey, under needs-you and the error mark and over the done mark and the spinner
both (`card_glyph`, `session_glyph`); a parked or dead record's flag paints nothing. The activity
row says `compacting context` with the pulse, on the card and in the ticket page's preview, the
peek's last step being history until it ends; the page's state word is `compacting`
(`glyphs::record_word`), and the shin thinks. Codex is untouched: its `/compact` is a real
maintenance turn (2026-09-10) and spins as before. Mesophon says nothing of it yet.

**Tests.** `glyphs::a_compaction_wears_its_own_slow_mark`, the goldens
`board_compacting_120x30` and `ticket_compacting_120x30`, the scenarios `manual-compact-end_turn`,
`manual-compact-interrupted`, `idle-compact` and `auto-compact-continuation`, and
`compact_e2e::a_compaction_is_painted_and_moves_nothing` on both roads (fails before the fix at
its first assertion: the manual window moved the ticket).

## T-831 — the rig's stand-in phone binds per board

`ci/rig.py`'s phone was one fixed `/tmp/msmn-rig-phone.sock`, which `Phone.__init__` removed
before binding: a second rig run in another worktree deleted the first's socket, and the first
board's `mesimon approve` reached the wrong phone or none. **Decision:** the socket is
`<rt_dir>/phone.sock` (`Rig.phone_sock`), beside `hook.sock`, so it fits `sun_path` as that does,
and the copied phone mod has that path patched in. A run removes only a file at its own board's
path, so no run touches another's. **Proof:** `ci/rig.py --only C1` on the real Sonnet (claude
2.1.308): PASS, `phone:allow` Bash → allow, `c1-allowed.txt` exists.

## T-872 — the Codex input roads read the sampler's screens (2026-10-22)

T-845 and T-847 left two per-tick forks on the writer thread beside T-857's sampler:
`drive_codex_inputs` captured a Codex seat's input screen every tick while words, a title or a
`/plan` were owed, and `press_steer` captured one on `settle_owed`'s cadence. **Decision:**
`want_codex_inputs` asks the sampler every tick for the screens of the seats
