`codex_input_waiting` names (Idle, the runtime ready, words or `/plan` owed, no Enter sent) and
of every pane with a steer owed; both roads read `self.screens` through `screen_since`, the
fence the Claude composer wait already used, now one helper for all four reads. The fence for a
Codex input is the later of the record's last state change and the owed entry's birth, so a
screen from a previous pane under the same session name, or from a running turn, is no input
yet; a steer's is its paste. A stale screen costs a steer press as a failed capture did (ten
presses, 5 s). The steer's Enter itself reads the pane live once, at the key, after the sample
says the box holds the words: a running turn can raise an approval dialog after the sample, and
an Enter there would answer it for the person (the commit review's catch). The live read
decides and the sample only spares it (`codex::steer_presses`): with no sample from after the
paste (a slow sampler under build load), the live box still gets its Enter, where requiring both
sent none and left the words in the box (the independent review's catch). `codex_steer`'s one read at the ask edge stays a fork, as do `send_brief`'s and
`press_plan`'s: edges, not ticks. `InputScreen` derives `Clone` so the plan step can hold one
while the writer mutates.

**Proof:** `cargo ut`; `provider_e2e`, `plan_mode_e2e`, `trust_accept_e2e` and `prompt_e2e`
36/36 twice with no wait widened; `ci/codex-lifecycle-e2e.py --live --case stop` on the real
Codex passed.

## A compaction's frames across a restart are no turn (T-894 review, 2026-10-22)

The review of T-894 found the window's one hole: a daemon restarted inside a quiet compaction
(the `U` chip, inside T-728's two minutes) came back with no window and read the tail at Low;
the compaction's two helper `SubagentStop`s (STALE-MAP T-577: the engine's own loops fire them
twice during a compaction) then promoted that Low `Idle` to `Running` at Medium, which
`on_working` takes, and the `PostCompact{auto}` with no window affirmed `Running` at High — with
no `Stop` to follow, the status probe called it an Esc and the crown heard a turn end.

**The compaction's `SessionStart` opens a missed window** (`COMPACT_LATE_MS`: not one within
30 s of a `PostCompact`, which is that compaction's start arriving late — the two are relayed on
their own, and 2.1.266 was seen sending it late), **a `SubagentStop` inside a window promotes
nothing**, and **a `PostCompact` with no window never invents a turn**: an automatic one affirms
`Running` only where the state already is one (`Running`, a held dialog) and says nothing to a
seat at rest, since Claude Code compacts an idle seat automatically too; a manual one leaves an
`Idle` where it is, at the confidence it had — the Low `Idle{Unknown}` it used to demote to held
the High-only auto-park off until something re-affirmed. **A vetoed `/compact` keeps its clock**:
no road reports the veto (the hook set fires nothing for "nothing to compact"; the mod's
`session.compact` sees the skip but speaks the hook set's names alone), so the seat reads
compacting, and is held from auto-park, for `COMPACT_STALE_MS`.

Tests: `attention::a_post_compact_with_no_window_invents_no_turn`,
`attention::a_restart_inside_a_compaction_reads_no_turn`, the scenario `restart-in-compaction`
(the review's frames), and `compact_e2e`'s restart phase through the real daemon.

## PR news reaches the card and the crown within seconds, and crowns stop polling pipelines (T-895, 2026-10-22, the author: "a PR named on a plain line under a ticket's `Summary` takes long enough to show on the card that it looks like a bug, and the other PR stories are slow too" ∙ "crowns sometimes watch a PR's pipeline themselves (`gh pr checks --watch`, sleep loops)")

**Why it was slow.** The forge's one cadence was the minute (`forge::EVERY`, checked on the 10 s
slow bucket, so 70–90 s worst case), with two exceptions: a turn's end's burst (T-761) only
where the train could take the ticket or the crown heard its turn, and the busy cadence (T-781)
only for a PR whose pipeline already read running or waiting. Every other story waited for the
minute: `write_note` forgot `summary_prs` and asked nothing; a `pr create` reached the daemon
twice — as a `PostToolUse` frame nothing read for it, and in the transcript ledger at the `Stop`
— and the ledger's landing asked nothing either; a review, a conflict, a merge or a pipeline's
first run on a quiet PR was the minute's. And `queue_forge_burst` pruned the owed tickets by
`forge_fresh`, which judges against the agent's last end of turn: for a ticket with no agent, or
one mid-turn, that is zero, so any read ever made the ticket "current" and dropped its ask.

**Decided: every event asks the forge now, and news warms the ticket; the minute stays.**
`Daemon::owe_forge_read(ticket)` is the one road: `forge.owed.insert(ticket, now)`, `warm`, and
`queue_forge_burst`, which now prunes by `State::settle_owed` (answered by a read begun since the
ask, or nothing to read) in place of `forge_fresh`. Four callers: (1) `write_note` compares the
`Summary`'s addresses before and after the write (`summary_prs_of`, by `same_url`) and asks on a
change; (2) `on_hook` reads a `PostToolUse` whose `tool_name` is `Bash` and whose
`tool_input.command` `is_pr_create` — the hook set's and the mod's frames carry both (the mod's
`postToolUseBody` keeps the envelope's `command`) — and `pr_created` feeds `pr_create_seen`, sets
`cost_due` so the ledger reads the result's address on the next bucket (a checkout ticket binds
by it alone) and asks at once (a worktree ticket's PR binds by its branch); (3)
`Ledger::apply_named` names the tickets whose `pr_urls` or `pr_acted` grew, and `on_cost_scanned`
asks for each — a `pr create` or a `gh pr review` at a `Stop`, mid-turn under `cost_due`, or on a
Codex seat with no hook road, is read in seconds; (4) `look_after_turn` looks at every worktree
ticket on a pull-requests board (`forge_follows`), train or crown or neither, where it looked only
for a train ticket or a crown's worker. **The warm window**: `State::warm` (memory only) stamps a
ticket on news — a read that changed its set with an open or merged PR in it (never a first read's
baseline, only its opening), a Summary write, a `pr create` — and `State::busy(now)` adds the
tickets inside `WARM_MS` (3 min) to the running-pipeline set, so the busy road (15 s) reads them:
a PR's first pipeline run, a quick review and a quick merge land in seconds, and the merge
commit's first run after a merge too. `queue_forge_busy` and `launch_forge_burst` are unchanged;
`BURST_MS` got a seam (`MESIMON_FORGE_BURST_MS`) beside `WARM_MS`'s.

**`EVERY` stays 60 s.** The four reported stories are covered by the events and the window; what
the minute alone still reads is news on a PR quiet for more than three minutes with no pipeline
running — a human's review hours later — and it reads it within 70 s as before. Shortening
`EVERY` to 30 s would double the standing cost of every repository on every board (60 → 120 list
calls per repository per hour against GitHub's 5,000) for that one story; the window costs at most
12 extra list calls per event, and a burst one. **Rate limits** (`forge::rate_limited`: `rate
limit`, `HTTP 429`, `429 Too Many`, `Too Many Requests` in the CLI's first line) fall into the
same 300 s `BACKOFF` a failed call does, and `State::trouble` names it on the advisory row —
`<repo>: rate limited by the forge ∙ read again in 5 min` — in place of the CLI's paragraph.

**Latency per story, before → after** (the e2es' measured numbers, a stub `gh` on an idle
machine; the real forge adds one call's round trip, under a second):

| story | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| a PR URL written under `Summary` | 70–90 s (the minute) | 0.12 s (`owe_forge_read` at the write; up to the 10 s floor after another read) |
| `gh pr create`, mid-turn | 70–90 s | 0.12 s (the `PostToolUse`; the same floor) |
| `gh pr create`, at a turn's end nobody heard | 70–90 s | 1.7 s (the idle edge's 1.5 s settle, the look, the burst) |
| a review, conflict, merge or first pipeline run on a PR with news inside 3 min | 70–90 s | ≤ 16 s (the busy cadence; 1.1 s in the e2e at 500 ms) |
| the same on a PR quiet for over 3 min, pipeline settled | 70–90 s | 70–90 s (the minute, unchanged) |
| a pipeline already running or waiting | ≤ 16 s | ≤ 16 s |

**The crown stops polling.** What led a crown to `gh pr checks --watch`: `get_ticket`'s `prs`
said `pipeline: running` and nothing beside it said who would notice the pass, and the one
sentence in `CROWN_WAKES` ("Nothing needs polling.") named no cadence and no command. Now
`CROWN_WAKES` says the board reads the forge on its own, in round numbers (about 15 seconds while
a pipeline runs or the PR just changed, about a minute otherwise), that a pass or failure, a
review, a conflict and a merge each arrive as a prompt, and that a watch command (`gh pr checks
--watch`, `glab ci status --live`) or a sleep loop keeps the session busy, which holds the merge
train and the wake itself — "the way to wait for a pull request's news is to end the turn". And
`get_ticket` carries `prs_about` (`mcp::PRS_ABOUT`, beside `prs`, on a pull-requests board) with
the same words where the crown reads the running pipeline. Both in the lint's voice
(`lint_tool_text`). USING.md's forge paragraph has the cadence and the crown's rule.

**Refuted.** A shorter `EVERY` (above). Reading the `PostToolUse`'s `tool_response` for the URL
and feeding it to the ledger from the hook: the ledger is the one keeper of `pr_urls` and reads
the transcript's own `tool_result`, which is the same text a bucket later; the hook road only
asks the read sooner. Warming on every set change, a first read included: a fresh board's first
pass would warm every ticket with a merged PR for three minutes, one `pr view` per PR the list
no longer holds every 15 s. Persisting `warm` in `forge.json`: a restart's first pass reads
everything, and what changed while it was down is news again.

**Tests.** `forge::a_warm_ticket_is_busy_for_the_window_and_an_owed_read_settles_on_a_read_since`
(the window, a ticket with no set, `settle_owed` from the ask's moment, the rate limit named);
`mcp::the_crown_is_told_the_board_reads_the_forge_and_polls_nothing` (`CROWN_WAKES` and
`PRS_ABOUT`, the lint). `forge_e2e::a_summary_address_and_news_on_a_warm_pull_request_are_read_within_seconds`
(the minute at 60 s: a Summary write binds its PR within the burst's floor; the ticket is read
every busy step; a review inside the window wakes the crown within seconds; past the window
nothing reads it) and `a_pr_create_is_read_mid_turn_and_at_a_gated_turn_end` (no crown, the train
unarmed: a `PostToolUse` `gh pr create` binds mid-turn and feeds `pr_create_seen`; a turn that
pushed and opened a PR with no hook road is read at its `Stop`, having been read by nothing
mid-turn). Rig F12 (`crown_never:pr checks,--watch,sleep,ci status,pr view`, a new check over
the crown's Bash calls and Monitors since the test began): the crown, asked to wait for a running
pipeline, ends its turn and reports on the board's `pipeline passed #42` wake. On the real Sonnet,
2026-10-22: PASS in 77 s — zero Bash calls, the crown's turn on the ask ended in 6 s ("Pipeline
on #42 is still running. Ending my turn…"), the forge wake came 9 s after the stub's pass, and
its turn on it said `F12 passed: #42`; the first run read the same and failed only `replies:done`,
the new check having shadowed the worker's transcript rows (fixed in the same ticket).

**Review (2026-10-22, independent, after the merge).** No storm and no writer fork; the
rate-limit handling and the wire are fine. Two fixes, on the same branch. (1) **A stuck owed
read**: `pr_created` owed `forge.owed[t]` on any Bash `PostToolUse` whose command passed
`is_pr_create`, but `settle_owed` cleared only on `at_ms[t] >= since`, and `at_ms` is written only
for a ticket a query names — a worktree with a branch, or a named PR. A checkout ticket whose
`gh pr create` printed no URL (it failed, `--help`, `--web`, `--dry-run`, or the words sat inside an
`echo` or a commit message) was never queried, so it stayed owed until a restart: `awaited(t)`
held every crown wake for that worker `FORGE_WAIT_MS`, and the tick priced a `forge_query` every
250 ms. Now `Daemon::forge_names` (a worktree with a branch, or an address in `named_prs`) gates
`owe_forge_read`, and `queue_forge_burst` hands `settle_owed` the owed tickets no read names any
more (a binding torn down, a Summary emptied); a checkout ticket's `pr create` owes nothing until
the ledger reads its address, and the ledger's landing owes it then. `is_pr_create` reads the
command through `shell_words`, so a quoted mention is one word and opens nothing, and a `create`
whose own segment carries `--help`, `-h` or `--dry-run` opens nothing. (2) **The words
over-promised**: `PRS_ABOUT` said the board "wakes the crown with each change", but `hear_forge`
wakes only where the crown hears — started by the crown, `watch_ticket`ed, or an unattended PR
under `crown_watches` — and a worker reading its own `prs_about` is never woken. Both texts now say
whom the wake is for (an agent the crown started, a ticket it watches, one with no agent), that
the session on the ticket itself is not woken, and that a repository whose last read failed or hit
a rate limit is read again in about five minutes, not 15 s. **Steady-state cost**: with many
agents ending turns, each turn's end and each `pr create` is one read of the ticket's repositories
under the 10 s floor, so a busy repository is read up to about 6 times a minute where the minute's
pass alone read it once; the warm window's reads sit inside the same floor (one per 15 s per
warm repository), and 6 a minute is 360 calls an hour per repository against GitHub's 5,000. Rig
F12 run again on the crown's new words: PASS. Tests: core `forge::an_act_and_its_result_name_the_pr_and_a_failed_act_names_none`
gained the `is_pr_create` cases; `forge::a_warm_ticket_is_busy_for_the_window_and_an_owed_read_settles_on_a_read_since`
the unnamed drop; `forge_e2e::a_summary_address_and_news_on_a_warm_pull_request_are_read_within_seconds`
ends on a watched checkout ticket whose `pr create` printed no URL: no read asked, and its turn's
wake comes within seconds, not held `FORGE_WAIT_MS` for a read nothing can make.

## The board's snapshot is asked off the UI thread (T-812, 2026-10-22, T-804's follow-up: "a slow daemon turn still freezes the board for the turn's length")

**What froze.** `App::pump` → `App::refresh` → `fetch` waited for every snapshot on the loop's
own thread: after each `BoardChanged` push (~14 a minute with one agent working) and after
nearly every mutating key (69 `self.refresh()` callers in `app.rs`, 8 more in its submodules).
T-804 took the parked records off the wire and T-842 the archived tickets, so the bytes were
no longer the cost; the daemon's writer turn was. A `refresh_panes` tick, a git call or build
load on the machine held the writer, the snapshot queued behind it, and the keys and the
spinner froze for the turn's length — the journal logs ~200 ticks over 1 s in a week, all
`refresh_panes`. T-856 had already taken the *reconnect* off this thread; the request itself
stayed on it.

**Applied.**
- **The lane.** `Transport::snapshot_detached` answers `Command::Snapshot` through a channel.
  The real client keeps a second connection for it (`Client::lane`, under a mutex, opened by
  `open_lane`: the observer's road with no `Subscribe` — a lane never reads a push, and a
  subscriber nobody drains grows its event channel by one entry per push for the board's
  life) and asks on a thread per call; a kept connection that fails outright was opened on a
  daemon that is gone (a `U` reload, a crash and a respawn) and is dialled once more, a
  timeout is not retried (the daemon is up and slow; a second wait would double it), and
  any failure drops the lane so the next ask dials. The merge's `request_detached` (T-431)
  stays a fresh connection per call: once a day, not fourteen a minute. The parse of the
  reply is the lane's reader thread's, as the board's always was its own.
- **One ask out, the rest coalesced.** `App::refresh_soon` drains the pushes already here
  (each was written after the change it names, and the daemon reads this ask after both),
  sends on the lane when nothing is out, and otherwise sets `snapshot_wanted`;
  `App::poll_snapshot` in `pump` lands the answer — `absorb` and what follows it, in
  `land_snapshot`, the one road every board takes — and asks once more when something
  wanted it meanwhile, unless a merge runs (its reply asks, as before). Pushes during one
  ask become one follow-up; a key and three pushes in flight are one. `refresh_soon` lands
  at once when the answer is already in, which a fake's always is, so the TestBackend
  tests behave as they did; only the held-answer fakes see the asynchrony.
- **Waited for, where the next line reads the fresh board.** `App::refresh` stays the
  synchronous fetch, on the board's own connection, and it lands the ask in flight first
  (`settle_snapshot`), so no board ever lands after a newer one; the drawer's `RescanExternal`,
  which answers with the board on this thread, settles first too. The callers kept on it:
  a duplicated or composed ticket (`select_ticket` of the id just made), a column named or
  renamed and `ReorderColumn` (the cursor follows the fresh column list), the tag sheet's
  delete, move and naming (its cursor over the registry), a note saved (the description
  word reads the note's rev), a terminal or an external conversation adopted (a rail index,
  a title), `SetWorkspace` (its sentence reads the answer), a spawn or a resume before a
  focus (the attach needs the record), the tiers editor's rows, a board linked (its name),
  and the practice board's first refresh. `send`/`send_on` ask; `send_now` waits. Everything
  else asks: the push road, the reconnect cadence, every Settings toggle, snooze, archive,
  restore, the asks and their queue, sleep and wake, the merge dialog's reply, the three
  returns from a handover, and the card move — `drop_ghost` no longer sets the cursor by
  index on a board it has not seen; the card is drawn where it was, the cursor on it, and
  `absorb`'s `follow_ticket` takes the cursor to where the daemon put it.
- **The reconnect cadence asks nothing on this thread.** `Transport::redial` brings the board's
  own connection back with no request riding it (`Ok(true)` up, `Ok(false)` while T-856's
  reopen dials, `Err` on a failed attempt); up, the lane asks, and the landing is what says
  `daemon back`. Before, the cadence's `refresh` blocked for one snapshot on the connection
  it had just reopened, and for `RESPONSE_WAIT` on a connection that was up and slow.

**Measured, so the archived cut is not done.** On a 677-ticket board of the author's shape
(648 archived, five notes each) the snapshot is 42 KB: T-842 already leaves the archived
tickets off the wire, and `ArchivedTickets` is the on-demand road the ticket proposed. What the
UI thread keeps of a snapshot is `absorb`, 325 µs debug and 84 µs release on that board (the
parse, now the lane's thread's, 647 µs and 130 µs). Nothing left to cut.

**Not done.** The ticket page's small reads — `poll_notes`, `poll_summaries`, `poll_held`,
`poll_archive`, `poll_shell_tail` — still ride the board's own connection synchronously from
`pump`, asked once per note revision or once per screen and again after each snapshot for an
archived ticket on screen; on a slow turn each is a wait of its own. The lane and
`poll_snapshot` are the pattern.

**Tests.** `app::a_snapshot_in_flight_blocks_no_key_and_no_frame` (a held answer: keys
resolve, frames draw, a move and three pushes become one follow-up, the cursor rides the
move once the board lands), `app::a_waited_refresh_lands_the_snapshot_in_flight_first`,
`app::the_reconnect_cadence_asks_the_lane_once_the_dial_lands`,
`client::the_snapshot_lane_keeps_one_connection_and_never_subscribes` (a listening socket at
a scratch repo's `orch.sock`: one Hello for two asks, none for Subscribe, one more dial after
a hang-up). **Owed:** a CHANGELOG line at the next bump — **Changed:** the board no longer
freezes while the daemon is slow to answer a refresh; keys and the spinner keep going and the
board lands when it comes.

## Wire twins and e2e helpers left by the sixth simplify pass (T-875, 2026-10-22)

Three leftovers the sixth simplify pass (T-867) named and did not take, because each touches a
wire name or a test shape.

- **`PeerAnswer` is the one board-ask answer.** `Response::PeerAsked` (daemon to daemon) and
  `Response::AgentAskedBoard` (to the asking crown) spelled `road`, `crown` and `reply` twice,
  and `agent_ask_board` took one apart to build the other. Now `PeerAsked(PeerAnswer)` and
  `AgentAskedBoard { board, #[serde(flatten)] asked: PeerAnswer }`: **the wire bytes are the
  same** (`command::tests::board_ask_answers_keep_their_bytes` pins both lines and an older
  daemon's answer without `reply`), and `ask_board`'s text is unchanged, so no rig run. The
  receipt's `reply` stays this board's own reading (`PeerAnswer { reply, ..asked }`), not the
  peer's.
- **A ticket's PR addresses are two lists that share none.** `TicketQuery` carries `created`
  (the `pr create`s' URLs) and `theirs` (acted on, the `Summary`'s), and
  `TicketQuery::named()` yields each with whether it is someone else's, the `pr create`s' first
  — the order `opened` had. `forge::sample` no longer asks `theirs` per address. `NamedPrs`
  builds the same two lists (`is_empty`, `into_all` for `forge_fresh`); T-895's
  `forge_names` and `opened_unread` behave as before.
- **E2e helpers in `tests/common/mod.rs`:** `TestClient::create_ticket(title)` (TODO, the
  board's default workspace), `TestClient::spawn_claude(ticket)` (launch words unsent) and
  `Harness::one_turn(c, sid)` (`UserPromptSubmit`, running, `Stop`, idle). Migrated:
  `boardlink_e2e`, `crown_e2e` and `provider_e2e`'s `create`/`spawn` pairs, `boardlink_e2e`'s
  `settle_idle` and `forge_e2e`'s module `turn`. **Left as they are**, the diff not a line
  each: helpers with another column, workspace or tier (`column_e2e`, `duplicate_e2e`,
  `tier_e2e`), a spawn that submits or returns the ticket too (`mod_turns_e2e`,
  `mod_bridge_e2e`, `state_lab_e2e`), `mcp_e2e`'s `turn` (Stop first, then a prompt) and the
  local `turn`s inside `forge_e2e`'s tests. New tests use the common three.

## Long briefs and asks arrive whole or are refused in words (T-896, 2026-10-22, "Long briefs and asks are cut silently at 4 KiB")

**Asked.** The author found a crown's brief cut past about 3,000 characters. Every road that
carries words to an agent capped them at 4,096 bytes with `cap_bytes` and told nobody: about
3,000 characters once a text holds `—` and `→`. `get_ticket`'s description ended in a bare `…`
that a crown read as the end; an `ask_agent`, an `ask_board`, a linked board's ask, a person's
ask and a column template were cut the same way.

**Measured, per road, before picking a number.**
- **The mod's `submit`**: rig P1 carries a 10 KB brief whole as the first prompt, and B1 (this
  ticket) an 8,719-character one, byte for byte. Nothing on our side caps it: the bridge is one
  JSON line over `orch.sock` (1 MiB a line) and the mod reads lines with no limit. A `submit`
  past 10 KB was not measured on Claude Code's side.
- **The paste road** (Claude Code 2.1.308, Codex 0.163, a private tmux, `load-buffer -` then
  `paste-buffer -p`, no Enter): a 32,660-byte text with 900 newlines became Claude's
  `[Pasted text #1 +900 lines]` chip, every line counted, and Codex's
  `[Pasted Content 29060 chars]`, every character. `brief_e2e` pastes 12 KiB through the same
  tmux road on both test roads.
- **Remote Control**: a letter rides a 256 KiB control frame (`mesimon-team::control::MAX_BYTES`);
  a linked board's ask rides `orch.sock`'s 1 MiB line.

**Built.**
- **One prompt cap, the note's: `PROMPT_MAX_BYTES = NOTE_MAX_BYTES` (32 KiB).** Every road above
  carries it, and words past it belong in a note an ask names. `sanitize_prompt` now returns
  `Result<Option<String>, String>`: past the cap it is `Err` with the count and the limit
  (`command::too_long_words`), never a cut. The `Result` is the enforcement, since no caller
  can drop the refusal the way the old callers could not see the cut. The crown's `ask_agent`
  adds where the rest goes ("words past it are a note: write_note holds them"), a crown's
  `ask_board` the same, and Mesophon's two prompt roads and its start answer with the daemon's
  words in place of "prompt is too long". Mesophon's own check and the TUI's fields read the
  same constant, so a field never holds what the daemon refuses.
- **`get_ticket`'s description: whole up to `mcp::DESCRIPTION_MAX_BYTES` (16 KiB), and past it
  a head that says so.** 16 KiB is the plan's bound beside it (`needs_you.plan`), so a routine
  read never carries more than a plan does. Past it, `description` is the longest head that
  fits ending in `…`, and the new `description_cut` says how long the whole is, how much is
  here, and that `read_note` with the note's id returns all of it (`mcp::describe`). The words
  are on the field itself, so a model that skipped the tool text still finds the rest. The
  tool's own text is at its 820-byte cap and did not change.
- **The brief a launch sends was never capped, and still is not.** `road::launch_words` is the
  one composer for the paste, the mod's `submit`, a wake and Codex's box, bounded by the note
  cap alone.
- **A template past the cap is never sent cut mid-sentence.** `sanitize_template` refuses it in
  words at the daemon, the Settings field and the TUI's fake. One that reaches the board anyway
  (a hand-edited `columns.toml`) is kept but stood down: `PromptSet::text` sends mesimon's own
  words, the Settings row reads `over the limit` with the count, and `doctor`'s `agent prompts`
  line warns `N over the limit`.

**Refuted.** Keeping 4 KiB with a "cut" marker on prompts: an agent reading a marker cannot ask
for the rest of an ask, and a sender told the count can split or write a note. Splitting a
long ask into several turns: two turns are not one prompt, and a turn edge between halves
changes what the agent does. Carrying the whole description in `get_ticket` up to the note
cap: every routine read would carry up to 32 KiB, and the head plus `read_note` costs one
call only on the rare long brief.

**Tests.** `command::a_long_ask_arrives_whole_and_a_longer_one_is_refused_in_words` (10 KiB whole,
32 KiB + 1 refused with count and limit, bytes not characters, the scrub before the count);
`prompts::a_long_template_arrives_whole_and_a_longer_one_is_refused_or_stood_down`;
`mcp::a_long_description_rides_get_ticket_whole_and_a_longer_one_says_it_was_cut`;
`road::a_long_brief_is_composed_whole_under_the_title`.
`brief_e2e::a_long_description_reaches_the_agent_whole_as_its_first_prompt` (a 12 KiB brief with
its fact last: every line reaches the stub in order under the title on the hooks road and the
mod's; `get_ticket` carries it whole; a 20 KiB one is a 16 KiB head with `description_cut`
naming the note, and `read_note` returns it whole).
`crown_e2e::the_crown_sends_now_into_a_working_turn` (a 32 KiB + 1 ask is refused naming
`write_note` and queues nothing; a 10 KiB ask lands whole). Rig B1 (`long_brief = 8000` with a
`tail`, a new pair of keys in `tests.toml`): the worker replies with the code word in the last
paragraph, and the crown, which never saw the brief, finds it with `get_ticket`. On the real
Sonnet, 2026-10-22, Claude Code 2.1.308: PASS in 34 s, first prompt 8,719 characters byte for
byte, both replies `tamarind`.

**Review (T-898), three fixes.** (1) The Settings field for a template opened on `text()`, which
sends the default for an oversized one, so Enter unchanged saved `None` over the person's
template: the field now opens on `custom()`, and Enter unchanged is refused in words and keeps
it (`app::an_oversized_template_opens_as_written_and_is_never_erased_by_enter`). (2) The phone
let 32 KiB wait at the relay, and a sealed letter is hex of the JSON it seals, so escaping could
take it past the 128 KiB mailbox: words that wait are capped at 16 KiB
(`MAIL_PROMPT_MAX_BYTES`, the worst ordinary escaping then fills half the mailbox), the sealed
envelope is measured as a ticket's is, and both refusals say how many KiB to cut and keep the
draft, before the away sheet on a first send (`ux.test.js`'s away-terminal flow). The live
road keeps 32 KiB. (3) An ask with pictures read a too-long text as no words and answered
that the words name no picture; `with_pictures` now returns the length refusal first
(`attachments_e2e`).

## A key that reads the board before it writes waits for its last press's board (T-812 review, 2026-10-22)

An independent review of T-812 (T-897's `Review` note) found five regressions with one root: a
key that read the displayed board, sent a change derived from it, and asked the next board on
the lane, so a second press read a board that had not caught up. Column settings (the whole
struct goes) undid each other in the daemon; `u` restored an older grace entry, or was not
offered at all; `>>` and `.` let the cursor follow the card out of its column; an answer older
than a `c` stood its parked focus down; two `^n`, two tag-colour presses or two tag toggles
stepped once.

**The rule.** Every ask is counted (`snapshot_sent`), the board on screen knows the count it was
asked at (`landing`), and `need_seq` is the count a board must have to show the last change this
board made. `App::catch_up` lands the ask out or fetches until `landing >= need_seq`; in the
common case the answer came within the frame and nothing waits. It runs before every
read-modify-write key: `set_column` and the two column text savers, the tier cycle, the tag
colour, toggle and quick cycle, the twelve board switches (manual merge, crown and its five
settings, agent tools, the brief, the board's workspace), sleep and wake (the key's `Ctx` is
rebuilt after it), `nudge`, `.` and every drop. The delete waits for its own board
(`send_now_on`), because `u` and its target are read off the grace band. Intents armed before an
ask are fenced by the count: `pending_spawn_focus` carries the count at the key and is judged
only by a later board, and a filing (`>>`, `.`) sets `cursor_hold` so the landing that shows the
move keeps the cursor home and the next card slides under it; a nudge rides its card as before.
Not delta commands on the wire: the wire is unchanged, and each of these keys already took one
round trip before it.

**Tests.** `a_column_edit_reads_the_edit_before_it`,
`undo_restores_the_ticket_just_deleted_not_an_earlier_one`,
`a_filing_keeps_the_cursor_home_when_the_board_lands_late`,
`an_answer_older_than_the_spawn_leaves_its_focus_parked`,
`repeated_presses_each_step_once_while_the_board_lands_late` (tier, tag colour, tag toggle), each
on a fake whose snapshot answers come late; the fake now keeps a grace band and applies tags and
tag colours. `a_snapshot_in_flight_blocks_no_key_and_no_frame` keeps its claim for keys that
read nothing (navigation, frames) and now shows a move waiting for the ask out.

## A `/compact` from the board, an Esc out of one, and an ask that met it (T-894, 2026-10-22, three bugs from the author's own seat)

The author's board, seq 5–47 of one daemon life: a `/compact` from the ask field sat 11 s as an
unacked paste (`paste_unacked`); an Esc out of it left the card on "compacting context"; and
the crown's `ask_agent` into that seat went down the mod and came back `prompt_submit_refused`
(`dropped`), its words left on the card as "prompt not sent". That mark was the crown's words,
not the `/compact`'s: the only writer of `unsent` in that life was the refusal.

**Measured** on Claude Code 2.1.308 in a scratch pane (hooks logged, the session file and the
screen sampled every 130 ms). A completed `/compact`: the composer empties at once, the session
file reads `busy`, `✻ Compacting conversation… (Ns · ↓ K tokens)` is painted above the composer
from ~160 ms, and `PreCompact`, a `SubagentStop`, `SessionStart{compact}` and `PostCompact` come,
then `idle` and `⎿ Compacted`. **An Esc 1.3 s in: `PreCompact` alone, no other hook, nothing in
the transcript; the file flips `idle` within 130 ms, the line goes, and `/compact` is put back
in the box.** The refusal's words are Claude Code's own for a plugin's input after a person's
Esc ("the session was stopped and nobody has sent input since", `n8e` in the binary): input is
held until the person types.

**A `/` command is acked off the screen**, as a `!` line is (T-876): `Owed::screen_acked`
(was `shell`) covers `road::is_command`, the feed says `command_sent`, and the ack is the box
read empty `SHELL_RENDER_MS` after the Enter. A command, like a `!` line, runs only from an
empty box, never kept unsent, and its ack leaves words already unsent as they were: it is the
box's own, not a prompt.

**The screen closes an interrupted compaction**: a compacting Claude pane's screen is wanted
every tick, and the window closes (`Signal::CompactionEnded`, moving nothing, feed
`compaction_ended_on_screen`) on two screens `COMPACT_CLEAR_MS` apart, both
`COMPACT_SCREEN_GRACE_MS` after the window opened, showing the composer and no
`Compacting conversation` line (`composer::compacting`). A veto that paints no line closes the
same way, so its ten-minute clock is now only the backstop. `SessionRecord::compacting` is now
set on the record as the window moves (reset at a restart), not only decorated.

**Words wait out a compaction**: `quiet::holds_against_words` holds a compacting Claude seat, so
a queued ask and the crown's ask wait for the window to close. **A submit refused in the stopped
words goes in by the paste road** (keys, which Claude Code takes, and the road every ask takes
on the hook set), owed and acked as a paste, the crown's ask still the turn's — **only into an
empty box**, read live: after an Esc out of `/compact` the box holds `/compact`, and words pasted
after it would run as the compaction's instructions. There, and on any other refusal, the words
stay unsent for the person's resend, and a crown ask reads `asked: dropped, by: agent` on the
crown's `get_ticket` (no wake: a new wake cause would change `crown.json`). A person's resend
then goes once they have typed in the pane or cleared its box.

Tests: `compact_e2e` (an Esc phase on a stub that paints the line, a queued ask held through a
window, and `a_slash_command_from_the_board_is_acked_off_the_screen`), `mod_turns_e2e`'s two
`a_submit_held_after_a_stop_…` tests (fake mod switch `mod-stopped-submit`), and the units
`composer::a_compaction_reads_off_its_spinner_line`, `attention::the_screen_closes_an_interrupted_compaction`,
`quiet`'s word hold and `refusal_tests`.

## A queued ask lands on a turn an API error ended (T-899, 2026-10-22, "After an API error, a prompt the person sends is queued behind a turn that already ended")

**The report.** A `StopFailure{server}` (ENOTFOUND) moved a seat running → `Failed`. The
person's Shift+Enter "continue" queued (the board's follow-up mode is Queue), the card read
`queued ∙ after its turn`, and nothing delivered it; a send-immediately in the same field did.

**Where it stalled: the daemon, not the TUI.** `quiet::is_working` and `holds_against_words`
already let words through on `Failed`, but `session_takes_words` — what a queued ask and the
crown's wake land on — also required `Idle`, so a failed seat was never ready, and
`ask_waits_on_ids` listed the ticket itself, which the card spells `after its turn`. The TUI never
read `Failed` as mid-turn: its field opens by the follow-up mode for any paned seat, the same at
`Failed` as at `Idle`, and its `after its turn` was the daemon's `waits_on`.

**The fix.** `quiet::takes_words`: `Idle` or `Failed`, and nothing in `holds_against_words`.
Every `FailReason` is a turn over with the agent at its composer; a limit is never `Failed`
(`Throttled` / `QuotaResume`, `stopped_on_limit`) and still holds the words (T-808). The person's
ask and the crown's (`ask_agent` rides the same queue) and the crown's wake all read it. A plan
relaunch and a tier switch keep their own gates (`session_idle`, `at_rest`), which still exclude
`Failed`: a tier switch on a failed seat is a separate question. `SessionRecord::pressable` was
left alone: it governs launch words' owed Enter, not a queued ask's paste, and no launch reaches
`Failed` before its prompt is acked.

**Tests.** `quiet::a_failed_turn_takes_words_and_a_limit_does_not`;
`shift_enter_on_a_failed_turn_asks_as_at_an_idle_one` (the field and its hint match an idle
seat's under both follow-up modes); `ask_queue_e2e::a_queued_ask_lands_after_an_api_error_and_waits_out_a_limit`
(an ask queued mid-turn lands on the `StopFailure{server_error}`, and one queued on a
`StopFailure{rate_limit}` stays), on both passes; it times out with the old `Idle`-only gate.

**Review: a native failure's class is read late.** On the native road (T-659) a `StopFailure`
arrives as `Failed{Unknown}` and the recovery re-reads the tail every 2 s for 60 s, and a
`rate_limit` found there becomes QUOTA. Until then the seat takes no words
(`agents::claude::failure_being_read`, the re-read's own spell, asked by `session_takes_words`):
a crown's ask pasted in that window would meet the limit. Once the spell ends unclassed, or a
non-limit class is read, it takes them. On the hook set's road Claude Code names the class itself
(2.1.308: every HTTP 429 is `rate_limit`; `unknown` is its fallback for an unmatched API status,
a gateway or provider credential error, or a non-API error), so `Failed{Unknown}` there is no
limit by Claude Code's own reading and is not held. Test:
`a_native_failure_takes_words_only_once_its_class_is_read_or_given_up`. No e2e: a native record
needs the `auto` road's probe on a faked enterprise account (`mod_auto_e2e`), and the 60 s spell
has no seam.

## The barrier comes before the read, and it has a deadline (T-812 re-review, 2026-10-22)

The re-review of `d861af37` (T-897's `Re-review d861af37`) confirmed the first five fixes and
found five more of the same family: the barrier ran inside the send, after the key had already
read the board for its value or target.

**Applied.** `catch_up` now runs before the read in the column rings that compute their value
outside `set_column` (`on working`, `on done`, `arrives`, the column workspace), in `grab`
before it picks the card and the column, in `u` before `undo_target`, and in the summary tick
before it reads the row and the note's revision. The undo roads wait for their own board — the
archive, the snooze, the unarchive and the restore — so `u` is offered and aimed off the grace
band and the archive that show the last change: two `u` restore two tickets, and an archive's
"u undoes it" is true on the next frame.

**The deadline.** `catch_up` returns whether it caught up, and every caller sends nothing when it
did not. It waits for one `client::RESPONSE_WAIT` end to end, across the ask out and the one more
it may send on the lane (`App::catch_up_wait`, which a test shortens); `settle_snapshot` waits
the same, never a bare `recv`. An ask a barrier gave up on stays out: `pump` lands it when it
comes and asks once more. And `land_snapshot` drops an answer asked before the board on screen,
so a waited-for fetch that overtook a held ask is never rolled back by it. Every connection's
writes now time out at `RESPONSE_WAIT` too (`client::hello`). CLAUDE.md no longer says such a
key never waits: it does, while the daemon is slow, and for that bound at most.

**Tests.** `column_rings_step_twice_while_the_board_lands_late`,
`a_second_filing_grabs_the_card_that_slid_under`,
`undo_twice_restores_both_and_an_archive_is_undoable_at_once`,
`a_second_summary_tick_carries_the_first_ticks_revision` (the fake now refuses a stale note
revision, as the daemon does), `a_barrier_gives_up_at_its_deadline_and_sends_nothing`,
`an_answer_older_than_the_board_on_screen_is_dropped`.

## The compaction close reads the spinner's place, and a command's ack keeps the queue (T-894 review by T-900, 2026-10-22)

T-900's review of `8bf691b0` found three holes. **A command's ack swept the queue**: `ack_owed`
ran `forget_queued` for every ack, so a follow-up queued behind a `/compact` (window open,
words held) was deleted by the command's screen ack and its asker told the person dropped it.
A `/` or `!` ack now forgets nothing, and a prompt's ack forgets only an ask queued at or before
its words went in (`forget_queued_before`, against the entry's `screen_after`): a follow-up is
never the earlier words' to take. **A narrow pane closed a running compaction** (the phrase never
stood on one row at ~20 columns), and **ordinary text held a window open** for ten minutes
(`/compact` restored with instructions that say the phrase, or output quoting it). The detector
now reads only the spinner's place: the nearest block of rows above the composer's top rule,
past blank and right-hung status rows (the effort row, `◐ medium · /effort`, by its glyph at any
width), never the composer and never scrollback above that block. Within it, a row led by a
spinner glyph (`· ✢ ✳ ✶ ✻ ✽`, or `*`) is joined with the rows it wrapped onto, up to the `⎿` tip,
and must read `Compacting conversation… (`, the timer's paren a quotation lacks.

Tests: `composer::a_compaction_reads_off_its_spinner_line` (every glyph, a pane captured on
2.1.308), `composer::a_wrapped_spinner_line_still_reads_as_compacting`,
`composer::the_phrase_in_ordinary_text_is_not_the_spinner`, and
`compact_e2e::a_slash_command_from_the_board_is_acked_off_the_screen` with a follow-up queued
behind the command (fails against the old sweep: the follow-up was dropped).

## A refused letter says why in Sent too (T-902, 2026-10-22, "Remote Control: a letter the relay or host refuses vanishes from Sent without its reason")

Mesophon's `say()` dropped every toast without a button while Sent was open, on the reasoning
that Sent's feed shows what became of a ticket. The feed lists only the tickets this browser
filed (`store.sent`), so a letter for an agent refused by the relay (`capacity`) or the host
(asleep, another agent, revoked), a note's refusal, a start's answer and Sent's own "too late"
and "needs the relay" replies were all silent there: the letter left its ticket's composer and
the words went back to the box with no word why.

**Now** `say()` speaks in every view, and the quiet in Sent is opt-in: `sayOfSent()` is the road
for an outcome the feed itself shows (a filed ticket sending, waiting, landed, refused,
unknown, picked up, unsent). Anything new goes through `say()` and is heard everywhere by
default. "Too late to take back", "Unsending needs the relay" and "Editing needs the relay" now
show in Sent, where their buttons are. Test: `mailPromptFlow` in `web/mesophon/ux.test.js` opens
Sent before a relay refusal and before a host refusal, waits for each reason's toast, and finds
the words back in the box.

## The intro is the first board's alone, and its marker says it was seen (T-903, 2026-10-22, "The intro hangs the installer in Terminal.app and cmux, Ctrl+C dead")

An install from cmux or the stock Terminal.app stopped where the intro should play: no output,
Ctrl+C dead. A coworker hit it in cmux.

**The cause, measured in a pty.** `install.sh` ran `mesimon welcome </dev/tty`, and T-869's
inline road built a ratatui `Viewport::Inline`, which asks the cursor position at once (CSI 6n).
crossterm 0.29 (no `use-dev-tty`) reads keys and replies from stdin through mio's kqueue, and on
macOS kqueue refuses the `/dev/tty` vnode that `</dev/tty` opens (the pty's own device, which a
shell normally hands a program, works). The event source never starts, every `poll_internal`
fails, and `read_position_raw` loops on `Err(_) => {}` with no deadline: one core at 98%, in
raw mode, so Ctrl+C was a byte nobody read. A terminal's answer made no difference: the pty
test hung the same with every query answered. Not the OS appearance probe or the colour query
(both bounded, and with the OS answering the terminal is not asked); `sample` put the spin in
`poll_internal<CursorPositionFilter>`. An inline-only cost: the board's road is fullscreen
and its stdin is the pty itself.

**Now.**
- `install.sh` runs no part of mesimon's terminal UI: it prints the picture (UTF-8 and tty
  guards kept) and the `next:` lines, always. `ci/test_installer.py` gives the installer a pty
  as its controlling terminal and a fake binary that lists `welcome` in `--help` and records a
  run of it; the old script fails that test.
- `mesimon welcome` stays for an older `install.sh`, plays nothing and exits 1 (that script then
  prints its picture), and is off `--help`, which that script greps before calling it.
- The intro plays on the first board only (`intro::before_board`), and its road asks the
  terminal nothing. Its closing clear was `Terminal::clear`, which asks the cursor position too
  (a 2 s wait on a terminal that never answers); a fullscreen `resize` clears the same and asks
  nothing. A key read error ends it unmarked instead of failing the board. Ctrl+C ends it at
  once; any other key skips to its end as before, where a key opens the board.
- **The marker means seen**: `played board <version>` when it reached its end, `skipped board
  <version>` when a key cut it short, written at that moment and never before it starts, so a
  killed run plays again. **A marker in the old format (`mesimon <version>`, or empty) reads as
  unseen**: it was written before the intro played, and the hung install wrote it too, so
  nothing in it says the person saw anything. Everyone who saw the intro at install sees it
  once more on their next board; the author accepted that as the only way to reach the person
  whose install hung. The demo recorder seeds the new words.

The board's own terminal queries before the intro (the kitty-keyboard probe and
`init_terminal`'s `Terminal::clear`, crossterm's 2 s bound each) are unchanged; they are the
board's start, as fast as before on a terminal that answers.

Tests: `only_a_marker_that_says_how_it_was_seen_is_believed`; and
`the_board_road_asks_the_terminal_nothing_and_a_key_ends_it`, which runs the board's road in a
child of the test binary inside a pty that answers nothing: a frame comes, the old marker is
still there before a key, Ctrl+C ends it inside 2 s marked `skipped`, a plain key shows the end
and the next ends it, left alone (at 20× pace) it marks `played`, and the child wrote no query
(CSI 6n, OSC 10/11, DA1, CSI ? u). Putting `Terminal::clear` back, or reading Ctrl+C as a
skip, fails it. `intro-install-end.txt` is gone with the inline road; the board's goldens are
unchanged.

## The linked boards' count is a header chip (T-905, 2026-10-22, "allow to enter the shared boards settings from the title")

The top row's ` ∙ N boards` (T-733, T-878) was the one mark the header's cursor could not stand
on. It is now `HeaderChip::Links`, the last chip, after the workflow's: present while the board
reaches another (`Ctx::links_mark`), named `boards` in `h`/`l`'s hints, and its Enter
(`reaches boards`) opens the Reaches boards list, as Remote Control's chip opens its dialog.
Opened from the chip, Esc puts the cursor back on it (`App::boards_from_header`, the
`remote_from_header` rule); opened from Settings, Esc still lands on the door. A click steps onto
it and a second click is its Enter, like every chip. On a row too tight for the count, the
count is still dropped whole, except while the cursor stands on it. While words light it
(`↯ relay asks`) the selected chip takes the selected ink, as the workflow's lit word does.

Tests: `header_links_chip_is_the_last_and_opens_reaches_boards` (keymap),
`links_chip_opens_reaches_boards_and_esc_returns_to_it` (app),
`links_count_is_a_chip_a_click_opens` (render). No golden changed: a golden is drawn with the
cursor on the board.

## Shared terminal output and explicit shell closure (T-904, 2026-10-22)

A person can run an unsupported command or independent reviewer in a ticket's `!`
terminal and share its output with the ticket's agent and the crown. Adoption alone
keeps output private, including records from earlier versions. `^s` on an adopted
shell's row toggles sharing; Shift+Enter on a shell or terminal row adopts if needed,
shares and opens a frozen capture in the ask editor. The person reviews and sends
that text through the existing ask delivery. Shift+Enter inside an attached application
keeps its existing meaning. Sharing is a grant for later reads too; stopping it cannot
recall output already delivered.

`get_ticket` describes the workflow and lists shells, sharing state and observed
foregrounds. `list_board` carries shell counts for the caller's own ticket and, for
the crown, other tickets. `read_shell` exports only explicitly shared shell output,
with the ticket/crown scope checked by the daemon. Its separate core capability grants
no generic session access or terminal input. Captures preserve blank lines, bound both
lines and bytes, identify the capture time and screen/scrollback source, and report
truncation. Foreground observations do not assert completion or an exit status.

`request_close_shell` is a crown request for the person, never authority to terminate.
The request is visible on the shell and in the needs-you indication. On its row, `x`
shows the consequence, Enter confirms, and Esc keeps the shell. A request expires in
five minutes, is bound to its pane, and is revoked when the crown changes. Attached,
busy or uninspectable shells remain open. The ordinary person's close remains on `x`;
opening the shell and exiting it is the manual route.

Parking agents leaves shells open and says how to close them. Snooze and archive
explain their shell/terminal blockers; neither silently closes a shell as part of
parking. Archive reclamation waits for both adopted shells and unadopted terminals;
explicit ticket deletion keeps its existing confirmed terminal cleanup.
Shell output is never copied into a ticket note automatically, and an unsupported
reviewer is not promoted to a managed agent by sharing its terminal.

Coverage: authorization and tool-tier tests; real-tmux adoption, sharing, revocation,
cross-ticket reads, close requests, busy/attached refusal and confirmation; TUI output
preview and snooze guidance; shared-shell and close-request goldens; rig SH1 exercises
a real worker reading the shared output and a crown requesting human-confirmed closure.

## T-907 — a send-now into a working Codex turn reads past a redraw (2026-10-22)

The crown's `ask_agent` with `deliver: now` to T-904's working Codex seat was refused twice with
`ANSWER_IN_PANE_FIRST` while no dialog was up: `codex_steer` took ONE `capture_input_screen` and
read anything but the box as a dialog. Measured on that pane (Codex 0.163, a 24-minute tool
call): 1 read in 4,000 found `cursor_flag 0` at row 16, i.e. Codex hides the cursor while it
redraws the `Working (…)` line, so a read landing mid-frame lost the box.

- `codex::steer_sight` reads up to `STEER_READS` (3) times, `STEER_READ_GAP_MS` (100) apart, so
  at most 200 ms on the writer, at the key (T-857 allows an edge's fork). The box on any read
  goes; a dialog on any read stops at once.
- `codex::dialog_shown` is the positive witness: the pane's LAST `›` row is a numbered choice
  (`› 1. Yes, proceed (y)`), as the approval, question and plan lists draw it. The last one,
  because the conversation keeps each sent prompt behind a `›` of its own.
- Only a dialog says `ANSWER_IN_PANE_FIRST`. Neither, on every read, is the new
  `command::COMPOSER_NOT_FOUND`: `could not find the agent's message box ∙ try again, or send it
  after its turn`. The runtime's own pending request is still checked earlier
  (`pane_waits_on_you`, `RequiresAction`); `codex_park` steers only a `Running` record.
- Not taken: the sampler's last screen as the witness. A dialog raised after it would be typed
  into (T-568); the live reads decide, as `steer_presses` does (T-872).

Coverage: `input_tests::a_redraw_never_reads_as_a_dialog_and_a_real_one_refuses_the_steer`
(the recorded working frame, hidden and on the status line, and 0.163's captured approval);
`provider_e2e::a_steer_reads_past_a_redraw_and_a_missing_box_is_no_dialog`, where the Codex
stub's `hide_ms` draws a frame with its cursor hidden for 150 ms (fails 3 of 3 at one read).

## One-off shell captures and scoped live reads (T-904 follow-up, 2026-10-22)

Shift+Enter on a ticket's shell row now prepares only a frozen capture for an
existing agent. Esc discards it without retaining an ask draft or granting live
reads. An unadopted terminal is still adopted in one press. No TUI key enables live sharing; the wire grant remains available.
The shell tools do not isolate same-user processes.
The capture prefill says only “Terminal output” and whether earlier output was omitted.

Core authorization takes the caller's ticket and crown facts for shell actions;
the daemon retains its ticket and sharing checks. Close-request refusals say busy
without process names. Records without an older pane key remain usable; recorded
keys still have to match. Read events record reader, shell and outcome, never output.
Idle shells do not block parking, snoozing or archiving. Ordinary parking retains
the live-child guard; archive teardown closes the worktree terminal as before. Attention counts take
an injected time; shell guidance is omitted on tickets without a shell or terminal,
and capture truncation excludes trailing screen padding and checks both row and byte limits.

Coverage adds cancellation/no-agent key tests, authorization-scope and legacy-key
unit cases, bounded-output cases, capture-without-sharing wire checks and metadata-only
read-feed checks. SH1 verifies successful shell reads, structured workflow answers,
no execution tools, and a live shell awaiting human closure confirmation.

## Terminal parity starts with the right color profile and query-free clears (T-909, 2026-10-22)

Mesimon can preserve its designed colors and interaction model across capable terminals.
Pixel-identical text also depends on the emulator's font rasterizer, cell metrics and user
profile. Treating every non-iTerm terminal as a lesser renderer hides application bugs;
treating RGB support as proof of every other capability hides a different set of bugs.

**Two concrete defects fixed.** `detect.rs` previously understood `COLORTERM=truecolor/24bit`
and otherwise only `TERM` containing `256color`, `linux`, or `dumb`. Without `COLORTERM`,
`xterm-ghostty` and `xterm-kitty` became **16 colors**, and a new Apple Terminal advertising
`xterm-256color` became **256**. This changes more than color precision: `Theme::new` selects
a different palette, `tints()` removes the tag ring below RGB, light-256 has no selected
background, and `mix()` cannot interpolate indexed colors. Losing the environment hint can
therefore flatten surfaces, remove distinctions and turn fades into steps.

The ladder now retains `NO_COLOR`, `MESIMON_COLOR`/`--color`, and `COLORTERM` precedence, then
recognizes explicit RGB terminal entries and known direct emulator identities. It recognizes
Terminal.app's **build** in `TERM_PROGRAM_VERSION` (465 and later), not the host's macOS
version: the host can be across SSH. The build boundary follows
[Ratatui's Terminal.app detection](https://www.ratatui.rs/examples/layout/flex/).
[Apple's Tahoe feature list, page 14](https://www.apple.com/my/os/pdf/All_New_Features_macOS_Tahoe_Sept_2025.pdf)
confirms 24-bit color; the old blanket claim that Terminal.app cannot display RGB is obsolete.
Unknown or old Apple versions still use their `TERM` fallback. No bundle-id inference is used.
`TMUX`, `STY`, screen/tmux terminal entries and multiplexer program names veto inference from
an inherited outer emulator. An explicit `COLORTERM` or RGB terminal entry still means what
it did. Generic `xterm-256color` alone still does not promise RGB.

| Evidence with `COLORTERM` absent | Previous profile | Current profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Direct `TERM=xterm-ghostty` or `xterm-kitty` | 16 | RGB |
| Direct Ghostty, kitty, WezTerm or cmux program identity, `TERM=xterm-256color` | 256 | RGB |
| Direct Apple Terminal build 465+, `TERM=xterm-256color` | 256 | RGB |
| Apple Terminal build below 465 or unknown, `TERM=xterm-256color` | 256 | 256 |
| Outer tmux/screen, no explicit RGB evidence | TERM fallback | TERM fallback |
| Generic `TERM=xterm-256color`, unidentified emulator | 256 | 256 |

`mesimon doctor` now prints **board colors**, including the reason for the selection. It
uses the same pure decision as the board, works in pipes and probes nothing. This describes
the current launch environment, not an already-running board in another terminal.

Second, Ratatui 0.30.2's `Terminal::clear` queries the cursor to preserve its position. In
our locked `ratatui-core` 0.1.2 this is `terminal/buffers.rs::clear`; crossterm can wait two
seconds for the answer. The fullscreen board does not need to preserve that cursor: the
next frame places it. `quiet::clear` uses the local size ioctl and fullscreen `resize` to
clear and invalidate the previous frame without a terminal query. Startup, Ctrl+L, resume
and returns from an attached session/editor use it. The intro shares the helper, extending
T-903's already-tested approach. The one-time keyboard negotiation and the key-release
handover fence remain: they answer questions the application actually needs.

**What the rest of the research changes about the approach.** These are distinct axes,
not a single "good terminal" flag:

- **Color and decoration.** `Theme::summary_under` currently assumes both RGB and 256-color
  terminals support independently colored underlines. SGR 58 and underline styles are
  separate from foreground/background RGB; the
  [kitty underline protocol](https://sw.kovidgoyal.net/kitty/underlines/) defines them
  separately. A future measured fallback should draw only the completed portion with a
  plain underline when underline color is unavailable. Do not downgrade the whole palette
  to fix one decoration, or infer underline support from the Apple RGB build boundary.
- **Glyph width.** `glyphs::done_unread` deliberately uses text-default emoji `✔` and already
  records the safer bold `✓` fallback. Emoji presentation, ambiguous-width settings and
  Unicode versions can disagree with Rust's width calculation. Ratatui buffer goldens prove
  cell intent, not the pixels an emulator paints. [WezTerm exposes its Unicode width
  version](https://wezterm.org/config/lua/config/unicode_version.html); [Ghostty documents
  grapheme-width modes](https://ghostty.org/docs/config/reference#grapheme-width-method).
  A portable glyph option should be independent of color: today ASCII is coupled to Mono.
  Measure the failing symbols before replacing the whole UI with ASCII or changing a
  user's terminal-wide Unicode policy.
- **Frame presentation.** The board already brackets changed frames with synchronized
  output (DECSET 2026), emits nothing for idle frames, and repairs covered wide-glyph
  cells in `quiet.rs`. [Ghostty's rendering guidance](https://ghostty.org/docs/help/synchronized-output)
  recommends that protocol to prevent tearing. Adding it again is not a fix. Check first
  paint, resize, full clear and attach/detach separately, and distinguish the board's output
  from Claude/Codex output inside tmux. A terminal that ignores synchronization can still
  expose intermediate writes; buffer goldens cannot establish flicker parity.
- **Keys.** The board already negotiates the kitty keyboard protocol and has legacy
  alternatives in `keymap.rs`. The [protocol's legacy encoding table](https://sw.kovidgoyal.net/kitty/keyboard-protocol/#legacy-key-event-encoding)
  demonstrates why Enter and Shift+Enter can be identical bytes. No decoder can reconstruct
  a modifier the terminal never sent. Keep the fallback actions discoverable and test
  press/repeat/release across the handover; do not force a protocol by emulator name.
- **Tmux is a separate hop.** The board normally draws directly; focused agents draw through
  Mesimon's private tmux. The [tmux RGB guidance](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/wiki/FAQ#how-do-i-use-rgb-colour)
  requires knowledge of the outer terminal's RGB support. Changing `default-terminal` or
  unconditionally declaring `*:RGB` is not proof that the attached endpoint supports it.
  Compare direct-board and attached-pane failures separately before changing this backend.
- **Terminal chrome.** iTerm tab color, subtitle and icon sequences are application-specific.
  Mesimon already has terminal-specific notification paths and generic title/progress
  mechanisms in `title.rs` and `notify.rs`. Matching the board does not require pretending
  another emulator supports iTerm's tab controls.

**A controlled visual comparison.** Use an ordinary external terminal and an isolated
fixture, not a board inside an agent pane. Compare the same build, fixture, theme, 120×30
cell grid and animation time in iTerm, Terminal.app and the reported alternative (cmux and
Ghostty are useful separate entries). Record application/build, `TERM`, `COLORTERM`,
`TERM_PROGRAM_VERSION`, `mesimon doctor`'s board-colors line, font family/size, cell spacing,
and whether tmux or SSH is between the board and the renderer. Do not capture the whole
environment. Compare once with defaults, then with the same installed font, opaque
background and matching cell metrics. Keep the two sets of results distinct.

For Ghostty/cmux, the relevant controls are `font-family`, `font-size`,
`adjust-cell-height`, `adjust-cell-width`, `font-thicken`, `minimum-contrast`, and
`background-opacity`. Contrast correction can change the relative brightness of muted
text, and font blending can change apparent weight without changing the requested RGB.
These are comparison variables, not settings Mesimon should silently write. The
[Ghostty configuration reference](https://ghostty.org/docs/config/reference) describes these
controls; [cmux's appearance documentation](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/blob/main/docs/customizing-appearance.md)
describes its libghostty rendering settings and their configuration locations.
[WezTerm's line-height control](https://wezterm.org/config/lua/config/line_height.html)
similarly changes row spacing independently of the application's cell grid.

Capture a selected and unselected card, all attention states, multiple tags, summary
progress at rest and during change, the mascot, rich text/diff, a dialog, a long/Unicode
name, resize and an agent round trip. Inspect both screenshots and a short recording:
seams and glyph fallback need pixels, tearing needs time. Include a 60×20 pass for narrow
geometry. A deterministic visual specimen using these existing renderers would make this
repeatable without live agents; it is the next useful validation tool if differences
remain, rather than another terminal-name special case.

**Scope and evidence.** This ticket establishes the two fixes above through source analysis
and regression tests; it does not establish pixel parity on other terminal applications.
The new environment-table tests cover missing color hints, Apple build boundaries, explicit
overrides, multiplexer inheritance and conservative fallbacks. The clear test proves that
an unchanged frame is repainted after external damage; the intro's real no-reply pty test
checks the shared clear path emits no query. Existing theme and geometry goldens remain the
expected design. Remaining underline/glyph/profile proposals require a reproduced visual
failure before changing that design.

Validation: the six detection tests passed; `cargo ut` passed 2,524 tests, including the
unchanged rendering goldens and the no-reply pty, and `m1_e2e` passed its real-tmux acceptance
check. Both gates ran through `ci/test-run.py` with clean fixture audits. The first targeted
run's cleanup failed because the sandbox denied `ps`; its registry had no sockets or repos,
and the command-scoped rerun completed cleanly. The first unit gate inherited `NO_COLOR=1`
from the agent and failed the existing ANSI underline-byte assertion; the passing run removed
that variable from the test process environment. Six standard unit entries are ignored:
four timing probes, the live-release download test, and the pty child invoked by its parent
regression test. No full nextest, Linux/Docker or live terminal visual comparison was run:
this changes client detection/clearing, not daemon state, the wire or tmux configuration.

## A worker the crown asks for what it cannot reach raises its hand (T-908, 2026-10-22, "A worker that can't do what the crown asked says so with raise_hand, not only in its pane")

The report: the crown told T-904's worker to `read_note key=T-906`; the board refused
with "not the board's coordinator … ^o crowns it", and the worker asked for the note in
its own pane, where nobody reads. The refusal offered the person a second crown (which
would unseat the first) and spoke of editing for a read.

`crown_target`'s refusal is spelled once, `server.rs::crown_refused`, for every keyed
road (`get_ticket`, `read_note`, `read_attachment`, `read_shell`, the keyed writes) and
for `ask_board`, in tool text's voice (the lint passes over it in the unit test). Under a
crown: "only the crown (T-1) reads or changes another ticket (T-9); the crown can copy
what is needed onto this ticket, and raise_hand on this ticket, naming what is missing,
reaches the person and the crown" — the last clause is "reaches the person" when the
crown does not hear this ticket's hand (`crown_claims(…, Raised)`: started or watched).
With no crown, the person's `^o` stays. `raise_hand`'s description says it wakes the crown
for a ticket it started or watches and covers a step the crown asked for that cannot be
taken; `WORKER_UNDER_CROWN` says pane words reach no one and the hand is the road.

Coverage: `crown_refusal_tests`, `crown_e2e` (every keyed road from a person's worker,
and `read_note` from a crown-started one), rig RH1 on Sonnet (refused `read_note` →
`raise_hand` naming the note → the crown woken, `raised`).

## Shell ownership through archive and capture cancellation (T-904 re-review, 2026-10-22)

The previous follow-up's archive interpretation is superseded: an awake adopted
shell refuses archive with the pre-T-904 “sessions still awake — sleep them first”.
The single-ticket, crown and bulk-offer roads use the same persisted awake-session
rule; none closes shells along the way. The worktree's unadopted `!` terminal still
ends at archive teardown. The latest explicit-close-only rule also holds snooze
and private-server restart before either parks any sessions; bulk sleep already
excludes shells. Only the person's individual close or confirmed crown request
can close an adopted shell. Unreadable child checks refuse, including malformed
or non-UTF-8 process evidence and a failed pane snapshot.

An unadopted terminal's Shift+Enter preview now changes no board record or pane
name. Esc leaves it unadopted; sending adopts only the pane generation captured
for that preview, and grants no live reads. The frozen text is unchanged by later
terminal output. The promise no longer refers to stopping sharing in the TUI.

Coverage: archive/offer and child-evidence unit regressions, actual preview/cancel/
send key tests, and terminal integration checks for deferred adoption, crown and
local archive refusal with the old words, two surviving shells, the exact bulk
offer count, and refusal of server restart. Archive reclamation retains coverage
of the separate worktree terminal's teardown. SH1 also checks that the agent
understands Esc does not adopt an unadopted terminal.

## Terminal.app animation residue is an ungrouped underline color (T-909 follow-up, 2026-10-22)

A Terminal.app screenshot showed cyan and red background blocks left in a card's reply
row after the crown animation, until visiting the card repainted it. The frame loop already
redraws after animation, so adding a final repaint would conceal the cause. Crossterm 0.29
emits underline RGB as `CSI 58;2;r;g;b m`. Terminal.app does not consume that entire form:
the component `46` becomes a cyan background command, `41` a red background command, and
`2` dims text. The renderer's cached colors then disagree with the terminal, so subsequent
cells can inherit paint the frame buffer never requested. A card visit rewrites those cells.

**Confirmed in the affected emulator by the user.** A standalone Python diagnostic in a
new Terminal.app window printed the same RGB component values 41–47 and 100–107 with the
same foreground and background, once with semicolons and once with colons. The user
confirmed that only the semicolon row showed colored blocks; the colon row stayed dark.
Window capture was unavailable to the agent, so this is user-confirmed visual evidence,
not an automated screenshot comparison. The diagnostic launched no Mesimon board.

`underline::UnderlineColors` now wraps the board's crossterm writer and converts only its
complete underline color commands: `58;2;r;g;b` to `58:2::r:g:b`, and `58;5;n` to `58:5:n`.
A terminal can understand or ignore the grouped parameter without interpreting its color
components as unrelated SGR commands. Foreground/background RGB, reset 59, cursor movement,
synchronization and UTF-8 text pass unchanged. The adapter handles commands split by
`write_fmt`, bounds its pending bytes, completes short writes and propagates I/O errors.
This retains full RGB and the animation; it needs no Terminal.app identity check, extra
screen query, or full-frame repaint. Existing idle silence and iTerm's underline repaint
workaround stay covered by the backend tests.

The same delimiter problem is described in [Vim issue 6687](https://github.com/vim/vim/issues/6687)
for an emulator supporting only the colon form. RGB support and semicolon-form SGR 58
support are independent, as the earlier research here cautioned. The new tests reproduce
the red/cyan-background misparse with a minimal legacy-SGR model, then verify the grouped
output preserves the requested background and intensity; check every split point and
byte-at-a-time output; preserve other sequences and incomplete input; and check short
writes/errors. The backend's existing animation test now verifies grouped underline colors
are what reaches the writer. No intended cell geometry or theme colors change.

Validation: `cargo ut` passed 2,535 tests with the six standard ignored entries described
above, and the ticket's binary built successfully. Both used the bounded runner with
`NO_COLOR` removed for the ANSI assertions; fixture audits were clean. Formatting and
`git diff --check` passed. No goldens changed. Full nextest, tmux e2e and Linux/Docker
checks were not rerun for this renderer-output-only fix; the affected emulator was checked
with the standalone diagnostic, not an interactive Mesimon board.

## Terminal.app needs plain underlines, not grouped underline colors (T-909 correction, 2026-10-22)

The preceding claim that Terminal.app safely ignores a grouped SGR 58 is refuted.
After that fix, leaving a card still left its title partially white on the terminal's
default background. The first diagnostic checked for colored blocks on a nearly default
surface; it did not establish that the existing foreground, background and attributes
survived the command. A second standalone Terminal.app diagnostic used cyan text on a
purple background, bold and underlined, with BEFORE and AFTER samples. The user confirmed
that only the grouped underline-color command lost the styling; SGR 59 did not.

`Quiet` now supplies the endpoint's `TERM_PROGRAM` to the underline writer. For
`Apple_Terminal`, it omits the renderer's custom RGB and indexed underline-color commands
entirely. Ordinary SGR 4/24 underlines and the harmless reset 59 pass through; the line
inherits the text's color. RGB text and backgrounds, selection weight, geometry, and
foreground/background animation are retained. Colored underline progress loses its separate
track/run colors on this endpoint. Other terminals retain the grouped encoding and iTerm's
repaint workaround. This capability is independent of the color profile: a newer Terminal.app
supporting RGB does not establish SGR 58 support. No terminal query or preference write is
introduced. The existing `TERM_PROGRAM` endpoint is used, not an inherited iTerm session id
or a host-OS assumption; a tmux endpoint keeps its own behavior.

Regression coverage checks the fallback at every write boundary and byte by byte, preserves
all surrounding styles and ordinary underlines, and retains colored output for other
endpoints. An actual `Quiet` draw/diff regression focuses and leaves a title with two
underline colors and compares the output with a plain-underline reference: the streams
must match exactly, including RGB text/background and weight changes, and a settled frame
must emit nothing. This tests the emitted stream, not just ratatui's cached cells. Buffer
goldens need no update because the adaptation is confined to terminal output.

Validation: the three targeted `apple_terminal` tests passed, followed by all 2,543
`cargo ut` tests (the same six standard ignored entries), and the ticket binary built.
The bounded runners reported clean fixture audits; ANSI tests ran with `NO_COLOR` removed.
Formatting and `git diff --check` passed. Full nextest, tmux e2e and Linux/Docker were not
rerun for this terminal-output-only change. The actual emulator diagnostic was checked
by the user; the fixed full board has not been manually inspected.

## Terminal parity has a replay, and plain progress keeps its meaning (T-909, 2026-10-22)

Omitting SGR 58 fixed corrupt paint but left the summary's run and track indistinguishable:
both became a full-width ordinary underline. Decoration support now reaches `Theme`
independently of its color profile. Without underline colors, RGB/256-color themes draw
only the rounded completed share, in the existing text color, and update its length directly
instead of attempting a color wave. Zero completed boxes draw no run. Text, backgrounds,
selection weight and tag colors retain the RGB palette. The output adapter still suppresses
SGR 58 as a final safeguard. Theme preview/restore, OS appearance changes, setup and tour
practice boards retain the endpoint capability. Other terminals keep their colored track
and wave. Tests cover every flavor, focus state, fraction, pulse phase, and theme/practice
transition; the real card's text, foreground and background match the colored reference.

**A repeatable comparison, using the real renderer.**
`ui/tests/terminal_comparison.rs` builds a synthetic board through the existing rendering
fixtures, captures actual `ui::draw` buffers and encodes both full frames and successive
diffs through `Quiet`. It exports 37 frames for each combination of Graphite/Chalk,
120×30/60×20, and native/Apple underline support. These include selection, leaving/opening
a card, summary rows/dialog, ticket page, legacy key hints, 100 ms crown-sweep samples,
leaving after the sweep, progress fractions, two tags, attention/error states, a rich note,
a diff, and a glyph sheet. Crown and summary sampling use the existing injectable render
clock; spinner specimens are explicit glyph frames. Every captured buffer is drawn twice
to assert idle silence, and Apple output must contain no SGR 58 or cursor query.

Generate the replay without opening a board or starting an agent:

```sh
env -u NO_COLOR MESIMON_TERMINAL_COMPARISON=/tmp/mesimon-comparison.json \
  python3 -B ci/test-run.py -- cargo test -p mesimon-tui terminal_comparison_export
```

In an ordinary external terminal, run
`python3 -B ci/terminal-compare.py /tmp/mesimon-comparison.json`.
The player selects Apple/native output from `TERM_PROGRAM`; `--endpoint` can override it
for diagnostics. `--theme chalk --width 60` selects the light/narrow specimen; the terminal
needs two additional rows for controls. `--autoplay --through 30` stops after leaving the
crowned card. Space steps, `p` goes back, `r` restarts, and `f` compares full repaint with
incremental output. Resizing back to a sufficient size restores a complete frame. `--keys`
shows received key bytes without forwarding them to Mesimon. Quit, Ctrl+C and SIGTERM
restore the screen and terminal mode. This tool writes no settings and runs no daemon,
tmux or agent; it is a developer comparison, not a new product flow.

**Measured external rendering.** The isolated replay ran in Terminal.app 2.15 (488) and
iTerm2 3.7.2. The initial profiles used SF Mono 11 and MesloLGS NF 13 respectively. Matching
MesloLGS NF 13 in the temporary Terminal tab made the font comparison meaningful; no saved
profile changed. Captured 120×30 dark-board frames show the intended colors and layout,
and both captured post-crown/leave-card frames have a uniformly tinted title. Comparing
those frames with a fresh full repaint revealed no visible card residue. The Apple fallback
shows only the completed run; iTerm retains the separate track. Font rasterization and
underline positioning still differ. The accented/CJK/emoji text in these board captures did
not justify replacing the glyph set or coupling ASCII to a color downgrade.

Limits: the replay is a renderer specimen, not an end-to-end input/attach recording. The
glyph sheet was captured in iTerm; later Terminal captures were unavailable because its
window was offscreen. Light/narrow and rich/diff cases were generated and tested but not
visually certified in both emulators. cmux and Ghostty were not installed. No claim of
pixel parity, identical tearing behavior, or a full live keyboard/mouse/attach comparison
follows from these screenshots. Existing legacy-key, paste, mouse-target and handover tests
remain the behavioral evidence; there was no reproduced defect warranting a keymap or
tmux-configuration change. `docs/USING.md` now explains the plain progress display and the
font/spacing/grid choices needed for a useful appearance comparison.

Validation: 1,186 TUI tests passed with golden regeneration (no golden diff); `cargo ut`
passed 2,547 tests with the six standard ignored entries; `m1_e2e` passed its real-tmux
acceptance test; the binary built. The replay's PTY regression passed stepping, full/diff,
idle silence, resize recovery and terminal-mode restoration. Its first harness attempt
waited before consuming final PTY output, and its next compared macOS's kernel PENDIN flag
as configuration; the corrected driver drains restoration output and excludes only that
bookkeeping bit. All final bounded runs had clean fixture audits. Full nextest and
Linux/Docker were not run for this client-rendering change.


## Fill solid terminal cells independently of font leading (T-909, 2026-10-23)

Terminal.app screenshots exposed two gaps that the board-only visual comparison missed:
the ticket description's `▎` looked dashed, and the mascot's full-block rows had horizontal
seams. A foreground block glyph need not cover the terminal's entire cell. The mascot and
intro now give every solid `█` the same foreground and background color. The background
fills any leading around the glyph, while two-color and half-cell pixels retain their
existing shape and colors. The source drawing, animation geometry and generated PNGs are
unchanged; this does not promise identical rasterization of half blocks across fonts.

Terminal.app's description bar uses a background-painted cell instead of `▎`. It is one
