cell wide rather than a quarter cell: continuity takes precedence over the thin-bar
preference on this endpoint. Text still begins in the same column. Other endpoints keep
the thin bar; Mono/ANSI8 keep their ASCII stroke. This rendering capability is independent
of color depth and underline support, and survives theme previews, setup and tour resets.
No saved terminal profile or font settings are changed.

The real-renderer replay adds a description with blank rows and a mascot specimen (39
frames per configuration). Terminal.app's default SF Mono 11 replay was captured and
inspected: the bar is continuous through blank lines, and the mascot's solid body has no
horizontal seams. Regression checks cover description geometry across all themes and
color profiles, every mascot pose's solid-cell backgrounds, the intro storyboard, and
capability preservation. Golden regeneration produced no golden changes: the glyph
geometry and source image remain the same; buffer color assertions cover the new paint.

Validation: 1,188 TUI tests passed with golden regeneration; `cargo ut` passed 2,549
unit tests, with the six standard ignored timing/network/PTY-child entries. Its first
run stopped at the unrelated doctor tree-size assertion (64 KiB reported for two 64 KiB
files); the unchanged test passed on the complete rerun. The real-tmux `m1_e2e` acceptance
test passed. Fixture audits were clean. Formatting and diff checks passed. Full nextest
and Linux/Docker were not run for this TUI-only change.


## Facial half blocks and measured Terminal.app keys (T-909, 2026-10-23)

A full repaint did not remove the reported extra eyes. The earlier solid-cell fix did
not cover mixed cells: an upper-half glyph with the lower eye color as its background
can expose that dark background in the font's leading as well as in the intended lower
half. On Terminal.app, the pixel encoder now swaps such a cell to a lower-half glyph,
putting the eye/mouth ink in the foreground and the body in the background. Both logical
pixel colors and their order stay unchanged. The intro uses the same encoder. This is a
font-gap mitigation, not a promise that a font draws each half exactly at a cell boundary.
Tests cover every animation pose and size across all colored palettes, compare the
logical pixels before/after, and prohibit a mixed facial cell from using eye ink as its
background. The replay adds both mascot sizes through open/blink/wave samples, and exports
the actual opening storyboard where its normal minimum-size check admits it.

**Keys measured manually, without a board.** A raw-input diagnostic captured Return as
`0d`, Shift+Return as `1b 0d`, and Ctrl+] as `1d`. The user reported that Ctrl+5 emitted
nothing and beeped. Automated physical-key injection was denied by macOS; no synthetic
input is presented as that measurement. This refutes the previous assumption that
Terminal.app necessarily collapses Shift+Return into Return.

Crossterm decodes Escape+Return as Alt+Enter; Mesimon used to discard Alt on Enter and
execute ordinary Enter. App now normalizes that explicit chord to Shift+Enter and tracks
its support independently of the extended-keyboard protocol. Terminal.app advertises the
chord from startup; another terminal that emits it learns support on the first press.
Other Shift+Control chords and key-release handling remain gated on real extended support.
The existing ask/composer/editor paths retain their actions and authorization. No terminal
profile is rewritten. The private tmux root table translates M-Enter to the same explicit
modified-Enter bytes as S-Enter, for fresh servers and at the next focus on surviving ones.
A supervised real-client PTY test sends plain Return, the measured Escape+Return and xterm
Shift+Return, checks the exact pane bytes, then detaches with Ctrl+] and verifies that the
byte never reached the pane and the pane survived; it runs on fresh and upgraded bindings.

Ctrl+5 remains bound where an endpoint sends it. The status line now hints Ctrl+] rather
than advertising a key Terminal.app did not emit. Doctor and the usage guide no longer
claim universal Ctrl+5 support, and advise the English layout for Ctrl+] where bracket
layouts differ. Exact physical Ctrl+5 support would require an endpoint mapping, outside
the app's input stream.

The requested opening animation was launched as a standalone replay in Terminal.app,
with no board, daemon or agent. Later replay windows were offscreen according to macOS,
and window capture failed. The user viewed the replay and accepted the improvement as
sufficient, while noting a remaining horizontal split through the eye. That residual
font-rendering seam is known; the change does not claim pixel parity with iTerm2.

Validation: `cargo ut` passed 2,553 tests. The TUI golden run passed 1,190 tests and
produced no golden changes. The real-client key regression passed in isolation. Full
`cargo nextest run --workspace` passed 2,807 tests, followed by all 254 alternate mod-road
integration tests; the fixture audit was clean (507 owners). Seven explicitly ignored
entries were not run directly: four timing probes, the live-network release check, and
two subprocess helpers exercised by their parent tests. The mod pass likewise skipped
its helper as a direct entry. Formatting and diff checks passed. Linux/Docker was not
run for this Terminal.app-specific correction.

## A move is drawn where it went before its board lands (T-910, 2026-10-23, "A moved card snaps back to its old column before it lands (>>), and Shift+hjkl moves it late")

**The report.** On `>>` the card went back to its old column for a moment, then jumped to the
new one; Shift+H/J/K/L moved it a beat late. Cause confirmed: T-812 asks the board after a
move on the lane and does not wait, and `drop_ghost` drew the card from the last board, where it
was still home, until that answer landed. The `>` ghost had already drawn it in its new place,
so `>>` read as a step back.

**What shipped.** A move the daemon took becomes a `Placement` (ticket, column, `before`, and
`need`, the ask count of the first board asked after it). `drop_ghost` lays it on `App.board` at
once, so the next frame draws the card where it went. `absorb` lays every placement still
pending over each board it takes, and retires a placement at the first landing whose ask count
reaches `need`. `Placement::lay` places the card the way `Daemon::order_within` does for
`Position::Before`, and leaves a card that is already there alone, so a board that already shows
the move does not change. The UI thread still never waits on that board.

- A refused move places nothing (T-450): the card stays home and the cursor stays on it.
- A nudge's cursor rides the card on the same frame (`follow_ticket`). `>>` and `.` keep it
  home, so the next card is under the cursor at once. `cursor_hold` is kept, and the comment
  saying an older landing draws the card home is corrected.
- `own_moves` is unchanged. The overlay means the landing no longer shows the card as moved, so
  `absorb_moves` would leave the stamp alive for up to 10 s. A retired placement therefore
  spends the stamp, as the landing did before (T-838).
- `catch_up` stays in front of every move key (CLAUDE.md's read-modify-write rule). A second
  nudge waits only for the first's board, which the overlay already drew, so a held Shift+J
  walks one row per press without jitter. **Refuted:** skipping `catch_up` when the board lags
  only by this board's own placements. The daemon's `BoardChanged` push for our own move comes
  through `pump`'s `refresh_soon` and raises `need_seq` anyway, so the skip would rarely apply,
  and it would split the barrier in two.

Tests in `app.rs` hold the snapshot back with the `Slow`/`Hold` seam (T-812):
`a_filing_is_drawn_where_it_went_before_its_board_lands`,
`a_nudge_is_drawn_where_it_went_before_its_board_lands`,
`quick_nudges_walk_the_card_without_jitter` and `a_refused_move_is_drawn_home`. The two T-812
tests that pinned "drawn home still" now pin the card slid under at once. There are no golden
changes. `cargo clippy -p mesimon-tui --all-targets -- -D warnings` fails on main as it is
(`large_enum_variant` on `Mode`); this ticket does not touch that.

## A tag step is drawn at once, and a board in flight is looked for every 8 ms (T-911, 2026-10-23, "Cycling a ticket's tags with the digit keys is slow since the board fetches in the background")

**The report.** "Also cycling tags on ticket is slow ever since i guess", on main e0f848d1:
since T-812 moved the snapshot off the UI thread.

**Measured** on the author's board (39 tickets, a 193 KB snapshot), debug build as the author
runs it:
- A `Snapshot` round trip on `orch.sock`, from a client outside the TUI: 9.4 ms min, 10.2 ms
  median, 12.3 ms p90, 17 ms max over 30 asks. Serialising that `Response` takes 3.9 ms of it,
  so the writer's turn plus the socket is about 6 ms. `daemon.log` has no `slow turn` since
  2026-10-22.
- In the TUI: parsing the line and `snapshot_of` take 3.7 ms, `absorb` 0.06 ms (0.8 ms at
  worst), a 200×50 frame 3 ms.
- **Most of the lag was the tick, not the board.** The lane's answer is landed by `pump` at the
  start of the next tick. An idle tick waits up to 100 ms in `event::poll` for terminal input,
  and nothing wakes it when the lane answers. So every key that asks `refresh_soon` (a tag,
  rename, archive, start, a note) showed its effect up to ~100 ms after its board was in, on
  a ~15 ms round trip: about 85 ms of the ~115 ms worst case was the tick. A second press while
  the ask was out also waited in `catch_up` for about one round trip. That wait is ~15 ms and
  the author does not feel it: quick moves and a held Shift+J do not stall on the real board.

**What shipped.**
- **The tick.** `App::frame_wait` is the tick's poll timeout. While a snapshot is in flight it
  is `SNAPSHOT_FRAME` (8 ms), so a board is drawn at most 8 ms after it lands. Otherwise it is
  16 ms while something animates and 100 ms at rest. **Cost:** every tick renders (~3 ms on
  this board) and writes only the cells that changed. One ~15 ms ask therefore costs one or two
  extra renders, and nothing is written for a render that changed nothing. The short frame
  lasts `SNAPSHOT_SOON` (1 s) per ask. A daemon slower than that is waited for at the idle pace,
  so a hung daemon is not rendered for every 8 ms. Waking the loop from the lane was the
  alternative, but crossterm's poll cannot wait on a channel too.
- **The overlay.** T-910's `Placement` is now `Laid { edit: Edit, need }`. `Edit` is `Move` (as
  before), `Tag` (the digits, `cycle_tag`, and the tag sheet's wear, `apply_tag`) and `TagColor`
  (the sheet's `c` and `C`). `App::lay` puts the edit on `App.board` once the daemon takes it.
  `absorb` lays every edit still pending over each board it takes, and retires an edit at the
  first landing whose ask count reaches `need`, as T-910 does for moves. A refused command lays
  nothing (T-450). `tag_flash` and the status line are as they were.
- **`catch_up_unless_laid`.** A read-modify-write key skips `catch_up` when this board laid an
  edit on the field the key reads, and that edit's board has not landed. For that field, the
  newest value this board knows is its own: the daemon took it, and every board asked before it
  lands has it laid on top. The only thing the wait adds is another mover's write to that same
  field inside that round trip, and that race exists with the wait too. The first press still
  catches up. This is not T-910's refuted test ("skip when the board lags only by our own
  placements"): that asked about the whole board, which pushes keep behind. This asks about the
  key's own field, so a push heard between two digits does not make the second wait. Used by
  the digits, `TagColor`/`TagColorBack` and `TagToggle`.

**Still `catch_up` every time, and why.** On the real board its wait is one ~15 ms round trip,
which nobody feels, and the 8 ms tick now draws each key's board when it lands:
- Moves, nudges, `.` and `u` (the crown's correction: the author tried them and they do not
  stall). They also read the column's order and the cards under the cursor, which other movers
  change.
- `^n`: the author says the tier cycle feels fine.
- The settings toggles: the column dialog's rings (`set_column`), crown, crown budget, crown
  mode, merge into, crown archives, reviewed PRs, crown watches, agent tools, the board
  workspace, `t` (manual merge) and the brief's switch. People rarely press them in a row.
- `x`, the text-field saves, the shell-output capture, and `TagToggle` while a name is being
  typed (it commits to the registry). Their reads are not this board's to lay.

Tests in `app.rs`, on the `Slow`/`Hold` seam:
- `a_digit_is_drawn_before_its_board_lands`.
- `quick_digits_walk_the_tags_without_a_wait`: three `SetTag`s with the right names and one ask.
  A 20 ms `catch_up_wait` would drop a press that waited, and the test fails with the skip
  turned off.
- `a_refused_digit_is_drawn_as_it_was`.
- `a_tick_looks_for_the_board_in_flight_soon`: `frame_wait` at rest, in flight, past
  `SNAPSHOT_SOON`, and after the landing.
- `repeated_presses_each_step_once_while_the_board_lands_late`: its tag-sheet half now pins that
  colour and wear step from what was laid, with no wait after the first press.

No golden changed. Clippy is clean apart from main's `large_enum_variant` on `Mode`.

## The crown holds one ticket out of the merge train for review, and returns it (T-919, 2026-10-23, "Let the crown hold tickets out of the merge train for review and return them after approval")

**Why.** A crown that wanted to review a worker's branch before it landed had no way to stop the
train. Telling the worker "do not merge" does nothing: the worker never merges, the train does,
as soon as the branch is ahead in a column it reaches and the agent's turn is over. So the person
turned the whole train off for the review. The person's `t` key already had the per-ticket flag
(`Ticket::manual_merge`, T-227). The crown had no road to it: `SetManualMerge` is in the
never-tier.

**What shipped.**
- **`hold_ticket`** is a crown tool: `key`, `seen`, and `action`, a required word, `hold` or
  `return`. It is never a toggle, so a retry cannot undo itself. On the wire it is
  `Command::AgentHoldTicket { key, hold, seen }`, admitted by `agent_allows` and on the `Full`
  rung. The tool is 820 bytes at the cap. Its `key` carries no description, as in
  `watch_ticket`, and `action` carries no `enum`: an enum in a schema is model-visible prose
  (`no_column_name_can_reach_a_schema`).
- **Authorization** is a new `Action::HoldFromTrain { crown }` in `authorize`. `Local` passes on a
  ticket. `Agent` passes only with `crown: true`, which the daemon sets from
  `Board::is_crowned`. Paired, Remote, Automation and Peer are denied whatever `Mutate` they
  hold. An agent's generic `Mutate` on a ticket is not the hold: an uncrowned worker is refused
  at `crown_target` first and by `authorize` second.
- **It is the person's own flag.** A hold sets `manual_merge`, so the planner (`train::lane`),
  `train_could_take`, `merge_by` and the crown's wake (`train_takes`) all read it unchanged.
  Who held it is the crown ledger's: `Daemon::crown_held`, kept in `crown.json` as `held` (same
  schema; a build that drops it leaves the flag as a person's hold). `get_ticket` carries `held`
  (`crown` or `person`) on every read, also before a branch exists. That is when a crown holds a
  ticket it will review. `merge.why` reads `held out of the train by the crown`. The `seen`
  stamp hashes the hold and whose it is, so a person's `t` after the crown's read makes the
  crown's write stale.
- **A person's `t` stays the person's.** The crown's return is refused on a person's hold. A
  person's `SetManualMerge` on a crown hold ends the crown's claim either way: off returns it,
  and an explicit on makes it the person's. When the crown leaves (uncrowned, crowned
  elsewhere, its ticket archived or deleted), its holds stay on the tickets as the person's
  (`release_crown_holds`, feed `hold_kept`). A review nobody will finish waits for a person,
  never for the train. A held ticket that leaves the board leaves the ledger.
- **Policy.** A hold is allowed under either crown mode, since it only withholds a merge. A
  return waits on `crown_mode.merges()` (autonomous), like `merge_ticket`: under supervised,
  the hand-back is a person's `t`. Refused: the crown's own ticket, a shared-checkout ticket
  (no branch to hold), and a hold on a merged branch.
- **A return is eligibility, not a merge.** Unlike a person's `t`, the crown's hold and return
  do not call `train.hand_touched`. The train's fuse and its refused-merge memory are gates the
  return does not clear. The ticket rejoins the planner's lists under the column's train
  setting, the seat, board order and the train's own busy test.
- **Receipt.** `Response::AgentHeld { key, held, by, changed, merge, detail, seen }`. The shim
  renders `outcome` as `held`, `already_held`, `returned` or `not_held`. Asking for the state
  the ticket is already in is no error and changes nothing. `detail` says what the hold does not
  do: a rebase turn the train already asked for is not taken back, a PR board's forge still
  merges, and a return under a disarmed train waits for the person.
- **Feed and card.** Feed `hold_ticket` / `return_ticket` (the crown as actor), touch words
  `held` / `returned`. `CROWN_WAKES` gains the review recipe in one paragraph: hold before
  delivery, the delivery wakes the crown, corrections by `ask_agent` while held, return once
  approved.

**The in-flight boundary.** A merge runs whole on the writer thread, so a hold lands before it or
after it, never during. After it, the branch reads `merged` and a hold is refused in words. A
rebase ask the train already pasted runs its turn (words that reached an agent are not taken
back); while held, the train merges nothing after it. Pinned by
`a_hold_inside_the_trains_rebase_turn_lets_the_turn_run_and_merges_nothing`.

**The delivery wake.** A held ticket has no train lane, so `train_takes` is false and a delivery
wakes the crown at once (`merge: crown`) instead of being deferred for the train (T-554).
`hear_deferred` already released a deferred delivery when a ticket left the train, so a hold
made after a delivery was deferred wakes the crown on the next tick.

**Tests.** Core: `the_train_hold_is_the_owners_and_the_crowns_alone` (authorize),
`the_crown_holds_a_ticket_out_of_the_train_by_name` (parse, description, cap, lint, rung,
`CROWN_WAKES`), the tool and command lists, and the ledger round trip. E2e, a new binary
`crown_hold_e2e`: the review on an armed train (held before the start, the delivery wakes the
crown, no merge and no rebase ask across passes, the correction lands while held, the return
lets the train merge, a merged branch is refused a hold); who may hold (uncrowned, a worker,
own ticket, checkout, no stamp, a person's `t` after the read, a person's hold, `t` on the
crown's, supervised, restart, the real shim's receipt, the crown leaving); and the rebase turn
above. `crown_e2e` and `mcp_e2e` pin 23 tools. Rig `HT1` asks the crown in plain words to keep a
branch from landing until its review, on an armed train.

**Not done.** The TUI shows no difference between a crown's hold and a person's beyond
`get_ticket`; the card reads the same `auto-merge` hint for both. Nothing tells the held
worker it is held. Its own `get_ticket` carries `held`, and that is all.

## A wake is not the work going on: the start receipt says what was sent (T-920, 2026-10-23, "Make crown wake receipts distinguish session resume from actual work continuation")

**What was wrong.** On T-919 a worker hit the account's limit; the crown parked it and called
`start_agent` naming another tier. The receipt read `status: woken`, and `CROWN_WAKES` said the
wake put it on that tier "to go on". The crown ended its turn and told the person the task had
resumed. A wake is `resume_session_in(id, false, plan)`: Claude Code comes back in its
conversation at an empty prompt box and nothing is submitted. A SessionStart idle is not a
turn, so no wake ever came to the crown either. `get_ticket` read idle for 42 s, until an
`ask_agent` with deliver now started the turn.

**What shipped.**
- `Response::AgentStarted.prompt: Option<StartPrompt>` (`#[serde(default)]`, omitted when
  `None`, so a daemon from before it says nothing). The daemon fills it at the start:
  `brief` for a spawn (the title and description are its first prompt, at launch or once the
  worktree is cut); for a wake, `Daemon::words_waiting_for`: `queued` when an ask of anyone's
  stands for the ticket and the queue will send it, or a resume still waiting for its worktree
  carries words; `held_for_person` when that ask waits for `^y`; otherwise `none`.
- The shim renders the word as `prompt` and a sentence beside it, `prompt_about`, as T-880 does
  with `wake`/`wake_about`. For `none`: nothing was sent, the session is open again (no claim
  about which conversation, see Not done), the agent stays idle with no turn and
  no wake for the crown until words reach it, `ask_agent` sends them once (deliver idle waits
  for it to be up), and `start_agent` again is not needed. For `queued`: no second ask or
  start. For `held_for_person`: the send is the person's step, raised with `raise_hand`. The
  shim only translates the daemon's word; it reads no state of its own.
- `CROWN_WAKES` (result data, so it may say what to do): the quota clause says the wake leaves
  the agent at its prompt box with nothing sent and that its work goes on in the turn
  `ask_agent`'s words start, sent once. The wake clause says a wake sends nothing and names the
  four words. `start_agent`'s description (at the byte cap) now says "A turn's end wakes this
  session", where it said "The board then wakes this session". The latter is false for a wake.
- **A queued ask follows the woken record into its pane.** An ask queued at `QueuedSeat::Wake(id)`
  (a crown's ask held for a person, or one the checkout held) survived a wake made by someone
  else, because `seat_stands` holds for the same record. Its delivery then went through
  `wake_with`, which found nothing asleep: a person's `^y` failed and the queue dropped the
  words as `queued_wake_failed`. `resume_session_with_cleanup_ack` now re-aims every such entry
  at `Pane(id)` on success. It then waits for the pane's idle like any ask, and
  `persist_queue` runs (a pane ask stays memory-only, as before). Without this fix, the new e2e
  fails at the person's send. This is what makes `queued` and `held_for_person` true.

**Not done.** The conversation word is not in the receipt. A wake whose history is missing
(`FreshWhenHistoryMissing`) starts a new conversation under the same record; the wake arm drops
`Spawned.fresh`, so the receipt does not know which happened, and `prompt_about` says only that
the session is open again, claiming no conversation either way. A crown-started worker can meet
this too: it took its brief, but its transcript can still go missing. No continuation words are
written by mesimon: the crown's `ask_agent` is the only road, so the zero-injection promise is
unchanged.

**Tests.** `cargo ut`: `a_start_prompt_is_its_own_word_and_absent_from_an_older_daemon`
(command), `the_crown_is_told_a_wake_sends_nothing` and the quota test's two new phrases (core
mcp), `a_start_receipt_says_what_reaches_the_agent_and_what_a_wake_did_not_send` (shim). In
crown_e2e, `the_crown_lets_one_agent_edit_the_others` pins `prompt: brief` on a start parked
behind its worktree cut. `a_usage_limit_needs_you_and_wakes_the_crown_that_started_the_worker`
now goes on past the tier wake:
- The receipt reads `woken` / `none`. The record, its `--resume` and its worktree cwd are the
  ones it parked with; a seeded transcript makes it a real resume, not a fresh one.
- After `SessionStart` it stays idle 2 s and nothing is typed anywhere.
- The crown's `ask_agent` (deliver idle) lands in W exactly once; its turn runs and ends on the
  same record and cwd.
- Parked again with a supervised crown's ask held: the next wake's receipt reads
  `held_for_person`, nothing goes on its own, and the person's `SendQueuedAsk` lands it once.
`a_wake_s_receipt_names_what_waits_and_it_goes_once` (added after the crown's review) covers
the receipt's queued and provisioning cases:
- **Queued.** The crown's ask to a parked shared-checkout worker waits behind the crown's own
  running turn (`queued`, wake `when_sent`). The `start_agent` wake then reads `queued`. Once
  the worker is up, the pending row is a pane `ask`, the words wait until the crown's `Stop`,
  and they land exactly once. With the reseat turned off, the test fails at "aimed at W's pane
  now".
- **Provisioning.** A worktree worker is squash-merged, parked and archived, so its tree is
  reclaimed and the next wake rebuilds it. A `start_agent` wake reads `waiting_for_worktree`
  with `none`, and nothing is typed once it is up. Reclaimed again, the crown's `ask_agent`
  wakes it, and its words ride the parked resume (wake `woken`). A second `start_agent` then
  reads `queued` and does not add a second paste: the words land exactly once.
Rig L2 is strengthened. The worker's brief has two parts, and part two waits for a later
prompt. The person's words ask the crown to carry it on with rig-alt "until it finishes". The
step ends on the worker's next Stop and the board's wake, not on `SessionStart`. Checks:
`crown:start_agent=2`, `crown:ask_agent_sent=1`, `prompts:2`, `replies:one,two`,
`cwd:worktree`, `tier:rig-alt`.
Run once on the real Sonnet (claude 2.1.309, mod road), 2026-10-23: L2 PASS in 80 s. The crown
called `sleep_agent` and then `start_agent` on rig-alt. The worker came back with
`SessionStart (resume)`, and the crown's single `ask_agent` ("Please go on with part two…") was
queued and then sent 10.6 s later. The worker answered `two` in its second turn, and the board
woke the crown with `answered`. Wakes, in order: finished, limited, answered.

## A failed attach gives the focus back, and Codex launches without its update prompt (T-923, 2026-10-23, "codex resumption is impossible now due to an update")

**What happened.** A Codex wake showed Codex's own "Update available" prompt. That prompt draws
before the native client dials mesimon's relay, so the runtime gave up ("native Codex connection
timed out"). Choosing "Update now" in the pane ran `npm install -g @openai/codex` under the live
app-server, which replaced the binary both processes ran: the attach came back non-zero
("interrupted"), and the next launches failed with `start Codex app-server: No such file or
directory` until the person repaired the install outside. From then on, every Enter on that
board, Claude included, answered "another session is focused".

**The focus leak.** `lib.rs`'s handover loop broke out on an attach error without telling the
daemon. The daemon had granted the token to this board's connection, and that connection was
still alive, so neither `FocusEnd` nor `on_client_gone` would release it: the board could not
open any session until it quit (a `U`, or the next failed attach after one, reproduces it).
`App::handover_failed` now gives the token back (`FocusEnd` for a session, `TerminalEnd` for the
`!` terminal), drops a pending GATE second half, and keeps the `focus failed: …` status. The
give-back is best effort and never an error out of the loop: an attach fails most often while the
daemon restarts or is down, when the give-back fails too, and a board that quit over it would be
worse than the leak. The status then carries both errors (`… ∙ focus not handed back: …`), and a
daemon that comes back new holds no token. Pinned by `a_failed_handover_gives_the_focus_back` and
`a_failed_give_back_keeps_the_board_up_and_says_both`.

**The update prompt.** Every Codex launch carries `-c check_for_update_on_startup=false` (a
per-launch flag on both the app-server and the native client; the person's `config.toml` is not
touched). Codex is updated outside mesimon. `provider_e2e` checks the flag is in the runtime
config. The key was verified present in codex-cli 0.164.0's config schema (its native binary
carries `check_for_update_on_startup`); the prompt's suppression was not observed live, since
0.164.0 was the latest release and no prompt was due.

**Not done.** `codex orphan kept: … its native pane remains live` appeared for the Codex pane of a
ticket deleted while its session sat idle; not investigated here.

## Ubuntu CI: the runner's own `gh`, and a pane tmux never reaped (T-917, 2026-10-23, "Restore Ubuntu CI: forge e2e failures and Codex startup-recovery timeout")

Every push to main had failed CI since 2026-10-08. Two causes were current on main at `7fb99ec5`,
and they are separate.

**`forge_e2e`, 27 of 34 failing since 2026-10-15: a test environment fault, not a product defect.**
The daemon looks for `gh`/`glab` on the captured login-shell `PATH` before its own
(`forge::find_cli`). `shellenv::capture` starts that shell from `/usr/bin:/bin:…`. GitHub's
Ubuntu runner ships a signed-out `/usr/bin/gh`, so it came before every test's stand-in, which sat
only on the daemon's own `PATH`. macOS has no `gh` in `/usr/bin`, so the suite passed there. The
GitLab tests passed on the runner too, because it has no `glab`. Reproduced on Debian 12 in
Docker with Debian's `gh` installed: 7/27, the runner's exact split. The fix is in
`Harness::boot_bare`: a `PATH` a test sets is also written to the fixture `HOME`'s `~/.profile`, so
the login shell names it too. `ci/test-linux.sh` now installs `gh`, so the local Linux gate meets
the same shadow. Product behaviour is unchanged: a person's login-shell CLI should win.

**`codex_startup_recovery_e2e` timing out intermittently: a tmux bug, now repaired in the daemon.**
A tmux before 3.6 built with libutempter (Debian's 3.3a and Ubuntu's 3.4 both link it) loses a
pane's exit. When the pane's pty closes, `server_destroy_pane` calls `utempter_remove_record`.
libutempter sets SIGCHLD to `SIG_DFL` while it waits for its helper, and on Linux that discards a
SIGCHLD that arrives meanwhile, even a blocked one. A pane process that turns zombie inside that
window is never waited for: tmux shows `pane_dead=1` with an empty `pane_dead_status`, never
fires `pane-died`, and the record keeps its pane, its seat and its checkout.

How it was established, on Ubuntu 24.04 with tmux 3.4 in Docker:
- `ps` showed the runtime as `[python3] <defunct>`, a child of the tmux server, for the test's
  whole 10 s.
- The server's `/proc/<pid>/status` showed SIGCHLD caught (`SigCgt`), not blocked, not pending.
- tmux 3.6a raises `kill(getpid(), SIGCHLD)` after that very call (`server-fn.c`); 3.3a through
  3.5a do not.
- macOS (tmux 3.6a, and a locally built 3.4 without utempter) never showed it.

The repair is that same raise, from outside:
- `pane_facts` now also reads `pane_dead_status`, `pane_dead_signal` and the server's `#{pid}`.
- `PaneFacts::unreaped` is a pane that is dead with neither a status nor a signal.
- The `nudge_unreaped` stage sends SIGCHLD to that pane's server (`nudge_reaper`) for any of our
  records that still holds its pane. It nudges again on every sample that shows the pane, and the
  journal says `unreaped pane: …` once per pane.
- tmux then waits for the child and fires `pane-died`, so the death still comes up the hook road.
  The stage decides nothing about the record, and "no polling for exits" stands.
- A SIGCHLD with no exited child costs the server one empty `waitpid` loop.

Results, with the 5-test binary run in a loop:

| Ubuntu 24.04, tmux 3.4 | Failed |
|---|---|
| Before (three loops) | 2/60, 8/80, 1/50 |
| After | 0/80 |

Four of the tests in the after-loop journalled the nudge, and each of those would have failed
without it. Debian 12's tmux 3.3a showed 0 failures in 40 runs before the fix: it has the same
unprotected call, and how often a race like this hits depends on timing.

Not covered:
- A death whose `pane-died` fired but whose hook frame was lost. The reap already happened, so
  there is nothing to nudge.
- No e2e forces the lost SIGCHLD. It cannot be provoked from outside tmux. The evidence is the
  Ubuntu loop above, and the unit test pins how the facts are parsed and what `unreaped` means.

**Older reds, from 2026-10-08 to 2026-10-12** (a fixture-audit failure, and
`worktree::the_init_script_runs_in_the_worktree…`), are from before current main and were not
investigated.

**Seen on macOS and not fixed here:**
- `ui::tests::terminal_app_description_bar_fills_every_row_without_moving_the_text` and
  `terminal_comparison::plain_progress_preserves_the_completed_share_and_the_rgb_card` (T-909)
  compare two draws cell by cell, and a spinner glyph can advance between them under load.
  Each passed 3/3 alone.
- `forge_e2e::the_crown_hears_the_forges_edges` counts forge wakes after a fixed 1.5 s sleep, and
  read 4 for 3 once under a concurrent suite. It passed 3/3 alone.
- `diff_e2e::the_board_diffs_its_own_checkout`'s `git add .` raced the daemon's
  `.mesimon/board/columns.tmp` once.

## The transcript dialog: `{ }` on a card reads its agent's conversation (T-921, 2026-10-23)

The author: "{ } on ticket card to reveal and scroll transcript messages … { } will scroll the
*messages* not the text. j k will scroll the current message text. stay in board, maybe a medium
dialog below the ticket." Designed as an interactive simulation first and approved after one
round (title `TRANSCRIPT (i of n)` with no agent name or state, no `enter` hint, `c copy`, Esc in
the footer only, the board receded as behind the other card dialogs).

**What it is.** `{` or `}` on a board card whose agent has a transcript opens `Mode::Transcript`
(`Scope::Transcript`, a dialog scope under Global), hung from the card by `dialog::placed` and
its notch, 68 wide and 14 rows inside, over `board::recede`. It opens on the newest message, at
its top. Inside, `{ }` step the messages (`TranscriptNewer`, with `{` derived to
`TranscriptOlder`), `jk` and the wheel scroll the message on show (`ScrollDown` through
`App::pager`, which now answers the board with the dialog's `Pager`), `c` copies it whole (up to
256 KiB, below) and Esc closes. Each message remembers where it was left. A message is a prompt, a reply or a notice;
the tool calls that follow one are its `n steps ∙ Read, Edit` on its first row, beside who wrote
it and when. A person's words wear the `▎` quote bar and keep their line breaks; a reply renders
through `rich` as the ticket page's preview does, cut with `~` while more is below. The body
starts in the title's column (two cells in), which fixes the one-cell offset the list dialogs
have between their title and their rows.

**Where the words come from.** The TUI reads the transcript itself, through
`mesimon_daemon::agents::read_transcript_reply` — the pager Remote Control reads (T-626) — the
same observe-tier read the card's peek makes (`peek.rs`). No wire command and no daemon
behaviour change: a running daemon needs no restart. The newest page is read on the key; the pages
before it are read on a thread of their own back to the file's start, so `(i of n)` counts the
whole conversation once they land (the message on show keeps its place, found by its key, as they
prepend). While the dialog is open the UI thread only stats the file, every 250 ms; what was
written since is read on another thread, one read in flight at a time, and lands in `pump` as a
snapshot does (T-812), with the messages rebuilt once per poll however many pages landed. That
read resolves the file again (`agents::transcript_file`: a Codex rollout's continuation, looked for
at least every 5 s), and `poll` is handed the record's path off the board each time, so a new
conversation (`/clear`, `/resume`, a Codex continuation) starts over on its newest message. A
reader on the newest message stays on it, and the title gains `∙ 1 new` until they step to it:
"new" is what came after the newest message they have been on, kept as that message's key. A file
cut short starts over too, on `nothing said yet` when it holds nothing. The session is the ticket's seat holder,
else its newest agent record, so a parked or finished agent's conversation still opens.

**Gates.** `Ctx::ticket_transcript` (the board, a card, an agent record with a transcript path),
`transcript_messages` (more than one, for `{ }`), `transcript_scrolls` (the message overflows its
window, for `jk`, measured by the last draw). `Verb::Transcript` joins `needs_repository`, so a
joined content-only board offers none. A card with nothing said yet says so on the status line
and opens nothing. Under its dialog the card is its title: the peek would repeat the dialog.

**The footer.** `{ } transcript` (prio 20) sits after `space ticket page` on a card that has a
conversation, so at 120 columns `tab describe` gives up its place there (three board goldens).

**A long message reads whole (the crown's review, T-925).** Remote Control's pager cut every row
at `TRANSCRIPT_ROW_MAX_BYTES` (8 KiB) inside `TranscriptRow::new`, so a long final report showed,
and `c` copied, its first 8 KiB. The cut moved to the page reader: `TranscriptRow::capped`, at
`Ask::row_max`, default 8 KiB, so a phone's pages are byte for byte what they were, and the dialog
asks for 256 KiB (`transcript::ROW_MAX`); past that it ends in `…`. A row still counts against the
page's 32 KiB, which only makes the dialog's pages shorter. The dialog's edge is drawn after the
message is measured, so `jk scroll` shows on the frame that opens a long one, not the next.

Tests: `transcript::tests` (steps belong to the message before them; opens on the newest, `unseen`
counts what came after, the ends hold), `golden_transcript_dialog_120`,
`test_transcript_dialog_steps_messages_and_scrolls_the_one_on_show`,
`test_transcript_needs_a_conversation`, and `braces_open_the_transcript_and_step_its_messages`
in the keymap.

## The crown reads the reason of a hand it was told of (T-922, 2026-10-23, "Keep a raised-hand reason readable after its notification reaches the crown")

**Seen on T-917.** A worker raised its hand mid-turn; the crown woke on `… raised its hand ∙
get_ticket key=… for state and notes`, read the ticket at once and found `state: working` and no
reason. **Cause:** two decisions that each held alone. T-414 keeps the reason out of the wake
sentence (one agent's words do not start another's turn) and sends the crown to `get_ticket`;
T-861's `lower_told_hands` takes `Ticket.raised` off in the same writer turn that sent the
sentence, and `get_ticket`'s only spelling of the reason was `state.raised`, read from that
field. T-888's five-minute memory of a lowered hand is the TUI's alone and never reached an
agent. `crown_e2e` asserted the hand was down after the wake and never read the ticket.

**Shipped.** The hand still comes down when the crown is told (T-861 unchanged: nothing counts
or lights a told hand), and its reason stays with the crown that was told:
- `Daemon::crown_hands` (worker → `ToldHand { reason, told_ms }`), filled by
  `lower_told_hands` from `Ticket.raised` just before it lowers it. Kept in `crown.json` as
  `hands` (same schema: a build that drops the field loses the reasons and narrows nothing), so a
  restart between the wake and the read keeps it.
- The crown's keyed `get_ticket` carries it as `told_hand { reason, told_secs }`
  (`AgentTicketView::told_hand`, `told_hand_view`), the way `asked` (T-568) rides that read.
  Not on the worker's own read, not on `list_board`, not on the crown's own ticket; another
  agent's keyed read is refused as before. `state.raised` keeps meaning a hand that is up.
- **Taken by:** the worker's next turn (`forget_told_hand` on the three turn-start roads beside
  `lower_hand_on`: `UserPromptSubmit`, Codex's new turn, the High `Idle{EndTurn}`/dialog →
  `Running` edge): it was given something, so the question is answered or overtaken. A new
  `raise_hand` with other words (the new hand is `state.raised`, and its telling replaces the
  entry). A new crown (`drop_crown_wakes`; it has heard nothing). The worker leaving the board,
  said where it leaves: archive and delete through `drop_crown_if`, a snooze in
  `snooze_ticket`; a restored ledger drops a worker missing or archived. One entry per worker, at
  most `RAISE_REASON_MAX_BYTES`: bounded by the board.
- **A turn begun while no daemon listened** (crown review of `3d3c04b8`): its `UserPromptSubmit`
  is lost, never queued, and the recovered turn comes back at Low, which takes no hand down, so
  the restored entry stood over an answered question. `restore_crown` reads the worker's Claude
  transcript (`tail::prompted_since`, the last 1 MiB, newest first, stopping at the first record
  dated before `told_ms`) and drops an entry a person's prompt (`adopt::user_prompt`) postdates.
  Not any Low edge: a tool's result or a reply after the telling is the hand's own turn going on
  (T-917's hand was raised mid-turn). **Limits:** a prompt further back than the window, a Codex
  worker (its rollout is another format) and a worker with no transcript keep the entry until
  their next hooked turn; a restart is the only gap the hooks have, so the read is once per entry
  at start and never on the tick.
- **A watch ending keeps it**: the crown it was told is still the crown holding the question.
- **Not taken by** the other T-861 roads (focus in or out of the pane, a park, the page's
  `LowerHand`): none of them gave the agent anything, and the crown is still the one holding the
  question. **A hand lowered before the sentence went keeps nothing**: the person dealt with it,
  and the wake that still names it does not resurrect it.
- **In `seen_token`, by its words and `told_ms`** (crown review of the first commit): two hands
  told inside one turn of the worker leave the column, notes, state, `state_changed_at` and
  `Ticket.raised` (down both times) exactly as the first read saw them, so a stamp without the
  told hand came back the same and an ask answering the first was accepted for the second.
  `told_ms` is the telling's moment, persisted, never elapsed time: the stamp holds still while
  nothing changes, and the same words told again are another hand with another stamp.
- `CROWN_WAKES` gains one sentence saying the hand comes down at the telling and where its reason
  is read; the wake template and `raise_hand`'s description are unchanged.

**Considered and refused.** Putting the reason in the wake sentence (T-414's rule, and arbitrary
worker text in an unsolicited prompt). Keeping the hand up until the crown acts (T-861's two
cards for one question). Letting `state.raised` fall back to the told reason (a hand that is down
would read as up). A note on the ticket (content made only to carry a pointer). A time window
(a crown woken while busy may read an hour later; the events above bound it instead).

**Tests.** `told_hand_e2e::the_crown_reads_the_reason_of_a_hand_it_was_told_of`: told and down,
read by the crown with `state: working` and no `state.raised`, refused to another agent, absent
on the worker's own read and the crown's own ticket, kept across a restart and the crown's own
turn, overtaken by a new hand and replaced at its telling, kept past the worker's Stop and taken
by its next prompt, nothing kept for a hand a person lowered first, and gone with an uncrown.
`told_hand_e2e::an_answer_read_against_one_told_hand_is_refused_for_the_next`: two hands told in
one worker turn, the first read's stamp refused (`changed since it was read`) and a fresh read's
accepted, the stamp still after a second, the same words told again a new stamp; a park keeps the
told hand, an archive takes it out of `crown.json` and an unarchive brings none back, a delete
takes it out. Without the stamp change the stale ask is accepted; without `drop_crown_if`'s
forget the archive keeps it.
`told_hand_e2e::a_prompt_while_the_daemon_was_down_takes_the_told_hand`: a restart over a tool's
result written in the gap keeps the reason, a restart over a prompt written there forgets it in
the read and in `crown.json`; without `restore_crown`'s transcript read it is kept.
`tail::prompted_since_reads_a_persons_prompt_and_nothing_else` covers the classifier.
Without the fix it fails at the first read exactly as T-917 read. `crown_e2e`'s two hand passages
(a started worker, a watched one) now read `told_hand` after the wake. `crownledger`'s round-trip
carries `hands`. Rig **RH2** (Sonnet): a worker asks a two-word question by its hand; the crown
answers it with exactly one `ask_agent` naming the first word, and the worker replies with it.

## A Codex crown measured on delegation and forge news, and told what the crown is for (T-916, 2026-10-23)

The author: a Codex crown delegates less than a Claude crown; what does the rig cover on Codex?
Before this, nothing measured a real Codex crown deciding anything: the question case drives the
crown's wire road itself, and the Claude rig's F tests spell out every tool call to a scripted
crown. Two live Codex cases now ask a crowned seat one thing in a person's words and read the
board, the feed and the native histories (`ci/rig/README.md` has the cases and their limits).

**What reaches a crown, traced on both providers.** The words are the same bytes: the agent brief
(`brief::TEXT`; Claude Code's system prompt, Codex's `SessionStart` context as a developer
message), the tool descriptions, and the crown's own `get_ticket` (`crowned`, and `crown`, which
was the wake words alone). Codex adds its own developer messages: a skills list, a permission
profile and `<multi_agent_mode>` ("do not spawn sub-agents unless the user ... explicitly ask"),
so a native child is not the competing road (none was spawned with `multi_agent` on). The policy
differs: the mod registers the board's tools with no permission check on Claude, while Codex
0.163 under on-request asks the person once for each board write the crown calls
(`set_workspace`, `start_agent`, `ask_agent`, `raise_hand`, `watch_ticket`; reads went unasked
through code mode). A crown whose person is away sits at `needs you` on every start. That is
recorded, not changed: the approval policy is Codex's and the person's.

**The demonstrated defect, fixed.** Nothing told a crown what the crown is for, and the brief says
the description and notes are the brief and "do not start work without them". On a crowned ticket
with no description, Luna (low) asked for a module and its test read its ticket and replied "the
ticket brief is empty and doesn't match the request. Please file this work on the correct ticket"
and did nothing. `mcp::CROWN_ROLE` now opens the crown's own view (`mcp::crown_view`, the role
then `CROWN_WAKES`; the receipts keep the wake words alone): the person's prompts are its brief
beside an empty description, a ticket's own work is filed with create_ticket and started with
start_agent in a session of its own, and coordination stays here. Described, not ordered; no
delegate-everything rule. With it, the same request gets "the request in this session is the
brief", and Luna wrote `greet.py` and `test_greet.py` into the checkout itself.

**Runs, each once on the change it tested (`target/rig/codex/<run>/`, Codex CLI 0.163.0,
`gpt-6-luna`, low, every turn context confirmed):**
- `delegate`, before the fix: failed, the refusal above (70,030 observed tokens, 1 turn).
- `delegate`, after it: failed, the crown did the work itself, one `apply_patch` in the checkout
  (110,752 tokens).
- `forge`: inconclusive. The crown delegated, but the fixture leaked the person's machine tiers
  (`$HOME/.local/state/mesimon/tiers.toml`) and the crown picked `deep`, a Claude tier, so the
  real `claude` started and stopped at its folder-trust dialog before any model call. The runner
  also read the bare board, which carries no worktrees or PRs. Both fixed: the crown fixtures' daemon runs on
  a `HOME` of its own (built-in tiers only, no personal skills, a fixture git identity, a `claude`
  that refuses to start, the rig's own login shell), and the cases read the snapshot.
- `forge`: failed on the run's 600k observed-token stop before the pipeline failed (611,743;
  90 % cached input: a Codex crown re-sends a ~60k context on every code-mode request). By then
  the crown had started the worker in a worktree and, on its "finished" wake, watched it and ended
  its turn saying the PR's news would wake it. Crown cases now carry their own allowance
  (`CASE_TOKENS`, 1M and 2M), which raises the run's default.
- `forge`: passed (406,360 tokens, 5 turns, 4 person approvals). On "has news from the forge
  (pipeline failed #42: test-linux)" the crown read the ticket, called start_agent on the busy
  ticket (refused, one agent per ticket), then ask_agent `deliver: now` naming the job, and ended
  its turn with no watch, sleep or poll; the worker read the words as a prompt.
- Claude rig `DL1` on Sonnet: passed. Told to do what the board's crown does with the same request,
  with the rig's rules against filing and starting lifted, the crown filed T-5 and started its
  agent in a worktree, wrote nothing, and heard the delivery. The rig's crown is scripted by its
  own brief, so this is the acceptance of the new words, not a parity measurement.

**Not yet explained.** Why Luna keeps a small request rather than filing it, with the role in its
view, is not settled by one sample. Candidates: the role reaches it as tool output under a
developer-level brief; Codex's base prompt favours doing the work; a two-file module reads as the
crown's own. A Claude crown on the same fixture and words was not run: the Codex rig drives
Claude only on its hook-set road, where every board write would also need a permission answer.
`delegate` was not re-run on the own-`HOME` fixture; its crown never reached a tier or a start.

Offline: `ci/codex_rig_test.py` (23 tests: selection, deadlines, token and native-turn stops,
the code-mode call readers, the approval rule, the own-`HOME` fixture, the stub forge on the
login-shell PATH). Gates: `cargo ut` (one run hit `worktree::tests::default_branch_reads_the_head_of_the_remote_the_checkout_uses`,
which shares a fixed temp path and passed alone and on the rerun), `crown_e2e`, the release
clippy, and `cargo nextest run --workspace` (2816 passed, 7 skipped).

**The rig's approver, matched exactly** (the same day, after a security review of the first
commit). The crown fixtures answer approvals a live model writes, so they now allow only Codex
0.163's one-tool approval for the server named `mesimon` and a tool in `BOARD_TOOLS` (the
dialog's `Allow the mesimon MCP server to run tool "<tool>"?`), a worker's git in three exact
shapes (`status [--short]`, `add` of relative paths with no option, `commit -m|-am <message>`;
no `diff`, `log` or `show`, whose options reach files) from a cwd that resolves to that worker's
own worktree, no shell character, and only the allow-once row. The passing forge run
was answered by the earlier substring rule; its approvals had the shape the exact rule takes
(read off its terminal capture and T-846's record), but the exact rule has not run live.

**Not this ticket's: why Ubuntu CI's `forge_e2e` fails** (T-917 owns it). This ticket found
that `forge::find_cli` looks for `gh` on the captured login-shell PATH before the daemon's own.
The e2e harness captures with `SHELL=/bin/sh`: on macOS that login PATH has no Homebrew, so the
stub on the daemon's PATH answers, while an `ubuntu-24.04` runner ships `/usr/bin/gh` on it. A
likely cause of the run's first-pass timeouts, not verified on a runner.

**Crown review: three false positives closed, and the final runs** (the same day). The review
found that `delegate` passed a shared-checkout worker, `forge` passed any ask followed by any
worker prompt, and "no implementation" saw only `apply_patch` and Write/Edit. Now:
- **Delegation is proven** (`delegation_problems`): the ticket's `created_by` is the crown's
  session and `created_from` its ticket; an agent's `create_ticket` and `start_agent` for it are
  in the feed; the worker is `started_by` the crown; and the snapshot's worktree for the ticket
  has a branch and a path that resolves to the worker's cwd, away from the checkout and under the
  board's worktrees. `forge` asks the same of the start, the ticket being a person's. The Claude
  rig's `filed` asks the same through the snapshot.
- **The forge ask carries the failure** (`heard_the_ask`): the prompt the worker reads holds
  the ask's own words, read off the crown's call where its arguments spell them, and names
  `test-linux` or PR 42 and that it failed (`conveys_failure`, whole words: "required" is not
  "red"). Words not read off the call are judged on the failure alone, and the manifest says so.
- **The crown's own work is any of these** (`implemented`): a native child, an `apply_patch`, a
  shell command that writes naming the work's files, the worktree or the branch
  (`command_writes`: redirection, the usual writers, `-c`/`-e` interpreters, and git's writes
  after any `-C`/`-c`), or a checkout whose HEAD or working tree moved, a tip the board merged
  from a worktree aside. The Claude rig's `crown_wrote_nothing:<names>` reads Bash the same way,
  against the checkout as the test found it. A write a command does not name is caught only by
  the checkout, and none in the worker's own worktree. Offline regressions cover each false
  positive (`ci/codex_rig_test.py`, 28).

Final runs, once each on the corrected cases, all cleanups clean:
- `delegate` (before the rebase onto T-919): **failed**, the honest model outcome again: no
  worker, one `apply_patch`, `greet.py` and `test_greet.py` untracked in the checkout (109,636
  tokens, 1 turn).
- `forge` (after the rebase): **failed** before any forge news: the crown read T-1 by key, never
  its own ticket, and ended its turn saying it could not move T-1 to a worktree "because it isn't
  crowned" (81,202 tokens, 1 turn). Every view carries `crowned`, false on any ticket but the
  crown's, and Luna read T-1's as its own. A wording candidate, not changed or re-run here.
  The earlier passing `forge` run is the evidence for the forge-news behaviour, under the
  weaker assertions; the corrected assertions have not seen it pass.
- Claude rig `DL1` on Sonnet (after the rebase, `e87f363a`): **passed**. T-8 was filed by the
  crown's session in `msmn/T-8-add-greet.py-and-its-unittest`, with no write of the crown's and
  the checkout as found. The crown ran on the hook-set road this time.

The seven tests nextest skips are `#[ignore]`d with their reasons:
- `restart_skew_e2e::client_connect_fixture_helper`: a subprocess helper the two restart-skew
  tests run.
- `search::tests::{how_long_a_big_board_takes, how_long_the_notes_take}`,
  `crownledger::tests::how_long_a_big_crown_ledger_check_takes` and
  `store::tests::how_long_a_big_sessions_save_takes`: they print a timing and are run by hand.
- `intro::tests::pty_child`: the pty test's own child.
- `release::tests::the_download_half_works_against_the_real_release_channel`: it needs the
  network.

**Second crown review: the checks failed a correct crown** (the same day, the review of `7e4ffd4e`
under T-925). The model outcomes above stand; these were the checks' own errors:
- **A board fast-forward read as the crown's write.** `merged_oid` names a commit only where patch
  equality found the merge; a fast-forward is an ancestor merge and names none, so a crown that
  delivered and then merged (or a train merge) moved HEAD unexcused. `board_tips` now excuses a
  HEAD at any board worktree branch's tip as well as a `merged_oid`; a commit past that tip is
  still the crown's. Both rigs use it.
- **Reads counted as writes.** `">"` matched `2>&1`, `2>/dev/null` and a JS `=>`; `echo` and
  `printf` alone counted too. A write by redirection is now output to a file (`REDIRECT`: not fd
  duplication, `/dev/null`, `=>` or `>=`), and `echo`/`printf` write only through a redirection or
  `tee`.
- **One PR read counted as polling.** `gh pr view` and `gh pr checks` were poll words; one read to
  learn which job failed, then yielding, is the behaviour the case asks for. A poll is now a watch,
  a sleep (Codex's own included), or the same forge read twice in the crown's calls.
- **`crowned: false` on a keyed read misled the crown** (the live `forge` failure above). The
  crown's view of another ticket left the field on, always false; Luna read T-1's as its own. The
  field is now `Option<bool>`, off the wire on another ticket's view, and said either way on a
  session's read of its own ticket (`AgentGetTicket`, and a keyed read whose key is its own).
  `crown_e2e` pins both.
- **`CROWN_ROLE` classified every change as a ticket's own** ("a change, a fix, a feature"), close
  to the delegate-everything policy the brief ruled out. It now describes the board's division
  without classifying work: the crown can file a ticket and start it, a session of its own does
  that ticket's work, and the board's own work is the crown's. **Its effect on delegation is
  unmeasured**: the Codex `delegate` run failed with the first wording, and no Claude crown was run
  without it. What it demonstrably fixed is the refusal on an empty description.
- **`filed` passed one good start beside bad ones.** Every ticket the crown started an agent on
  must now hold, as the Codex rig's `delegation_problems` does.
- **An ask not read off its call passed on the failure words alone.** The `forge` case now ends
  `inconclusive` there (`Inconclusive`, which the runner records apart from a failure).
- The fixture-HOME note left `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md`: it is a fact about this rig, kept in
  `ci/rig/README.md` and above.

Offline regressions: the fast-forward with no `merged_oid` (a real temporary repository), the
reads that are no writes, one PR read against the same read twice, and the inconclusive class
(`ci/codex_rig_test.py`, 30).

Runs after the corrections and the rebase onto main (`34670d8c`), once each, no retries, all
cleanups clean:
- `forge` (Luna, low): **passed**, the first pass under the corrected assertions. The crown
  started T-1 in its worktree; on the forge's wake it called `get_ticket` and `ask_agent` alone,
  and the worker read the crown's words, read off its call: "PR #42 pipeline failed: test-linux.
  Please inspect the failing check/logs and fix the cause …". No watch, sleep, poll or write of
  the crown's. Approvals answered: `start_agent`, `ask_agent`. 579,292 tokens, 1 person's turn.
  One sample: the `crowned` fix and this pass coincide, and one run does not prove the cause.
- `delegate` (Luna, low): **failed**, as before: the crown called `get_ticket`, then wrote
  `greet.py` and `test_greet.py` with `apply_patch` in the checkout, and started no worker. 91,340
  tokens, 1 turn. The reworded role changed nothing measurable here.
- Claude rig `DL1` (Sonnet): **passed**. T-11 was filed by the crown's session and started in
  `msmn/T-11-add-greet.py-with-greet-name-and`, no write of the crown's, the checkout as found,
  and the crown's turn on the delivered wake ended. Its `expect` words were brought in line with
  the new role after the run; the checks are unchanged.

**`delegate` on Sol** (the same day, after the merge, at the person's ask: Luna had failed it).
The model was `--model gpt-6-sol --effort low`, the id exactly as the authenticated `model/list`
names it, with `low` among its efforts. `gpt-6.1-sol` is listed too, as the account's default;
the named id was used. One run with the same bounds, no retries, cleanup clean.
- **Failed**, 123,297 tokens, 1 person's turn.
- Unlike Luna, the crown delegated and wrote nothing itself: no `apply_patch`, no shell write,
  no native child.
- The crown's calls, in order: a tool search, `get_ticket`, a tool search, `list_board`,
  `create_ticket` (T-2 "Add greet.py and unittest", tagged FEATURE, `workspace:
  "shared_checkout"`, a description that says to run the test), `get_ticket` on T-2, then

- It failed on the case's own requirement: a worker in a worktree of its own, away from the
  checkout the crown works in. Sol chose the shared checkout for both calls.
- `forge` was not run on Sol, since its `delegate` did not pass.

This is one sample. It says Sol's choice here was to file and start, which is the delegation the
person found missing, and that it picked the crown's own checkout as the worker's workspace.
Whether that choice is wrong for a two-file change is the person's call, not the rig's: the

## The crown's wake waits for a person at the crown's box (T-918, 2026-10-23, "The crown wake holds while a person is attached to the crown's pane")

**The problem.** The board's sentence to the crown (T-414) went in whenever the crown's agent
took words (`session_takes_words`). Nothing asked whether a *person* was typing in that box, so
a wake could land in a half-typed prompt, and its Enter sent both. T-537's note "Delivery road
assessment: paste vs monitor" argued for keeping the paste road and holding it, not a Monitor.

**What shipped.**
- **Two facts, sampled off the writer.** `pane_facts` reads `#{session_attached}` in the same
  `list-panes` fork as the titles (`PaneFacts::attached`). `absorb_panes` keeps the set in
  `Daemon::attached`, in memory only, as the foregrounds are. The box is the sampler's screen of
  the pane, read by `composer::read` (Claude) or `codex::composer_holds_text`.
- **`person_hold`** names the reason: a tmux client has the pane open (`when you leave`), or
  the box holds words nobody sent (`after your draft`). `crown_wake_blocked` adds it for a
  `QueuedSeat::Pane` only. A parked crown has no pane, and a `Start` seat is already blocked.
- **The draft clause goes beyond the ticket's brief, on purpose.** Holding only while a client
  is attached leaves the commonest case open: the person types half a prompt, goes back to the
  board, and the wake joins their draft at once. When they come back to the board, the card
  says why the wake waits.
- **The row.** The `crown_wake` `Pending` row carries the reason in `held` (the field already
  says why a row waits: `agent asked`), and `pending_row` says `crown wakes ∙ when you leave` /
  `crown wakes ∙ after your draft`. That outranks `after its turn`. `is_held` is about queued
  asks only, so `^y`/`^u` still leave the row alone. There is no new wire field.
- **Cadence.** `drain_crown_wakes` runs every 4 ticks (1 s). While a wake waits, the crown's
  facts and screen are asked of the sampler once a second (`want_person`, `PERSON_READ_MS`),
  and the sample's landing delivers. The wake
  therefore goes up to about 1 s after the person leaves (rig A1 measured 1.9 s before this
  correction, and 12 ms after it, on 87026e2d). Without this the box
  would not be sampled at all, and the facts only on the 2 s poll bucket. A crown that is
  mid-turn is read on the bucket only.
- **No read on the writer (review of ff317618).** The first cut asked tmux afresh at the paste
  (`client_quiet_secs`, `capture_input_screen`) on the writer, against the brief. Now a Claude
  crown's wake goes in only on the pane sample that has just landed, when that sample read
  both the crown's clients and its box (`person_read_at`: `attached_at` equals that pane's
  screen time). The drain's 1 s pass only asks for that sample (`want_person`), and
  `on_pane_sampled` runs `drain_crown_wakes(Some(at))` as it lands. Nothing about a person is
  forked for on the writer, and the paste rests on reads from the same sample.
- **Codex: the paste and its Enter (review of ff317618).** A Codex crown's wake is parked and
  pasted by `drive_codex_inputs`. Its Enter comes 500 ms later (`codex_input_due`), and that
  Enter sends the whole box. The first cut checked only before the paste, so a person who came
  in during those 500 ms had their keys sent with the wake: the very bug. Now:
  - **Before the paste:** a sample that read clients and box together, at or after the box was
    last seen, with nobody in the pane and no draft.
  - **Before the Enter:** `codex_wake_box` reads a sample from after the paste:
    - `Wait` while a person is in the pane, while the box is not the composer, or while it is
      empty (Codex has yet to draw the paste), up to the composer's wait.
    - `Ours` when the box holds exactly the words pasted (`codex::composer_shows`: the words,
      wrapped, or Codex's `[Pasted Content N chars]` placeholder for a long paste). This is
      the only case that presses Enter.
    - `Theirs` for anything else (a word added or removed, or the words gone with no turn).
      Nothing is pressed or typed and the box is left as the person made it. Since the review
      of f5f9c8d7 the wake is owed again, told nothing (below); the first correction kept it
      as unsent words with `crown_wake_failed`, and the news was lost.
  - `owed.sent` keeps the pasted words for that comparison, for the crown's wake only.
  - `person_hold` does not read mesimon's own pasted wake as a draft, so the wait never blocks
    on its own paste.
- The feed has nothing new for a delivery. `crown_wake_sent` still fires on delivery, and the
  `woke` touch is still made when the wake is owed, not when it is pasted.

**The guarantee, and what it is not.**
- **Claude, hook road.** The window runs from the sample's reads (facts first, then screens, in
  one worker pass) to the paste on the writer: the sample's own duration plus the hand-off, tens
  of ms on an idle machine and longer under load (T-856). A person who attaches and types
  inside it is not caught. The paste and its Enter are one call (`paste_text`), and no Enter
  is pressed later.
- **Mod road.** `$.prompt.submit` types nothing into the box, and a submit keeps a draft
  in the box (measured in T-931, Claude Code 2.1.309), so since T-931 neither hold applies to a
  wake that goes by the mod's submit. A mod that never polled, an older one, or a slash-command
  wake keeps the paste road and the holds.
- **Codex.** The paste and the Enter each rest on a sample read together and not older than the
  250 ms tick that reads it plus the sample's duration. The Enter needs a sample from after the
  paste. A person who types in the gap between that sample and the Enter is not caught.
- **A parked crown** (Claude or Codex) is woken with the words as a launch's. The pane is new
  and nobody is in it, so those words keep the launch road's own presses, unguarded.
- **Who counts as attached.** Any tmux client of the private server: the board's own focus,
  a hand `tmux attach`, a control-mode client. Remote Control is not a tmux client, so a
  phone holds nothing.
- **Known cost, as the ticket says.** A crown a person sits in for an hour hears nothing for an
  hour. So does a crown whose box holds a forgotten draft, and the card says so. If it hurts,
  the fallback is the per-board switch the ticket names, not a different road.

**Tests.**
- `crown_e2e::a_codex_crown_s_wake_waits_for_a_person_and_never_sends_their_words`, on the
  synthetic runtime, whose screen the test draws. It covers five cases:
  - an ordinary delivery, where the Enter waits until the box shows the paste;
  - a person in the pane (`when you leave`, nothing pasted), then the draft they leave
    (`after your draft`), then the paste once the box is empty;
  - a person who comes in between the paste and its Enter, where no Enter goes until they
    leave;
  - a parked crown woken with the words;
  - a box the person changed after the paste: no Enter and no keys (what follows it changed
    in the review of f5f9c8d7, below).

  Three mutations each fail it: the Enter guard always `Ours`, the attached check removed,
  and `Theirs` read as `Ours`.
- `codex::the_box_shows_the_wake_as_pasted_and_a_persons_edit_is_not_it`.
- `crown_e2e::the_crown_wake_waits_for_a_person_at_the_crown_s_box`, on a stub whose composer
  keeps the cursor in its box (`BOX_STUB`). It attaches a `-C` client, has W1 deliver, and
  checks the row reads `when you leave` with nothing pasted. Then it types `half a thought`
  and detaches: the row reads `after your draft`, with nothing pasted. Then it sends Enter:
  `half a thought` is recorded alone, and the wake lands on its own line.
- The rest of `crown_e2e` holds unchanged on both roads (28/28 hooks, 28/28 mod).
- `app.rs::the_owed_row_names_what_it_waits_on` covers the row's words.
- `backend-tmux` covers the parse.
- Rig `A1`, on real Sonnet: `person_in_crown`, a crown start, then `person_leaves` (hold
  12 s), with the check `held_for_person`. It also proves that a real Claude Code composer
  reads as empty after the person leaves. A false `after your draft` would hold the wake and
  fail the step.

**Corrections from the review of f5f9c8d7 (T-925's crown).**
- **A Codex wake is told at its Enter, not its paste.** A Claude road enters the words as it
  delivers them (`paste_text`, a mod's `submit`), so `told` runs there as before. A Codex box
  takes them and its Enter waits on a person, so the drain moves the wakes and what they tell
  (`Telling`: each card's column as sent, the hands they are about, the card's line) into
  `Daemon::crown_wake_entering` (`crownwake::Entering`). The Enter, or a turn the runtime
  reports begun on it (a person's own Enter), applies `told` and says `crown_wake_sent`.
  `Theirs`, or the owed entry gone (`lose_entering`), puts the wakes back ahead of any owed
  since (`owe_again`, folding by worker), so the crown hears them later. The row shows
  meanwhile: `crown wakes ∙ sending`, or the person's word.
- **Whitespace-free comparison.** Codex wraps a word that does not fit mid-token and at a
  hyphen, so `composer_shows` compares with every blank taken out. And `Theirs` needs a person:
  `Entering::person_came` is set by a sample since the paste that found a client attached.
  With nobody seen, a box that holds text but does not read as the wake is Codex's drawing of
  it (a long box whose `›` row scrolled away, an earlier prompt's `›` read in its place), and
  the Enter goes. An empty box after the composer's wait is the words gone, and owed again.
  Anchoring on the paste's own `›` row was not done: the whitespace-free compare and the
  person rule cover the case without it.
- **Once a second.** `drain_crown_wakes` runs on every landed sample, and each landing asked
  for the next, about 8 forks a second while a draft sat in the box. `want_person` now asks at
  most once per `PERSON_READ_MS` (1 s), whoever calls.
- **A restart during the Enter wait.** `Entering` is kept in `crown.json` (`entering`, same
  schema: an older build drops it and reads the words as a draft, which sends nothing).
  `resume_crown_entering` rebuilds the owed entry at start: `sent` and `codex_input_due` for
  words in the box, or parked again as the wake for words handed over before their paste
  (taking the seat's `unsent`, so T-849's re-park does not send them as a plain prompt). The
  box is then the board's own, never `after your draft`, and its Enter goes on the same terms.
  A latched `codex_submit_sent` was the wake entered; a seat that cannot take it has the wakes
  owed again, `after a restart`.
- **Fail closed.** `codex_wake_box` with no `sent_at` or `sent` on the entry is `Wait`.
- The misplaced doc comment on `BOX_STUB` went back to its test.

**Accepted limits, from that review.**
- The Codex paste rests on a sample up to a tick old (plus the sample's duration, and up to
  1 s for the clients since `PERSON_READ_MS`): a person who starts typing in that gap makes a
  mixed box. It is never sent if they stay in the pane past one sample; a person who
  attaches, types and detaches between two samples is not seen, and that box is entered.
- A woken crown's launch words (Claude or Codex) have no person check: outside the brief.

**Tests added.** The Codex e2e's box wraps mid-token at a width chosen so every break falls
inside a word, and draws the first delivery with its `›` row scrolled away. The edit case now
attaches, edits, detaches, and checks the row says `after your draft`, nothing pressed, no
`crown_wake_sent`, then the wake pasted again into the cleared box and told at its Enter. A
seventh case restarts the daemon while the Enter waits on an attached person: the next daemon
holds it (`when you leave`), never reads it as a draft, pastes nothing again, and enters it
once they leave. Four mutations each fail the e2e: no `resume_crown_entering`; `person_came`
ignored; the compare joined at spaces; told at the paste. `crownledger`'s round trip carries
`entering`; `app.rs` covers `sending`. `want_person`'s once a second has no test of its own:
no unit test builds a `Daemon`.

**Corrections from the review of f4a7df97 / 4471a8ff (T-925's crown).**
- **A person's turn never tells the wake.** `ack_owed` told the wake whenever the crown's new
  turn began while it was owed, so a person's own prompt, sent before the paste or after
  clearing the pasted wake, counted it told and the crown never saw it. The review proposed
  telling it there only when pasted and `!person_came`. That was refused because
  `person_came` is sampled at most once a second, and a person who attached, cleared and sent
  inside that second read as nobody: the e2e caught it. The board's own Enter already tells the
  wake and closes `entering`, so a turn that begins while it is still open met a person's
  Enter, and the wake is owed again (`wake_not_entered`, which now takes the seat). The cost:
  a person who presses Enter on the unedited pasted wake has the crown hear it twice.
- **A restart assumes a person came** (`resume_crown_entering` sets `person_came`): nobody
  watched the pane while no daemon ran, so a box that no longer reads as the wake is the
  person's, never entered.
- **A crown change cancels the old seat's Enter.** `drop_crown_wakes` drops that seat's
  `CROWN_WAKE` entry and `codex_input_due`. The words stay in the box as they are.
- **The row says `sending` while the Enter judges the box**, never `after your draft`
  (`crown_wake_person`). `after your draft` appears only once `Theirs` has owed the wake again.
- The restore filters `entering.wakes` to tickets still on the board. The `entering` field's
  comment says what an older build loses: the wakes moved into it, and their bookkeeping.

**Tests.** Three more Codex e2e cases:
- a person's own prompt while the wake waits for its paste (the box's cursor hidden);
- a person who clears the pasted wake and sends their own words.

  In both, nothing is told, and the wake is owed (`when you leave`), pasted once they leave
  and told at its own Enter.
- the crown taken off while its Enter waits on a person, which presses nothing.

The edited-box case now waits for `Theirs` itself: the entry dropped, then `after your
draft`. Two more mutations fail the e2e: the ack telling the wake, and `drop_crown_wakes`
leaving the entry.

## A crown hears the workers an earlier crown started, and every ticket it holds (T-927, 2026-10-23, "A crown hears nothing from workers a previous crown started, though hold_ticket says their delivery wakes it")

**What happened.** The person moved the crown from T-915 (Codex) to T-925 (Claude). Workers on
T-916, T-917, T-918 and T-922 carried `started_by` = T-915's ticket. The new crown held all
four with `hold_ticket`, whose receipt said "its delivery wakes this session". All four
delivered, and no wake came for 47 to 62 minutes. Two predicates were at fault, and the
restart in that window was not:
- **`Board::started_by_crown` compared `started_by` with the ticket wearing the crown now.**
  A worker an earlier crown started "woke nobody" (T-414's rule). Every other crown road
  already read `started_by.is_some()`: `ask_agent`'s send, `sleep_agent`, `answer_agent` and
  `accept_plan` (`crownplan.rs`), `archive_ticket`'s refusal, `start_agent`'s wake of a parked
  worker, and the spawn budget. So the new crown could steer those workers and could not hear
  them. T-920 reached it only through `answered your ask`, the one cause that skips the claim.
- **`crown_hears` never read `crown_held`.** A hold made by the crown woke the crown only when
  the crown had also started the agent. The receipt and `CROWN_WAKES` promised more than that.

**The rule.** The crown seat owns what a crown started, not the ticket that wore the crown.
`started_by_crown` means "a crown started it, a crown is worn now, and it is not the crown's
own ticket". On a handover the new crown hears the old crown's workers from their next event,
and their `get_ticket` keeps `under_crown`. Nothing is rewritten. `started_by` stays
provenance, and a person's agent (`started_by: None`) never becomes the crown's. The
old seat's owed wakes and baselines are still dropped (`drop_crown_wakes`, T-414), so the new
crown's first look at an inherited worker has no baseline, and a branch that is ahead reads as
a delivery. This was the smallest rule that is true. Copying the old crown's workers into
`crown_watched` was refused, because a watch hears less (no questions, plans or lingering)
than the crown's other tools let it act on. Rewriting `started_by` was refused too, because it
loses provenance and needs a migration for no gain.

**A hold is heard like a watch** (`held_by_crown`, in `crown_hears` and `crown_claims`). It
covers delivered, finished, raised, limited, merged and forge news, with no `crown_watches`
switch, because the receipt promises the wake. A held person's agent still keeps its question,
plan and lingering for the person, as a watched one does. A crown-started agent is heard in
full through provenance. A person's `t` makes the hold the person's (T-919), and the crown's
hearing ends with it.

**What the crown is told: unchanged.** "An agent the crown started" names the board's crown,
and the hold sentence in `CROWN_WAKES` is true now, so no rig test was added. The person's
banners (`notify.rs`) ask the same predicate: while a crown is worn, an inherited worker's news
goes to the crown and no longer to the person.

**Tests.** `board.rs`: `a_worker_an_earlier_crown_started_is_the_crowns_now`. `crown_hold_e2e`:
`a_new_crown_hears_the_old_crown_s_workers_and_the_tickets_it_holds`. Crown A starts a worker.
A person starts their own agent, both in worktrees. The crown moves to B while the worker is
mid-turn. B holds the person's ticket, the daemon restarts, and both deliveries wake B (the
line in B's pane and B's `woke` touch), never A. Without the predicate change the test fails at
`under_crown`. Without `held_by_crown` it times out on the held ticket's wake.

## The rig no longer grades where a crown's delegated worker works (T-929, 2026-10-23)

**Decided by the person.** On Sol, the Codex `delegate` case filed a ticket and started its
worker on `shared_checkout`. The case failed only because it required a worktree. The person's
verdict was "sol did ok". `create_ticket` and `start_agent` both require `workspace`, and
`CROWN_WAKES` offers both values, so the workspace is the crown's choice. A rig that grades the
choice measures a preference the board never states.

**The rule.** Codex's `delegate` (`delegation_problems(..., shared=True)`) and Claude's `filed`
(DL1) accept either workspace. Every other requirement still holds: the crown's own session
files the ticket from its ticket, the feed carries an agent's `create_ticket` and `start_agent`
for it, `started_by` is the crown, and the worker is the only agent seat on that ticket
(`seat_problems`, new). A worktree worker keeps the old checks (`place_problems`): a branch,
the binding's path is the cwd, away from the checkout, and under the fixture's worktrees. A
